# PROJECT AUDIT: AnnualStatement_oldv2 (project B)

A complete "Project Archaeology" of one of the author's two GST programs: what it does, how it is built, every rule it applies, what goes wrong, and how it came to be. It is written for the author (a CA/GST consultant, not a programmer) and for whoever later compares it with project A and rebuilds a merged program.

(b) **Running.** This computer runs Linux (Python 3.14.6, PyQt5 5.15.11 running Qt 5.15.19, openpyxl 3.1.5 - the library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel -, lxml 6.1.3 - a fast XML-reading library that openpyxl uses when it is installed; B itself never imports it; ⚠ these are the audit computer's versions, not requirements of B) and has **no Excel and no pywin32** (pywin32 = the Python add-on that lets Python drive Excel and other Windows programs). Pure-Python parts (file-name recognition, name cleaning, folders and copies, settings and history files, the summary and consolidated workbooks, the window itself) were **run** on realistic made-up inputs in scratch copies under `/root/merge-scratch/run/<task>/`, never in the repository: with `python -B` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (no compiled files written), the home and temporary folders redirected into the scratch folder, and windows drawn "offscreen" (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`: Qt draws in memory, without a screen). Because B's window cannot even be loaded without pywin32 (headline 1), window runs used empty stand-in modules with pywin32's names that only let the loading succeed. (c) **Excel through COM** (COM = Windows' way for one program to remote-control another; here Python drives Microsoft Excel) cannot run here and was **traced by reading**; for the order of B's own calls, recording stand-ins ("fake COM": small objects that only write down which call is made) were used - they prove nothing about what a real Excel does. (d) **Verification.** Every section was re-checked by an independent verifier who reopened every `file:line` and re-ran the main scripts on fresh copies (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-*/`); corrections are marked in place. `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy`, the copy every line number refers to, is byte-identical to the repository (RAN, Section 2.0: git blob hashes - git's fingerprint of a file's exact content - of all 41 files match). |

| **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** | Confidence of an inference: clear from the code or reproduced / a reasonable inference from several clues / a guess. **NOT SURE** always comes with a way to check. |
| **[GST RULE]** | The code decides a tax figure; which return, table, sheet or cell a figure or file belongs to (for example the output sheets "Table 6J Match" and "Table 8D Limits" ⚠, `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:130-153`); a rate, limit or threshold; rounding; the financial year or tax period; GSTIN, PAN or state-code logic; ITC eligibility or reversal; or a due date. When in doubt, a rule is tagged. **For these the audit says exactly what the code does and never whether it is correct**; no law was looked up and no version is recommended. |

| **DEAD** | Defined but never used by the program. "DEAD (in practice)" = could run but never does with the shipped configuration or screens; "DEAD (write-only)" = stored but never read back. B has no tests, so nothing is "used only by tests". |

## SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Project B is a Windows desktop program, "GST File Organizer v4.0", that takes **one folder holding many clients' GST Excel downloads**, recognises each file **only from its name** as one of six kinds - GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B Export, Sales, Sales Reco or Annual Report [GST RULE] ⚠ (`utils/constants.py:13-75`; apart from its size, dates and first 8 bytes, the Python code never reads a client file's contents, `core/file_parser.py:171-215`, Section 4.1) - groups the files per client and state, copies (never moves) them into a dated folder tree `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>/<client>-<state code>/Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>/` (`core/file_organizer.py:67-298`), and builds for every client an **ITC report and a Sales report** from the author's own two Excel templates (pre-built workbooks the program fills in) by writing the copied files' folder paths and file names into each template's "Links" sheet, the sheet the template's Power Query reads (Power Query = Excel's built-in data-import tool; `core/excel_handler.py:65-217, 540-627`). In its fourth step it opens a time-stamped copy of each report in Microsoft Excel, makes Excel refresh the queries by pressing keys, checks one cell, reads 22 configured cells [GST RULE] ⚠ (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:33-228`) and writes them, for all clients, into one workbook `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx` (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:20-174`); every tax figure itself is produced inside the author's templates, which are not in the repository (Appendix X2.1).

It is built for the author's own CA/GST practice (HIGH: the audit method says the author is a CA/GST consultant who built the tool, `Project_Audit_FINAL.md:7`, and the file kinds and templates are those of an annual-statement job), where an annual-statement batch means sorting several downloads per client for many clients, pointing each client's two reconciliation workbooks at the right files, refreshing every workbook and copying the key figures into one summary - work B turns into one window of four tabs, "Step 1: Setup", "Step 2: Validation", "Step 3: Processing" and "Step 4: Extract & Refresh" (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:90-93`); whether colleagues also run it, and on how many clients, is not recorded anywhere in the repository (NOT SURE - Appendix X6 Q51 and Q63 ask the author).

It is built with **Python** and uses **PyQt5** for the window (`requirements.txt:5`; `main.py:37`), **openpyxl** (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel, but drops Power Query when it saves an existing workbook) for the two workbooks it creates itself, the processing summary and the consolidated extraction workbook (`core/excel_handler.py:31-33, 308-346`; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:8-10`), and **Microsoft Excel through COM via pywin32** to fill the templates, refresh their Power Query and read the figures back (`core/excel_handler.py:19-28, 95-217`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15, 165-366, 478-587`), with Windows Script Host (Windows' built-in scripting object) typing the refresh keys (`report_processor.py:216`, keys at `:238-248`); its window therefore opens only on a Windows PC with pywin32 installed (headline 1), and `requirements.txt:2` says "Python 3.7 or higher required" ⚠ although only Python 3.10 or newer gets the newest build of every package it needs (the newest `pyqt5_sip`, PyQt5's helper package, needs 3.10 ⚠; older builds that still satisfy `requirements.txt` can be installed on 3.7-3.9), and B's code was compiled successfully on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 - the only versions tried - and parses under Python 3.7 grammar rules, but was never run on Windows here (Section 9.4; RAN (verifier) `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/scripts/compile_all.py` on 3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16 and 3.14.6: 38 files, 0 errors, 0 failures under the 3.7 grammar check). [Corrected during verification - originally "the newest builds of its packages need Python 3.10 or newer"; per Section 9.4 only `pyqt5_sip` needs 3.10, the others 3.8 or 3.9; the 3.7 grammar check and the read-back of figures through COM were added.]

B reached its present form in one burst: after the 12 shared commits (31-08-2025 to 30-10-2025, the Tkinter "v3.0" organiser plus a separate Tkinter "Power Query Extractor"), a single AI-assisted commit on the morning of 07-02-2026 (`c258047`, "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6", B only (after the split)) rewrote the whole window layer in PyQt5 and merged the two programs into one four-tab window, `a62d3cc` deleted the old Tkinter files two minutes later and left the program unable to start until `c21f788` repaired one import line 27 minutes after that, and two more commits on 08-02-2026 and 09-02-2026 (`7e09e5c`, `b0e7d0e`) restyled the screens towards the old look and twice rebuilt how Step 4 finds the reports (Section 12A) - while the business core (`core/`, `utils/`, `power_query_extractor/`) was left almost untouched apart from logging and error-catching clean-ups and a few lines of dead code removed in `c258047` (for example an unfinished duplicate of the header-writing code in `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py`; READ (verifier) `git show c258047`) and, in `7e09e5c`, the scan's handling of tiny or damaged files (Section 8.3.3, Section 12C.2), and no GST rule value changed at all (no B-only commit touches `utils/constants.py` or `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py`; READ every diff, HIGH; headline 9).

**Current state: an unfinished rewrite that stopped - work-in-progress, dormant since 09-02-2026** (HIGH for the facts; MEDIUM that it was set aside rather than merely paused): all 34 features exist and 30 of them "work with defects", but the problem-file list (`B-F9`) and the old extractor entry point (`B-F31`) are broken and two features are dead - the EXPORT LIST button has no action connected (`B-F10`, `gui/views/validation_view.py:186-200`) and the per-client folder-name option has plumbing but no control (`B-F5`, `models/app_state.py:83`); other plans were left half-done (a central signal hub that nothing imports, `models/signals.py`; window size and last tab saved but never read back, `B-R117`); installing it as its own files say gives a program that cannot open (`requirements.txt:13-14`, headline 1); the README still describes the v3.0 Tkinter program (`README.md:1, 361`); B has no tests and its history holds no record of a run on Windows (Appendix X3; X6 Q63); nothing has been committed or pushed since 09-02-2026, eight and a half months before this audit (RAN (me): GitHub `pushed_at` and `git ls-remote`, 23-10-2026), while project A received 34 commits of its own up to 27-07-2026 (RAN (me): `git rev-list --count A/main` → 46, `git log -1 A/main` → 27-07-2026) - and A's older document calls "a PyQt5 migration … subsequently abandoned" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:18` in project A, written 04-03-2026 and rewritten 05-03-2026), a statement of intent only: the three commits it means are dated 07-02-2026, not 2026-03-04, and are B's `main` line, which went on with `7e09e5c` and `b0e7d0e` (Section 12A); the "separate branch" it names (`copilot-worktree-2026-03-04T11-52-56`, `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:8` in A) exists today in neither GitHub repository, neither checkout and not in the combined history, so whether it once existed as a local branch on the author's PC cannot be checked from here (NOT SURE - only the author can say). [Corrected during verification - originally "whose "separate branch" and "2026-03-04" are wrong"; the branch's name looks like a time stamp of 04-03-2026 and project A's audit rates it CANNOT VERIFY, so only its absence today is established.] Section 6 rates B's defensive coding **MODERATE** overall and **FRAGILE** exactly where it drives Excel, produces the consolidated figures or starts up, and Section 7 lists **82 gaps, 20 of them HIGH**: 39 lie wholly in code B shares with A, 17 partly, and 26 come only from B's own commits; of the 20 HIGH ones, 11 are wholly shared (so project A very probably carries them too - to be checked in the comparison), 5 partly, and 4 (`B-G12`, `B-G20`, `B-G32`, `B-G67`) are B's own (RAN (me): count of the lists in Section 7.10 "Where the gaps come from").

### Headline findings

The most important findings of Sections 3, 5 and 7 and of Appendix X1. Each item names its IDs, the code (`file:line` at `b0e7d0e`), how it was established and where the full entry is. The first three are the ones to read first.

**Read these three first**

1. **The program cannot open at all without pywin32, and B's own installation files leave pywin32 out** - `B-G32` (HIGH; `B-F1`, `B-F30`, `B-R124`, `B-R125`; Section 3 `B-F1`; Appendix X1 finding 1; X4.6 `D1`). `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` imports the five pywin32 modules (`pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`) with no fallback, and the window loads that file while it is itself being loaded (`gui/__init__.py:7` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25` → `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` → `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10`), whereas `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` and `utils/helpers.py:473-483` guard the same imports. `requirements.txt:13-14` lists pywin32 only as a comment (`# pywin32>=306`), so the README's installation `pip install -r requirements.txt` (pip = Python's package installer; `README.md:97-102`) gives a program that stops with "Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'" and the advice "pip install PyQt5 openpyxl" (`main.py:49-54`), which does not help. RAN (me): `main.py` without pywin32 → exit code 1 (the number a program hands back when it ends: 0 = normal, anything else = failure), that message, and a one-line `gst_organizer.log` in the start folder; `launch_extractor.py` → "Failed to launch: No module named 'pythoncom'", exit code 1, no log file. RAN (verifier) on a fresh copy in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/` (`out/main_nopywin32.txt`, `out/launch_nopywin32.txt`): the same messages, exit code 1 both times, an 83-byte one-line log in the start folder of `main.py` only. This dates from `c258047` (B only (after the split)): at `47a1492` the Tkinter organiser did not load the extractor and could open without pywin32 (RAN by the Section 12 writer on extracted copies of each commit: Sections 12B.7 and 12F.5; Appendix X1 finding 1). B therefore runs only on Windows, although `README.md:52` still lists macOS and Linux. One side effect is protective: B's openpyxl fallback for report filling, which silently strips Power Query while reporting success (RAN, Appendix X1 finding 1, `B-R97`), cannot be reached through the window - it would come back if the import were simply made optional.

2. **Nine of the 22 figure columns of the consolidated Step 4 workbook show a different cell from the one the configuration names** [GST RULE] ⚠ - `B-G1` (HIGH; `B-F23`, `B-R79` to `B-R83`; Appendix X1 finding 8; X4.6 `D2`). In `PQ_Extraction_Report_*.xlsx` the IGST, CGST and SGST columns of the sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" show the values read from `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15`, not their configured cells `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1` and `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1` (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:156-228`). Cause: for each column the code first takes the first extracted field whose name merely *contains* the column title (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:130-133`) and only afterwards the exact field (`:136-138`); the one-word titles "IGST", "CGST", "SGST" match the earlier "GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST/CGST/SGST" fields. Precisely, the configured cell is used only when the J15/K15/L15 value read is empty (`None`: an empty cell or a missing sheet); an empty text gives "Missing" and 0 gives 0 (RAN, Section 5 `B-R83`). RAN (me) (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S1/scripts/check_consolidator.py`: one invented marker per configured cell, stored the way `report_processor.py:507-539` stores them, through the real `DataConsolidator.create_report`): "output sheets 9, figure columns 22, columns OK 13, mismatched 9", each of the nine receiving J15, K15 or L15; the same result was RAN in Sections 3, 7 and 8 and Appendices X1 and X4. RAN (verifier) independently through the real `ReportProcessor._extract_data` with stand-in Excel objects that answer each configured cell with its own invented marker, then the real `DataConsolidator.create_report` (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/scripts/consolidator_via_extract.py` → `out/consolidator_via_extract.txt`): again 13 OK / 9 mismatched, the same nine columns; and with `Diff GSTR-3B!J15` set to nothing / an empty text / 0 / a missing sheet, the "IMS Reco" IGST column showed the configured cell / "Missing" / 0 / the configured cell (`scripts/consolidator_j15_variants.py` → `out/j15_variants.txt`). It began with `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), which added those three sheets to an unchanged look-up; project A's audit reports the same 13 / 9 (`A-G1`). The workbook looks complete and nothing warns; no test exists. This is a technical mismatch between the configuration and the code - **which cell each column should show is the author's call**.

3. **A Power Query refresh cannot be trusted as done, and Step 4 acts on whatever window has the keyboard focus** - `B-G6`, `B-G62`, `B-G61` (all HIGH; `B-F19`, `B-F20`, `B-F26`, `B-R66` to `B-R71`, `B-R102`, `B-R103`; Appendix X1 findings 3 to 6). Step 4 opens each report copy in a visible, maximised Excel obtained with `Dispatch` (pywin32's plain "give me an Excel" call, which may hand back an Excel that is already running; `report_processor.py:174, 181-183`), asks Windows to bring that Excel forward and then types Alt+A, R, A ⚠ (Excel's English ribbon keys for Data → Refresh All) into whichever window has the keyboard focus (`:213-249`) - also when Excel could not be brought forward, which is only written to the program log (`:226, 229-230`), and also when every attempt to open the workbook was refused and no workbook is open (`:195-205`; RAN (fake COM), X1 finding 4). It then waits fixed times - 19 seconds plus the wait setting plus the larger of 10 seconds and the wait setting, i.e. 39 seconds per report at the default of 10 (`:139-141, 207-319` - the last 3 of the 19 fixed seconds are the 2 s after saving at `:307` and the 1 s after closing at `:319`; RAN, Section 5 `B-R68`) [line range corrected during verification - originally `:139-141, 207-298`, which leaves out `:307` and `:319`] - and **always saves the copy** (`wb.Save()` at `:305`, before the result is decided at `:310-313`), also after an error dialog or a failed check. Apart from "no error dialog seen", the only proof of success is that a sheet named "Info" (any letter case) exists and its cell `BB2` [GST RULE] ⚠ holds something other than nothing, a blank text, 0 or one of eight Excel error texts (`:589-636`), which a value already in the file also passes (RAN (fake COM): with BB2 left from another client and no refresh at all, B reported success, ✓ and every figure; X1 finding 6). Excel's own refresh commands (`RefreshAll`, `BackgroundQuery = False`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`), which Standard 12 asks for, appear nowhere in B and in none of its 17 commits (RAN, `git log -S`, Section 9.13; X1.3.6: the refresh session misses 11 of the Standard-12 rules that apply to it). The "error dialog" check looks at every visible window of every program on the desktop and picks the first whose title contains one of ten words (for example "error", "cannot", "missing" or "microsoft excel") and whose window type is a standard dialog (`:368-404`, word list `:376-387`, dialog types `:392`), and clicks the first button whose text merely contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue" (`:443-476`): RAN with stand-in windows (X1 finding 5; Section 3 `B-F26`), another program's dialog was recorded as the refresh error and its button clicked, an Excel question was answered "Yes", and a button "Look up…" was clicked because it contains "ok". What real Excel and Windows do with the keys and clicks is READ only: HIGH for the code, MEDIUM for the effect on a real desktop.

**Further headline findings**

4. **Step 3 takes over the user's own open Excel, hides it and closes it** - `B-G63` (HIGH; `B-F13`, `B-F14`, `B-R96`, `B-R99`; Appendix X1 finding 2; X4.6 `D4`). `core/excel_handler.py:110-115` first grabs a running Excel (`GetActiveObject` = "attach to the Excel that is already open", normally the user's own) and only otherwise starts one; it sets `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` on it (`:118-120`), and at the end switches the prompts back on (`:204-205`) and **always** calls `Quit()` (`:209`), because the test under the comment "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:206-207`) reads `self.excel_app`, which is set only once, to "nothing" (`:55`). This happens once per report, twice per client. RAN (fake COM, X1 run S3 "user_excel"): the user's own unsaved workbook was still open when `Quit()` was called; what a real Excel then does (a hidden "save changes?" prompt) is MEDIUM. In Step 4, `Dispatch` (`report_processor.py:174, 487`) may also hand back the user's running Excel (MEDIUM), and the second open attempt closes every workbook of the same file name in that Excel **without saving** (`:691-697`). Standard 12 asks for a separate, private Excel (`DispatchEx`), which B never uses (X1.3.6). Nothing stops Steps 3 and 4 from driving Excel at the same time (`B-G74`; RAN, Section 3 `B-F34`).

5. **Reports and clients are reported as successful when they are not** - `B-G5`, `B-G4`, `B-G19`, `B-G20` (HIGH), `B-G2` [GST RULE] ⚠ (MEDIUM-HIGH) (`B-F9`, `B-F13` to `B-F15`, `B-R50`, `B-R52`, `B-R53`, `B-R56`, `B-R60`, `B-R95`; Appendix X1 finding 7; X4.6 `D6`). The template is copied to the final report name before it is opened (`core/excel_handler.py:122-129`), so any failed fill leaves the **unfilled template under `ITC_Report_…xlsx` / `Sales_Report_…xlsx`**, which Step 4 later lists and refreshes like a real report (RAN (fake COM), X1 runs "long_path" and "excel_dies"). A template without a "Links" sheet produces no error on screen (only a line "Links sheet not found! Creating one..." in the program log, `:151`): the Excel path writes into the first sheet whose name merely contains "link", or else adds a new "Links" sheet and writes into that, and the openpyxl path writes nothing - and the report still counts as made (`:131-153`, `:233-244`). Links cells for file types the client does not have are skipped (`:162`), so the template's own content stays in them [GST RULE] ⚠, and every processed client always gets both reports whatever files it has (`B-R50`). A client counts as "Success" when its folders were made, its files copied and its organisation report written without an error escaping - even if both its reports failed, because report failures are caught inside the report step and only counted (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:98-147` against `:204-239`; RAN, Section 7 `B-G19`: with a folder given as both templates, "Processing complete: 1/1" and an Errors sheet saying "No errors encountered"). The summary workbook's "Variations" sheet always says "No file variations found", because the worker hands it an empty list (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:73`); the list of unrecognised or invalid files never reaches the user anywhere, only its count (`B-F9` "broken") - a regression from the split point, where the scan's list was passed (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:161@47a1492`).

6. **"Refreshed" means only "such a file exists", and failed figures look like missing ones** - `B-G7` (HIGH), `B-G10` [GST RULE] (MEDIUM-HIGH), `B-G9` (MEDIUM) (`B-F18`, `B-F20`, `B-F21`, `B-R63`, `B-R70`, `B-R88`, `B-R136`; Appendix X1 finding 9; X4.6 `D13`). The refreshed copy is made before Excel is even started (`report_processor.py:118-120`), so a failed refresh still leaves an unrefreshed `…_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`; the Step 4 list then shows that version as "Refreshed (date)" in green because any `*_Refreshed*` file exists (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:466-479`), and "Skip refresh" re-uses the newest such file and reports success with ✓ and every figure (`report_processor.py:100-111`; RAN (fake COM), X1 runs "no_excel" and "skip_after_failed"). Conversely, a report whose refresh check failed has **every figure written as "Missing"** although the cells were read (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:116-117`), which looks the same as "not ticked" or "not found" (RAN, X1 E2E). Both searches use the fixed text `_Refreshed`, so a changed Step 4 "File suffix" breaks Skip refresh and the status (`B-G9`).

7. **Step 4 can show, and write into, an older batch; "Resume" does not resume** - `B-G12`, `B-G13` (both HIGH; `B-F12`, `B-F18`, `B-R38`, `B-R39`, `B-R44`; X4.6 `D5`, `D7`). Step 4 takes as "latest" the `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder whose name sorts last (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:430-448`); the names begin with the day of the month, so a December folder beats a later October one. RAN (me) with the same sort on invented folder names: "Annual Statement-311225 1000" (31-12-2025) was chosen over "Annual Statement-211026 0335" (21-10-2026); the real window chose the same (RAN, Section 3 `B-F18`, X4.6 `D7`). RAN (verifier) (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/scripts/dayfirst_sort.py` → `out/dayfirst_sort.txt`, three invented empty folders, the October-2026 one modified last): the Step 4 expression chose "Annual Statement-311225 1000", the Re-Run / Resume expression chose "Annual Statement-211026 0335". Its consolidated workbook and extraction log then go into that older folder. Re-Run and Resume choose differently - by the folder's last-modified time (`core/file_organizer.py:158-169`). And every processing run makes a new minute-stamped `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder (`core/file_organizer.py:98-104`; time from `utils/helpers.py:23-25`), so "Resume" skips files only when repeated within the same clock minute and otherwise copies everything again, and "Re-Run" overwrites only within the same minute (RAN, Section 7 `B-G13`); the radio buttons (`gui/views/setup_view.py:343-347`), the help card (`:510-512`) and the README (`README.md:142-145`) describe the modes three different ways.

8. **Files are recognised by name only; one hyphen or one spelling difference silently misfiles them** [GST RULE] ⚠ - `B-G17`, `B-G16`, `B-G15` (all HIGH; `B-F4`, `B-F6`, `B-R5` to `B-R11`, `B-R17`, `B-R21`, `B-R22`, `B-R32`). The six name patterns take client and state as "one or more characters that are not a hyphen" (`[^-]+`, `utils/constants.py:13-62`): a client written with a hyphen is mis-split (client "Client", state "D Exports") in GSTR-2B Reco, Sales Reco and Annual Report names, and makes GSTR-3B, Sales and IMS Reco names unrecognised; "Sales-Reco-…" is read as a Sales file of a client "Reco" (RAN, Section 3 `B-F6` and the registry; RAN (verifier) `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/scripts/names.py` → `out/names.txt` with invented names: the same splits, refusals and "Reco" client; "Tamil Nadu" / "Tamilnadu" → TN / TAM, "Delhi" / "DL" → DL / DL). A client is the name text exactly as written plus a state code (`core/file_parser.py:258-262`), so "Tamil Nadu" and "Tamilnadu" (codes TN and TAM) make two clients while "Delhi" and "DL" make one; the state table (39 names, 36 two-letter codes ⚠, `utils/constants.py:234-275`) invents codes for names it does not know (`utils/helpers.py:485-511`). Two different clients can end up in one client folder after "Private" → "Pvt", "Limited" → "Ltd" and the length cut (default 35 characters, applied even while the "Max length" box is greyed out; `utils/helpers.py:513-537`; RAN, Section 7 `B-G15`, `B-G24`). The period, month, date and year parts of the names are stored but never checked or used (`core/file_parser.py:93-102`, `B-R23`), and B has no financial-year, GSTIN, PAN, rate, threshold or due-date logic anywhere (READ, search of every `.py` file; registry scope notes). These are described only; whether any of them is right is the author's call.

9. **Where the GST rules live, and how stable they are** [GST RULE] ⚠ - Section 5, Section 12C.2. 45 of the 144 rules are tagged [GST RULE] and 28 carry a ⚠ value (RAN (me): count of the registry). They sit in the six file-name patterns and six expected file types (`utils/constants.py:13-75`), the state table and its fallback (`utils/constants.py:234-275`; `utils/helpers.py:485-511`), the Links-sheet cells (`utils/constants.py:96-120`; the values are prepared by `core/excel_handler.py:540-627` and written at `:159-165`, or `:246-250` on the openpyxl path) [citation made precise during verification - originally "written by `core/excel_handler.py:540-627`", which only prepares them], the `Info!BB2` refresh test (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:589-636`) and the 22 extraction cells in 9 output sheets, including the GSTR-9 labels "Table 6J Match" (sheet "T6 of R9", K29) and "Table 8D Limits" (sheet "T8 of R9", G6) ⚠ (the code never says "GSTR-9"; that "R9" in the sheet names means GSTR-9 is an inference, MEDIUM - the templates are not in the repository) (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:33-228`). **No GST rule value - file-name pattern, expected type, state code, Links cell, extraction cell, sheet name or the BB2 check - was ever modified or removed in B's whole history**; values were only added, the last time when `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) added six extraction sheets (14 cells), which started headline 2 (READ every diff, HIGH; Section 12C.2). GST-tagged *behaviour* changed in three places only: per-report (ITC / Sales) selection in `bd176bf` (shared; `B-R61`, `B-R70`, `B-R88`), the unrecognised-file hint no longer reaching the summary workbook from `c258047` (`B-R12`), and a client-folder length floor of 5 in `c258047` that could cut the state code off, with the floor of 15 restored in `7e09e5c` (`B-R32`) (both B only (after the split)).

10. **Start-up and window errors are invisible or end the program; the log lands in the start folder** - `B-G34` (HIGH), `B-G35`, `B-G36`, `B-G33`, `B-G44` (MEDIUM) (`B-F1`, `B-F27`, `B-F30`, `B-F32`, `B-R121`, `B-R125`; Section 9.9). Start-up errors are only printed to the console (the black text window) and logged (`main.py:49-59`); there is no `sys.excepthook` (Python's hook for errors nothing else caught; READ, search: none), no error file and no message box, so under `pythonw` (the console-less Python that the author's Standard 13 launcher uses, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:962`) nothing at all is visible (RAN, Section 9.9). An error in any window handler ends the program at once (exit code 134 - the number Linux reports for a program that aborts itself), without saving the settings - for example a damaged `~/.gst_organizer/session_state.json` followed by View > Dark Mode (RAN, Section 3 `B-F1` case D) - and one wrongly typed value in `settings.json` stops the window being built (RAN). RAN (verifier), with empty stand-ins for pywin32 (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/out/caseD.txt`, `out/caseE.txt`): `"recent_source_folders": "C:/old"` plus View > Dark Mode → "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'insert'" (`models/cache_manager.py:49`), exit code 134, `settings.json` unchanged; `"client_name_max_length": "35"` (text instead of a number) → "Critical error: setValue(self, val: int): argument 1 has unexpected type 'str'", exit code 1, no window. `gst_organizer.log` is opened by a bare name (`main.py:20`), so it lands in whatever folder the program was started from - under the Standard 13 launcher one shared log in the shared program folder, holding client folder names, Links values and every extracted figure (Appendix X2.7; `B-G64`) - and `launch_extractor.py` sets up no program log at all (`launch_extractor.py:1-28` has no logging set-up; RAN (me): no file created), although a Step 4 run started from it still writes its `Extraction_Log_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.txt` into the run folder (`gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:109-121`) [clarified during verification - originally "writes no log at all"].

11. **Three of the four Browse buttons are invisible, nothing is locked during a job, and Step 4 rarely says why a report failed** - `B-G67` (HIGH), `B-G74`, `B-G70`, `B-G71` (MEDIUM), `B-G56` (MEDIUM-HIGH) (`B-F3`, `B-F16`, `B-F24`, `B-F29`, `B-F34`; Section 10 `U2`-`U5`, `U14`). The Source, ITC and Sales "Browse" buttons (`gui/views/setup_view.py:204-206, 234-236, 252-254`) draw white text on white because the card behind them sets `QWidget { background: white; }` (a Qt style rule that paints every element inside the card, buttons included, white; `gui/widgets/colored_section.py:62`) (RAN, Section 10: 100 % white pixels; RAN (verifier) `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S1/out/browse_pixels.txt`: all three buttons 100.0 % white in light mode; the fourth, Target "BROWSE", has its own orange-red style, `gui/views/setup_view.py:308-323`). While processing or extraction runs, START, DRY RUN, SCAN FILES and Start Extraction stay clickable, both Excel jobs can run together, and closing the window is accepted at once (RAN, Section 3 `B-F34`). For many failures (Excel cannot start, no report found, a report type not ticked, a cell not readable) the reason goes only to the program log, and the reasons that do reach the screen arrive as ordinary blue lines; after a run in which every refresh failed, Step 4 still shows "Refreshed" in green and its tab dot turns green (RAN, Section 10 `U3`, `U4`, `U25`). The on-screen logs add every line as web markup (HTML) to one text block, so they drop any text between "<" and ">" and slow down sharply as they grow (about 49 seconds of window time for 2,000 lines; RAN, VW).

12. **What is solid (a reassurance)** - Appendix X1 finding 13, Section 6.5, `B-R42`. Client source files are only checked (size, dates, first 8 bytes) and copied (`core/file_parser.py:176, 195-196`; `utils/helpers.py:169`); templates are only checked and copied (`core/excel_handler.py:78, 124, 228`); Step 4 refreshes a copy and never the Step 3 report (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:118-120`). RAN (X1 E2E): the SHA-256 fingerprints (a SHA-256 fingerprint identifies a file's exact content) of all 17 invented source and template files were identical before and after a whole Step 1-4 run. The three long jobs run in background threads (parallel lines of work inside the program, so the window stays usable) that never touch a window element directly (RAN, Section 3 `B-F34`), errors are contained per file, client and report, and none of the 91 error handlers is a bare `except:` (Section 6.1; `c258047` replaced all 26). No code anywhere kills an Excel process (RAN, X1 finding 11).

## SECTION 2: PROJECT STRUCTURE MAP

This section maps every file of project B (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2`, branch `main`, snapshot `b0e7d0e`, 09-02-2026, the PyQt5 window that calls itself "GST File Organizer v4.0"), says which file starts the program and how, and lists the dead code (code that nothing in the running program ever uses) at every level: files, classes, functions and methods, constants and variables, dictionary keys, stored values, parameters, imports and screen elements.

### 2.0 How to read this section

- **Paths** are repository-relative (`core/file_parser.py:136` = line 136 of that file at `b0e7d0e`). An old version is written `path:line@commit`.
- **Line counts** are the real number of lines. 18 of the 41 files have no line-break character after their last line, so the file list `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_files.txt` (made with `wc -l`, which counts line-break characters) shows one line fewer for those 18 files. Examples: it shows `.gitignore` as 81 (real 82), `utils/helpers.py` as 536 (real 537), and the three docstring-only package files `power_query_extractor/config/__init__.py`, `power_query_extractor/core/__init__.py` and `power_query_extractor/gui/__init__.py` as 0 lines, although each holds one line (a docstring). The 38 Python files have **7,821** real lines (`wc -l` says 7,805). RAN: a Python count of every tracked file (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/count_and_hash.py`).
- **READ** = established by reading the code. **RAN** = established by running something, always on a copy under `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/` (copy `proj/`), with `python -B` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (no compiled files written), `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` (Qt draws windows in memory, because this Linux machine has no screen), the home folder redirected (`HOME=/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/home_*`) and the start folder set to scratch folders (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/cwd_*`). After all runs, `diff -rq` showed `proj/` still identical to `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy`, and `find … -name __pycache__` found 0 folders in either (RAN).
- **Verification pass.** Every `file:line` in this section was re-opened against the code (or `git show <commit>:<path>` for `@commit` citations), and the main RAN claims were re-run on a second copy under `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S2/` (`python -B`, stand-ins as below): line counts and blob hashes, the AST counts, both entry points with and without the stand-ins, the `sys.modules` list, the EXPORT LIST receivers, the widget counts and objectNames, the old-settings re-import, the same-minute organiser runs and the Browse-button pixels. Lines marked "added during verification" were added in that pass.
- **B-copy is identical to the repository.** RAN: for all 41 tracked files, `git hash-object` of the file in `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy` equals the blob hash in `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined ls-tree -r B/main` (41 of 41).
- **Stand-ins for pywin32.** This machine has no Excel and no pywin32 (the Python add-on that lets Python drive Windows programs such as Excel). Project B's window cannot even be imported without pywin32 (2.7). For the runs that needed the window, tiny stand-in modules named `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui` were put first on Python's search path (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/stubs/`). They only let the import succeed; any real Excel call through them raises an error. Every statement that depends on them says so.
- **Confidence** on inferences: **HIGH** (clear from the code or reproduced), **MEDIUM** (a reasonable inference), **LOW** (a guess; how to check is given).
- **Commit labels.** The 12 commits shared by A and B (`edac6a3`, `cbfa4a5`, `6237597`, `9c56a1c`, `d674386`, `5ea77c2`, `1cb878b`, `01862a0`, `1c48722`, `4c42758`, `bd176bf`, `47a1492`) are marked "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025". B's own 5 commits (`c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`, `7e09e5c`, `b0e7d0e`, 07-02-2026 to 09-02-2026) are marked "B only (after the split)".
- **[GST RULE]** marks anything that decides a tax figure, which return, table, sheet or cell a figure belongs to, a state code, a period and so on. For these this section only says what the code does; it never says whether it is right. **⚠** marks values that change over time (return and table names, template cell positions, state lists, package versions) so the author can check them.
- **Registry IDs** (`B-F…` features, `B-R…` rules) are those of `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_registry.md`. See Section 3 for features and Section 5 for rules.

**Tags used on every file** (from the author's audit method):

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [CORE] | essential program logic (including the two start files and the three background-job controllers, which run the scan, the processing and the extraction) |
| [UI] | the window and what the user sees and clicks |
| [CONFIG] | settings files and configuration tables |
| [DATA] | templates, samples or input/output data |
| [UTIL] | helper code used by several parts |
| [TEST] | automated tests - **no file of B carries this tag: B has no tests** (2.8.12) |
| [DOCS] | documentation |
| [TOOLING] | files for development tools (in B's history: the AI coding assistant's permission file; none at the snapshot) |
| [GENERATED] | created automatically when the program runs; "safe to delete" is stated per file, because some generated files are the user's real output or settings |

**Plain-English terms used in this section** (explained once here):
- *module* (one `.py` file of Python code); *package* (a folder of modules that contains an `__init__.py` file; Python runs that file whenever anything inside the folder is first used).
- *import* (one file asking to use code from another file); *re-export* (a package's `__init__.py` importing names from its own modules so that other code could write `from package import Name`); `__all__` (an optional list in a module naming what it "officially" offers to `from package import *`); `__version__` / `__author__` (informal labels a module may carry).
- *class* (a blueprint for objects, for example the main window); *instantiate* (create an object from a class); *method* (a function that belongs to a class); *attribute* (a value stored on an object, written `self.name`); *property* (a method that is read like an attribute, without brackets); *dataclass* (a class that mainly holds named values, called fields).
- *parameter* (an input a function accepts); *default* (the value used when the caller gives none).
- *entry point* (the file a person runs to start a program).
- *dead code* (code that exists but is never used by the running program); *unreachable* (code that can never run because of how the code around it is written); *dormant* (code that could run, but the shipped configuration or screens never make it run); *write-only* (a value that is stored or saved but never read back).
- *AST* (abstract syntax tree: Python's own parsed form of a source file; the scripts used here read it to list every definition and every use without running the program).
- *signal / slot / connect / emit* (Qt's messaging system: an object *emits* a named *signal*; every function *connected* to it - a *slot* - then runs); *callback* (a function handed to another piece of code to be called later, for example on a click or by Windows when it lists windows); *worker thread* (a second line of work running beside the window so the window does not freeze; Qt's `QThread`).
- *COM* (Windows' way for one program to drive another, here Python driving Excel; needs pywin32); *openpyxl* (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel); *PyQt5* (the Python version of the Qt window toolkit that B uses).
- *current folder* (the folder a program was started from; a file name with no folder part is created there); *home folder* (`%USERPROFILE%` on Windows, for example `C:\Users\<user>`); *system temp folder* (`%TEMP%` on Windows).
- *Power Query* (Excel's data-import tool; its queries live inside the report workbook and are re-run by "refresh"); *Links sheet* (the sheet of the ITC and Sales templates into which the program writes folder paths and file names for the template's queries).
- *git* terms: *commit* (one saved change in the history); *blob hash* (git's fingerprint of a file's exact content); *trailer* (a `Key: value` line at the end of a commit message, such as `Co-Authored-By:`); *tracked* (a file git keeps in the repository; *ignored* = a file git is told never to keep, by `.gitignore`).
- *docstring* (the text in triple quotes at the top of a file, class or function that describes it; Python ignores it when running); *module-level function* (a function written directly in a file, not inside a class); *lambda* (a small unnamed one-line function, often handed to a button, a sort or a dictionary); *type hint* (a label such as `Optional` or `Tuple` that only documents what kind of value a function expects; Python does not check it).
- *event loop* (Qt's wait-for-clicks loop that keeps the window alive until it is closed); *objectName* (a name given to a screen element so that a style rule such as `QPushButton#primary` can target it); *HTML* (web-page formatting text, used here to colour log lines and the scan summary).
- *JSON* (a plain-text format for saved data, used by the settings files); *UTF-8* (a text encoding that can show any character, including ₹ and emoji); *stem* (a file name without its extension, e.g. `Report` for `Report.xlsx`); *stat* (asking Windows for a file's size and dates).
- *8.3 short path* (Windows' old-style shortened form of a long path, such as `C:\PROGRA~1\...`, used here as a retry when Excel cannot open a long path); *ZIP / OLE first bytes* (the fixed bytes at the start of every `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` file, which is a ZIP package, or of an old `.xls` file, which uses Microsoft's OLE format); *bare `except:`* (an error catcher that catches every error without naming it); *shebang line* (a first line such as `#!/usr/bin/env python` that tells Linux or macOS which program runs the file; Windows ignores it); *virtual environment* (a private Python installation for one project).
- (Added during the completeness check, for terms this section uses without explaining them:) *CI files* (continuous-integration settings, such as a `.github/` folder, that make a server check every change automatically); *`pytest.ini`* (the settings file of pytest, Python's usual test runner); *exception* (the error object Python raises when something fails); *traceback* (Python's list of the calls that led to an error); *log levels* INFO / WARNING / ERROR (how important a log line is; INFO is the ordinary level); *root logger* (Python's default log channel, which every module's log lines reach); *`QApplication`* (the Qt object every PyQt5 program creates first); *widget* (any visible element of a window: a button, a box, a list); *GUI* (graphical user interface: the program's windows); *ETA* (estimated time still needed); *`EnumWindows` / `EnumChildWindows`* (Windows functions that list every top-level window on the desktop, or every element inside one window).

So every re-export in the 8 package files is unused; the files still run because Python runs a package's `__init__.py` before any module inside it.
- **The chain that makes pywin32 a start-up requirement:** `main.py:38` → `gui/__init__.py:7` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25` → `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` → `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10` → `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` (`import pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`, with no guard). RAN: the traceback of `import gui.pyqt_main_window` without pywin32 passes through exactly these lines. RAN without stand-ins: `import gui.views.setup_view` and `import power_query_extractor.core.report_processor` both fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'`. By contrast `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` and `utils/helpers.py:475-483` guard the same imports (B-R124).
- **What can be used without the window:** `core.*`, `utils.*`, `models.app_state`, `models.cache_manager`, `models.run_history`, `power_query_extractor.config.cell_mappings` and `power_query_extractor.core.data_consolidator` import without PyQt5 and without pywin32 (RAN). Importing `core.file_parser` alone also loads `core.excel_handler` and openpyxl (because `core/__init__.py:6-8` runs first) and therefore switches off all Python warnings (`core/excel_handler.py:17`) (RAN: `core.excel_handler` and `openpyxl` were in `sys.modules`).
- `gui/widgets/collapsible_group.py` is loaded at every start only because `gui/widgets/__init__.py:4` imports it whenever a view imports `gui.widgets.colored_section` (RAN: `gui.widgets.collapsible_group` was in `sys.modules`).
- No circular import exists today: `utils/constants.py` imports nothing from the project (`utils/constants.py:6-7`), so the "avoid circular import" comment at `utils/helpers.py:490` describes an old problem (`6237597`, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025, changed it from `utils.constants` to `.constants`) (MEDIUM that the late import is still needed - it is harmless either way).

It appends (not inserts) its folder to the search path (`:8`), which is redundant when run as a script. | RAN with stand-ins: window opened on tab 3 "Step 4: Extract && Refresh" (shown on screen as "Extract & Refresh"); application name "launch_extractor.py"; no log file in the start folder; on close `session_state.json` held `"active_tab": 3`. RAN without pywin32: prints "Failed to launch: No module named 'pythoncom'", exit code 1 (B-F30). |
| 3 | `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` | not mentioned by B's README any more as a command; formerly called by the v3 `launch_extractor.py` | Would configure `pq_extractor.log` and open the Tkinter extractor window. | **Broken**: RAN `python -m power_query_extractor.extractor_main` (stand-ins on the path, so pywin32 is not the cause) → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'power_query_extractor.gui.extractor_window'` at `:9`; RAN `python power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` → `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package`. Nothing imports it (B-F31). |

Both working entry points end in the same window; the difference is only the starting tab and the missing logging set-up in `launch_extractor.py`. Neither matches the author's Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`): there is no `Run [App Name].bat` started with `pythonw.exe -B -s` (`:951-975`), no `sys.excepthook` / `threading.excepthook` with a log file and message box (`:984-1029`; B prints errors to a console that a double-clicked program does not show, `main.py:49-59`, `launch_extractor.py:22-24`), the log goes to the current folder instead of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` (`:1035-1040`; `main.py:20`), and settings go to `~/.gst_organizer` (`models/cache_manager.py:17`) instead of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\`. Stated as facts only; the full comparison belongs to Section 9.

### 2.8 Dead code at every level

#### 2.8.0 How the dead code was found

Every item below was first listed by a script and then confirmed by reading the code at the cited lines (and, where the item could be exercised, by running the program).

| Script (all in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S2/`) | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `dead_scan.py` | Parses all 38 Python files into their AST; lists every class, function, method, nested function, module-level name and class-level name with every use (plain names, `x.name` attribute uses, identifier-like strings, keyword arguments and `from … import name`), separating re-exports inside `__init__.py` files; builds the import graph and what each entry point reaches; lists attributes stored but never read, parameters never read inside their own function, local variables never read, unused imports, and every `.connect(`, lambda, `getattr`/`hasattr`, `moveToThread` and Windows window-listing call | `out/imports.txt`, `out/defs.tsv`, `out/attrs.txt`, `out/params.txt`, `out/locals.txt`, `out/unused_imports.txt`, `out/indirect.txt` |
| `receivers.py` | For the 21 method names defined in more than one class (for example `reset` in `FileParser`, `ProcessingView` and `ProcessingState`; `addLayout` in `CollapsibleCard`, `CollapsibleGroup`, `ColoredSection` and every Qt layout), lists every use with its receiver (`self.x`, `section.x`, `layout.x` …) and the function it sits in, so that a plain name count cannot hide a dead method | `out/receivers.txt` |
| `transitive.py` | Marks as dead every function whose only uses sit inside dead code | console (found `FileOrganizer._is_folder_empty`) |
| `defaults.py` | For every parameter with a default value, lists every program call and whether it supplies that parameter | `out/defaults.txt` |

| `git grep` / `git log -S` on `/root/merge-scratch/combined` | When each dead item was added and whether it had callers at `edac6a3`, `47a1492`, `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `7e09e5c` | quoted in the "Since" columns |

## SECTION 3: FEATURE INVENTORY

This section lists every feature of project B (AnnualStatement_oldv2, branch main, snapshot b0e7d0e of 09-02-2026, the PyQt5 window that calls itself "GST File Organizer v4.0") and documents, feature by feature, what it does, where it lives, what goes in and what comes out, how the user starts it, and one concrete worked example ("trace") followed through the code to the real result. The **first part** of the section gives the table of all 34 features and the full entries for **B-F1 to B-F17** (start-up, Step 1 Setup, Step 2 Validation, Step 3 Processing). B-F18 to B-F34 (Step 4 Extract & Refresh and the cross-cutting features) follow in the second part, further down this section. [Corrected during self-review - originally stated "This file is the first part of the section", but the assembled audit holds both parts of Section 3 in one document, so "file" referred to the writer's working file.]

**How the traces were made (read this once).**

- Every feature ID and rule ID (B-F…, B-R…) is the one in the project-B registry (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_registry.md`). Locations are `file:line` in project B at b0e7d0e, repository-relative (for example `core/file_parser.py:243`). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **RAN** = the code was executed on made-up inputs and the result is quoted from the output. **READ** = the statement comes from reading the code line by line. Every inference carries a confidence word: **HIGH**, **MEDIUM** or **LOW**.
- All runs used a scratch copy of the code (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/proj`, byte-for-byte equal to the repository; checked with `diff -rq` after the runs: no difference, no `__pycache__` written) and `/root/merge-scratch/venv-B/bin/python -B` (Python 3.14 with PyQt5 5.15, openpyxl 3.1.5). The program's per-user folder was redirected to scratch folders (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/home/...`) so nothing touched a real home folder. Scripts are in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/scripts/`, their printed output in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/work/*_out.txt`.
- **Independent re-run (verification).** Every script named in this part was run again by the verifier on a fresh copy of the code (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S3a/proj`, `diff -rq` against the repository: identical, no `__pycache__`), output in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S3a/work/*_out.txt`. All quoted results came out the same; only clock-based stamps differ (for example "231026 1216" instead of "211026 0640" in folder and file names, and the run times), because those runs took place on another day.
- **Why some runs needed "stand-ins".** This computer runs Linux and has neither Excel nor pywin32 (the Python add-on that lets Python drive Windows programs such as Excel through **COM**, Windows' remote-control mechanism). Project B's window cannot even be imported without pywin32 (see B-F1). To run the window at all, small fake modules with the pywin32 names (copied from the Excel reader's run folder into `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/fakewin/`) were put first on Python's search path. In the window runs they only make the import succeed; they decide nothing. Because the computer is Linux, `core/excel_handler.py:21` sends report creation down its **openpyxl** branch (openpyxl = a Python library that writes .xlsx files without Excel) instead of the Excel branch the author's Windows PC uses. Everything else in Steps 1-3 (scan, tables, dry run, folders, copies, summary workbook, run history) is the same code on both systems. The Excel (COM) branch itself is traced by **reading**; a separate run with *recording* stand-ins shows the **order** of the requests B makes to Excel (marked "fake-COM run") - that proves the Python control flow only, never how real Excel reacts.
- **Made-up clients** used in the traces (invented names, no client data): **<Client A>** = "ClientA Traders", Maharashtra, with a GSTR-2B Reco file, three GSTR-3B files and an Annual Report but **no** IMS Reco, Sales or Sales Reco file; **<Client B>** = "ClientB Private Limited", Gujarat, with all six file types and ten monthly GSTR-3B files (15 files); **<Client C>** = "ClientC Co", Tamil Nadu, with one GSTR-3B file, two Sales files and one more GSTR-3B file whose state is written "Tamilnadu"; **<Client D>** = "Client-D Exports", Kerala, with a hyphen inside its name; **<Client E>** = "ClientA Traders and Distributors", Maharashtra (a long name). Traps placed in the same folder: an `.xlsm` file, an unrecognised "Purchase Register", a 300-byte file, a file in a sub-folder and an Excel lock file (`~$...`). The builder is `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/scripts/mk_source.py`.
- **GST rules** (anything that decides a tax figure, which return, sheet or cell a thing belongs to, a rate, limit, rounding, period, GSTIN/PAN/state-code logic, ITC eligibility or a due date) are tagged **[GST RULE]**. For them this section only says what the code does; it never says whether that is right. Values that can change over time (return names, template cell positions, sheet names, the state list) carry **⚠** so the author can check them.
- Plain-English words used throughout: **thread** (a second line of work running at the same time, so the window does not freeze while a job runs); **signal** (Qt's message from one object to another, used to send progress from a background thread to the window); **regular expression / regex** (a text pattern used to recognise file names); **glob** (a wildcard file search such as `*.xlsx`); **stem** (a file name without its extension); **JSON** (a plain-text file format the program uses for its settings).

> **Two facts shape almost every trace below.** (1) Project B's window cannot start at all unless pywin32 is installed, yet `requirements.txt:14` leaves pywin32 commented out (B-F1). (2) On the author's Windows PC, Step 3 report creation takes over an Excel the user already has open, hides it and closes it at the end (B-F13). Both are described in full in their entries.

### B-F1: Start-up and dependency checks

**What it does.** When the user starts the program, `main.py` makes the console accept any character, sets up the program's log file, tells Python where the program's own files are, builds the four-tab window and shows it. If something the program needs is not installed, it prints a message on the console and stops.

**Where it lives.**

| Step | file:line | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| Console text | main.py:11-13 | If a console exists (`sys.stdout` has a `buffer`), re-wraps it as UTF-8 so symbols such as ✓ can be printed. |
| Program log | main.py:15-23 | `logging.basicConfig(level=INFO, ...)` with a `FileHandler('gst_organizer.log')` - a file name without a folder, so it lands in the folder the program was started from - and a copy to the console (details in B-F32). |
| Import path | main.py:26-29 | `setup_environment()` puts the folder of `main.py` first on Python's import path. |
| Start | main.py:32-47 | Imports PyQt5 (37) and the window (38), creates the application (40), names it "GST File Organizer" version "4.0" (41-42), builds the window (44), shows it (45), runs it (47). |
| Errors | main.py:49-59 | A missing module (ImportError) prints "Missing module: …", "Please install required packages:", "  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl" and exits with code 1 (49-54); any other start-up error prints "Critical error: …" and exits 1 (56-59). |
| Window build order | gui/pyqt_main_window.py:35-68 | Default settings (39), empty scan result (40), processing state (41), settings store (42, creates `~/.gst_organizer`), run history (43), theme manager (44), old-settings import (47, B-F2), saved settings (50-51), three controllers (54-56), window, tabs, menus, signal wiring, restoring the screen values (59-63; the restore at 174-190 also fills Step 4 from disk), theme (66), log line "GST File Organizer v4.0 initialized" (68). |
| The import that needs pywin32 | gui/__init__.py:7 → gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25 → gui/controllers/__init__.py:4 → gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10 → power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15 | `report_processor.py` imports `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui` with no guard, and it is pulled in while the window module itself is being imported. |
| Declared dependencies | requirements.txt:1-14 | `PyQt5>=5.15.0` (5), `openpyxl>=3.1.2` (8), `lxml>=4.9.0` "Optional but recommended" (11), and `# pywin32>=306` **commented out** (13-14). |

**Input → Output.** Installed Python packages + the saved settings file `~/.gst_organizer/settings.json` → the open window, **or** console text and exit code 1.

**User interaction.** The user types `python main.py` in a console (README.md:110-113). The repository has no `.bat` launcher or shortcut; `launch_extractor.py` (B-F30) is a second way in that opens the same window on Step 4.

#### B-F1 concrete trace (RAN: `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/scripts/t_f1_startup.py`, output `work/f1_out.txt`)

Four realistic starts were run as separate programs, each from its own empty start folder.

**Case A - a fresh office PC set up exactly as README.md:97-102 says (`pip install -r requirements.txt`, which installs PyQt5, openpyxl and lxml but not pywin32).**

1. main.py:12 - a console exists, so main.py:13 re-wraps the output as UTF-8.
2. main.py:16-23 - logging is configured; the `FileHandler` immediately creates `gst_organizer.log` **in the start folder** (RAN: `work/f1/A/gst_organizer.log` appeared, 83 bytes).
3. main.py:63 calls `main()`; main.py:35 puts the program folder on the import path; main.py:37 imports PyQt5 (succeeds).
4. main.py:38 `from gui.pyqt_main_window import GSTOrganizerWindow`: Python first runs `gui/__init__.py`, whose line 7 imports the window module; the window module's line 25 imports `gui.controllers.scan_controller`, which first runs `gui/controllers/__init__.py`, whose line 4 imports the extraction controller, whose line 10 imports `report_processor`, whose line 11 is `import pythoncom` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'` (a kind of ImportError).
5. main.py:49 catches it; line 50 logs it; lines 51-53 print; line 54 exits with code 1. The settings folder `~/.gst_organizer` is never created, because the window constructor was never reached.

Actual output (RAN): exit code **1**; console:

```text
 Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'

Please install required packages:
  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl
```

and the log file holds one line, `… - root - ERROR - Import Error: No module named 'pythoncom'`.

> **The advice does not fix the problem.** Both packages it names are already installed; the missing one is pywin32, which requirements.txt:14 leaves commented out. Following the README on a new PC therefore gives a program that cannot open. (HIGH, RAN.)

**Case B - the same PC with pywin32 present (here: the stand-ins), no saved settings.** The window constructor runs in the order listed above: `CacheManager()` creates `~/.gst_organizer` (models/cache_manager.py:31-33); `load_run_history` finds no file and returns an empty history (models/run_history.py:138-148); `migrate_from_old_cache` returns at once because there is no old file (models/cache_manager.py:101-102); `load_settings` finds no file and returns the defaults (models/cache_manager.py:57-62); `_restore_settings` fills the boxes with empty values and, because the target is empty, Step 4 shows "No target folder configured." (gui/pyqt_main_window.py:421-424). RAN result: window title **"GST File Organizer v4.0"**, size 1400 x 900, minimum 1200 x 800, tabs `['Step 1: Setup', 'Step 2: Validation', 'Step 3: Processing', 'Step 4: Extract && Refresh']` (the doubled `&&` shows as one "&" on screen), current tab 0, status bar "Ready", application name/version "GST File Organizer" / "4.0", exit code 0 after the window was closed. On closing, `closeEvent` (gui/pyqt_main_window.py:601-608) wrote `settings.json` (the 11 default keys) and `session_state.json` = `{"active_tab": 0, "window_size": [1400, 900]}`.

**Case C - a hand-edited settings file in which `pq_wait_time` was typed as text: `{"pq_wait_time": "10"}`.**

1. models/cache_manager.py:59-61 loads it; `AppSettings.from_dict` (models/app_state.py:41-46) keeps any key that is a field name and checks no types, so `pq_wait_time` becomes the text "10".
2. gui/pyqt_main_window.py:185 calls `spin_wait_time.setValue("10")`; Qt requires a whole number and raises `TypeError`.
3. The error leaves the window constructor and is caught by main.py:56 → "Critical error: setValue(self, val: int): argument 1 has unexpected type 'str'" printed and logged with the full traceback → exit code 1.

Actual output (RAN): exit 1, the window never appears. The only remedy is to repair or delete `~/.gst_organizer/settings.json` by hand.

**Case D - the per-user file `session_state.json` holds `"recent_source_folders": "C:/old"` (text instead of a list, e.g. after a hand edit), the window opens, and the user ticks View > Dark Mode.**

1. The menu action calls `_toggle_dark_mode` (gui/pyqt_main_window.py:594-597), which calls `_save_settings` (210-214), which calls `CacheManager.save_settings` (models/cache_manager.py:41-55).
2. Line 47 reads `recent = "C:/old"`; line 48: the source folder is not inside that text; line 49 `recent.insert(...)` → `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'insert'`.
3. Nothing catches it: B installs no `sys.excepthook` (a hook that receives errors nothing else caught; grep over all .py files: 0 hits). PyQt5 5.15 then **aborts the whole program**.

Actual output (RAN): the process ended with signal 6 (abort; a Linux shell reports it as exit code 134); the traceback appeared only on the error stream of the console; nothing was added to `gst_organizer.log`; no message box; the settings were not saved.

**What the trace shows against what the feature should do.** Bugs (all listed for Section 7):

1. The window cannot start without pywin32, while the dependency file comments pywin32 out and the error message recommends the wrong command (Case A, RAN). The window itself does not need Excel to scan or organise; the hard dependency comes only from the unguarded import in `report_processor.py:11-15`, while `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` and `utils/helpers.py:473-483` guard the same imports (an inconsistent pattern).
2. Start-up errors are only printed on the console (main.py:51-53, 58) and written to `gst_organizer.log` in the start folder (main.py:50, 57); no message box is shown. Started without a console (double-click with `pythonw`, as the author's Standard 13 requires), the user sees nothing at all on screen. (READ; HIGH.) [Corrected during verification - originally said the errors were "only `print()`ed"; main.py:50 and 57 also log them.]
3. One wrong value type in the settings file stops the program from starting (Case C, RAN).
4. Any error inside a button or menu handler kills the window without saving and without a message (Case D, RAN).
5. No check of the Python version, of Windows or of Excel, and no offer to install missing packages (READ: nothing in main.py:1-63 does this).

**Comparison with the author's Standard 13 (facts only).**

| Standard 13 (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md) | Project B |
|---|---|
| Users double-click a shortcut to `Run [App Name].bat`, which starts `pythonw.exe -B -s main.py` (lines 951-975) | No launcher; README tells users to type `python main.py` (README.md:110-113) |
| `main.py` installs `sys.excepthook` and `threading.excepthook` that write an error file and show a message box (lines 984-1029) | Neither hook; start-up errors are printed and logged to `gst_organizer.log` (main.py:49-59), no message box, and an error in a handler aborts (Case D) |
| Logs and settings in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` (lines 1035-1040) | Log in the start folder (main.py:20); settings in `~/.gst_organizer` (models/cache_manager.py:17) |
| Find the app's own files from `APP_DIR` (the program's own folder), never from the current folder (line 1034) | The import path is taken from the program's own folder (main.py:28-29), but the log file name has no folder, so it follows the current folder (main.py:20) |
| Exact package versions in requirements.txt (lines 937-940) | Minimum versions only (`>=`), pywin32 commented out (requirements.txt:5-14) |
| Desktop windows with PySide6 (Standard 12 table, line 833) | PyQt5 (requirements.txt:5) |

**Older documents against the code.** README.md:52 says "Windows 10/11 (best), macOS, Linux": the program cannot open on macOS or Linux (Case A). README.md:104-108 shows the requirements file as `openpyxl>=3.0.0` and `pywin32>=305; sys_platform == 'win32'`: the real file has neither line. README.md:275 says the error to expect is "No module named 'win32com'": B reports `pythoncom` first. README.md:110-113 (`python main.py`) is still the way to start it, but only with pywin32 installed.

### B-F2: One-time import of old v3 settings (migration)

**What it does.** The first time the new window opens on a PC where the old Tkinter version (v3.0) was used, it copies the old saved settings (folders, templates, processing mode, the include-name tick, the maximum length, dark mode) into the new settings file and leaves a marker file so that the import never runs again.

**Where it lives.** models/cache_manager.py:93-131 (`migrate_from_old_cache`); called once at gui/pyqt_main_window.py:47, after the run history is loaded (43) and before the settings are loaded (50). The old file was written by the v3 program: keys at gui/main_window.py:330-339@47a1492 and the recent-folders list at gui/utils/cache_manager.py:29-46@47a1492 (key `recent_folders`). Marker: `~/.gst_organizer/.migrated` (models/cache_manager.py:99, 127).

**Input → Output.** `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json` (v3) → `~/.gst_organizer/settings.json`, `~/.gst_organizer/session_state.json` and the marker `~/.gst_organizer/.migrated`.

**User interaction.** None; automatic when the window opens, if the old file exists and the marker does not.

#### B-F2 concrete trace (RAN: `scripts/t_f2_migration.py`, output `work/f2_out.txt`)

Input: an old v3 file written with exactly the keys the v3 program wrote - source folder `D:/Clients/FY-Source`, ITC and Sales template paths, target `D:/Clients/Output`, `processing_mode` "rerun", `include_client_name` true, `dark_mode` false, `client_name_max_length` **0**, and `recent_folders` = [`D:/Clients/FY-Source`, `D:/Clients/Older-Source`].

1. `CacheManager()` (models/cache_manager.py:31-37) creates the empty folder `~/.gst_organizer`.
2. models/cache_manager.py:98-99 - paths of the old file and of the marker. Line 101: the old file exists and the marker does not, so the import continues.
3. Lines 105-106 read the old JSON.
4. Lines 109-118 build the new settings: `source_folder`, `itc_template`, `sales_template`, `target_folder` copied; `processing_mode` "rerun"; `include_client_name` → `include_client_name_in_folders` = true; `client_name_max_length` = 0 (the default 35 at line 116 applies only when the key is missing); `dark_mode` false. The three Step 4 settings get their defaults.
5. Line 119 `save_settings` (lines 41-55): the session file is empty, so the recent list is `[]`; the source folder is not in it, so it is inserted and `session_state.json` is written (lines 48-52); then `settings.json` is written (line 54).
6. Line 122 looks for `recent_source_folders` in the old file. The v3 program wrote that list under `recent_folders`, so the result is `[]` and lines 123-124 are skipped.
7. Line 127 creates the marker; line 128 logs "Migrated settings from old cache file".

Actual output (RAN): files `['.migrated', 'session_state.json', 'settings.json']`; `settings.json` holds the 11 keys with `"processing_mode": "rerun"`, `"include_client_name_in_folders": true`, `"client_name_max_length": 0`; `session_state.json` = `{"recent_source_folders": ["D:/Clients/FY-Source"]}` - the second old folder is gone.

8. Second start with a changed old file: skipped at line 101 because the marker exists (RAN: the source folder stayed `D:/Clients/FY-Source`).
9. The window built from these settings (RAN): `window.settings.client_name_max_length` = 0, but the "Max length" box shows **15** (Qt keeps a spin box inside its range 15-100, gui/views/setup_view.py:375, 647), the tick is on and "Re-Run" is selected. When processing starts, `_collect_settings` reads the box (gui/pyqt_main_window.py:203), so processing receives **15**.
10. A damaged old file (cut-off JSON) on a fresh profile, started twice: each start logs the WARNING "Failed to migrate old cache: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 27 (char 26)"; no settings and no marker are written, so the import is retried at every start (RAN).

**What the trace shows against what the feature should do.** Bugs (for Section 7):

1. The old recent-folders list is never carried over: the writer used `recent_folders`, the reader asks for `recent_source_folders` (a write/read key mismatch; RAN). Low impact today because B never shows the recent list (B-F27).
2. **A saved maximum length of 0 becomes an effective limit of 15 characters**, not 35: the migration copies 0 (line 116), the spin box shows 15, and processing uses the box value. The v3 program replaced 0 by 35 when loading (gui/main_window.py:352-354@47a1492). So a user whose old file held 0 gets client folders cut to 15 characters without being told. (RAN; this adds to the registry, which records only that 0 is copied as 0. Likelihood that a real v3 file holds 0: LOW.)
3. A damaged old file is retried at every start with only a log warning (RAN). If writing `settings.json` fails, the marker is still created, because `_save_json` swallows write errors (models/cache_manager.py:141-142) before line 127 runs (READ; LOW). [Corrected during self-review - originally only READ with LOW confidence, but Section 7 (B-G24) RAN it: with `settings.json` unwritable the log said "Failed to save settings.json" and then "Migrated settings from old cache file", and the marker was set (Section 7 me r4; verifier `v1_migration.py`) - now RAN, HIGH.]
4. The old file is left in place (READ).
5. Deleting `~/.gst_organizer/.migrated` while the old v3 file still exists makes the next start import the old v3 settings again, over the current ones (RAN by the Section 2 writer, 2.4.1 #6: the source folder and the wait time went back to the old values; READ `models/cache_manager.py:100-101`: the import runs whenever the old file exists and the marker does not) [added during self-review from the Section 2 writer's flag for this feature].

**Older documents against the code.** README.md:27 ("Session Memory: Remembers your last used folders and settings") - the folders are remembered as settings, but the list of recent folders is neither migrated nor shown.

**Origin.** c258047 (B only (after the split), 07-02-2026). Rule: B-R118.

| Read for saving and processing | gui/pyqt_main_window.py:194-214 | `_collect_settings` reads the boxes as they are; `_save_settings` stores them (models/cache_manager.py:41-55). |

Sales template."); the target must be non-empty ("Please select a target folder."); the target need not exist (it is created later, core/file_organizer.py:61-65). |

**Input → Output.** Typed or picked paths → the settings fields `source_folder`, `itc_template`, `sales_template`, `target_folder`, used by the scan (B-F6), processing (B-F12 to B-F15) and Step 4 (B-F18, which reads the last **saved** target, gui/pyqt_main_window.py:421).

**User interaction.** Typing or pasting into the four boxes, or clicking Browse / BROWSE.

#### B-F3 concrete trace (RAN: `scripts/t_f3_setup.py`, output `work/f3_out.txt`)

Input: <Client A>'s source folder exists with one GSTR-3B file. The user (1) pastes the folder path the way Windows Explorer's "Copy as path" gives it, **with double quotes**; (2) types an ITC template path that is in fact a **folder** (`.../NotATemplate`), picks a real Sales template, and types a target folder that does not exist yet.

1. SCAN FILES → `_on_scan_requested` (gui/pyqt_main_window.py:218). No scan starts (RAN: the scan controller's thread stayed empty).
2. The same path with one trailing space → "Folder not found: …/Source " on this Linux machine (RAN). On Windows the file system normally ignores a trailing space at the end of a path, so there it would probably pass (MEDIUM; not testable here).
3. The path without quotes → the scan runs (B-F6); before it starts, line 227 saves all settings, so `settings.json` now holds the four boxes as they are at that moment.

In the worker, `_create_report` (gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:204-239): line 210 the path is not empty; line 215 it exists; line 220 output `ITC_Report_ClientA_Traders_MH_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`; line 225 calls `create_report_from_template`; its existence check (core/excel_handler.py:78) passes because the folder exists, and the chosen branch then copies the "template" to the report path - on this Linux run as the openpyxl branch's first step (core/excel_handler.py:228); on Windows the Excel branch first attaches to or starts an Excel and hides it (110-120) and only then copies (124). Copying a folder raises an error; the openpyxl branch catches it (260-262) and returns False; on Windows the Excel branch catches it at 191-193 and also returns False, after Excel has already been started (READ). Line 233 then logs "❌ Failed to create ITC report" - the reason is only in the program log.

Actual output (RAN): message box **"Successfully processed 1/1 clients"**; summary workbook: Successful 1, ITC Reports Created 0, Sales Reports Created 1, Report Creation Errors 1; "Client Status" says "Success"; the "Errors" sheet says "No errors encountered".

With no starting folder, Qt opens the folder last visited in a file dialog during this session, or the program's current folder for the first dialog (MEDIUM - Qt's own behaviour, not tested here; on Windows the native dialog may also remember a folder of its own; how to check: on the Windows PC, type a path into the box, click Browse and see where the dialog opens). [Corrected during verification - originally said Qt "then opens at the program's current folder", which holds only for the first dialog of a session.]

6. A source box changed after the last scan is not noticed: START processes the old scan's files (READ: gui/pyqt_main_window.py:366-371 uses `self.scan_result`, never the box).
7. Settings are saved when a scan starts, after processing, on File > Save Settings, on the dark-mode switch and on closing - not when START is pressed (READ; details in B-F27).

README.md:138-141 tells the user to "Click Browse" - three of the four are invisible.
