### B-F34: Background jobs and run guards

#### What it does (plain English)

The three long jobs — scanning (Step 1), processing (Step 3) and extraction (Step 4) — each run in a background thread, so the window keeps responding. Each job's controller refuses to start a second job **of the same kind** while one is running; it tells only the program log, not the user. Jobs of **different** kinds are not stopped from running at the same time. Workers never touch the window directly; they send signals, which Qt delivers to the window's own thread.

#### Where it lives

| What | File and lines |
|---|---|
| Scan: refuse if running ("Scan already in progress", program log only), new thread + worker, connections, start, clean-up; **no Stop** | `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:57-80` (guard `:59-61`), `:88-94` (no stop method: RAN grep) |
| Processing: the same, plus a Stop flag | `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:256-279` (guard `:259-261`), `:281-284`, `:292-298` |
| Extraction: the same, plus a Stop flag | `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:138-165` (guard `:142-144`), `:167-170`, `:178-184` |
| A worker's own catch-all: error → signal → message box in the window | `scan_controller.py:24-41`, `processing_controller.py:35-40`, `extraction_controller.py:36-41` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:318-322`, `:412-415`, `:563-565` |
| What is disabled while a job runs: only that job's own Start (and Stop enabled), and SCAN FILES during a scan | `gui/views/processing_view.py:132-135`, `gui/views/extraction_view.py:392-395`, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:231` |
| Window close: saves settings and session, accepts at once, no check for running jobs | `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:601-608` |
| Data shared between threads without locks: the Skip setting; the window's scan data, changed by the processing worker | `extraction_controller.py:54-55`; `core/file_organizer.py:216-229` via `processing_controller.py:30` |
| Rules | B-R111, B-R112 |

#### Input → Output

- **Input:** a request to start a scan, a processing run or an extraction.
- **Output:** a background job whose progress, log lines and result reach the window by signals — or, for a second request of the same kind, nothing but a program-log line.

#### User interaction

Automatic whenever a job is started (SCAN FILES / RE-SCAN; START / Start Processing; Start Extraction); Stop for processing and extraction; closing the window.

#### Origin

The QThread-worker pattern was introduced with the PyQt5 window in **c258047** (07-02-2026, B only (after the split)) (READ notes MW). Before the split the Tkinter program (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) also ran processing in a background thread, but that thread changed window elements directly, which shared commit 6237597 only partly wrapped (READ notes SH; not traced here).

#### How the code decides, step by step (READ)

1. Start request → the controller checks `self._thread and self._thread.isRunning()`; if so, it writes a warning to the program log and returns (e.g. `extraction_controller.py:142-144`). The window has by then already done its own part — for example switched tab or, for a re-scan, cleared the scan log (`pyqt_main_window.py:227-231`).
2. Otherwise it creates a new `QThread` (Qt's object for one background thread) and a worker object, moves the worker into the thread, connects its signals — eight for extraction (`extraction_controller.py:155-163`) and processing (`processing_controller.py:269-277`), seven for the scan (`scan_controller.py:70-78`, which has no log signal) — and starts the thread (e.g. `extraction_controller.py:146-165`).
3. The worker's `run()` catches every error and sends it as an `error` signal (`extraction_controller.py:36-41`); the window shows "Scan Error" / "Processing Error" / "Extraction Error".
4. Nothing ties the three controllers together, so a scan or a processing run can start while an extraction runs, and the other way round. Processing and extraction both drive Excel; Step 3's report creation first attaches to any running Excel (`core/excel_handler.py:110-112`), which could be Step 4's visible one (READ, MEDIUM; B-F13).
5. Stop sets a flag that is read only between items (B-F16, B-F24); scanning has none.
6. Closing the window runs `closeEvent` (`pyqt_main_window.py:601-608`): it saves settings and the session and accepts; a running worker is neither stopped nor waited for.
7. When a thread finishes, `_cleanup` deletes whatever thread and worker the controller holds **at that moment** (`extraction_controller.py:178-184`); if a new job of the same kind was started in between, the new running thread is deleted — RAN by MW (e13, run on the scan controller, whose `_cleanup` `scan_controller.py:88-94` is identical; timing widened on purpose): "QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running", exit code 134 (LOW likelihood).

#### Concrete trace

**Run 1 — three jobs at once** (RAN `scripts/t34b_jobs.py` → `out2/t34b.txt`; offscreen window; the extraction worker is held inside its first Excel wait as if Excel were refreshing; Step 3 takes B's openpyxl path because this is not Windows). Target folder with one earlier run folder `Annual Statement-050126 0900` (one ITC report of `ClientA-DL`); a source folder with two files of an invented `ClientD` in Gujarat; two small templates.

| Step | What the user does | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ticks all, presses **Start Extraction** | extraction thread running |
| 2 | presses **Start Extraction** again | no message box; program log only: "Extraction already in progress" |
| 3 | presses **SCAN FILES** | the scan ran to the end in its own thread **while the extraction thread was still running**; client found `ClientD-GJ`; the window switched to Step 2 |
| 4 | presses **START** on Step 2 | processing ran to the end in a third thread, still while the extraction was running; box "Processing Complete — Successfully processed 1/1 clients"; a new run folder `Annual Statement-231026 1326` was made in the same target |
| 4b | (automatic) | the processing end rebuilt the Step 4 tree: it now showed **"Source: Annual Statement-231026 1326"**, with 0 ticked rows — while the extraction was still working on `Annual Statement-050126 0900` |
| 5 | (the extraction is released) | it finished and wrote `Extraction_Log_20261023_1326.txt` and `PQ_Extraction_Report_20261023_1326.xlsx` into the **old** run folder; the tree still showed the new one |
| — | threads used (RAN) | window: `MainThread`; extraction: `Dummy-1`; scan: `Dummy-2`; processing: `Dummy-3` (Python's names for threads started by Qt) |

**Run 2 — closing the window during an extraction** (RAN `scripts/t34c_close.py` → `out2/t34c.txt`; the real event loop and the same exit path as `main.py`; each fixed wait shortened to 0.05 s but really waited). The user ticks one version (ITC and Sales) and presses Start Extraction; 0.3 s later closes the window.

| What | Observed |
|---|---|
| At the moment of closing | extraction thread running |
| `closeEvent` | accepted at once, window gone; `settings.json` written; `run_history.json` **not** written |
| The program's exit | `app.exec_()` returned 0 and the process **ended with exit code 0, with no message** while the worker was still inside the ITC refresh |
| Left on disk | the ITC report, an **unrefreshed copy** `ITC_Report_ClientA_DL_050126_0900_Refreshed_231026_1326.xlsx` (same size as the report), the Sales report untouched; **no consolidated workbook, no extraction log, no run history** |

On Windows with real Excel, the visible Excel that the refresh had started is a separate program and would most likely stay open with the copy loaded (READ, MEDIUM — how to check: on a test PC close B during a Step 4 refresh and look for EXCEL.EXE in Task Manager). (The Excel notes, XL §5.2 step 8, expected Qt to abort the program in this case (MEDIUM); in this run it did not — it ended normally with exit code 0.)

**Run 3 — Stop and second start during an extraction**: see B-F24 Run 2 (RAN): the second Start press is refused with a program-log line only; Step 3's Start Processing and Step 2's START stay enabled.

#### Traced output versus what the feature claims

1. **A second job of the same kind is refused with no on-screen word** (RAN) — B-G71 in Section 7.
2. **Jobs of different kinds run at the same time**: a scan and a processing run completed during an extraction, and the processing end switched the Step 4 list to another run folder mid-extraction (RAN Run 1) — B-G74.
3. **Closing the window during a job is accepted at once**: the job is cut off, half-made files stay (an unrefreshed copy), and no report, log or history is written (RAN Run 2) — B-G40.
4. **A late clean-up can delete a newer running thread and abort the program** (RAN by MW e13; LOW likelihood) — B-G41.
5. **Stop acts only between items; scanning cannot be stopped at all** (READ; RAN in B-F24) — B-G39, B-G70.
6. **Shared data is changed across threads without locks** (the Skip setting; the window's scan data) — RAN by DC T5e for the scan data — B-G75, B-G76.
7. Good: **no worker touches a window element directly** (RAN: thread names above; RAN by VW/MW thread maps).

#### Older documents versus code

- README.md:279 "Processing seems frozen → large files take time, check log" — in B the window does not freeze during the three jobs (they run in threads); the Step 4 list-building, however, walks the target folder on the window's own thread (B-F18, B-G58).
- README.md says nothing about running jobs at the same time or about closing the window during a run.

Output `work3/t3_out.json` and `work3/PQ_Extraction_Report_20261023_1323.xlsx`; it needs no stand-in modules.

The stand-ins are never called in these runs. Excel itself cannot run on this Linux machine, so every Excel step is **READ** (with the fake-Excel call-order runs of the reader agents cited where they exist: notes PQ = `B_code_pq_models_startup.md`, XL = `B_excel_pq_safety.md`, LT = `B_live_traces.md`, CU = `B_code_core_utils.md`, OF = `B_outside_files_state.md`, MW = `B_code_mainwindow_controllers_theme.md`, VW = `B_code_views.md`, DC = `B_dead_code_patterns.md`, DO = `B_docs.md` (its probes are in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-D/`), H1 = `B_history_part1.md`, H2 = `B_history_part2.md`).
  - The original code copy `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy` was checked byte for byte before and after (SHA-256 - a file fingerprint - of all 41 files identical; no `__pycache__`).
  - Verification pass (task VERIFY-B-S45, 23-10-2026): `t1_flow.py`, `t2_step4_tree.py`, `t2b_step4_tree_newonly.py` and `t3_lookup.py` were re-run on a fresh copy of the code in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S45/` (`python -B`, `HOME`/`TMPDIR` in scratch). Every result quoted below was reproduced; only the clock times in names differ (for example `Annual Statement-231026 1353` instead of `…211026 0637`). Extra checks (pattern edge cases, state fallbacks, name cleaning, settings.json shapes, ASCII escaping) are in `scripts/v1_rules.py` there. `B-copy` was again byte-identical afterwards.
- **Invented test names only.** "ClientA" (shown as <Client A>) and "ClientB Private Limited" (shown as <Client B>) are made-up names used in the runs; no client data was used. `<target>` stands for the scratch target folder.
- **Confidence** for anything inferred: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW. **[GST RULE]** marks anything the author owns (which return file, sheet or cell a figure belongs to, state codes, periods …); this section only says what the code does with it, never whether it is right. **⚠** marks a value that can change over time.
- Plain-English terms used below (first use): *worker thread* = a background line of work so the window does not freeze; *signal* = Qt's message from one object to another (here: from the worker thread back to the window); *dict* = a Python table of named entries ("key → value"); *JSON* = a plain-text settings format; *COM* = the Windows mechanism by which Python drives Excel (through the pywin32 add-on); *openpyxl* = a Python library that reads and writes .xlsx files without Excel; *glob* = a wildcard file search such as `*.xlsx`; *regex* / *regular expression* = a text pattern that a name must fit; *HTML* = the text format of web pages, which Qt can show with colours; *UTF-8* = the usual way of storing text with letters of any language; *NTFS* = the Windows disk format; *stem* = a file name without its extension; *mtime* = a file's or folder's "last modified" time; *Level-1 / run folder* = `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>`; *Level-2 / client folder* = `<client>-<state code>`; *Version folder* = `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>`; *category folders* = the three folders inside a Version folder; *variations* = the code's word for problem files; *Links sheet* = the template sheet into which B writes folder paths and file names for the template's own Power Query (Excel's built-in data-import feature).

> **The one thing to keep in mind while reading the flows:** the Python code never reads the *contents* of a client's input file. It reads only the file **name**, the size, the dates and the first 8 bytes (core/file_parser.py:171-215). Every tax figure is produced inside the author's two templates by their Power Query, outside this repository; B only (a) tells the templates where the copied files are (Links sheet), (b) makes Excel refresh them by simulated keystrokes, and (c) copies chosen cells of the refreshed copies into one consolidated workbook.

The file name is turned into structured data in four steps (all **[GST RULE]** ⚠ where they decide a return type or a state code - the file-name patterns and the state list change over time, ⚠ added during the completeness check; values in Section 5):

| Step | Before | After | Where | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | File name text | pattern key, type ⚠, category, folder value, client text, state text, period/date/month/year text (`metadata`), optional `warnings` | core/file_parser.py:56-124; utils/constants.py:13-62 | B-R5 to B-R11, B-R18, B-R23 |

## SECTION 5: BUSINESS RULES AND DOMAIN LOGIC

This section lists **every rule of the project-B registry (B-R1 to B-R144)**, grouped by the registry's 16 categories and in ID order, then every remaining hard-coded value (5.17), the rules that exist in several places with different values (5.18), items the registry lacks (5.19), where the older README disagrees (5.20), and the rules that could only be read here, with how to check them (5.21).

### 5.0 How to read this section

- Each rule heading reads `B-R<n> · <short name>` followed by its tags:
  - **[GST RULE]** - the code decides something the author owns: a tax figure; which return, table, sheet or cell a figure belongs to; a rate, limit or threshold; rounding; the financial year or period; GSTIN, PAN or state-code logic; ITC eligibility; a due date. When in doubt the rule is tagged (as the registry did). For these rules this audit **only says what the code does**; it never says whether that is correct and recommends nothing.
  - **⚠** - the rule holds a value that can change over time (return and table names, template cell positions, state lists, dates). The ⚠ is also placed next to the individual value inside the text so the author can check each one.
  - **DEAD** - defined but never used; "DEAD (in practice)" = can run but never does with the present configuration or screens; "DEAD (write-only)" = stored but never read back.
- Under each heading: **Rule** (what the code actually does, with exact values), **Where** (every file:line, including copies of the same value), **Origin** ("shared - before the split on 30-10-2025" for code from the 12 shared commits edac6a3 … 47a1492, "B only (after the split)" for B's commits c258047, a62d3cc, c21f788, 7e09e5c, b0e7d0e), **Evidence** (READ / RAN, with the note or script that ran it), and **Notes** where something else needs saying.
- Script and note names: RAN in this task = `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S45/scripts/t1_flow.py`, `t2_step4_tree.py`, `t2b_step4_tree_newonly.py`, `t3_lookup.py` (extraction mapping tables, the consolidated look-up with five kinds of J15 value, the consolidated layout, and the refresh-wait arithmetic; output `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S45/work3/t3_out.json`); reader-agent notes as in Section 4.1 (CU, PQ, MW, VW, DC, XL, OF, LT), plus the registry's own runs (`/root/merge-scratch/run/REGISTRY-B/scripts/check1.py`, "REG check1").
- Invented names only (<Client A>, "ClientA", "ClientB Private Limited", "Alpha Test Traders" from the LT notes …). No client data.

### 5.1 Category 1 - Input-file recognition (B-R1 to B-R16)

#### B-R1 · Which files the scan looks at
- **Rule:** Only the **top level** of the chosen source folder is searched; sub-folders are ignored with no message. The search asks for `*.xlsx`, then `*.xls`, then `*.xlsm` (a non-recursive glob), drops every name starting with `~$` (Excel's lock files), and sorts the rest by full path. Any error while listing (for example a network folder that has disappeared) returns an empty list, so the user sees "No Excel files found" rather than an error. Other extensions (`.csv`, `.json`, `.xlsb` - Excel's binary workbook format - …) are ignored silently and counted nowhere. On Linux the glob is case-sensitive (`.XLSX` is not found); on Windows Python's glob ignores case (reasoned from Python's behaviour, HIGH). `.xlsm` files are collected but no pattern accepts them (B-R6 to B-R11), so they always end up unrecognised.
- **Exact values:** globs `'*.xlsx'`, `'*.xls'`, `'*.xlsm'`; lock-file prefix `'~$'`; error → `[]`.
- **Where:** utils/helpers.py:249-266 (globs 255-257, `~$` 259-260, sort 262, error 264-266); called at core/file_parser.py:146-152. The same three extensions are typed again at gui/pyqt_main_window.py:469 and in the dead constant utils/constants.py:179 (B-R14).
- **Origin:** globs and sort shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3); the `~$` filter and the removal of the per-file `validate_excel_file` call came in 7e09e5c (B only (after the split)). Before 7e09e5c, files under 1 KB or with a wrong signature were dropped silently here; since then they reach the parser and become variations (B-R2, B-R3).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1: 15 paths found; `.csv`, `~$` file and sub-folder file never looked at; LT §6.2: `.XLSX` not found on Linux; OF t2).

#### B-R2 · Minimum file size 1024 bytes
- **Rule:** A file smaller than 1024 bytes (1 KB) is not parsed; it goes on the variations list with the issue "File too small to be valid Excel".
- **Exact values:** `size < 1024`; issue text `File too small to be valid Excel`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:181-191. Dead duplicate: utils/helpers.py:231-233 (`validate_excel_file`, never called since 7e09e5c). The unused `EXCEL_SAFETY['verification_size_min']` is a **different value, 10240** (utils/constants.py:222; B-R108).
- **Origin:** in the parser since 7e09e5c (B only (after the split)); the 1024 limit itself existed in `validate_excel_file` from edac6a3 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1: a 104-byte file → this variation, and it is left out of "total files"; LT §6.2).

#### B-R3 · Excel signature check (first 8 bytes)
- **Rule:** The first 8 bytes are read; they must start with `PK\x03\x04` (zip package: .xlsx / .xlsm) or `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0` (old OLE format: .xls), otherwise the file becomes a variation "Invalid or corrupted Excel file". If the file cannot be read: "Cannot read file: <error text>". Nothing beyond these bytes is ever read by Python, so a fake file holding only the header bytes is accepted.
- **Exact values:** read length 8; signatures `b'PK\x03\x04'`, `b'\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0'`; issues `Invalid or corrupted Excel file`, `Cannot read file: <e>`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:193-215. Dead duplicates: utils/helpers.py:235-243 (`validate_excel_file`) and utils/constants.py:182-185 (B-R15).
- **Origin:** in the parser since 7e09e5c (B only (after the split)); same check in `validate_excel_file` since edac6a3 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §6.2: a fake `.xls` with only the header bytes was accepted; a text file named `.xlsx` was rejected).

#### B-R4 · Files whose size and dates cannot be read
- **Rule:** If the operating system cannot report a file's size and dates (for example a broken shortcut), the file is skipped silently: it appears in no list and no count; only the warning `Cannot stat <name>: <error>` reaches the program log. Any other unexpected error for one file is added to the parser's own error list, which nothing outside the parser reads.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:174-179; 254-256 (`self.errors`, no reader - grep).
- **Origin:** 7e09e5c (B only (after the split)).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §6.2: a broken link dropped silently).

#### B-R5 · How a file name is matched to a pattern · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** File names are compared with the six patterns **in this fixed order**: GSTR-2B-Reco, ImsReco, GSTR3B, Sales, SalesReco, AnnualReport. Matching ignores letter case, must start at the first character and cover the whole name; the **first** pattern that matches wins. The captured client and state are trimmed of spaces; a part is stored only if it is non-empty before trimming. A file that matches but whose client or state is empty after trimming becomes a variation "Could not parse filename"; a file that matches nothing becomes a variation "No matching pattern found" plus the log warning `Could not parse filename: <name>`. Because every pattern starts with a different fixed word, no name can match two patterns.
- **Exact values:** order as above (dict order of `FILE_PATTERNS`); `re.IGNORECASE`; `.match` + `$`; issues `Could not parse filename` (fallback text) and `No matching pattern found`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:56-124 (loop 77-118, `break` 118, parts 93-102, error 120-122), 228-252; patterns utils/constants.py:13-62.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3; constants.py never changed since).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §1.2: 70 names, none matched two patterns; t1).

The six patterns in full (utils/constants.py:13-62). `[^-]+` means "one or more characters that are not a hyphen"; `(.+)` means "anything, hyphens included"; `\.xlsx?$` means the name ends in `.xls` or `.xlsx` (any case).

| Order | Key | Regular expression (exact) | Type ⚠ | Category (never read) | "folder" value (never read) | Parts captured | Example text in the code ⚠ | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GSTR-2B-Reco` | `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | GSTR-2B Reco | ITC | itc | client, state, period | `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | B-R6 |
| 2 | `ImsReco` | `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})\.xlsx?$` | IMS Reco | ITC | itc | client, state, date | `ImsReco-ClientName-State-DDMMYYYY.xlsx` | B-R7 |
| 3 | `GSTR3B` | `^(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?GSTR3B-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | GSTR-3B Export | GSTR3B | gstr3b | client, state, month | `GSTR3B-ClientName-State-Month.xlsx` | B-R8 |
| 4 | `Sales` | `^Sales-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | Sales | Sales | sales | client, state, start_month, end_month | `Sales-ClientName-State-StartMonth-EndMonth.xlsx` | B-R9 |
| 5 | `SalesReco` | `^SalesReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | Sales Reco | Sales | sales | client, state, period | `SalesReco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | B-R10 |
| 6 | `AnnualReport` | `^AnnualReport-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | Annual Report | Annual | root | client, state, year | `AnnualReport-ClientName-State-Year.xlsx` | B-R11 |

#### B-R6 · Pattern "GSTR-2B-Reco" · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **Rule:** `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` → type ⚠ "GSTR-2B Reco", parts client, state, period. Client and state cannot contain a hyphen; the period `(.+)` takes everything else, so a hyphen inside a client name silently shifts the split (client "Client", state "A", period "<rest>"). Only `.xls` / `.xlsx` (any case). A trailing " (1)" or "_Refreshed_…" is absorbed into the period.
- **Where:** utils/constants.py:14-21; used core/file_parser.py:78-102; hint text typed again at core/file_parser.py:321-322 and on screen at gui/views/setup_view.py:493 (`GSTR-2B-Reco-Client-State-Period`).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT O01-O08, O05 hyphen mis-split; REG check1: client "Client", state "A"; t1 `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientA-Delhi-Apr24-Mar25.xlsx` → period "Apr24-Mar25").

#### B-R7 · Pattern "ImsReco" · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **Rule:** `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})\.xlsx?$` → type ⚠ "IMS Reco", parts client, state, date. ### 5.2 Category 2 - Client identity and name cleaning (B-R17 to B-R20)

#### B-R17 · Client key "<client>-<state code>" · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** A client is identified by the key `"<client text>-<state code>"`: the client text exactly as written in the file name (trimmed, letter case kept) plus the state code from B-R21 / B-R22. Files written with "Delhi" and "DL" therefore merge into one client, while "Tamil Nadu" and "Tamilnadu" (codes TN and TAM) or `<Client A>` and `<client a>` become separate clients. The client's displayed state is that of the **last** file processed; file count and total size are summed. The same key is shown as "Folder Name" on Step 2 (B-R134), used for processing run-history records (B-R120) and for the dead per-client folder setting (B-R36).
- **Exact values:** `client_key = f"{client}-{state_code}"`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:258-278 (code 261, key 262, last state wins 266-268); used at gui/views/validation_view.py:367-379, gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:151, 165, 177, core/file_organizer.py:118.

#### B-R18 · Client and state name checks (warnings nobody sees) · DEAD (in practice)
- **Rule:** Client and state texts are each checked: empty or blank → "Client name cannot be empty"; shorter than 2 characters → "Client name too short"; longer than 100 → "Client name too long"; containing any of `< > : " / \ | ? *` → "Client name contains invalid characters". The **same** check is used for the state, so its messages also say "Client name …" (prefixed "State name issue:"). It runs only when both are non-empty. Inside the check the length is measured on the text exactly as passed in (only the "empty" test trims it), but the parser has already trimmed client and state (core/file_parser.py:98, 100), so in practice the trimmed length counts. The result is stored as `warnings` on the file record and never read or shown - the file is used anyway.
- **Exact values:** minimum 2, maximum 100 characters; character class `[<>:"/\\|?*]`; prefixes `Client name issue: ` / `State name issue: `.
- **Where:** utils/helpers.py:321-342; called at core/file_parser.py:104-115.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §2.6: 20 inputs; "State name issue: Client name too short").

#### B-R19 · "Private" → "Pvt", "Limited" → "Ltd" - two different methods
- **Rule:** The abbreviations are applied in two ways: (a) in file-name cleaning (B-R20) as **plain, case-sensitive text replacement anywhere in the name** ("PRIVATE LIMITED" is not shortened; "Privateer" becomes "Pvter") - used for copied file names, the bracketed client name in category folders and the client part of report names; (b) in the client-folder name (B-R32) as **whole words in any letter case**. One client can therefore be "Pvt Ltd" in its client folder and "PRIVATE_LIMITED" in its report names. Not applied to the client key (B-R17), the organisation-report name (B-R40) or the Step 2 display.
- **Exact values:** (a) `.replace('Private', 'Pvt')`, `.replace('Limited', 'Ltd')`; (b) `re.sub(r'\bPrivate\b', 'Pvt', …, flags=re.IGNORECASE)`, `re.sub(r'\bLimited\b', 'Ltd', …, flags=re.IGNORECASE)`.
- **Where:** (a) utils/helpers.py:77-79; (b) utils/helpers.py:515-518.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1: folder `ClientB Pvt Ltd-TN`, copy `GSTR3B-ClientB_Pvt_Ltd-Tamil_Nadu-Apr.xlsx`; LT K03/S03: "PRIVATE LIMITED" abbreviated only in the folder key; REG check1).

#### B-R20 · File-name cleaning (`sanitize_filename`)
- **Rule:** In order: empty → `unnamed`; split into stem and extension at the **last dot** (so for a client name like "<Client A> Pvt. Ltd" the part ". Ltd" is treated as an extension and re-attached uncleaned); a `/` (and `\` on Windows) counts as a folder separator and the text before it is lost; abbreviations (B-R19 a); control characters (codes 0-31 and 127-159) → `_`; each of `< > : " / \ | ? * [ ] { } + = ! @ # $ % ^ , ; '` and the back-tick and `~` → `_` (hyphen, `&`, round brackets and dot are kept); runs of spaces or underscores → one `_`; leading and trailing `_`, `.` and spaces removed; empty → `unnamed`; stem cut to `200 − len(extension) − 10` characters (185 for ".xlsx", 190 with no extension); the extension is put back unchanged.
- **Exact values:** default `max_length=200`; reserve `10`; invalid-character string `'<>:"/\\|?*[]{}+=!@#$%^,;\'"`~'` (the double quote appears twice); fallback `'unnamed'`; strip set `'_. '`.
- **Where:** utils/helpers.py:66-112; callers core/file_organizer.py:86 (category bracket), 254 (copy name); gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:112 (report name). Imported but unused at core/excel_handler.py:37.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §2.2: 36 inputs, e.g. "Zeta Mock Pvt. Ltd" → `Zeta_Mock_Pvt. Ltd`; "Alpha/Beta Traders" → `Beta_Traders`; t1: `(1) GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-Jun.xlsx` → `(1)_GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-Jun.xlsx`). Python-version dependence of the "last dot" split: LOW confidence for Pythons older than 3.14 (LT §2.3). [Corrected during self-review - originally left at LOW confidence, but Section 7 (B-G80, RAN me) settled it; re-RAN in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW/scripts/pyver_sanitize.py` on a scratch copy with `python -B`: a name ending in a dot keeps it on 3.14.6 ("Alpha Test Traders." → `Alpha_Test_Traders.`, "ClientA Co." → `ClientA_Co.`) but loses it on 3.11.17, 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 (`Alpha_Test_Traders`, `ClientA_Co`); "Zeta Mock Pvt. Ltd" → `Zeta_Mock_Pvt. Ltd` on all four. HIGH for these four versions; others not tried.]

#### B-R22 · Made-up code for a state not in the table · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **Rule:** A state name not in the table gets a made-up code: with **two or more words**, the upper-cased first letters of the first two words; with **one word**, the first three characters of the *original* text, upper-cased (the comment says "2-3 characters" but it is always up to three). #### B-R24 · The six expected file types · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **Rule:** Every client is expected to have six file types: ⚠ "GSTR-2B Reco", ⚠ "IMS Reco", ⚠ "GSTR-3B Export", ⚠ "Sales", ⚠ "Sales Reco", ⚠ "Annual Report". Missing types = expected minus found, stored sorted alphabetically.

#### B-R25 · Only GSTR-3B may have several files · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **Rule:** "GSTR-3B Export" may have any number of files (comment "GSTR-3B can have multiple files (monthly filings - unlimited)"); any **other** type with two or more files gets the remark `Multiple <type> (<n> files)`. The number of GSTR-3B months is not checked, and GSTR-3B files from different years raise no remark.
- **Exact values:** `len(files) > 1`; exemption `file_type == 'GSTR-3B Export'`; remark `f"Multiple {file_type} ({len(files)} files)"`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:290-299.

#### B-R26 · Completeness percentage · [GST RULE] (rounding - tagged by the when-in-doubt rule; not a tax figure)
- **Rule:** Completeness = (number of the six types found ÷ 6) × 100, rounded to **one decimal place**. It counts types, not files: a client with all six types and duplicates shows 100.0. The processing summary shows it as text `x.x%`.
- **Exact values:** `round(len(found_types) / len(expected_types) * 100, 1)`; summary `f"{…:.1f}%"`.
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:301-303; shown core/excel_handler.py:422.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1: 100.0, 33.3, 16.7; summary sheet showed `100.0%`, `16.7%`, `33.3%`).

#### B-R27 · Client status and its colours · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** No missing type and no remark → "Complete" (icon ✅); at least one missing type → `Missing <n> files`, where n is the number of missing **types** (even if there are duplicates too) (icon ⚠️); otherwise → "Has duplicates" (⚠️); before analysis "Unknown". The icons are never shown. Step 2 colours the whole row: exactly "Complete" → green `#107C10`; text containing "Missing" → orange `#FF8C00`; anything else → red-orange `#D83B01`. "Complete Only" ticks rows whose status is exactly "Complete"; the count label and the statistics count exactly "Complete".
- **Where:** core/file_parser.py:41 (default), 305-314; gui/views/validation_view.py:387-393, 407-410, 441-447; core/file_parser.py:342-343; dead property models/app_state.py:65-68.

#### B-R29 · Scan statistics
- **Rule:** "total files" = files that passed the size and signature checks (rejected files are excluded, so it can be lower than the number of Excel files present); "parsed" = files whose name matched a pattern (including a match with an empty client); "unparsed" = total − parsed; clients; complete (status exactly "Complete"); incomplete; "variations" = length of the problem list (which **does** include rejected files); total size (and formatted, B-R142); files per type; parsing rate and completion rate in % (not rounded; shown with one decimal).

### 5.6 Category 6 - Folder layout and naming (B-R30 to B-R41)

#### B-R30 · Time stamps for names
- **Rule:** The processing time stamp is the PC's local time as `DDMMYY HHMM` (day first, two-digit year, to the minute). It is taken **once when the organiser is created** (for folder names) and **separately once at the start of the worker** (for report and summary names, with the space replaced by `_` → `DDMMYY_HHMM`); the two can differ by one minute. Two runs in the same minute get the same names and reuse the same folders. Backups take their own `DDMMYY_HHMM` stamp at backup time. A `DDMMYY`-only helper exists but is never called.
- **Exact values:** `"%d%m%y %H%M"` (utils/helpers.py:25), `"%d%m%y"` (29, dead), `"%d%m%y_%H%M"` (33); space → underscore at gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:114, 187.

### 5.7 Category 7 - Copying and versioning of files (B-R42 to B-R47)

#### B-R42 · Copy, never move; check by size only
- **Rule:** Source files are only read and copied - never moved, renamed, changed or deleted. Each recognised file is copied with its contents and file dates (`shutil.copy2`) to `<destination folder>/<cleaned name>` (B-R20), overwriting a file of that name. The copy is "verified" only by comparing sizes: on a mismatch the copy is deleted and the file fails with "Copy operation failed"; a missing source fails the same way. An interrupted copy can leave a partial file under the final name (no temporary name).
- **Where:** utils/helpers.py:142-185 (source check 161-163, copy 169, size check 172-178, delete 177); core/file_organizer.py:253-277.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ (grep: no `remove`, `rename`, `move`, `replace` on sources); RAN (LT §6.4: identical SHA-256 before and after six runs; t1).

#### B-R43 · An existing copy: backup, skip or overwrite
- **Rule:** When the destination copy already exists (only possible within the same Version folder, i.e. the same clock minute, or when two source names clean to the same name): **Fresh** → first copy it to `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><extension>` in the same folder (a second backup in the same minute overwrites the first; a failed backup does not stop the overwrite), then overwrite; **Resume** → no copy, status "Skipped", error "File already exists"; **Re-Run** → overwrite with no backup. Backups stay in the category folders permanently.
- **Exact values:** backup name `f"{path.stem}_backup_{timestamp}{path.suffix}"`, timestamp `%d%m%y_%H%M`.
- **Where:** core/file_organizer.py:259-270; utils/helpers.py:187-204 (name 194-196).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §6.3 runs 1-5, §6.5 name collision; CU).

#### B-R44 · The three processing modes
- **Rule:** Keys `fresh`, `rerun`, `resume` (an unknown key raises `ValueError("Invalid processing mode: …")`). Fresh = a new run folder each run; Re-Run and Resume = reuse the latest run folder (B-R38) but **always add a new Version folder**, so Resume skips files only when repeated within the same minute and otherwise copies everything again. Every ticked client is processed in full in every mode. The Step 1 buttons map positions 0/1/2 to fresh/rerun/resume (an unknown saved mode shows Fresh).
- **On-screen texts (they disagree with each other and with the code):** radio buttons "Fresh - Create new folder structure (recommended for first time)", "Re-Run - Add new version folders to existing structure", "Resume - Continue previously interrupted processing" (gui/views/setup_view.py:343-347); help card "Fresh: New timestamped structure", "Re-Run: Overwrite existing", "Resume: Skip already processed" (gui/views/setup_view.py:510-512).

### 5.8 Category 8 - Report creation and template Links cells (B-R48 to B-R60)

Step 3 makes two reports per processed client by copying a template workbook and writing folder paths and file names into its "Links" sheet. The figures themselves are produced later by the template's own Power Query; B never writes a tax figure into a report. Every Links-cell rule below is a template contract, tagged **[GST RULE]** where it decides which return file feeds which part of a report (the registry's when-in-doubt choice).

#### B-R48 · Exactly two templates, checked only for existence
- **Rule:** The user supplies one ITC template and one Sales template, by typing a path or with a file picker. Before processing each must be non-empty and must exist - a *folder* path also passes `Path.exists()`. The check is repeated for every client inside the worker ("<type> template path is empty!" / "<type> template not found", each counted as a report error) and once more inside the report code, which raises `FileNotFoundError("Template not found: <path>")`. Nothing checks the extension, the sheets, or that the template contains Power Query queries. The template file itself is only read (copied); it is never opened or changed.
- **Exact values:** picker filter `"Excel Files (*.xlsx *.xlsm)"`; section text "Select your Excel template files (.xlsx or .xlsm)"; window messages "Please select a valid ITC template." / "Please select a valid Sales template."; worker messages `❌ {report_type} template path is empty!` / `❌ {report_type} template not found`.
- **Where:** gui/views/setup_view.py:218-261 (fields; text 221), 610-622 (pickers; filter 612, 619); gui/pyqt_main_window.py:353-358; gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:210-218; core/excel_handler.py:78-79.
- **Origin:** the existence checks are shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (`47a1492:gui/handlers/processing_handler.py` and core/excel_handler.py from edac6a3). The picker filter `*.xlsx *.xlsm` is B only (after the split) (c258047); the "(.xlsx or .xlsm)" text came in 7e09e5c. At the split the Tkinter picker offered `"*.xltx *.xlsx"` (`47a1492:gui/handlers/file_handler.py:31, 42`) and the text said "(.xlsx or .xltx)" (`47a1492:gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:121`).
- **Evidence:** READ (grep: no check of sheets, extension or `DataMashup`); RAN by OF (t4: a template without a Links sheet still "succeeded").
- **Notes:** README.md:120-121 says ".xlsx or .xltx" - it disagrees with the picker (see 5.20). Standard 12 asks for a Power Query check (`customXml/item*.xml` containing `DataMashup`) before any openpyxl save into a workbook the app did not create (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:846-850); B makes no such check (relevant only to the openpyxl path, B-R97).

- **Rule:** `TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS = {'.xlsx', '.xltx', '.xltm'}` is defined but never read. It disagrees with the picker (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`) and with README.md:120-121 (`.xlsx` or `.xltx`).

#### B-R50 · Every processed client always gets both reports · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** For every client that reaches the report step, an ITC report is attempted and then a Sales report, whatever source files the client has. There is no check that a report's inputs exist; a missing input only leaves its Links cells unwritten (B-R56). A client with nothing but GSTR-3B files therefore still gets a Sales report whose Links cells are all left as the template had them. The dry run (B-R135) announces both reports for every ticked client.
- **Where:** gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:116-130 (ITC 117-122, Sales 125-130); dry run gui/pyqt_main_window.py:340-341.

- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (Section 4.5.4, t1: the Sales report of `ClientB Pvt Ltd-TAM`, a client with one GSTR-3B file, was "created" with no cell written).

#### B-R51 · Report file names · [GST RULE] (state code in the name)
- **Rule:** `ITC_Report_<client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` and `Sales_Report_<client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`, both in the Version folder. `<client>` = the cleaned client name (B-R20: spaces become `_`, case-sensitive Private/Limited abbreviation); `<state code>` = the scan's code for the client, or the fallback code (B-R21, B-R22); the time stamp is the worker's own stamp with the space replaced by `_` (B-R30). The extension is **always `.xlsx`**, whatever the template's type, while the template bytes are copied unchanged (B-R52): an `.xlsm` or `.xltx` template becomes a macro or template package under an `.xlsx` name (MEDIUM that Excel then refuses to open it - not runnable here). A re-run in the same minute overwrites the report without a backup (the input-file backup of B-R43 does not apply to reports). The prefixes `ITC_Report_` and `Sales_Report_` are the only link between Step 3 and Step 4 (B-R39, B-R61).
- **Exact values:** `f"ITC_Report_{safe_client}_{safe_state}_{safe_ts}"`, `f"Sales_Report_{safe_client}_{safe_state}_{safe_ts}"`, `f"{report_name}.xlsx"`; `safe_ts = timestamp.replace(' ', '_')`; `safe_state = client_info.get('state_code', get_state_code(client_info['state']))` (the fallback call is evaluated even when the key exists, so an unknown state logs its warning again).
- **Where:** gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:111-130, 220; copy at core/excel_handler.py:124 (COM path) and 228 (openpyxl path).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (`47a1492:gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:229-235, 292-293`, same expressions); moved into gui/controllers/processing_controller.py in c258047 (B only (after the split)).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1: `ITC_Report_ClientA_DL_211026_0637.xlsx`, `Sales_Report_ClientA_DL_211026_0637.xlsx`; OF t4: an invented `.xltx` template copied to an `.xlsx` name kept its "template" content type).

#### B-R52 · Template copied to the final report name before filling
- **Rule:** A report is made by copying the template file byte for byte (with its file dates, `shutil.copy2`) straight to the final report path, waiting 0.5 s ("Give Windows time to complete the copy"), and only then opening and filling that copy. No temporary name is used. If filling fails, the unfilled template copy stays under the report's normal name, and Step 4 later lists and refreshes it as if it were a real report (it matches `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`).
- **Exact values:** `time.sleep(0.5)` after the copy (COM path only; the openpyxl path has no wait).
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:122-129 (COM path), 227-231 (openpyxl path); picked up later by gui/pyqt_main_window.py:461-462 and power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:76-89.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by XL (E3b, fake COM: a fill failure left the copied template on disk under the report name) and CU (openpyxl twin with a merged Links cell).

#### B-R56 · How the Links values are formed and written · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** (a) Folder paths are absolute and put in Windows form (`/` → `\`, `clean_windows_path`); an empty path gives `''`. (b) File names are the **stem** (name without extension, `Path(name).stem`) of the **first** file of that type in scan order (sorted by full path, B-R1); further files of the same type are copied (B-R42) but never linked. (c) Every value is written as text (`str(value)`). (d) An empty value is **skipped**, so whatever the template already holds in that cell stays (it is not cleared). (e) Each cell write has its own error handling: a failed cell is logged ("Failed to update <cell>: <error>") and the next cell is tried. (f) An unknown report type gives an empty map: nothing is written and the report still counts as created. (g) If building the values fails part-way (for example a file record without a name), the error is only logged ("Error preparing template data: ...") and the report is made with the values prepared so far. (h) Each written value is logged at INFO level as `"  <cell> = <first 50 characters>..."`, so folder paths with client names reach the program log (B-R121). (i) The function also computes the state code (`state_code = get_state_code(client_info['state'])`) and never uses it - it can only add "Unknown state" warnings, or raise if the record has no state.
- **Exact values:** `str(Path(path)).replace('/', '\\')`; `Path(filename).stem`; `files[0]`; `if value:`; log slice `value[:50]`.
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:540-627 (unused state code 550; first file e.g. 561-562, 572-573, 583-584, 595-596, 606-607, 617-618; error 624-625), 159-167 (skip 162, text 163, log 165, per-cell error 166-167), 246-252 (openpyxl twin); utils/helpers.py:311-315 (`clean_windows_path`), 446-448 (`extract_filename_without_extension`).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3); the unused state code became unused in c258047 (B only (after the split)), which removed the debug line that printed it.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (CU openpyxl twin: a template value placed in B10 survived for a client with no IMS file; t1 in Section 4.5.4; LT §7: the stem helper cuts at the last dot - run on the bare text "Zeta Mock Pvt. Ltd" it gives "Zeta Mock Pvt"). In the app the helper always receives a full file name that ends in `.xls` / `.xlsx` (the patterns require it, B-R5), so only that extension is removed and a dot inside the client name survives (a double extension `….xlsx.xlsx` keeps one `.xlsx`) - READ, HIGH.
- **Notes:** a stem loses the extension, so the template's query must add it back; an `.xls` input would be stored as `….xls` but linked as a bare stem (whether the query copes is not visible here; question for the author).

#### B-R60 · When a client counts as "Success"
- **Rule:** A client is counted as successful - and listed in the processing summary's "Client Status" with status `Success` - when its folders were created and copying raised no exception, **even if some copies failed or both reports failed**. Report failures only raise `report_errors` ("Report Creation Errors"). Per-file copy errors are caught inside the organiser (status `Failed` / `Skipped` on the file, core/file_organizer.py:232-283), report errors inside `_create_report`, and organisation-report errors are only logged (core/file_organizer.py:300-362), so in practice only an exception that escapes folder creation (`create_client_structure` re-raises, core/file_organizer.py:140-144) - or an unexpected error in the worker's own bookkeeping - makes the client `Failed`: counted, added to the "Errors" sheet as "Processing Error", and left out of "Client Status". The per-file results go to "File Mapping" only for successful clients.
- **Exact values:** `summary_data['successful_clients'] += 1` with `'status': 'Success'`; failure row `{'time': '%H:%M:%S', 'client': <key>, 'type': 'Processing Error', 'message': str(e)}`; log `  ❌ Failed <key>: <error>`.

### 5.9 Category 9 - Power Query refresh (B-R61 to B-R72)

All of this runs on Windows through Excel (COM) and could not be executed here; it is **READ**, with the call order confirmed by the reader agents' fake-Excel runs (PQ `t_pq.py`, XL E5, LT §4). Times are in seconds.

#### B-R61 · Which file is refreshed · [GST RULE] (when in doubt: which file the figures come from)
- **Rule:** For each ticked Version folder and each ticked report type (ITC first, then Sales), the report to refresh is the **first** file the folder listing returns for `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` or `Sales_Report_*.xlsx` in that Version folder. The pattern also matches earlier refreshed copies (`ITC_Report_…_Refreshed_….xlsx`), so a later run can refresh a copy of a copy, depending on the order in which the operating system lists the folder (RAN on Linux: it happened; on Windows NTFS, which lists alphabetically, the original usually comes first with the default suffix because `.` sorts before `_` - MEDIUM). No file found → `{success False, error "No ITC report found"}` (or "No Sales report found"), no data. A report type that is not ticked gets `{success False, error "Not selected for processing"}` and no data, without any file search.
- **Exact values:** `f"{report_type}_Report_*.xlsx"` with report_type `ITC` / `Sales`; `report_files[0]`; defaults `client_data.get('process_itc', True)` / `get('process_sales', True)` (the window always passes both keys).
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:39-89 (not ticked 50-68; pattern 76; listing 77; first file 89).
- **Origin:** pattern and first-file choice shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3); the ITC/Sales choice was added in bd176bf (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §4.7-4.8 on Linux: an older `_Refreshed_` copy was chosen as the "original"; XL E6; OF t8).

#### B-R62 · Name of the refreshed copy
- **Rule:** The refreshed copy is `<report stem><suffix>.xlsx` in the same Version folder, where *suffix* = the Step 4 "File suffix" text with every `{timestamp}` replaced by the current time as `DDMMYY_HHMM`. The copy is a plain file copy (`shutil.copy2`, overwriting a file of the same name); only the copy is ever opened and saved - the original report is never modified. An empty suffix makes the copy's name equal the original's: the copy fails ("are the same file") and that report fails. A suffix without `{timestamp}` gives the same name every run (each run overwrites the last copy). Characters Windows forbids in file names are not checked. The extension is always `.xlsx`.
- **Exact values:** default suffix `"_Refreshed_{timestamp}"`; `datetime.now().strftime("%d%m%y_%H%M")`; `suffix_pattern.replace("{timestamp}", timestamp)`; `f"{original_file.stem}{suffix}.xlsx"`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:91-94, 118-120. **The default suffix text is typed in five places:** report_processor.py:28; models/app_state.py:22; gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:24 and 139; gui/views/extraction_view.py:136.
- **Origin:** fixed name `_Refreshed_{timestamp}` shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3, `…/report_processor.py:71@edac6a3`); user-editable suffix bd176bf (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §4.8: suffix without `{timestamp}` overwrote; PQ / XL E5: empty suffix → "same file" error).

#### B-R63 · "Skip refresh (use existing refreshed files)"
- **Rule:** When the Step 4 tick is on, the newest (by modification time) existing `<stem>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` in the Version folder is used instead of refreshing, with status `{success True, error None, validation_message "Skipped - Using existing refreshed file"}` - even if that earlier refresh had failed. The search is fixed to `<stem>_Refreshed_*.xlsx`, so with a suffix that does not start with `_Refreshed_` (for example `_PQ_{timestamp}`) the earlier copies are not found and a normal refresh runs; if no such copy exists the code logs "No existing refreshed file found - will refresh" and refreshes. The tick reaches the refresh code by overwriting the module-level setting `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS['skip_refresh']` at the start of every extraction, so the file's own default (`False`) never takes effect in the app. The 3-second wait and the cell reading (B-R82) still happen.
- **Exact values:** glob `f"{original_file.stem}_Refreshed_*.xlsx"`; `max(existing_refreshed, key=lambda x: x.stat().st_mtime)`; tick text "Skip refresh (use existing refreshed files)", default off.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:96-115; gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:53-55; power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:249; gui/views/extraction_view.py:140-141.

#### B-R66 · The Excel used for the refresh
- **Rule:** COM is initialised (`CoInitialize`), then `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` - not `DispatchEx`, so it may attach to an Excel that is already running (MEDIUM, cannot be tested here). Its settings: `Visible = True` (comment "Keep it visible to avoid issues"), `DisplayAlerts = False`, `WindowState = -4137` (maximised). Setting these three is tried up to **5 times, 2 s apart**; after the fifth failure it logs "Could not set Excel properties, continuing anyway..." and continues. The copy is then opened with the Step 4 open routine (B-R99), tried up to **3 times, 3 s apart**, but the retry happens only when the error text contains "Call was rejected by callee" (Excel busy); any other open error ends the refresh. If all three attempts are rejected, the loop simply ends and the code carries on with **no workbook** (the keystrokes are still sent, and the later save fails with a `'NoneType'` error that becomes the refresh status).
- **Exact values:** `max_retries = 5`, `time.sleep(2)`; `excel.WindowState = -4137`; `range(3)`, `time.sleep(3)`, text `"Call was rejected by callee"`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:165-205 (CoInitialize 171; Dispatch 174; settings 176-190; open 192-205).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by PQ (fake COM: three "rejected" errors → keystrokes sent anyway, then the save error).
- **Notes:** Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx`, `Visible = False` and never taking over the user's Excel (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:851-855); stated as fact only - the comparison belongs to Section 8.

#### B-R67 · How the refresh is triggered: keystrokes
- **Rule:** A Windows Script Host shell object (`WScript.Shell`) tries to bring the window whose title is Excel's caption to the front (`AppActivate(excel.Caption)`), up to **3 times, 1 s apart**; a failure is only logged ("Could not activate Excel window, continuing anyway...") and the keys are sent anyway. After 1 s it types `%a` (Alt+A), waits 1 s, types `r`, waits 1 s, types `a` - Excel's ribbon key tips for Data → Refresh All → Refresh All (MEDIUM: this depends on the Excel version and its display language; English key tips assumed). The keys go to **whichever window has the keyboard focus** at that moment. There is no `RefreshAll()`, no `BackgroundQuery = False`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()` and no check that the queries finished.
- **Exact values:** `Dispatch("WScript.Shell")`; `range(3)` with `time.sleep(1)`; `time.sleep(1)`; `SendKeys("%a")`, `sleep(1)`, `SendKeys("r")`, `sleep(1)`, `SendKeys("a")`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:213-249.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:195-228@edac6a3`, already with 1 s gaps; the comments "Increased from 0.5" at 239 and 244, and "Increased from 3 to 5" on the load wait at 209, record an earlier version that is not in the repository).
- **Evidence:** READ; fake-COM call order RAN by PQ / XL E5 (open → SendKeys `%a`, `r`, `a` → Save).
- **Notes:** the log line "→ Sending Alt key..." describes `%a`, which is Alt+A (report_processor.py:237). Standard 12's refresh recipe is at rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867 (fact only).

#### B-R68 · Fixed waits per refreshed report
- **Rule:** No step waits for Excel to report that it is done; every wait is a fixed sleep:

| Step | Wait | Line |
|---|---|---|
| "Waiting for workbook to fully load" after opening | 5 × 1 s | report_processor.py:207-211 |
| after bringing Excel to the front | 1 s (plus up to 3 × 1 s if activation fails) | 220-232 |
| between the three keystrokes | 1 s + 1 s | 239, 244 |
| "Waiting for Power Query refresh to complete" | *w* × 1 s (the Step 4 wait time, default 10, range 5-120) | 253-258 |
| error-dialog checks | up to 5 × 1 s (stops early when a dialog is found) | 260-278 |
| "Giving additional time for complex queries" | max(10, *w*) × 1 s (logged every second second) | 280-286 |
| final error check | none | 288-298 |
| after `Save()` | 2 s | 307 |
| after `Close()` | 1 s | 319 |
| "Waiting for file to be released..." before reading | 3 s | 139-141 |
| (open routine, only on open failures) | 3 s, 2 s | 698, 706 (B-R99) |

  In total about 19 + *w* + max(10, *w*) seconds per report when Excel answers at once and no dialog appears, plus two Excel start-ups (RAN arithmetic in t3: 34 s at *w* = 5, **39 s at the default 10**, 79 s at 30, 139 s at 60, 259 s at 120); twice per client when both reports are ticked. The Stop button is not looked at inside these waits (B-R112).

#### B-R69 · Always save, then close twice, quit
- **Rule:** After the waits: the Info!BB2 check runs (B-R71); then the workbook is **always** saved (`Save()`), also after an error dialog or a failed check; then `Close(SaveChanges=True)`. The clean-up (`finally`) closes it once more with `SaveChanges=False` (the workbook is already closed, so this fails silently), calls `Quit()` and `CoUninitialize()`. Any error inside the keystroke-to-close block returns `{success False, error <text>}` (log "Error during refresh"); any error before it returns the same shape (log "Excel error"). No exception reaches the caller.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:300-366 (check 301; save 305; close 317; inner except 332-337; outer except 339-344; finally 345-366).

- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by PQ (fake COM order: Save → Close(True) → Close(False) → Quit).

| BB2 content | Result (message) |
|---|---|
| no sheet named info | fail - "Info sheet not found" |
| empty (`None`) | fail - "Cell BB2 is empty" |
| only spaces | fail - "Cell BB2 is blank" |
| text equal to `0` or `0.0` after `str()` and trimming (also the numbers 0 and 0.0) | fail - "Cell BB2 contains 0" |
| upper-cased text equal to one of `#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NAME?`, `#NULL!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#N/A`, `#NUM!`, `#ERROR!` | fail - "Cell BB2 contains error: <text>" |
| any error while checking | fail - "Validation error: <error>" |
| anything else | pass - "Validated - Client Name: <BB2>" |

  BB2 is never compared with the client being processed; a value already in the template, or left from an earlier refresh, passes; a number such as 00 or 0.00 written as text would pass; an Excel error returned through COM as a large negative number would pass (MEDIUM; RAN with an assumed value -2146826246). Nothing in B writes BB2 - the template's queries presumably do (MEDIUM; the log calls it "Client Name"; the templates are not in the repository, so the author has to confirm).
- **Exact values:** `sheet.Name.lower() == 'info'`; `Range('BB2').Value`; `cell_str == '0' or cell_str == '0.0'`; the eight error texts above.

#### B-R82 · How the mappings become cell reads · [GST RULE] (when in doubt: decides which cell is read)
- **Rule:** (1) When the configuration module is first imported, every mapping whose input sheet **and** input cell are both non-empty is entered as `CELL_MAPPINGS[report type][input sheet][cell] = "<output sheet>_<output column>"` with spaces → `_`, and the label is stored in `FIELD_DISPLAY_NAMES`. Two mappings with the same report type, sheet and cell would overwrite each other (none today); a mapping with an empty sheet or cell is not read but still gets a column. Changing the file needs a restart. (2) For each report, a **second, hidden Excel** opens the refreshed copy (B-R101) and, for the report type (`ITC` reads only ITC_Report files, `Sales` only Sales_Report files), takes each listed sheet by **exact, case-sensitive** name; a missing sheet gives `None` for all its fields (log warning "Sheet '<name>' not found"); otherwise each cell's `.Value` is read (Excel's value: numbers, text, dates or error codes as COM returns them - MEDIUM, not runnable here) and stored **twice**, under the field name and under the bare cell address (e.g. `J15`); a cell that cannot be read gives `None` under both. (3) Every field and value is written to the screen log, the extraction log file and the program log ("✓ <field>: <value>" / "✗ <field>: None"). (4) Any error during reading → no data at all for that report (`{}`).
- **Exact values:** `if mapping['input_sheet'] and mapping['input_cell']`; `f"{sheet_name}_{mapping['output_column']}".replace(' ', '_')`; `if sheet.Name == sheet_name`; `ws.Range(cell_ref).Value`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:255-278 (build 264-278); power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:496-564 (mapping 497; sheet search 515-519; missing sheet 521-527; read 532-545; summary log 554-562), 566-568 (error → `{}`).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3). The comment "Backward compatibility" (cell_mappings.py:259) refers to the older hand-written format, still visible in the file `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings copy.py` (a direct `CELL_MAPPINGS` with field names such as `itc_diff_igst`), which 47a1492 deleted (READ: `git show "47a1492^:power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings copy.py"`).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t3 printed `CELL_MAPPINGS`; LT §4.10: a duplicate sheet+cell in a custom configuration kept only the last field name; a lower-case report type `itc` made a group that is never asked for).
- **Notes:** the bare-address copies of all sheets share one dictionary, so the same address on two sheets of one report would overwrite each other - it matters only for calculations (B-R84) and for the substring look-up's order (B-R83).

#### B-R83 · Consolidated value look-up (substring first, exact name second) · [GST RULE]
- **Rule:** For each output column, the consolidator first walks the extracted data **in reading order** and takes the value of the **first field whose name contains the column label** (a case-sensitive text test) - and stops there, even if that value is empty. Only if that value is `None` does it try the exact field name `"<output sheet>_<output column>"` (spaces → `_`). Labels that contain a space never match a field name (field names use `_`), so they always fall through to the exact field name and show their own configured cells. The one-word labels `IGST`, `CGST`, `SGST` (B-R79, B-R80, B-R81) first match `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST` / `_CGST` / `_SGST`, which come first in reading order - so **9 of the 22 columns** show `Diff GSTR-3B` ⚠ J15 / K15 / L15 (template cell positions). The figure written into those columns therefore depends on the order of the extracted data, not on the configured cell. A value of `None` or `''` then becomes "Missing" (B-R88).

| J15 value read (RAN, t3) | "IMS Reco" IGST shows | "GSTR-3B Difference" Diff IGST shows |
|---|---|---|
| a value (marker) | the J15 value | the J15 value |
| `None` (empty cell or sheet missing) | its own AA1 (via the exact name) | "Missing" |
| `''` (empty text) | **"Missing"** (AA1 not consulted) | "Missing" |
| `0` | **0** (J15's zero) | 0 |
| 1234.5 | 1234.5 (with `#,##0.00`) | 1234.5 |

- **Exact values:** `if mapping['output_column'] in field_name: value = field_value; break`; fallback `if value is None and mapping['input_cell']: … extracted_data.get(key)`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:125-138.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025: the look-up is from edac6a3; it started to show cells other than the configured ones when 47a1492 added the one-word labels (the first three output sheets all had labels with spaces). The same line exists in project A (PQ notes; comparison later).
- **Evidence:** RAN (t3 table above, `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S45/work3/t3_out.json`; t1 in Section 4.5.7; LT §4.6 with reversed key order: the three sheets then showed the `Extra_In_GSTR2B` values; PQ; DC T3; XL E5).

#### B-R84 · Calculated columns · [GST RULE] · DEAD (in practice)
- **Rule:** A mapping may name a calculation `{type, cell1, cell2}`; the two operands are looked up by **bare cell address** in the extracted values (no sheet name); empty or missing values count as 0; a value that `float()` (Python's conversion to a decimal number) cannot convert (for example `'1,000'`) → "Error"; types `subtract` (cell1 − cell2), `add`, `multiply`, `divide` (cell1 ÷ cell2; divisor 0 → "Div/0"); any other type → "Unknown"; any other error → "Error" (logged). Calculations are skipped when the refresh failed (the row shows "Missing"). No mapping uses a calculation.

### 5.11 Category 11 - Consolidated output layout (B-R86 to B-R95)

Two workbooks are written with openpyxl (a Python library that writes .xlsx files without Excel): the consolidated extraction workbook at the end of Step 4 (B-R86 to B-R93) and the processing summary at the end of Step 3 (B-R94, B-R95). Neither contains Power Query, so openpyxl is safe for them.

#### B-R86 · Consolidated extraction workbook: when, where, name
- **Rule:** At the end of an extraction with at least one result (also after Stop), one workbook `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx` (year first, to the minute) is saved into the run folder (Level 1) shown on Step 4. A second extraction in the same minute overwrites it silently. Any error while building or saving it (for example a value openpyxl cannot store, such as a time-zone-aware date or a tuple (a fixed list of values) from a multi-cell range) loses the whole workbook and shows only `  Report error: <text>` in the Step 4 log (red); the run still ends normally. When the error is raised while openpyxl is already writing the file (the time-zone-aware date), a half-written file that Excel and openpyxl cannot open is left under the normal name and would replace a good report of the same minute; when it is raised earlier (the tuple, while the cell is filled), no file is written (RAN Section 7 me r3; RAN Section 3 B-F23 t23; B-G43) [Corrected during self-review - originally stated only that the whole workbook is lost, but Section 3 (B-F23) and Section 7 (B-G43) revealed the leftover broken file; re-RAN in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW/scripts/tz_consolidator.py`: TypeError, a 5,057-byte `PQ_Extraction_Report_<minute>.xlsx` without `[Content_Types].xml` left, which openpyxl cannot open].
- **Exact values:** `datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M")`; `f"PQ_Extraction_Report_{timestamp}.xlsx"`; success log `  Report saved: <name>` (green); progress 95 "Creating report...".
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:160-174 (name 163-165; save 167; error re-raised 172-174); gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:86-95 (only `if results`, 87; folder 92; error 94-95).
- **Origin:** workbook and name shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3). Its place: at the split the stand-alone extractor saved it in the Level 1 folder (`47a1492:power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:808`); c258047 put it in the target folder itself; b0e7d0e moved it back into the Level 1 folder (both B only (after the split)).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (t1 and t3: `PQ_Extraction_Report_20261021_0637.xlsx`, `PQ_Extraction_Report_20261023_1323.xlsx`; LT §4.10: same-minute overwrite; a tuple value → `ValueError: Cannot convert (1, 2) to Excel`, whole report lost).

#### B-R87 · Layout of each output sheet
- **Rule:** One sheet per configured output sheet, in configuration order (B-R73 to B-R81), after a "Summary" sheet that is inserted first (B-R90). On each output sheet: A1 = `"<sheet name> Report"`, bold 14 pt, merged A1:C1; row 3 = headers `Client Name`, `Successfully Run`, then the configured column labels in order - bold white 12 pt on blue `0078D4`, centred, thin borders; data from row 4, **one row per extracted Version folder** (not per client); column A = the Step 4 display name `"<client folder> / <version folder>"` (not the client's name); every data cell has a thin border; column widths = longest text + 2, at most 50 (the Summary sheet is **not** width-adjusted - RAN t3, a detail the registry does not list). A Version folder that was ticked only for Sales still gets a row in every ITC sheet (with ✗ and "Missing"), and the other way round.
- **Exact values:** `Font(bold=True, color="FFFFFF", size=12)`, `PatternFill(start_color="0078D4", …)`, `Font(bold=True, size=14)`, `merge_cells('A1:C1')`, `start_row = 3`, `min(max_length + 2, 50)`.

### 5.12 Category 12 - Excel handling and safety (B-R96 to B-R110)

COM (Windows' mechanism for one program to drive another) through pywin32 is used in three places: Step 3 report filling (core/excel_handler.py), Step 4 refresh and Step 4 reading (power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py). None of it could run here; everything is **READ**, with fake-Excel call orders from the reader agents (CU t_fakecom, XL E3-E5, PQ t_pq). How this compares with the author's Standard 12 is Section 8's job; the Standard's line numbers are given only where a rule touches it.

#### B-R96 · Step 3 Excel: attach, hide, always quit
- **Rule:** For each report: `CoInitialize`; first `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` - this **attaches to an Excel the user already has open**, if any (log "Using existing Excel instance"); otherwise `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (log "Created new Excel instance"). On that Excel it sets `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` - so the user's own Excel windows disappear while reports are made, and `Visible` is never set back. The workbook is saved twice (`Save()`, then `Close(SaveChanges=True)`). At the end it sets `ScreenUpdating = True` and `DisplayAlerts = True` (not protected: if Excel has died these raise and the rest of the clean-up is skipped) and then **always calls `Quit()`**, because `self.excel_app` is never set to anything but `None` - the comment "Don't quit if Excel was already open" is not what happens. So an Excel the user had open is closed, with alerts switched back on (MEDIUM what real Excel then does with the user's unsaved workbooks - a hidden "save changes?" prompt or lost work; not testable here). This happens once per report, so twice per client. The `__del__` method that would quit `self.excel_app` never does anything.
- **Exact values:** `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")`, fallback `Dispatch("Excel.Application")`; `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False`; `if self.excel_app is None: excel.Quit()`.
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:95-217 (CoInitialize 107; attach 110-115; settings 118-120; save 173, 176; end 203-211; CoUninitialize 213-217), 55 (`excel_app = None`), 57-63 (`__del__`).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3); only bare `except:` clauses were narrowed in c258047 (B only (after the split)), no behaviour change.
- **Evidence:** READ; fake-COM RAN by CU (t_fakecom: `('excel.Quit', 'USER-OWN-EXCEL')`) and XL (E3).
- **Notes:** Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx`, a hidden Excel with `DisplayAlerts = False`, never taking over the user's own Excel, and `Quit()` in `finally` (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:851-856).

#### B-R97 · openpyxl fallback for report filling · DEAD (in practice)
- **Rule:** If the PC is not Windows (`platform.system() != 'Windows'`) or `win32com.client` / `pythoncom` cannot be imported, `USE_WIN32COM` stays False and reports would be made with openpyxl instead: copy the template, `load_workbook(…, data_only=False, keep_links=True)` (macros are not kept: `keep_vba` defaults to False), write the non-empty values into an exact (any-case) `Links` sheet, save, close. Saving with openpyxl **drops the workbook's Power Query** (RAN by XL E2), and also the shapes drawn on its sheets, such as text boxes and buttons (RAN, Appendix X1.4.3 F5 - added during the completeness check); the only signals are log warnings: "win32com not available. Install with: pip install pywin32", "Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!" (also shown on Windows without pywin32) and "Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!". A cell write that raises `KeyError` or `ValueError` (Python's errors for a missing key and for an unusable value) is skipped with a warning; any other error - for example a mapped cell inside a merged range - makes the whole report fail ("Fallback method error: …"), leaving the copied template on disk. Through the app this path cannot be reached, because the window cannot start without pywin32 (B-R124).
- **Exact values:** `USE_WIN32COM = False` unless `platform.system() == 'Windows'` and both imports succeed; `load_workbook(str(output_path), data_only=False, keep_links=True)`; `except (KeyError, ValueError)`.
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:19-28 (import guard; root-logger messages 26, 28), 83-93 (choice; warning 90), 219-262 (fallback; warning 224; per-cell 246-252; failure 260-262).
- **Origin:** fallback shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3). The merged-cell failure is B only (after the split) (c258047 narrowed `except: pass` to `except (KeyError, ValueError)`; at the split such a cell was silently skipped and the report succeeded - H1 notes, RAN there).

#### B-R98 · Step 3: opening the report copy
- **Rule:** The path is made absolute; a missing file raises `FileNotFoundError("File not found: …")`. If a workbook with the same full path is already open in that Excel, it is reused (and later saved and closed - closing a workbook the user had open). Otherwise `Workbooks.Open(path)` with no options. On failure, if the error text contains `-2147352567` (COM's general "exception occurred") or the word `path`, or the path is longer than 218 characters (B-R100), one retry is made with the Windows 8.3 short path (the old DOS-style short name, `GetShortPathName`; unchanged on non-Windows and on disks without 8.3 names) when it differs; otherwise, or if that also fails, the **original** error is raised. No `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended`, no `ReadOnly` check.
- **Exact values:** `"-2147352567" in str(e) or "path" in str(e).lower() or path_length > 218`; log `Using short path: ...<last 50 characters>`.
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:264-306; utils/helpers.py:473-483 (`get_short_path`: Windows only, any error → the path unchanged).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; fake-COM RAN by CU (original error propagated, report False); LT §7 (`get_short_path` on Linux returns the path unchanged).
- **Notes:** Standard 12 asks for `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` and a `workbook.ReadOnly` check (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:857-859).

#### B-R99 · Step 4: opening the refreshed copy (refresh and reading)
- **Rule:** (1) The file must exist (`FileNotFoundError`); one byte is read to prove it can be opened (any error re-raised). (2) A workbook with the same full path already open in that Excel is reused. (3) If the path is longer than 218 characters ("Excel's typical limit"): `/` → `\` and the long-path prefix `\\?\` (local path) or `\\?\UNC\` (network path starting `\\`) is added. (4) Attempt 1: `Workbooks.Open(path)`. (5) Attempt 2: close **every** workbook with the same file name in that Excel **without saving**, wait 3 s, open again. (6) Attempt 3: wait 2 s; if Windows gives a different 8.3 short path, open that (if this fails, the message "Could not get short path" is logged and the next step runs); else, if the prefix was added, open the original path; else `Workbooks.Open(Filename=<path>, UpdateLinks=0, ReadOnly=False, IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True, Notify=False)`. (7) If everything fails: "❌ All attempts failed. Final error: …"; when the error contains `-2147352567`, advice lines ("File is open in another program", "File is corrupted", "Path is too long (<n> chars)", "OneDrive/SharePoint sync issue", and for long paths "📋 Path length is definitely an issue!" / "Consider enabling long path support in Windows"); the error is raised. `workbook.ReadOnly` is never checked.
- **Exact values:** `path_length > 218`; prefixes `'\\\\?\\'` and `'\\\\?\\UNC\\'` (Python text for `\\?\` and `\\?\UNC\`); waits `time.sleep(3)`, `time.sleep(2)`; error texts cut to 200 / 100 characters (B-R123).
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:638-747 (exists 643-645; access 647-654; reuse 656-660; long path 664-680; attempt 1 682-689; attempt 2 691-701; attempt 3 703-731; failure 732-747).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; fake-COM RAN by PQ (attempt order).
- **Notes:** a second copy of the same idea with different behaviour exists for Step 3 (B-R98). Attempt 2 (point 5 above) closes workbooks of the same *name* from any folder in that Excel without saving - if `Dispatch` attached to the user's Excel (B-R66), that could be one of the user's own workbooks (MEDIUM).

- **Rule:** Every **visible and enabled top-level window on the whole desktop** (of any program, not only this Excel) counts as an error dialog when its title, in lower case, contains one of `microsoft excel`, `error`, `problem`, `cannot`, `failed`, `unable`, `could not`, `exception`, `invalid`, `missing` **and** its window class is one of `#32770` (standard Windows dialog), `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword` (Office dialogs). Any error while looking counts as "no dialog".

#### B-R103 · Error-dialog handling: text and closing
- **Rule:** The dialog's text = its title plus the texts of its child controls whose class name contains `static` or `text` and whose text is longer than 5 characters, joined with spaces, runs of white space collapsed, cut to 200 characters; if nothing is found (or on any error) the text is "Power Query error occurred". It is written to the program log (warning "⚠️ Error detected: …" / "⚠️ Late error detected: …") and becomes the refresh's error (B-R70). On screen (and so in the extraction log file, B-R122) it appears only inside the later line "⚠️ Refresh completed with errors: <text>" (report_processor.py:322), and only when the Info!BB2 check passed: a failed check replaces the dialog text with "Refresh validation failed: …" (report_processor.py:310-313), so the dialog text is then in the program log only. [Corrected in verification - originally said "written only to the program log".] The dialog is then closed: the first child **button** whose text (lower case) contains `ok`, `close`, `yes` or `continue` is clicked (`BM_CLICK`) - a text test, so "Yes" answers whatever the dialog asked, and `ok` also matches words such as "Book"; if no such button exists, a close message (`WM_CLOSE`) is posted; then 0.5 s.
- **Exact values:** `len(child_text) > 5`; `combined_text[:200]`; button words `['ok', 'close', 'yes', 'continue']`; `win32con.BM_CLICK`, `win32con.WM_CLOSE`; `time.sleep(0.5)`.
- **Where:** power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:406-441 (text), 443-476 (close), 268-273 and 291-296 (use).
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ; fake-COM RAN by PQ.
