#### B-R110 · COM start and stop in worker threads
- **Rule:** Each Excel function that runs in a worker thread starts with `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` and calls `pythoncom.CoUninitialize()` in its own clean-up (`finally`), while the Excel objects are still held in that function's local variables. In Step 3, the un-initialise is skipped if the unprotected `ScreenUpdating` / `DisplayAlerts` lines of B-R96 raise.
- **Where:** core/excel_handler.py:107, 213-217; power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:171, 362-366, 484, 583-587.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3). The worker threads themselves are B only (after the split) (c258047, QThread); at the split the same functions ran in Tkinter background threads.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Notes:** Standard 12: `CoInitialize()` first, the Excel work in a separate function, `CoUninitialize()` after that function returns, so no Excel object is still held (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:872-875).

### 5.13 Category 13 - Performance and operational constants (B-R111 to B-R114)

The Excel waits and retries are under B-R66 to B-R68 and B-R99; every remaining number is collected in 5.17.

#### B-R111 · Background jobs: one thread per kind
- **Rule:** Scanning, processing and extraction each run in their own background thread (a `QThread`, so the window keeps responding); at most **one thread per kind**, so at most three at once. A second job of the same kind is refused silently - only "Scan already in progress" / "Processing already in progress" / "Extraction already in progress" in the program log. Jobs of different kinds can run at the same time (processing and extraction both drive Excel). Closing the window neither stops nor waits for a running job (RAN by MW e11). After a job ends, its thread and worker objects are released (`deleteLater`); a late clean-up can delete a newer running thread and abort the program (RAN by MW e13 with widened timing; LOW likelihood). No widget is touched from a worker thread: results come back by Qt signals.
- **Exact values:** `if self._thread and self._thread.isRunning(): logger.warning(...); return`.
- **Where:** gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:57-94 (guard 59-61); gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:256-298 (guard 259-261); gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:138-184 (guard 142-144); gui/pyqt_main_window.py:601-608 (close).
- **Origin:** B only (after the split) (c258047, QThread pattern). At the split the Tkinter app used its own background threads (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by MW (e3, e4, e9, e11, e13, e17).

#### B-R112 · Stop
- **Rule:** Stop sets a flag that is looked at only **between clients** (processing) or **between Version folders** (extraction). The item in progress - with all its Excel waits - runs to the end. A stopped run then finishes like a normal one: processing still writes the summary (if any client succeeded), shows "Processing Complete - Successfully processed k/N clients", saves run history and moves to Step 4; extraction still writes the consolidated workbook and the log file and turns the Step 4 dot green. The log shows "Processing stopped by user" / "Extraction stopped by user" (yellow). Scanning has no Stop.
- **Where:** gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:80-83, 281-284; gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:60-63, 167-170.
- **Origin:** B only (after the split) (c258047).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by MW (e5).

#### B-R113 · Progress figures and time texts
- **Rule:**
  - **Processing:** before each client, `idx ÷ total × 100` with the text `Client i/N: <client> | ETA: <time>`; the time left is "Calculating..." for the first client and afterwards (clients left including the current one) × (elapsed time ÷ clients finished); then 95 "Creating summary report..." (only when a summary is made, B-R94) and 100 `Complete | <m>m <s>s`.
  - **Extraction:** before each Version folder, `idx ÷ total × 100` with `Processing i/N: <client folder> / <version folder>`; then 95 "Creating report..." (only with results) and 100 "Extraction complete"; the log ends with "Extraction complete: <results>/<total> clients processed" - this counts attempts, not successes.
  - **Scan:** one message per file (`[i/N] <name>`, plus "Finding Excel files...", "Found N files, processing..." or "No Excel files found"); the status bar shows `Scanning... P% (i/N)` with P = `int(i / N × 100)`.
  - **Time texts** (ETA): under a minute `<s>s`; under an hour `<m>m <s>s`; otherwise `<h>h <m>m` (whole numbers, cut not rounded).
  - The progress bars take whole numbers only (`int(percent)`: fractions are dropped).
- **Exact values:** `tracker.update(0 if idx == 0 else 1, …)`; `"Calculating..."`; `format_duration` thresholds 60 and 3600; `f"Complete | {mins}m {secs}s"`.
- **Where:** gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:55-56, 86-90, 185, 196-198; utils/helpers.py:369-416 (`ProgressTracker` 369-403, `format_duration` 405-416); gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:65-67, 89, 97-98; core/file_parser.py:147-158; gui/pyqt_main_window.py:238-242; gui/views/processing_view.py:137-140; gui/views/extraction_view.py:397-400.

#### B-R119 · run_history.json: content, limits, persistence
- **Rule:** Four parts:
  - `runs`: one entry per processing run - `timestamp` (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, taken when the run is recorded), `total_clients`, `successful_clients`, `failed_clients`, `total_files`, `reports_generated`, `processing_mode`; **only the last 50 kept**.
  - `client_history`: per key, a list of client records with the fields `client_key`, `client_name`, `state`, `run_timestamp`, `processing_mode`, `files_organized`, `itc_report_created`, `sales_report_created`, `itc_report_path`, `sales_report_path`, `output_folder` (= the client folder path), `pq_refreshed`, `pq_refresh_timestamp`, `pq_extraction_data`, `errors` - **never trimmed**; `itc_report_path`, `sales_report_path` and `errors` are never filled.
  - `last_run_timestamp`; `total_runs` (counts every run, also beyond 50).
  It is rewritten whole, in place (not atomic), after each processing run and after each extraction (JSON indent 2, UTF-8, `default=str`, so the extraction result's date-time comes back as text). It is loaded once at start, protected against unreadable files (→ empty history, then overwritten at the next save, so a damaged history is silently replaced) but **without type checks**: wrong inner types (for example `"runs": 5` or `"client_history": []`) load without a warning and then crash the next `add_run` / `add_extraction_result`, i.e. when the next processing or extraction result is recorded, before anything is saved (RAN LT §5.2 #32-35). In the window this is not just an error: the crash happens inside a screen handler, so PyQt5 aborts the whole program (exit code 134 in a console) at the end of processing, after all the output has been written, without a message and without a settings save (RAN Section 3 B-F17 Case C, `{"runs": 5}`; `models/run_history.py:58` called from `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:379`; B-G35, B-G36) [Corrected during self-review - originally stated only that the next add_run "crashes", but Section 3 (B-F17) and Section 7 (B-G36) revealed that in the window the crash aborts the program]. The extraction records hold every extracted figure, the file paths and the BB2 text, kept indefinitely in the user profile. With two copies of the app open, the last one to save wins (whole-file rewrite).
- **Exact values:** `if len(self.runs) > 50: self.runs = self.runs[-50:]`; `datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')`.
- **Where:** models/run_history.py:16-148 (record fields 16-33; history 36-42; add_run 44-71, cap 69-71; add_extraction_result 73-95; save 128-136; load 138-148); models/cache_manager.py:36, 66-72; gui/pyqt_main_window.py:43, 377-380, 554-558; gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:149-160.
- **Origin:** B only (after the split) (c258047).
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN by LT §5.2 (#24-#37: 60 runs → 50 kept, `total_runs` 60, per-client history 60 records).

- **Rule:** Processing records are stored under the scan key `"<client>-<state code>"` (B-R17), and the Step 2 "Last Run" column shows the newest record's `run_timestamp` under that key (refreshed only at the next scan). Extraction results are stored under `"<client folder> / <version folder>"` (the Step 4 display name): the **latest record under that key is updated in place** (`pq_refreshed = True` - even when the refresh failed - `pq_refresh_timestamp`, `pq_extraction_data` = the whole result, so a second extraction of the same version replaces the first one's data), or a new mostly empty record is created. No screen reads the extraction records. Even without the "/ <version>" part, the client *folder* name can differ from the scan key (abbreviation and cut, B-R32).

Windows Script Host (`WScript.Shell`) and an installed Excel are also needed for Steps 3-4; no version of Excel or Python is checked.

#### B-R125 · main.py start-up and its error messages
- **Rule:** (1) If a console exists, its output is re-wrapped as UTF-8. (2) Logging is configured (B-R121). (3) The program folder (from the file's own location, not the current folder) is put first on Python's import path. (4) The application is named "GST File Organizer", version "4.0"; the window is built and shown. (5) A missing module: the log gets "Import Error: <error>" and the console prints "Missing module: <error>", "Please install required packages:", "  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl", exit code 1 - advice that does not fix the usual cause (pywin32). (6) Any other start-up error: "Critical error: <error>" (log with traceback, console), exit code 1. No message box, no error file, no `sys.excepthook` (a hook that catches errors nothing else caught): under pythonw (the console-less Python) nothing is visible, and an error that escapes a window handler later aborts the whole program (exit code 134, RAN by MW e10; of the window's handlers only the scan-result handler has its own try/except, gui/pyqt_main_window.py:245, 313-316, and the three workers catch everything in their own `run`).

#### B-R136 · Step 4 tree and the "Refreshed" status
- **Rule:** One bold parent row per client folder (status column `"<n> version(s)"`, grey) and one child row per kept Version folder (name shown with two leading spaces). All boxes start unticked at every rebuild (start-up, after processing, after extraction, "Refresh List"). Status: `Refreshed (dd/mm/yy HH:MM)` in green if any file `*_Refreshed*` with extension `.xlsx` / `.xls` / `.xlsm` (not starting with `~$`) exists in the Version folder - the time is the newest such file's modification time, not a record of a refresh - else `Pending` in orange. A copy left by a failed refresh, or an unrelated file with "_Refreshed" in its name, also counts; one refreshed ITC copy marks the whole version; a custom suffix (B-R62) that does not contain `_Refreshed` always shows "Pending". Buttons: ITC Only, Sales Only, Select All, Deselect All (they touch only tickable boxes) and Refresh List. Each version with at least one tick becomes a request `{name "<client folder> / <version folder>", client_key (the client folder name; never used later), version_folder, process_itc, process_sales}`. Header label `Source: <run folder name>`, or one of: "No target folder configured.", "Target folder does not exist.", "No 'Annual Statement-...' folders found in target.", "Error scanning: <error>", "No processed clients found in <run folder name>"; "No data loaded" before the first fill.

### 5.17 Every hard-coded value, constant and lookup table (one place)

The rules above already give each value with its rule. This part lists them all together - including the operational and safety numbers - so that a rebuild can check nothing is lost. The lookup tables reproduced in full above are referenced, not repeated: state table (B-R21, 5.3), file-name patterns (B-R5 table, 5.1), hint table (B-R12), destination table (B-R37), Links cells (B-R54, B-R55), extraction mappings (5.10), BB2 check (B-R71), settings keys (B-R116), summary sheets (B-R95), message texts (B-R131), help texts (B-R141). Evidence for this part: READ, cross-checked against the reader agents' full magic-value scan (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-X-DEAD/magic_output.txt`, DC P-05).

### 5.19 Items the registry lacks (UNREGISTERED)

The registry was checked against the code while this section was written. These rule-like items have no registry ID; per the audit conventions they are described here without inventing an ID.

#### UNREGISTERED: Extraction output folder falls back to the target folder · DEAD (in practice)
- **Rule:** The extraction worker takes the run folder it is given; when none is given, its output folder (consolidated workbook and extraction log) is the **target folder itself**. The window never starts an extraction without a run folder (B-R133: "No Level 1 folder available."), so the fallback cannot be reached through the screens.
- **Exact values:** `self.level1_folder = Path(level1_folder) if level1_folder else self.output_folder`.
- **Where:** gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:28-29; guard gui/pyqt_main_window.py:512-515.
- **Origin:** B only (after the split) (b0e7d0e; c258047 always used the target folder).
- **Evidence:** READ.

#### UNREGISTERED: Every organiser path is built by `safe_path_join`, which drops empty parts
- **Rule:** Run, client, Version and category folders, every copy and the organisation report are joined with `safe_path_join`, which silently leaves out empty name parts and raises `ValueError("No valid path components provided")` when nothing is left. An empty client-folder or file name would therefore not raise an error at the join but put the item one level higher (not reachable with today's recognition rules, which require a non-empty client and state - B-R5; LOW).
- **Exact values:** `valid_parts = [p for p in parts if p]`.
- **Where:** utils/helpers.py:49-64; used at core/file_organizer.py:94, 102, 132, 153, 176, 255, 314.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ.

#### UNREGISTERED: `FileOrganizer.get_summary` · DEAD
- **Rule:** Would report the organiser's counts: `folders_created` as the number of **distinct** folders (`len(set(...))`), `files_processed`, `successful_copies`, `failed_copies`, `skipped_files` (= the rest), `errors`, plus time stamp, mode and target. It is never called. Its distinct count differs from the organisation report's "Folders Created", which counts every append, including the run folder once per client in Fresh mode (B-R40: 6 / 12 / 18 for three clients).
- **Where:** core/file_organizer.py:392-408; compare 345-351.
- **Origin:** shared - before the split on 30-10-2025 (edac6a3).
- **Evidence:** READ (grep: no caller).

Details found that refine registered rules (kept under those rules, not new IDs): the consolidated "Summary" sheet gets no column widths (B-R87, B-R90); the processing summary is saved in, and Explorer opens, the run folder of the first client whose folders were made (B-R94, B-R139); a scan-display error is shown as "Error displaying results: <error>" (B-R139); an empty text `''` in `Diff GSTR-3B` J15/K15/L15 gives "Missing" (and a `0` gives 0) in the three one-word output sheets instead of their own cells (B-R83).

## SECTION 6: EDGE CASES AND DEFENSIVE CODE

### 6.0 How to read Sections 6 and 7

**What these two sections cover.** Project B = goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2, branch main, HEAD b0e7d0e (09-02-2026), the PyQt5 window that calls itself "GST File Organizer v4.0". Section 6 lists every unusual situation the code deliberately handles (an "edge case" is an input or situation at the edge of what is normal: an empty folder, a missing sheet, a blank value, a duplicate file) and lists every `try/except` block (the place where the program catches an error so that it does not stop). Section 7 lists what the code does NOT handle, numbered B-G1 … B-G82.

**Where the code came from.** The 12 commits edac6a3 … 47a1492 are "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025"; c258047, a62d3cc, c21f788, 7e09e5c and b0e7d0e are "B only (after the split)". Each item that matters for the later comparison with project A says which of the two it comes from. Project B has one branch, main (a second name in the local checkout, `claude/pensive-feynman-0mz1aa`, points at the same commit and holds no extra work; it was created when this audit's copy was prepared - Section 12, "Branch awareness") [Corrected during self-review - originally stated "one branch, main" without the second name, but Section 12 ("Branch awareness") revealed a second ref at the same commit].

**Evidence words.**
- Every statement about the code cites `file:line` in project B at b0e7d0e (repository-relative; the scratch copy has the same line numbers). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **READ** = established by reading the code line by line.
- **RAN** = the code was executed on made-up inputs. "RAN (me rN)" = run for this section on 23-10-2026 by `scripts/rN_*.py` in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S67/` (outputs `out/rN.txt`); "RAN (me tN)" = the small runs `scripts/t1_cheap_reruns.py` … `t5_qt_key.py` made by an earlier, interrupted run of this same task on 21-10-2026 (outputs `out/t1_output.txt`, `out/t2_output.txt`, `out/t4_output.txt`, `out/t5_output.txt`; t3 was an inline command whose outputs are `out/t3_stdout.txt` and `out/t3_stderr.txt`). [Corrected during verification - originally said all five outputs were `out/t1_output.txt` … `out/t5_output.txt`; t3 has no such file (RAN `ls out/`).] The most important runs were repeated by the verifier on 23-10-2026 in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S67/` (copies of r1-r5, r7, r8, t4 and the r6 start-up cases on a fresh copy of B, plus `scripts/v1_migration.py`); every output matched apart from time stamps and the fingerprints of text files that contain time stamps. All runs used a copy of B (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S67/proj`, checked identical to `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy` with `diff -rq` after the runs, no `__pycache__` written because every run used `python -B`), and `HOME` / `TMPDIR` pointed into the run folder, so B's settings folder and temporary folder could only land in scratch. 7.12 lists every run.
- "Section 3, B-Fn trace" = a run made for this audit's Section 3 (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B/S3a.md`, `S3b.md`; scripts under `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3a/` and `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3b/`).
- "RAN (DC T5e)", "RAN (LT §6.2)", "RAN (MW e11)" and so on = run by an earlier reader agent; the short names are the notes: **DC** = dead-code and silent-bug notes (`B_dead_code_patterns.md`, items D-, P-, S-, tests T1-T10); **XL** = Excel and Power Query notes (`B_excel_pq_safety.md`, findings and experiments E1-E7); **OF** = outside-files notes (`B_outside_files_state.md`); **LT** = live traces (`B_live_traces.md`); **DO** = documents notes (`B_docs.md`); **CU**, **PQ**, **MW**, **VW** = the code notes for core/utils, power_query_extractor/models/start-up, the main window/controllers/theme, and the views (`MW e1-e17` and `VW t1-t9` are their experiments); **SH** = the 12 shared commits (`shared_history_12_commits.md`). All are in `/root/merge-scratch/notes2/`.
- Excel through COM (Windows' mechanism by which one program remote-controls another, here Python driving Excel) cannot run on this Linux computer. Those parts are traced by reading. Some were helped by "fake COM" runs: stand-in modules that only record which Excel commands B sends, in which order. A fake-COM run proves B's own Python control flow, never how real Excel behaves.
- Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence. "NOT SURE" always comes with a way to check.

**IDs.** Features B-F1 … B-F34 and rules B-R1 … B-R144 are those of the registry `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_registry.md`. Gaps B-G1 … B-G82 are numbered in Section 7 in the order they appear; 7.10 lists them all in one table.

**[GST RULE] and ⚠.** [GST RULE] marks anything that decides a tax figure, which return, table, sheet or cell a figure belongs to, a rate, limit or threshold, rounding, the financial year or tax period, GSTIN / PAN / state-code logic, ITC eligibility or a due date (when in doubt, tagged). For these the audit says only what the code does; it never says whether it is right. ⚠ marks a value that can change over time (return and table names, template sheet names and cell positions, state lists, file-naming conventions, Excel's keyboard shortcuts, Python and package versions) so the author can check it.

**Client confidentiality.** All test runs used invented names ("Alpha Test Traders", "Beta Demo Industries" and so on, or `<Client A>`, `<Client B>`). File-name PATTERNS that the code recognises are quoted exactly, because they are code, not client data.

**No tests.** Project B has never had an automated test (RAN, DO C2: no committed path containing "test" in B's whole history). None of the edge cases below is protected by a test. For the later comparison: project A's pure-logic tests, run against B's code by the A-tests reader, fail exactly where B behaves differently - 7 failures, all in name cleaning ("Private"/"Limited" replaced case-sensitively and inside words, B-G18) and IMS Reco names ending in "(N)" (rejected by B, B-G48) - and A's file-operation tests cannot even be imported against B (RAN, `A_tests.md` §11).

**Plain-English words used in Sections 6 and 7**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `try/except` block, handler | The place where the program catches an error (an "exception") so that it does not stop. "Handler" = one `except` part. A **bare `except:`** catches everything, including the Ctrl+C key. |
| logged | Written to the program log file `gst_organizer.log` (B-F32); the user does not see it unless they open that file. |
| swallowed | Caught and ignored: nothing on screen, nothing in the log file. |
| re-raised | Caught, then passed on to the code that called this function. |
| fallback | Instead of failing, the code continues with a substitute value or a second method. |
| worker thread | A second line of work running next to the window, so the window keeps responding (scanning, processing and extraction each start one). |
| signal | Qt's message from one object to another; B's workers report to the window only through signals. |
| slot / handler | The window function that runs when a button is clicked or a signal arrives. |
| screen log | The dark text box on Step 1 (scan log), Step 3 or Step 4 where B writes coloured lines. |
| COM / pywin32 | Windows' way for Python to drive Microsoft Excel; pywin32 is the Python add-on that provides it (modules `pythoncom`, `win32com`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`). |
| openpyxl | A Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel. When it saves an existing workbook it drops the Power Query part. |
| Power Query, refresh | Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC and Sales templates; "refresh" re-runs its queries. |
| SendKeys / key tips | Pressing keyboard keys by program, into whatever window has the keyboard focus / the letters Excel shows on its ribbon when Alt is pressed (Alt, A = Data tab; R, A = Refresh All in an English Excel ⚠). |
| glob | A wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`. |
| mtime | A file's or folder's "date modified". |
| stem | A file name without its extension. |
| regular expression (regex) | A text pattern used to recognise file names. |
| JSON | The plain-text format of B's settings and history files. |
| UNC path / mapped drive | A network path written `\\server\share\...` / the same share shown as a drive letter such as `Z:`. |
| 8.3 short path | The old DOS-style short form of a Windows path, shorter, so it can get under a path-length limit. |
| `\\?\` prefix | A prefix Windows accepts in front of a path to switch off the usual 260-character limit. |
| CoInitialize / CoUninitialize | The two calls that switch COM on and off for one thread. |
| pythonw | The Python program that runs without a console window (what the author's Standard 13 launcher uses). |
| exit code 134 | The code a program ends with when it is aborted (killed by itself), here by Qt after an unhandled error. |
| NTFS | Windows' own disk format. |
| traceback | Python's raw error listing: the error message plus the chain of program lines that led to it. "Logged with traceback" = that listing is written to the log file. |
| Python error names | `ImportError` (a module is missing), `OSError` / `FileExistsError` / `PermissionError` / `IsADirectoryError` (the disk or the operating system refused), `TypeError` / `ValueError` (a value of the wrong kind), `AttributeError` (a value lacks the feature asked of it, for example a list where a table of keys was expected), `KeyError` (a key is not in a table). |
| HTML | The text format of web pages; B's screen logs treat each message as a small piece of HTML (`<span>` with a colour), so characters such as "<" are read as formatting. |
| event loop | Qt's never-ending loop in the window's own thread that handles clicks, key presses and signals; the program ends when it ends. |
| lock | A guard that lets only one thread (or one program) use a shared thing at a time. B has none. |

### 6.1 Overview in plain words

Project B is written in a "catch it and carry on" style. It has 91 `except` handlers in 90 `try` statements, and none of them is a bare `except:` (RAN (me), `scripts/try_inventory.py`, output `out/inv.tsv` and `out/inv.err`; the count matches DC P-02). The three long jobs - scanning, processing and extraction - each run in a worker thread, and each worker catches every error and reports it to the window, which shows a message box (READ: `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:39-41`, `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:38-40`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:39-41`; boxes at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:318-322`, `:412-415`, `:563-565`). Inside the jobs, errors are contained at the level of one file, one client or one report, so one bad item rarely stops the batch.

The other side of this style is that many problems are only written to the program log file, which the user rarely opens, or are swallowed completely, and the job still ends with a success message. Section 7 lists where that hides wrong results. This section lists what B does handle.

| A second job of the same kind while one is running | Refused (a scan while a scan runs, processing while processing runs, extraction while extraction runs) - silently, see B-G71 and B-G74. | `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:59-61`; `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:259-261`; `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:142-144` | RAN (LT §6.2; MW e17) |
| The same file name already open in the Step 4 Excel | The second open attempt closes same-named workbooks in that Excel without saving, then retries (see B-G63 for the risk). | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:691-699` | READ |
| "Skip refresh" ticked and earlier refreshed copies exist | The newest one (by modification time) is re-used instead of refreshing again (see B-G7 for the risk). | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:100-111` | RAN (me r5 skip_reuses_failed_copy; LT §4.8) |
| The same source folder chosen again | Not added twice to the recent list. | `models/cache_manager.py:48` | RAN (LT §5.2 #05) |
| Importing the old v3 settings more than once | A marker file `.migrated` stops a second import. | `models/cache_manager.py:99-102`, `:127` | RAN (LT §5.2 #39) |
| State written as full name or as its code | "Delhi" and "DL" give the same client key, so their files join one client (whether that is wanted is for the author; Section 7, B-G16). [GST RULE] ⚠ | `core/file_parser.py:261-262`; `utils/helpers.py:485-511` | RAN (me r1 part 2; LT §6.2) |

#### 6.2.6 Null, blank and zero values

| Edge case | What B does | Where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refresh check cell BB2 empty, only spaces, or 0 | Counted as a failed refresh ("Cell BB2 is empty" / "is blank" / "contains 0"). [GST RULE] ⚠ (cell BB2, B-R71) | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:607-623` | RAN (me t4 and r5; LT §4.9) |
| Extracted value None or empty text | Written as "Missing" in the consolidated report. | `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:141-142` | RAN (me r3; LT §4.5, §4.10) |
| Extracted value 0 | Kept as 0 (not "Missing"); the "#,##0.00" number format is applied only to non-zero numbers. [GST RULE] (display) | `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:149-150` | RAN (me r3 B_types; LT §4.10) |
| Blank operand in a calculated column | Counted as 0; divide by 0 gives "Div/0"; non-numeric text gives "Error". No configured column uses calculations today (dead in practice, B-R84). | `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:176-206` | RAN (LT §4.10) |
| `settings.json` containing `null` | Defaults, no warning. | `models/cache_manager.py:59-62` | RAN (LT §5.2 #12) |
| Max length 0 or negative passed to the organiser | Replaced by 35 (but see B-G24: the screen turns a migrated 0 into 15 before the organiser sees it). | `core/file_organizer.py:42` | READ |

#### 6.2.7 Other defensive measures

| Measure | Where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Source files are only read and copied - never moved, renamed, changed or deleted. | `core/file_organizer.py:273`; `utils/helpers.py:169` | RAN (me r2: source fingerprints unchanged; LT §6.4: identical SHA-256 fingerprints - a short fingerprint of a file's bytes that changes if one byte changes - before and after six runs) |
| Templates are copied before anything is written; the template file itself is never changed. | `core/excel_handler.py:124`, `:228` | READ (XL §6.1) |
| Step 4 refreshes a time-stamped copy, never the report made in Step 3. | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:91-94`, `:118-124` | RAN (me r5: only copies were refreshed; LT §4.4: original checksums unchanged) |
| A copy whose size differs from the source is deleted and the file fails. | `utils/helpers.py:171-178` | READ |
| Workers never touch screen elements; all messages go through Qt signals, which run in the window's own thread. | all three controllers | RAN (DC T4b; MW e3) |
| Each Excel function that runs in a worker thread starts COM with `CoInitialize()` and closes it with `CoUninitialize()`; Excel is quit in a `finally` block (code that runs whether or not an error happened). (The author's Standard 12 points that are not met are in Section 7: B-G38, B-G63, B-G77.) | `core/excel_handler.py:107`, `:195-217`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:171`, `:345-366`, `:484`, `:569-587` | READ |
| The Windows-only Explorer call is guarded by a platform check and a `try`. | `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:404-410` | READ |
| No network library is used and no password or token is stored anywhere. | whole code base | RAN (DO R97: grep for network modules found none) |
| Errors reach the user in three ways: message boxes for whole-job failures, coloured lines in the screen logs for per-client and per-report failures, and the program log for everything. | see 6.3 | READ |

#### 6.2.8 What B's README claims about safety, and what the code does

README.md (unchanged since d674386, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) describes the v3 Tkinter program; it is a source of intent, not of truth. Where it claims defensive behaviour, the code disagrees as follows (DO §2; every row re-checked in the code for this section, READ unless stated).

| README claim (line) | What the code does |
|---|---|
| "All file operations use temporary files and verification steps" (README.md:7, 42, 260) | No temporary file is used anywhere. `core/excel_handler.py:52-53` creates an empty folder `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp` that is never used. Reports are made by copying the template straight to the final name (`core/excel_handler.py:124`, `:228`); copies go straight to their destination (`utils/helpers.py:169`). |
| "Files are verified before finalization" / "Multiple verification steps" (README.md:43, 261, 310) | Copies: sizes compared (`utils/helpers.py:172-178`). Reports: "does the file exist" (`core/excel_handler.py:183-189`, `:258`). `EXCEL_SAFETY['verification_size_min']` (`utils/constants.py:222`) is never read. |
| "Clean saves: No VBA macros or external links preserved" (README.md:44, 262) | The openpyxl path keeps external links (`keep_links=True`, `core/excel_handler.py:231`); the Excel path saves the whole workbook as it is (`:173`). |
| "Original files are never modified" (README.md:47, 306) | True for source files and templates (RAN, me r2; LT §6.4). |
| "Backups created for existing files" (README.md:307) | Only in Fresh mode and only when the same Version folder is reused within the same minute, or when two names clean to the same name (`core/file_organizer.py:259-265`; RAN me r2, LT §6.3). |
| "Windows 10/11 (best), macOS, Linux" (README.md:52) | The window cannot start without pywin32, a Windows-only add-on (RAN me r6; B-G32). |
| "Resume: Continue interrupted processing" (README.md:145) | Resume re-copies everything into a new Version folder unless repeated within the same minute (RAN me r2; B-G13). |
| "Review variations tab for naming issues" (README.md:156) | There is no such tab; only the number of problem files is shown (B-G20). |
| "Processing seems frozen → large files take time" (README.md:279) | Processing runs in a worker thread; the progress bar moves once per client (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:89-90`). The screen logs themselves are the slow part (B-G56). |
| "Logs saved to gst_organizer.log" and "pq_extractor.log" (README.md:289-291) | One log, in the folder the program was started from (`main.py:20`), and none at all when started through `launch_extractor.py` (B-G44); `pq_extractor.log` belongs to the broken `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` (B-G45). |
| "Excel files must be closed during processing" (README.md:314) | Not enforced; Step 3 actively attaches to an open Excel (`core/excel_handler.py:111`; B-G63). |
| "Windows path limit of 260 characters applies" (README.md:317) | The code treats more than 218 characters as long (`core/excel_handler.py:293`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:668`); nothing shortens paths beforehand (B-G54). |
| "Extensive error checking", "Bulletproof Excel Handling" (README.md:28, 309) | Opinion; see the rating in 6.5 and the gaps in Section 7. |

### 6.3 Inventory of every try/except block

**How the inventory was made.** A small script read the syntax tree of every `.py` file of B (Python's built-in `ast` module, which reads code without running it) and listed every `except` handler with the line of its `try`, its function and what it catches (RAN (me): `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S67/scripts/try_inventory.py` on the copy `proj/`, output `out/inv.tsv`, counts in `out/inv.err`: "TOTAL try 90 handlers 91 finally 3"; the earlier interrupted run of this task made the same list, `try_inventory.tsv`). Every one of the 91 rows was then checked by reading the code (READ). The counts match the dead-code notes (DC P-02: 91 clauses, 0 bare `except:`, 15 whose body is only `pass`).

**Words used in the "Handling" column.** *Logged* = written to the program log `gst_organizer.log` (only when B was started with `main.py`; started with `launch_extractor.py`, no log file is written at all, B-G44). *Shown* = the user sees something on screen. *Swallowed* = the error is dropped with `pass`, nothing anywhere. *Re-raised* = passed on to the code that called this function. *Debug* = written at DEBUG level, which the program log does not record (it records INFO and above, `main.py:17`), so in effect swallowed. "Blue" = the message arrives in the Step 4 screen log as an information line even when it reports an error, because the refresh code never passes a level (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:30-37`; B-G71).

**Live or dead.** *Dead* = the code around it never runs in the app as it stands (the registry's DEAD markers).

### 6.4 How the edge-case handling came about (history)

- **Present from the first commit (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025):** the six file-name patterns, the 1 KB and signature checks (then inside `validate_excel_file`, which made the scan drop such files silently: `utils/helpers.py:210-247@47a1492` called from `find_excel_files` at `utils/helpers.py:260@47a1492`), the backup / skip / overwrite branches, the state-code fallback, the Excel retries for "Call was rejected by callee", the 218-character long-path handling, the error-dialog closer and the BB2 check (SH §1.13, §5; XL §9). The retries and long-path code are, in the shared-history reader's words, traces of problems met before 31-08-2025 (MEDIUM).
- **c258047 (07-02-2026, B only (after the split))** replaced all 26 bare `except:` clauses (commit message "Fixed all 26 bare except: clauses with specific exception types"; RAN `git show c258047`: 26 bare clauses removed; among all `except` lines the commit adds (replacements and handlers in its new files together) 34 are `except Exception`, the others `(TypeError, ValueError)`, `(KeyError, ValueError)`, `(OSError, ValueError)` and, in Tkinter files deleted the same day by a62d3cc, `tk.TclError`; confirmed: 0 bare clauses at HEAD, RAN) [corrected during verification - originally "by `except Exception:`" only], moved the three jobs into Qt worker threads - for the scan this was new (in v3 it ran on the window thread, `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:57-72@47a1492`), while processing and extraction had already run in plain Python threads (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:107@47a1492`, `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:741@47a1492`) [corrected during verification - originally "moved the three jobs into worker threads" without this distinction] - added the pythonw-safe console wrapper (`main.py:11-13`) and the settings / history files with their read protection. The same commit made pywin32 necessary for start-up (B-G32) and left the summary's problem list empty (B-G20).
- **7e09e5c (08-02-2026, B only (after the split))** moved the size and signature checks into the scanner (one `stat` and one 8-byte read per file), so too-small and fake files now appear in the problem list instead of vanishing; added the `~$` skip; and put a `try` around the scan-results display (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:245-316`; RAN `git log -S"Error in scan completion handler"` → 7e09e5c).
- **b0e7d0e (09-02-2026, B only (after the split))** added the Step 4 disk walk with its two `OSError` guards (including the `~$` skip in its "Refreshed" check, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:470`) and the Extraction_Log file with its `OSError` guard.

### 6.5 Rating of the defensive coding

**Overall rating: MODERATE** - B handles the common cases (missing or empty folders, badly named or non-Excel files, missing template files, missing sheets, empty cells, damaged JSON text, Excel being busy) without crashing, and it never changes the user's source files or templates. It is not ROBUST, because many of these "handled" cases end in a silent wrong result, and three areas are FRAGILE. Confidence HIGH (91 handlers read one by one; the main failure paths re-run for this section).

| Area | Rating | Why (evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| Scanning and recognising files (B-F6 to B-F9) | MODERATE | Bad, small, unreadable and unmatched files are caught one by one and listed (6.2.1, 6.2.2; RAN me r1, LT §6.2). But a file whose size cannot be read is dropped without trace, an unreachable network folder looks empty, hyphens and spelling variants silently split or merge clients, and the problem list is never shown (B-G16, B-G17, B-G20, B-G22, B-G46 to B-G48, B-G55). |
| Organising and copying (B-F12, B-F15) | MODERATE | Errors are contained per file and per client, sources are never touched (RAN me r2; LT §6.4), copies are size-checked. But partial copies stay under their final names, name collisions overwrite or skip silently, two clients can share one folder, and a client is "Success" whatever happened to its reports (B-G13, B-G14, B-G15, B-G19, B-G26). |
| Excel automation (Steps 3 and 4: B-F13, B-F14, B-F19, B-F20, B-F26) | FRAGILE | Retries and clean-up exist, but the refresh is typed by simulated keystrokes into whatever window has the focus, success is judged by one cell, the user's own Excel can be taken over and closed, nothing times out, and several of the author's Standard 12 "Excel through COM" rules are not met (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:844-878`; XL §3) (B-G5, B-G6, B-G38, B-G39, B-G61, B-G62, B-G63). |
| Consolidated extraction report (B-F22, B-F23) | FRAGILE | Missing sheets and empty cells give "Missing" instead of crashing, but 9 of 22 columns can carry another cell's figure, a failed check hides figures that were read, and one unusual cell value loses the whole workbook (RAN me r3; B-G1, B-G10, B-G11, B-G43). |
| Start-up, settings and history (B-F1, B-F2, B-F27, B-F32) | FRAGILE | Damaged JSON *text* is survived, but a missing Windows add-on, a wrong value type, a wrong file shape or an unwritable start folder stops the program with, at most, a console message, and any error in a window handler ends the program (RAN me r4, r6, r7; B-G32 to B-G37, B-G44). |
| Threads and job control (B-F16, B-F24, B-F34) | MODERATE | Workers never touch the screen (RAN DC T4b, MW e3) and duplicate jobs of the same kind are refused; but jobs of different kinds can run together, closing the window does not stop them, Stop works only between items and nothing times out (RAN MW e5, e11, e13; B-G39, B-G40, B-G41, B-G74). |

## SECTION 7: EDGE CASES NOT HANDLED (GAPS AND VULNERABILITIES)

### 7.0 How to read this section

Each gap has an ID (B-G1 … B-G82), the place in the code, what happens, how the user notices (or does not), a severity, the evidence and the related registry IDs. 7.7 is the silent-bug scan the audit method asks for (closures, mutable defaults, off-by-one and so on); 7.8 runs the "what would break if…" scenarios for every major feature and points back to these IDs; 7.10 lists all IDs in one table. Evidence words, note names and the [GST RULE] / ⚠ markers are explained in 6.0.

**Severity scale used here.**
- **HIGH** - can silently produce wrong figures or wrong files, lose the user's work, damage a workbook, act on other programs, or stop normal use, in situations that happen in ordinary office work.
- **MEDIUM** - wrong, misleading or failed output in plausible but less common situations, or a significant obstacle the user can work around.
- **LOW** - cosmetic, rare, latent (needs a configuration change to bite) or only a maintenance trap.

Severity describes the technical consequence. For anything tagged [GST RULE], only the mechanism is described: whether the rule itself is right is the author's decision, and "which cell is right" is always the author's call.

### 7.1 Missing validations that could silently corrupt data

#### B-G1 - The consolidated Step 4 workbook fills 9 of its 22 figure columns from a cell other than the one its configuration names [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:125-138` (the look-up), fed by `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:536-539` (each value stored under its field name and its bare cell address) and `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:255-278` (field names built as "<output sheet>_<output column>" with spaces turned into "_"); the three affected output sheets are configured at `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:155-228`.
- **What happens:** for each output column the consolidator first takes the FIRST extracted field whose name merely CONTAINS the column title (`:130-133`), even if that value is empty, and uses the exact field name only if the result is None (`:136-138`). Titles with a space ("Diff IGST", "IGST Diff", "Taxable Value", "Table 6J Match" ⚠) never match an underscore field name and fall through to the exact name, as configured. The one-word titles "IGST", "CGST", "SGST" of the output sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" match `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST/CGST/SGST` first, because "GSTR-3B Difference" is the first group in the configuration. Those 9 cells therefore show the values read from `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15` ⚠ instead of their configured cells `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1`, `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1` ⚠ (B-R79, B-R80, B-R81, B-R83). Two more details: the figure written depends on the ORDER of the extracted data (with the same data in reverse order, six columns showed the `ExtraInGSTR2B` cells instead); and if the Diff GSTR-3B cell holds an empty TEXT (''), the exact-name fallback is skipped too and the column shows "Missing" although its own cell has a value (only None triggers the fallback).
- **How the user sees it:** not at all. The workbook looks complete; the three sheets repeat the GSTR-3B difference figures client by client.
- **Severity:** HIGH (silent figures taken from cells other than the configured ones, in a delivered workbook).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r3, marker values that name their own source cell: "as_configured 13 of 22", the 9 differences listed one by one; reversed order: 16 of 22, the 6 differences come from `ExtraInGSTR2B`); RAN (me t1: empty text in J15 → "Missing" in the IMS Reco IGST column; None in J15 → the configured `IMS_Reco!AA1` appears); also RAN by LT §4.6, DC T3, XL E5, OF t7 and the registry's check1.py.
- **Related:** B-F23, B-R73 to B-R83. The look-up dates from edac6a3 and the one-word titles from 47a1492 (both shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), so project A may carry the same defect (comparison later). Which cell should feed each column is the author's call; the code simply does not do what its own configuration says.

#### B-G2 - Links cells for file types a client does not have keep whatever the template holds [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:161-163` (Excel path) and `:248-250` (openpyxl path): `if value:` skips empty values; `prepare_template_data` sets '' for a missing type (`:565-566`, `:576-577`, `:587-588`, `:599-600`, `:610-611`, `:621-622`).
- **What happens:** for a client without, say, an IMS Reco file, cells B10/B11 ⚠ of the ITC report's Links sheet are not touched (B-R54, B-R55), so any path or file name saved in the template - for example from the client used to build the template - stays, and the template's queries would read THAT file.
- **How the user sees it:** Step 2 shows the client as "Missing n files", but the report is built anyway ("✅ Success") and may carry another client's data in that block.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH (depends on what the real templates hold in those cells; the templates are not in the repository).
- **Evidence:** RAN (XL E7 and CU, openpyxl stand-in: a template whose B10/B11 held values kept them); READ (Excel path).
- **Also (Section 3, B-F13 and B-F14 traces, RAN):** every processed client always gets both an ITC and a Sales report, even with none of that report's inputs (B-R50) [GST RULE] - for example a client whose only files are GSTR-3B exports still gets a Sales report in which no Links cell is written at all (`core/excel_handler.py:590-622` writes only empty values, which `:162` skips) - and each such report is counted as created ("✅ Success"). Which reports a client should get is the author's call.
- **Related:** B-F13, B-F14, B-R50, B-R54, B-R55, B-R56. Shared - before the split (edac6a3). Question Q2 in 7.11.

#### B-G3 - Only the first file of each type is written into the Links sheet; further files of that type are copied but never linked [GST RULE]

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:561-563`, `:572-574`, `:583-585` (ITC), `:595-597`, `:606-608`, `:617-619` (Sales): always `files[0]`; the order is the scan order, sorted by full path (`utils/helpers.py:262`).
- **What happens:** a client with two GSTR-2B Reco files (for example two half-years), two Sales files, or two Annual Reports gets the remark "Multiple …" on Step 2 (B-R25), both files are copied, but only the alphabetically first one is named in the report. For GSTR-3B only the folder is written (B2), so what the template reads there depends on its own queries (B-G29).
- **How the user sees it:** Step 2 shows "Has duplicates" in red-orange; nothing says which file the report will use.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (LT §6.2: "Multiple GSTR-2B Reco (2 files)" for a client whose report then links one file only, CU).
- **Related:** B-F13, B-F14, B-R25, B-R56. Shared - before the split (edac6a3). Question Q3.

#### B-G4 - A template without a `Links` sheet produces no error

- **Where:** Excel path `core/excel_handler.py:142-153` (falls back to any sheet containing "link", else ADDS a new `Links` sheet), success decided by `:183-189`; openpyxl path `:244-258` (writes nothing, returns True).
- **What happens:** the report is saved and counted as created. On the Excel path the paths are written into a new, empty sheet the template's queries never read; on the openpyxl path nothing is written at all. A sheet called, for example, "Hyperlinks" would be filled instead of the real one. Nothing checks the template before processing (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:353-358` only checks that the path exists).
- **How the user sees it:** "✅ Success: ITC_Report_….xlsx"; the reason ("Links sheet not found! Creating one...") is only in the log file.
- **Severity:** HIGH (every report of the run is useless, reported as success).
- **Evidence:** RAN (DO R42, openpyxl path: a Sales template without Links gave "✅ Success"); READ (Excel path).
- **Related:** B-F13, B-F14, B-R53, B-R59. Shared - before the split (edac6a3).

#### B-G5 - A failed report leaves the unfilled template copy under the report's normal name; Step 4 later treats it as a report

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:124` copies the template to the final report path before Excel opens it at `:129`; the openpyxl path does the same at `:228`. On failure nothing deletes the copy (`:191-193`, `:260-262`).
- **What happens:** if Excel fails after the copy (cannot open the copy, cannot add a missing Links sheet, cannot save, or Excel dies), `ITC_Report_<client>_<code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` stays in the Version folder with the template's original Links values. Step 4 lists the version as having an ITC report (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:461-462`) and refreshes it. [Corrected during verification - "a cell write raises" had been listed as a cause; a failed cell write is caught cell by cell (`core/excel_handler.py:166`, #4 in 6.3), the report is still saved and counted as created, so that case leaves a partly filled report, not a failed one.]
- **How the user sees it:** a red "❌ Failed to create ITC report" in the Step 3 log (without a reason), but the client is "Success" (B-G19) and the file looks normal on disk.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (XL E3b, fake COM: "output file left on disk: True"); READ.
- **Related:** B-F13, B-F14, B-F18, B-R52. Shared - before the split (edac6a3).

#### B-G6 - A refresh cannot be confirmed: key presses, fixed waits, one test cell, and the copy is saved whatever happened [GST RULE] ⚠ (cell BB2)

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:213-249` (bring Excel forward, press Alt+A, R, A ⚠), `:253-298` (fixed waits and dialog checks), `:300-330` (BB2 check, save first), `:589-636` (`_validate_refresh`).
- **What happens:** there is no `RefreshAll`, no `BackgroundQuery = False`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` and no check that a connection is still refreshing anywhere in B (READ, grep; XL §2). The time from the last key press to the save is fixed: wait time + up to 5 s of dialog checks + max(10, wait time) s (25 s at the default 10 s; B-R68). The only proof of success is that `Info!BB2` ⚠ is not empty, not "0"/"0.0" and not an error text (B-R71, described only). A value already in the file - left in the template, or from an earlier refresh - passes, and so does another client's name. The workbook is saved (`:305`) BEFORE the check result is used (`:310-313`), so a copy whose check failed, or whose refresh showed an error dialog, is still saved under the refreshed name.
- **How the user sees it:** a slow query, a refresh that never started (keys landed elsewhere, B-G62; non-English key tips, B-G51) or a partial refresh is reported "OK" / ✓ with old figures whenever BB2 already held a value.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r5, recording stand-ins: with BB2 empty the result was "Refresh validation failed: Cell BB2 is empty" and the copy was still saved, `saves: 1`; me t4: BB2 holding another client's name → "Validated - Client Name: <Client B>"; also RAN by the Section 3 writer, B-F20 Scenario A (t24b): the stand-in performed no refresh at all, yet B logged "✅ Refresh completed successfully" and "Validated - Client Name: …" because BB2 already held a value - cited during self-review at the Section 3 writer's request); READ for the waits. The author's Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`) records, as tested, that a save during an unfinished refresh stored the old data; this is a technical comparison, not a recommendation.
- **Related:** B-F19, B-F20, B-R66 to B-R71. Shared - before the split (edac6a3; configurable wait from bd176bf).

#### B-G7 - "Skip refresh" re-uses any earlier refreshed copy as a success, and the Step 4 "Refreshed" status only means "such a file exists"

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:96-111` (skip branch: newest `<stem>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` by date, status success "Skipped - Using existing refreshed file"); `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:466-479` (status "Refreshed (dd/mm/yy HH:MM)" if any `*_Refreshed*` file is in the version folder).
- **What happens:** a refreshed copy left by a FAILED refresh (B-G6), or the unfilled copy of B-G5 refreshed later, is re-used with "success" on the next Skip-refresh run. Such a copy exists even when Excel never started: the copy is made (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:120`) before Excel is asked for (`:174`), so with no Excel installed an unrefreshed `<stem>_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` is left, the tree then shows "Refreshed", and Skip refresh re-uses it with success and ✓ figures (RAN Appendix X1 S4 "no_excel" and "skip_after_failed") [added during self-review from the Appendix X1 writer's flag; confirmed by READ of `report_processor.py:117-124, 170-174`]; its figures then appear with ✓ in the consolidated workbook. The tree shows green "Refreshed" for the same reason; any unrelated file with "_Refreshed" in its name also counts, and one refreshed ITC copy marks the whole version as refreshed.
- **How the user sees it:** the first run shows FAIL for that report; a later Skip-refresh run shows OK with the stale or partial figures.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r5 skip_reuses_failed_copy: `{'success': True, 'validation_message': 'Skipped - Using existing refreshed file'}`, extraction read the old copy); RAN (MW e6b, e9: "Refreshed" after failed refreshes; OF t8: unrelated file counted).
- **Related:** B-F18, B-F21, B-R63, B-R136. Skip option and its re-use branch shared - before the split (already in edac6a3: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:76-93@edac6a3`, tick box `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:189-198@edac6a3`); tree status B only (after the split) (b0e7d0e). [Corrected during verification - originally dated the Skip option to bd176bf; RAN `git log -S"skip_refresh"` → first in edac6a3; bd176bf added the wait-time and suffix options.]

#### B-G8 - The report search pattern also matches B's own refreshed copies, so a later run may refresh a copy of a copy

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:76-77` (`glob("ITC_Report_*.xlsx")`), `:89` (`report_files[0]`, unsorted); the copies keep the prefix (`:94`). The Step 4 tree uses the same pattern (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:461-462`), so a version holding only refreshed copies still counts as "has a report".
- **What happens:** whichever matching file the folder listing returns first is treated as the original. When a refreshed copy comes first, B copies and refreshes it again (`…_Refreshed_201026_0900_Refreshed_231026_1138.xlsx`), and with Skip refresh the search for `<stem>_Refreshed_*` then finds nothing and a new refresh runs.
- **How the user sees it:** extra double-suffixed files in the version folder; figures from a copy of an older refresh.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (HIGH on file systems that do not list in name order; on a local Windows NTFS disk the original normally comes first, because "." sorts before "_" - MEDIUM, not run on Windows; network shares may differ).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r5 copy_listed_first, listing order forced: original = the old copy, a copy of the copy was made and extracted); RAN on this Linux disk without forcing (LT §4.7: two of three clients; DC T6; XL E6).
- **Related:** B-F19, B-F21, B-R61. Shared - before the split (edac6a3).

#### B-G9 - A changed "File suffix" breaks Skip refresh and the "Refreshed" status; an empty suffix fails; a suffix without {timestamp} overwrites

- **Where:** the copy's name uses the screen's suffix (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:92-94`), but Skip refresh searches only `<stem>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` (`:102`) and the tree only `*_Refreshed*` (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:468`); the suffix box is free text (`gui/views/extraction_view.py:134-138`), not checked.
- **What happens:** with any suffix that does not contain "_Refreshed", Skip refresh never finds the earlier copy and refreshes again, and the tree always shows "Pending". An empty suffix makes the copy name equal the original: Python refuses ("are the same file") and the report fails. A suffix without "{timestamp}" gives the same copy name every time, so each run silently overwrites the previous copy. Characters Windows forbids in file names (`\ / : * ? " < > |`) are not rejected.
- **How the user sees it:** "Pending" that never turns green; refreshes that "Skip refresh" should have skipped; a FAIL with an unexplained "same file" message in the log file.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r5 custom_suffix_skip, empty_suffix, suffix_without_timestamp; LT §4.8; MW e6b).
- **Related:** B-F21, B-R62, B-R63, B-R65. Suffix option shared - before the split (bd176bf); tree status B only (after the split) (b0e7d0e). Question Q12.

The Summary sheet's "ITC Reports Processed x/n" counts refresh successes, not reports with figures (B-R90).

#### B-G11 - Unusual cell values are written into the consolidated workbook unchecked [GST RULE] (display)

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:141-150`; values come straight from Excel's `.Value` (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:535`).
- **What happens:** through COM an Excel error cell (#N/A, #DIV/0!) usually arrives as a large negative whole number, not as text (MEDIUM, from knowledge of pywin32; not runnable here). Such a number passes the BB2 check (B-G6) and is written as a figure with the "#,##0.00" format. Text that looks like a number ("12,345") stays text; a cell holding text that starts with "=" is written as a live formula; True is formatted as a number; a currency-formatted cell may arrive as a Decimal value and is written without the number format (MEDIUM).

#### B-G13 - "Resume" does not resume and "Re-Run" does not overwrite; when Resume does skip, the report links name a file that does not exist

- **Where:** `core/file_organizer.py:98-104` (every run makes a new `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder), `:158-179` (Re-Run/Resume re-use the newest run folder), `:259-270` (skip / backup / overwrite only when the copy already exists in THAT version folder), `:216-229` (cleaned names written back only after "Success"); mode texts `gui/views/setup_view.py:343-347`, `:510-512`.
- **What happens:** a Resume or Re-Run in a later minute copies every file again into a new version folder; every ticked client is processed in full in every mode. Only a repeat within the same clock minute meets existing copies: Resume then marks them "Skipped / File already exists" and keeps the ORIGINAL (uncleaned) file name in the scan data, so the Links cells written next name a file that is not in the folder (B-R57). The screen describes the modes in two places that disagree, and README.md:142-145 adds a third wording: the buttons say "Re-Run - Add new version folders…", "Resume - Continue previously interrupted processing"; the help card says "Re-Run: Overwrite existing", "Resume: Skip already processed"; the README says "Re-Run: Add new versions to existing structure", "Resume: Continue interrupted processing". [Corrected during verification - originally "the screen offers three different descriptions"; there are two on screen (READ `grep -n -i "resume\|re-run" gui/views/*.py`), the third is the README.] The run folder that Re-Run and Resume re-use is the one most recently MODIFIED (`core/file_organizer.py:165-169`), so saving any file into an older batch folder sends the next Re-Run or Resume into that older batch (RAN, Section 3 B-F12 trace, run 7), while Step 4 picks its "latest" by name (B-G12).
- **How the user sees it:** after an interrupted run, Resume repeats all the work in a new version folder; the summary shows everything copied again.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r2: Resume at 10:05 after a run at 10:00 → new `Version-211026 1005`, files "Success"; Resume again at 10:05 → all "Skipped", names after the run still uncleaned, e.g. "GSTR-2B-Reco-Gamma Sample LLP-Tamil Nadu-Q1.xlsx" while the copy on disk is "GSTR-2B-Reco-Gamma_Sample_LLP-Tamil_Nadu-Q1.xlsx"); RAN (LT §6.3, DC T9, DO probe_resume).
- **Related:** B-F12, B-R38, B-R43, B-R44, B-R57. Logic shared - before the split (edac6a3); the screen texts B only (after the split) (c258047, 7e09e5c). Question Q4.

- **What happens:** the box looks inactive but its value cuts every client folder name; it does not limit the bracketed name it sits next to (B-R35). A v3 settings file holding 0 is copied as 0, shown as 15 (the box's minimum) and then used as 15 - the v3 program had replaced 0 by 35 (`gui/main_window.py:352-354@47a1492`).
  Two more defects of the same one-time import (B-F2), added during verification from the Section 3 B-F2 trace and re-run:
  - **Writer and reader disagree on the recent-folder key** (the kind of mismatch the audit method's step 4 asks for): the v3 program wrote its recent source folders under `recent_folders` (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:34@47a1492` and `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:43@47a1492`), but B's import reads `recent_source_folders` (`models/cache_manager.py:122`), so the old list is never carried over; only the current source folder is put into the new list by `save_settings` (`:47-52`). This needs `settings.json` itself to be unwritable while its folder is writable (for example a read-only or locked `settings.json`, or a folder of that name); if the whole folder is unwritable, `touch()` fails too, the error reaches handler #42 and the import is retried at the next start (READ, HIGH).

Import defects: RAN (verifier, `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S67/scripts/v1_migration.py` → `out/v1_migration.txt`: an old file holding `recent_folders` `['/old/src', '/old/src2']` gave `recent_source_folders` `['/old/src']` only; with a folder where `settings.json` should be, the log said "ERROR: Failed to save settings.json …" and then "INFO: Migrated settings from old cache file", `marker_set: true`, settings "NOT WRITTEN"; the same result as me r4 migrate_settings_unwritable; Section 3, B-F2 trace).

### 7.2 Error conditions that would crash the program or stop a whole run

#### B-G32 - Without pywin32 the window cannot start at all, although the dependency file leaves pywin32 out and the error message recommends the wrong command

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` imports `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con` and `win32gui` with no guard; it is loaded at start-up through `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10` ← `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:27` (and `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4`, `gui/__init__.py:7`, so importing ANY screen module needs pywin32). `requirements.txt:13-14` has "# pywin32>=306" commented out; `main.py:49-54` advises "pip install PyQt5 openpyxl". `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` and `utils/helpers.py:473-483` guard the same imports - an inconsistent pattern.
- **What happens:** on any PC without pywin32 - including a Windows PC set up with `pip install -r requirements.txt` (MEDIUM: inferred from the same import chain, not run on Windows) - the program stops before the window opens. Scanning and organising do not need Excel, but cannot be reached either. The openpyxl fallback in `core/excel_handler.py:219-262` is therefore unreachable through the app (B-R97); if it is ever reached (for example once the import is made optional), its save drops the templates' Power Query and also any shapes drawn on a template sheet, such as text boxes and buttons, while reporting success (RAN Appendix X1.4.3 F1 and F5; F5 added during the completeness check; whether the real templates have shapes is NOT SURE). Nothing at start-up checks the Python version, the operating system or that Excel is installed, and nothing offers to install a missing package (READ `main.py:1-63`; Section 3 B-F1 trace): a PC with pywin32 but without Excel opens the window, and only Step 3 / Step 4 fail, report by report, with "Failed to create" or "FAIL" (B-G71).
- **How the user sees it:** from a console: "Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'", the wrong advice, exit code 1. Without a console: nothing (B-G34).
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r6a: exactly those three lines, exit 1; `launch_extractor.py`: "Failed to launch: No module named 'pythoncom'"; LT §9.1; XL E1; DC T1).
- **Related:** B-F1, B-F30, B-R124, B-R125. Made by c258047 (B only (after the split)), which put the extractor into the main window; at the split point (47a1492) the organiser started without pywin32 (XL §4.2).

#### B-G33 - A start folder in which the log file cannot be created stops the program before any message

- **Where:** `main.py:16-23` - `logging.FileHandler('gst_organizer.log')` runs when `main.py` is loaded, outside the `try` in `main()` (`:34`).
- **What happens:** started from a folder that is read-only (for example a protected shared folder) or where a folder of that name exists, Python stops with a traceback (a raw error listing) before `main()` runs.
- **How the user sees it:** a Python error listing in the console, or nothing under pythonw.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r6b: with a FOLDER named `gst_organizer.log` in the start folder → `IsADirectoryError` traceback from `main.py:20`, exit 1; same as me t3 on 21-10-2026). A permission-denied folder could not be simulated here (the runs are made as an administrator account, which ignores file permissions); the path is the same `open` call (HIGH by reading).
- **Related:** B-F1, B-F32, B-R121. Shared - before the split (`main.py` set up logging at load time already at 47a1492).

#### B-G34 - Started without a console, every start-up failure is invisible; there is no error hook and no error file

- **Where:** `main.py:49-59` and `launch_extractor.py:22-24` only `print()`; no `sys.excepthook` or `threading.excepthook` anywhere (READ, grep: no hit).
- **What happens:** the author's Standard 13 starts apps with `pythonw.exe` and no console (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:951-963`), where `print()` shows nothing; Standard 13's `report_fatal_error` writes `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<App>\logs\error_*.txt` and shows a message box (`:995-1029`). B has neither, so a missing package (B-G32), a damaged settings file (B-G36) or an unwritable start folder (B-G33) makes the program simply not appear. The only trace is a line in `gst_organizer.log` in whatever folder was current - and not even that via `launch_extractor.py` (B-G44).
- **How the user sees it:** double-click, nothing happens.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (me r6a shows the messages go to the console only).
- **Related:** B-F1, B-F30, B-R125, B-R127. Shared - before the split (v3 printed too) and B only (after the split) (c258047 rewrote `main.py` without adding a hook).

#### B-G35 - Any error inside a window handler ends the whole program (exit code 134), without saving

- **Where:** no `sys.excepthook`; PyQt5 5.15 aborts the program when a Python error escapes a slot or an overridden Qt method. Unprotected handlers: `_on_processing_completed` (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:373-410`, except the Explorer call), `_on_extraction_completed` (`:549-561`), `_save_settings` (`:210-214`), `_toggle_dark_mode` (`:594-597`), `closeEvent` (`:601-608`), `_on_dry_run` (`:326-343`), `_on_start_processing` (`:345-371`), `_populate_extraction_from_disk` (`:419-504`, only `OSError` caught), `_on_scan_requested` (`:218-232`, which also calls `_save_settings` at `:227`) and `_on_start_extraction` (`:506-547`) [the last two added during verification, READ].
- **What happens:** for example a `session_state.json` that is not a JSON object (B-G36) makes `CacheManager.save_settings` raise inside `_save_settings`; switching dark mode or closing the window then kills the program at once. Closing that way also skips saving the settings and the session.
- **How the user sees it:** the window vanishes; with a console a traceback is printed first.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (rare trigger, total effect).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r7 dark_toggle_with_bad_session and close_with_bad_session: traceback from `models/cache_manager.py:47`, exit 134 both times; MW e10, VW t3: any slot error → exit 134).
- **Related:** B-F1, B-F27, B-F28, B-R125. B only (after the split) (c258047).

#### B-G36 - Settings, session or history files of the wrong shape or type stop the start, or crash the next save

- **Where:** `models/cache_manager.py:57-62` (a JSON list or text in `settings.json` reaches `AppSettings.from_dict`, which calls `.items()`), `models/app_state.py:41-46` (no type checks), `models/cache_manager.py:46-52` (session file assumed to be an object with a list), `models/run_history.py:118-126` and `:44-71` (inner types not checked).
- **What happens:**
  - `settings.json` = `[1, 2]` or `"hello"` → `AttributeError` while the window is built → the program does not start ("Critical error").
  - A wrong value type, for example `"pq_wait_time": "10"` (text instead of a number) or `"dark_mode": "yes"` → accepted by the loader, then `QSpinBox.setValue` / `setChecked` raises while the window is built → no start.
  - `client_name_max_length` as text stops the start in the same way (`gui/views/setup_view.py:647`); the organiser itself would also fail on such a value (`TypeError` at `core/file_organizer.py:42`, RAN me r2), but processing always reads the screen's box.
  - `session_state.json` = `[]`, or `recent_source_folders` as text → `save_settings` raises → abort when called from a window handler (B-G35); also at every scan (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:227`).
  - `run_history.json` = `{"runs": 5}` → loaded without complaint; the next `add_run` raises inside `_on_processing_completed` → abort after a whole processing run, before the history is saved.
  Only damaged JSON *text* is survived (defaults, and the file is overwritten at the next save).
- **How the user sees it:** the program does not open, or vanishes after a run; the only remedy is to delete files in `~/.gst_organizer`, which nothing tells the user.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (needs a damaged or hand-edited file; effect total).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r4: settings_list, settings_text → `AttributeError`; settings_wrong_types → `'10'`, `'yes'`, `'abc'`, `'banana'` accepted as they are; session_is_list, session_recent_is_text, history_runs_is_number → `AttributeError`; me r7 bad_settings_type → "window NOT built: TypeError setValue(self, val: int): argument 1 has unexpected type 'str'"; LT §5.2 #07, #13-14, #17-20, #32-35; MW e7).
- **Related:** B-F2, B-F17, B-F27, B-R116, B-R117, B-R119. B only (after the split) (c258047).

#### B-G37 - A file or blocked path where the settings folder should be stops the start

- **Where:** `models/cache_manager.py:31-33` (`mkdir` of `~/.gst_organizer` in the constructor, called at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:42`).
- **What happens:** if `~/.gst_organizer` exists as a FILE, or the profile folder is not writable, `FileExistsError` / `PermissionError` stops the window being built.
- **How the user sees it:** "Critical error: …" in a console, nothing without one.
