## SECTION 8: DESIGN DECISIONS (INFERRED)

### 8.0 How to read this section

This section tries to answer "why was it built like this?" for project B (goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2, branch main, snapshot `b0e7d0e`, 09-02-2026, the PyQt5 window that calls itself "GST File Organizer v4.0"). The original chat history is lost, so every "why" below is an **inference** (a reasoned guess from the code, its comments, its names and its history), and each one carries a confidence level as the audit method asks:

- **HIGH** = clear from the code or from a commit message that matches the diff.
- **MEDIUM** = a reasonable inference from several clues.
- **LOW** = speculation from thin evidence. "Not sure - here is how to check" is used where nothing in the repository can settle it.

Every statement about the code cites `file:line` in project B at `b0e7d0e` (repository-relative). Old code is cited as `path:line@commit`. Each fact says how it was established: **READ** (I read the code) or **RAN** (code was executed on made-up data in a copy). "RAN (me)" means I ran it for this task, in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S89/` (scripts listed in 9.13); "RAN (verifier)" / "READ (verifier)" marks a check made by the verification pass of this section, in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S89/` (also listed in 9.13); "RAN (XX)" means a working-note author ran it (abbreviations as in the registry: CU core/utils notes, PQ Power Query/models/start-up notes, MW main-window/controllers notes, VW views notes, DC dead-code/pattern notes, XL Excel-safety notes, OF outside-files notes, DO documents notes, LT live traces, SH shared history, H1/H2 B history parts 1/2). Excel-through-COM behaviour could not be run on this Linux machine; it is traced by reading.

History labels: the 12 commits `edac6a3` … `47a1492` are **shared - before the split on 30-10-2025**; `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`, `7e09e5c` and `b0e7d0e` are **B only (after the split)**. B has one branch, main (a second name in the local checkout, `claude/pensive-feynman-0mz1aa`, points at the same commit `b0e7d0e` and holds no extra work; it was created when this audit's copy was prepared - Section 12, "Branch awareness") [Corrected during self-review - originally stated "one branch, main" without the second name, but Section 12 ("Branch awareness") revealed a second ref at the same commit].

IDs: features B-F1 … B-F34 and rules B-R1 … B-R144 come from the registry (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_registry.md`); gaps B-G1 … B-G82 come from Section 7. **[GST RULE]** marks anything that decides a tax figure, a return / table / sheet / cell, a rate or threshold, rounding, a period, GSTIN / PAN / state-code logic, ITC or a due date; for these I only say what the code does, never whether it is right. **⚠** marks a value that can change over time (template cell positions, table numbers, state lists, package versions) so the author can check it.

Plain-English terms used in this section (each is also explained where it first matters):

- *Framework / library*: ready-made code a program builds on. *Window toolkit*: the library that draws windows and buttons (Tkinter, PyQt5, PySide6).
- *COM*: the Windows mechanism by which one program (here Python) remote-controls another (here Excel). *pywin32*: the Python add-on package that gives access to COM and to other Windows functions (its parts are called `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`).
- *Dispatch / DispatchEx / GetActiveObject*: three pywin32 ways of getting an Excel. `GetActiveObject` grabs an Excel that is already running (normally the user's own); `Dispatch` asks for "an Excel" and may be handed a running one; `DispatchEx` always starts a separate new Excel (what the author's Standard 12 asks for).
- *SendKeys / AppActivate*: Windows Script Host functions; `AppActivate` tries to bring a window to the front, `SendKeys` types keystrokes into whatever window has the keyboard focus, as if a person pressed them. *Key tips*: Excel's ribbon keyboard shortcuts (Alt, then letters).
- *Power Query*: Excel's built-in data-import feature; its queries live inside a workbook and are re-run by "Refresh All".
- *openpyxl*: a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel; when it saves an existing workbook it silently drops Power Query (Standard 12, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:827`).
- *Thread / worker thread*: a second line of work running at the same time, so the window does not freeze. *QThread*: Qt's thread object. *Signal / slot*: Qt's message from one object to a function in another.
- *Module / package*: a `.py` file / a folder of modules with an `__init__.py` file. *Re-export*: an `__init__.py` that imports names from its sub-modules so that other code could write `from utils import X`. *`__all__`*: the list of names a package offers that way. *Facade*: one object or function that hides several others behind a simple front.
- *Import guard*: wrapping an import in `try/except ImportError` or a platform check, so that a missing package or a different operating system does not stop the program.
- *Dataclass*: a Python class used mainly to hold named fields. *JSON*: a plain-text file format for settings.
- *Constant*: a value written once with a name (for example `FILE_PATTERNS`) instead of being typed wherever it is needed. *Magic value*: a value typed directly into the logic.
- *Glob*: a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`. *mtime*: a file's or folder's "last modified" time. *Stem*: a file name without its extension.

### 8.1 The main inferences at a glance

| # | Decision visible in the code | Inferred reason | Confidence | Where explained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Python, with Excel itself (through COM) for every workbook that holds Power Query, and openpyxl only for workbooks the program creates | openpyxl destroys Power Query when it saves; an earlier version "corrupted" templates | HIGH (Python), MEDIUM-HIGH (the corruption history) | 8.2.1, 8.2.3, 8.2.4 |
| 2 | Tkinter replaced by PyQt5 in one AI-assisted rewrite (`c258047`) | thread-safe screen updates, style sheets, an end to Tkinter work-arounds | MEDIUM-HIGH (what was gained); LOW (why PyQt5 rather than PySide6) | 8.2.2 |
| 3 | Two programs (organiser + Power Query extractor) merged into one four-tab window | the separate extractor never found the organiser's settings, and the user had to run two programs | MEDIUM-HIGH | 8.3.2 |
| 4 | The business core (`core/`, `utils/`, `power_query_extractor/`) was left almost untouched by the rewrite | protect the file-name, folder and cell rules that worked in real use | HIGH | 8.3.3 |
| 5 | Power Query is refreshed by typing Alt+A, R, A into a visible, maximised Excel, then waiting fixed times | a person's way of refreshing that "worked"; the code comment says Excel must stay visible "to avoid issues"; the method predates git | MEDIUM (that it was chosen because it worked); LOW (what failed before) | 8.4.1 |
| 6 | Step 3 attaches to an Excel the user already has open | speed and reuse; the plan to leave such an Excel open was never finished | MEDIUM (reason); HIGH (unfinished) | 8.4.2 |
| 7 | Reports are made at their final place; no temporary-file stage, although a temporary folder is still created | a temporary-file design existed or was planned before git and was dropped | MEDIUM | 8.4.3 |
| 8 | No folder-listing cache: Step 4 walks the target folder every time | a one-day experiment with a remembered list (run history) gave wrong rows, so the author went back to "what is on disk" | HIGH (history); MEDIUM-HIGH (preference) | 8.4.4 |
| 9 | Step 4 refreshes a time-stamped copy and never the Step 3 report | never damage the base report; allow re-runs | HIGH | 8.4.5 |
| 10 | Python only writes folder paths and file names into each template's "Links" sheet; the GST work happens in the template's Power Query | the reconciliation logic stays in Excel, where the consultant maintains and checks it | MEDIUM-HIGH | 8.4.8 |
| 11 | Long-path tricks (218-character limit, 8.3 short names, `\\?\` prefixes) | real failures with deep folders and long client names, met before git | HIGH (met in use) | 8.4.10 |
| 12 | Many retries and fixed sleeps around Excel | Excel refusing calls while busy ("Call was rejected by callee") | HIGH | 8.4.11 |
| 13 | Folder and file names stamped `DDMMYY HHMM` | keep every run, readable day-first dates | MEDIUM | 8.4.12 |
| 14 | Layers `models/`, `gui/views/`, `gui/controllers/`, `gui/theme/` added around the old core | a planned clean-up of the Tkinter "god object" (one object that everything called) | HIGH | 8.3.3 |
| 15 | Constants module, re-export `__init__.py` files and a central signal hub exist but are largely bypassed or unused | written in a sweep (partly AI-generated) and never connected | HIGH | 8.7.4, 8.8 |

### 8.2 Why this framework and these libraries

#### 8.2.1 Python

- **What the code shows.** Every program file is Python (38 `.py` files, 7,821 lines; `B_files.txt` gives 7,805 because it counts line breaks with `wc -l` and 16 of the files have none after their last line: `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_files.txt`; RAN (me) `compile_all.py` also counted 38) [Corrected during self-review - originally "7,805 lines", but Sections 1 and 2 (2.1) revealed that 7,805 is the `wc -l` count and the real number is 7,821; re-RAN: 38 files, 7,821 lines, 7,805 line breaks]. The project has been Python since the first commit `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), and compiled-file headers committed in `edac6a3` show the code was run with Python 3.12 and 3.13 between June and August 2025 (RAN (SH) §1.16).
- **Inference.** Python was the author's default from the start; the later Standard 12 makes this explicit ("Python is the default for every app", `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:819-823`). **HIGH.**

#### 8.2.2 The window toolkit: Tkinter until the split, PyQt5 since `c258047`

- **What the history shows.** The shared program (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`) used Tkinter (Python's built-in window toolkit). B's first own commit, `c258047` (07-02-2026, B only (after the split)), rewrote the whole screen layer in PyQt5 (a Python wrapper for the Qt 5 toolkit) and `a62d3cc` deleted the Tkinter files two minutes later (RAN (H1) `git show --stat`). `c258047`, `a62d3cc` and the fix `c21f788` all carry "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6" (READ, `git log`), so the rewrite was done in one AI-assisted session (HIGH).
- **Problems the old Tkinter code had to work around** (READ (SH) §1.3, §1.13, §0; READ (H1) Part 3):
  - buttons wired with `bind('<Button-1>')` instead of `command=` (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:115, 161, 199, 306, 318@47a1492`), with comments about "working mouse events" and "proper event binding" (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:20, 103@47a1492`) - such a button still fires when "disabled" [Corrected during verification - originally cited only `:20,103`, which are the two comments; the bindings themselves are at `:115` onwards; READ (verifier) `git show 47a1492:gui/tabs/setup_tab.py`];
  - a late-binding bug (a small inline function that reads a loop variable only later, so it sees the last value) introduced in `6237597` when worker-thread updates were wrapped in `root.after(0, lambda …)` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:36-52@6237597`);
  - a 212-line "recursive widget walker" to switch dark mode (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py@47a1492`);
  - a scan that froze the window (it ran on the window's own thread).
- **What the rewrite's message says it gained** (`c258047`, READ): "QThread-based background workers", "QSS stylesheet-based theming (replaces recursive widget-walking)" (QSS = Qt Style Sheets, CSS-like text that sets colours and fonts), "Signal/slot architecture replaces 305 self.app.xxx callback references".
- **Inference.** The move to Qt was made to get safe background work with screen updates, style sheets for the theme, and a cleaner structure - exactly the three things the Tkinter code struggled with. **MEDIUM-HIGH.**
- **Why PyQt5 and not PySide6 or Qt 6.** Nothing in the code or the messages says. **LOW**: a common default of the AI assistant at the time. Facts for the author (not a recommendation): PyQt5's licence is GPL v3 and its Qt library is LGPL v3 (RAN (me): `License:` fields of the downloaded wheels, 9.13); the newest PyQt5 build for Windows ships Qt 5.15.2 ⚠ (RAN (me), 9.1); Standard 12 names PySide6 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:833`).
- **The author still wanted the old look.** `7e09e5c` (08-02-2026, B only) restyled the new screens to look like v3: "Colorful card-based layout matching the original Tkinter UI" (`gui/views/setup_view.py:3`), "Color palette matching the old Tkinter UI" (`gui/theme/theme_manager.py:9`) (READ (H2)). **HIGH** that the visual layout of v3 was valued; the toolkit change was about mechanics, not looks.

#### 8.2.3 openpyxl - only for workbooks the program creates itself

- **What the code does.** openpyxl writes the processing summary (`core/excel_handler.py:308-346`, B-F15) and the consolidated extraction workbook (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:20-174`, B-F23) - both brand-new workbooks with no Power Query. The template copies are filled through Excel (COM) instead (`core/excel_handler.py:95-217`). openpyxl is used on a template copy only in the fallback `_create_report_openpyxl` (`core/excel_handler.py:219-262`), which logs "Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!" (`:224`) and cannot be reached through the window since `c258047` (B-R97, RAN (XL) E1).
- **Evidence of an earlier openpyxl-only version.** The file header says "WINDOWS VERSION - Uses Excel COM to preserve Power Query and all Excel features" (`core/excel_handler.py:2-3`); the README warns of "Excel file corruption - a common issue in earlier versions" (`README.md:5-7`) and lists "Excel corruption prevention" measures (`README.md:39-47`). RAN (XL) E2: B's own fallback, run on a synthetic workbook carrying a Power Query part, returned success and the saved copy had lost the query part (RAN (verifier) `scripts/pqdrop.py`: same result).
- **Inference.** A version before git made the reports with openpyxl, lost the templates' Power Query (the "corruption"), and the author moved report creation to Excel through COM, keeping openpyxl for new workbooks where nothing can be lost. **MEDIUM-HIGH.** This matches the author's later, tested rule in Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:827-828`).

#### 8.2.4 Excel through COM with pywin32

- **What the code does.** Three Excel sessions: Step 3 report filling (`core/excel_handler.py:95-217`), Step 4 refresh (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:165-366`) and Step 4 reading (`report_processor.py:478-587`). Windows-only window functions (`win32gui`, `win32con`) find and close error dialogs (`report_processor.py:368-476`).
- **Inference.** Only Excel can refresh Power Query and save a workbook without losing its queries, so COM is unavoidable for the templates. **HIGH.** How each session uses COM (and how far that is from Standard 12) is in 8.4.1, 8.4.2 and 8.4.6.

#### 8.2.5 lxml

- **What the code does.** `requirements.txt:10-11` lists `lxml>=4.9.0` as "Optional but recommended for better performance". No file imports it (RAN (me) import scan, 9.2). openpyxl uses it automatically when it is installed (RAN (me): `openpyxl.xml.LXML` is `True` with openpyxl 3.1.5 and lxml 6.1.3).
- **Inference.** Added for openpyxl speed. **HIGH** for the intent; whether it makes a measurable difference for B's small workbooks was not measured (not sure - check by timing the consolidated report with and without lxml installed).

### 8.3 Why the code is structured this way

#### 8.3.1 The layers at the snapshot

```text
main.py, launch_extractor.py                    entry points (start-up)
   └── gui/__init__.py  →  gui/pyqt_main_window.py   the window: wiring, plus some logic
         ├── gui/views/*.py          the four tabs (signals out, methods in)
         ├── gui/controllers/*.py    background jobs (QThread workers)
         │      ├── core/*.py + utils/*.py           v3 business core: scan, folders, copies, Links cells
         │      └── power_query_extractor/**         refresh, cell reading, consolidated workbook
         ├── models/*.py             settings, scan result, run history, JSON store (no Qt)
         └── gui/theme/*.py, gui/widgets/*.py        style sheets and two small widgets
```

READ (imports, RAN (me) `imports_out.txt`; RAN (verifier) `scripts/imports.py`): views import only PyQt5, `pathlib` (`gui/views/extraction_view.py:6`) and, from the program itself, only `gui.widgets.colored_section` (`gui/views/setup_view.py:14`, `gui/views/validation_view.py:12`) [Corrected during verification - originally "only PyQt5 and `gui.widgets.colored_section`"; the Step 4 view also imports the standard-library `pathlib`]; controllers import the core (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:10-14`, `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:8-9`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10-11`); `core/*` and `utils/*` import nothing from `gui/` or `models/`.

#### 8.3.2 Two programs merged into one window (`c258047`)

- **Before.** At the split there were two programs: the organiser (`python main.py`, Tkinter, three tabs) and a separate "Power Query Extractor" (`python launch_extractor.py`, its own Tkinter window `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py@47a1492`) (READ (SH) §10.2).
- **After.** One window with four tabs; `launch_extractor.py` now only opens that window on the fourth tab (`launch_extractor.py:17-18`).
- **Clues to the reason.** The old extractor looked for the organiser's saved settings in the wrong place (a file in the start folder instead of the home folder: `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:38-42` versus `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json`), so its promised "auto-loads target folder from cache" (`README.md:171`) never worked (READ (SH) §1.10, defect O1). The rewrite's message says "Unified two separate apps (main organizer + PQ Extractor) into one 4-tab window" and "Auto-populates extraction tab from processing results" (READ `c258047`).
- **Inference.** One workflow (Setup → Validation → Processing → Extract), one settings store, and Step 4 knowing what Step 3 produced. **MEDIUM-HIGH.**
- **Side effect, not intended (HIGH, RAN (me) 9.5).** The extractor's unguarded Windows-only import (`report_processor.py:11-15`), harmless while the extractor was a separate program, became part of the window's start-up, so the whole program now needs pywin32 to open (B-G32, B-R124).

#### 8.3.3 New layers around an untouched core

- **What changed and what did not.** `c258047` created `models/` ("Framework-agnostic state layer (dataclasses + persistence)"), `gui/views/`, `gui/controllers/` and `gui/theme/`. It did **not** touch `utils/constants.py` (file-name patterns, folder templates, Links-sheet cells, state codes) or `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py` (which report cells are read) - READ (H1) `git show --stat c258047`: "no regex, folder template, cell mapping, state-code table or extraction mapping changed in this commit". Neither did `7e09e5c` or `b0e7d0e` (READ (H2)). [GST RULE] content therefore dates from the shared commits (B-R5 to B-R11, B-R21, B-R54, B-R55, B-R73 to B-R81 ⚠).
- **The stated aim.** `models/app_state.py:1-4`: state "that was previously scattered across the Tkinter GSTOrganizerApp god object" (a *god object* is one object that every part of the program reaches into). `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:2-3`: "Thin QMainWindow that wires controllers to views. Replaces the old Tkinter GSTOrganizerApp god object."
- **Inference.** Keep the rules that had been proven in real use and rebuild only the screens and the plumbing around them. **HIGH.** Separating state (`models/`) from screens was meant to let the state be used without the window. RAN (me) `layer_imports.py`: with PyQt5 blocked, `models.app_state`, `models.run_history`, `models.cache_manager`, `core.*`, `utils.*`, `power_query_extractor.config.cell_mappings` and `power_query_extractor.core.data_consolidator` all import; `models.signals` does not (it needs PyQt5).

#### 8.3.4 Configuration kept in Python files

- **What the code does.** All business configuration is Python: `utils/constants.py` (patterns, folder names, Links cells, modes, state codes) and `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py`, whose docstring is a user manual ("Cell Mapping Configuration - MASTER VERSION … HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE", `cell_mappings.py:1-27`) with a commented example block to copy (`:229-241`) and a "DON'T EDIT BELOW THIS LINE" marker (`:255-257`). Only user choices (folders, options) are in JSON (`models/cache_manager.py:35`).
- **Inference.** The author edits the rules with an AI assistant directly in the code rather than through a settings screen; Python dictionaries also allow comments next to each rule. **MEDIUM.** Consequence: a change needs a restart (the derived tables are built once at import, `cell_mappings.py:264-278`), and a typing mistake in the file stops the program (not checked by any test - B has none).

#### 8.3.5 The "thin" window is not thin

- **What the code does.** `gui/pyqt_main_window.py` is 608 lines and holds logic of its own: the dry run (`:326-343`, B-F11), the scan-statistics text (`:244-316`, B-F7), the disk walk that builds the Step 4 tree (`:419-504`, B-F18), the tab dots (`:567-590`, B-F29) and the completion handling (`:373-415`).
- **History.** These were added by `7e09e5c` and `b0e7d0e` (READ (H2): "grows from 'wire views' into also owning the scan log text, statistics display, the disk scan for extraction and tab status").
- **Inference.** Quick features were placed where the data was at hand, so the window slowly became a new god object; its docstring ("Thin", `:2`) describes the plan of `c258047`, not the snapshot. **HIGH.** Effect: the disk walk runs on the window's own thread (B-G58).

#### 8.3.6 The Power Query package kept its own shape

`power_query_extractor/` still has the layout of the separate extractor (`config/`, `core/`, an empty `gui/` whose only module was deleted in `a62d3cc`, and the broken entry point `extractor_main.py`, B-F31). It uses relative imports (`from ..config.cell_mappings import …`, `report_processor.py:16`; `data_consolidator.py:11`) while most of the rest of B imports by top-level name (`from utils.constants import …`, `core/file_parser.py:13`); the other relative imports are in `models/cache_manager.py:11-12` (`from .app_state …`), `utils/helpers.py:491` and the package front files (`__init__.py`) [Corrected during verification - originally "the rest of B imports by top-level name"; READ (verifier) import scan]. **HIGH** that this is the leftover of the two-program era rather than a design choice for the snapshot.

### 8.4 Why some things are done in a complex way, and the likely domain reason

Each sub-section gives: what the code does (READ unless marked), the clues, the inference with its confidence, and what it costs today (cross-references to Section 7 gaps). None of this judges a GST rule.

#### 8.4.1 Power Query refreshed by keystrokes into a visible Excel (B-F19, B-R66 to B-R69)

**What the code does**, per report, in `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:165-366`:

1. `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` (`:171`), then `win32com.client.Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (`:174`) - not `DispatchEx`.
2. Up to five tries, two seconds apart, to set `Visible = True` with the comment "Keep it visible to avoid issues" (`:181`), `DisplayAlerts = False` (`:182`) and `WindowState = -4137` (maximised, `:183`); after five failures it carries on anyway (`:190`).
3. Opens the copy in up to three attempts, three seconds apart, as long as Excel answers "Call was rejected by callee" (any other error ends the open at once) (`:192-205`), then waits five seconds "to fully load" (`:207-211`, comment "Increased from 3 to 5").
4. Creates a `WScript.Shell` object (`:216`), tries three times to bring the Excel window to the front with `AppActivate(excel.Caption)` (`:218-230`), and sends `SendKeys("%a")` (Alt+A), `"r"`, `"a"` one second apart (`:236-249`, comments "Increased from 0.5"). These are Excel's ribbon key tips for Data → Refresh All → Refresh All (MEDIUM: depends on the Excel version and display language).
5. Waits the user's wait time (`:253-258`), checks five times for an error dialog (`:260-278`), waits `max(10, wait time)` more seconds (`:280-286`), checks once more (`:288-298`).
6. Checks cell Info!BB2 (`:300-301`, B-R71 ⚠), saves **whatever happened** (`:303-307`), closes with `SaveChanges=True` (`:316-319`), and in `finally` closes again, quits Excel and un-initialises COM (`:345-366`).

There is no `RefreshAll()`, no `BackgroundQuery = False`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()` and no check that a connection is still refreshing (READ; RAN (XL) grep: none of these names in any `.py` file).

**Clues to the reason.**

- The method is older than git. RAN (me): in the compiled copies committed with `edac6a3`, the older one of `report_processor` (Python 3.12, source dated 25-06-2025 by its header, RAN (SH) §1.16) contains the name `SendKeys` once and `RefreshAll` zero times; the Python 3.13 copy is the same (counts only; nothing else was read from those files). RAN (me) `git log -S`: no commit of B's history ever contained `RefreshAll`, `DispatchEx` or `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`. So if a COM refresh was ever tried, it was before 25-06-2025, and the reason it was dropped is lost.
- The only comment is "Keep it visible to avoid issues" (`:181`). A refresh that Excel runs in the background returns at once; saving straight away keeps the old data - the exact problem the author later tested and wrote down in Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`: a plain `RefreshAll()` followed at once by a save "stored the old 2 rows"). Power Query prompts (privacy levels, missing source, credentials) are also only answerable in a visible Excel.
- The waits were tuned by trial: a "WAIT 7 SECONDS AS REQUESTED" comment sat over a ten-second loop at `edac6a3`; `bd176bf` (shared) made the wait a user setting (5-60 s, now 5-120 s, `gui/views/extraction_view.py:126-128`) "with configurable wait time" (READ (SH) bd176bf).
- The rest of the refresh code is built around the keystroke method: the error-dialog closer (8.4.7) exists because a keystroke gives no return value and Excel's error boxes would otherwise block; the BB2 check exists because nothing else tells the program whether the queries ran.

**Inference.** The author automated what a person does by hand - open the report, press Data → Refresh All, wait, save - because that reliably updated the figures in the office's Excel, while a refresh started from code either returned before the queries finished or failed invisibly. **MEDIUM** for "chosen because it worked visibly"; **LOW** for any specific earlier failure (no surviving evidence). The domain reason for refreshing at all is **HIGH**: each client's report template reads that client's organised files through the Links cells (8.4.8), so its Power Query must be re-run per client before the check figures can be read.

**Constraint any change must respect (technical, for Section 11).** The refresh must really have finished before the save; Standard 12 records that a plain `RefreshAll()` followed at once by a save keeps stale data (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`). The author's tested sequence is in Standard 12 itself; this audit does not choose between methods.

**What it costs today.** B-G6 (refresh cannot be confirmed; copy saved whatever happened), B-G51 (depends on Excel version, language, an unlocked screen and nobody touching the PC), B-G57 (about 39 seconds per report at the default wait), B-G61 and B-G62 (dialog clicking and keystrokes can reach other programs), B-G39 (nothing times out).

#### 8.4.2 Attaching to an Excel that is already running (B-R96; Step 4: B-R66, B-R101)

**What the code does.**

- Step 3 (making the reports, `core/excel_handler.py:95-217`): first `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` - attach to an Excel the user already has open, logging "Using existing Excel instance" (`:110-112`) - and only if that fails `Dispatch` (`:113-115`). It then sets `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` on that Excel (`:118-120`). In `finally` it sets `ScreenUpdating` and `DisplayAlerts` back to True (`:204-205`) and, under the comment "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:206`), calls `Quit()` when `self.excel_app is None` (`:207-211`). `self.excel_app` is set to `None` in `__init__` (`:55`) and never assigned anywhere (READ; DC D-29), so `Quit()` always runs - also on the user's own Excel (RAN (XL) E3 with stand-in COM objects: the user's instance was hidden and told to quit while the user's workbook was open in it).
- Both open routines first look for a workbook with the same full path already open in that Excel and reuse it (`core/excel_handler.py:273-277`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:657-660`); the Step 4 routine's second attempt closes every workbook with the same file name without saving (`report_processor.py:692-699`).
- Step 4 uses `Dispatch` for both its sessions (`report_processor.py:174, 487`), which may also be handed a running Excel (MEDIUM; not testable here).

**Clues.** The never-assigned `self.excel_app`, the comment at `:206` and the dead `__del__` that would quit `self.excel_app` (`:57-63`) are three pieces of one plan: "reuse the user's Excel if there is one, and leave it open afterwards". Only the first piece was written. The reuse-an-open-workbook branches suggest the author met "file already open" situations. The shared run log of `edac6a3` (described by kind only) records six "Created new Excel instance" lines and no "Using existing Excel instance" line (READ (SH) §1.11), so in the logged runs no user Excel was attached.

**Inference.** Attaching was meant to avoid starting a new Excel twice per client (speed) and to avoid two Excels fighting over the same files; leaving the user's Excel open was intended but never finished. **MEDIUM** for the reason, **HIGH** that the intent is unfinished.

**What it costs today.** B-G63 (the user's Excel is hidden and closed; Step 4 may reuse it and close same-named workbooks without saving), B-G38 (if Excel dies the clean-up itself fails), B-G74 (Step 3 and Step 4 can run at the same time and both drive Excel). Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx` and "Never take over the user's own open Excel" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:851-855`).

#### 8.4.3 Building reports on local disk and then copying - B does not do this

**What the code does.** B makes every report directly at its final place in the target folder: it copies the template byte for byte to the final report name (`core/excel_handler.py:122-125`, then a 0.5-second pause "Give Windows time to complete the copy"), opens that copy in Excel (`:129`), writes the Links cells (`:159-167`) and saves it in place (`:173-177`). The Step 4 refreshed copy is likewise made at its final name in the Version folder before Excel opens it (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:118-120`). No file is written to a temporary name and renamed afterwards (READ; RAN (XL) §6.2 grep: no `os.replace`, `rename` or `shutil.move` anywhere).

**Remnants of a temporary-file design.**

| Remnant | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A folder `<system temp>/gst_excel_temp` is created every time a processing run starts | `core/excel_handler.py:52-53` (B-R105) | never used, never deleted (RAN (OF) t4) |
| `EXCEL_SAFETY['temp_prefix'] = 'temp_gst_'`, `'backup_prefix'`, `'verification_size_min'` 10240 | `utils/constants.py:217-228` (B-R106 to B-R109) | copied into `self.safety_config` (`core/excel_handler.py:54`) and never read |
| `.gitignore` ignores `temp_gst_*` and `backup_*` | `.gitignore:52-53` | no code makes such names |
| "All file operations use temporary files and verification steps" | `README.md:7`, `:42-43` | not true of the code (DO R20-R22) |

All of these were already unused at the first commit (READ (SH) §1.14), so the design was abandoned (or only planned) before git.

**Inference.** A version before 31-08-2025 - probably the openpyxl version that "corrupted" files (8.2.3) - either worked through temporary files or the README and constants describe a safety plan that was never coded; when report creation moved to Excel through COM, the template was simply copied to the final name. **MEDIUM.** A domain reason for a local-copy stage would be target folders on a network share or OneDrive (the open routine's advice text mentions "OneDrive/SharePoint sync issue", `report_processor.py:741`), but B does nothing special for them (**LOW** that this was the motive).

**What it costs today.** A failed fill leaves the unfilled template copy under the report's normal name, and Step 4 later treats it as a report (B-G5); interrupted copies stay under their final names (B-G26).

#### 8.4.4 Caching folder listings - B does not do this

**What the code does.** B keeps no cache of folder contents (RAN (me) grep: no `lru_cache`, no `functools`, no stored listing). The Step 4 tree is rebuilt by walking the target folder on disk every time - at start-up (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:190`), after processing (`:384`), after extraction (`:561`) and on "Refresh List" (`:171-172`) - with `iterdir` and `glob` on the window's own thread (`:419-504`). The only things B "caches" are settings, session values and run history in `~/.gst_organizer/` (`models/cache_manager.py:16-37`); that is what the `c258047` subject means by "enhanced caching".

**History - an experiment with a remembered list, reverted the next day.**

| Commit | Where the Step 4 list came from | What went wrong (RAN (H2)) |
|---|---|---|
| `c258047` / `c21f788` (07-02-2026, B only) | the processing results of the current session (`_populate_extraction_from_results`) | empty after a restart; client keys used the state as written, so clients whose state was spelled out were not found |
| `7e09e5c` (08-02-2026, B only) | the run history file (`_populate_extraction_from_history`), the "latest" version by reverse name order | wrong "latest" version (day-first names), phantom rows after every extraction, empty on another PC |
| `b0e7d0e` (09-02-2026, B only) | a fresh walk of the disk (`_populate_extraction_from_disk`, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:419-504`) | still at the snapshot; the run folder is chosen by name (B-G12) |

**Inference.** The author learned within two days that a remembered list goes stale and went back to "show what is actually on disk", as the old stand-alone extractor had done (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:497-550@47a1492` - latest run folder by modification time at `:517`, READ (me) and (H1)). **HIGH** for the history, **MEDIUM-HIGH** for the preference.

**What it costs today.** The walk can pause the window on a large or slow network target (B-G58); it uses the last *saved* target folder, not the text on screen (B-G28).

#### 8.4.5 Step 4 refreshes a time-stamped copy, never the Step 3 report (B-R62)

**What the code does.** The copy is named `<report stem><suffix>.xlsx`, suffix from the Step 4 box with `{timestamp}` replaced by `DDMMYY_HHMM` (`report_processor.py:91-94`), made with `shutil.copy2` (`:120`); only the copy is opened, refreshed, saved and read (`:124`, `:144`). An empty suffix makes the copy name equal to the original, and the copy then fails with "same file" rather than touching the original (RAN (PQ) `emptysuffix`; RAN (verifier) `scripts/emptysuffix.py`: Python's "same file" error (`SameFileError`), original unchanged).

**Inference.** Keep the Step 3 report as a clean starting point, so a failed or half-finished refresh never damages it and the refresh can be repeated; each refresh also leaves a dated record. **HIGH** (the code makes the original untouchable); the "audit trail" purpose is **MEDIUM**.

**What it costs today.** Copies accumulate; the report search `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` also matches them (B-G8); a custom suffix is not recognised by "Skip refresh" or by the tree status (B-G9, B-G7).

#### 8.4.6 Two Excels per report in Step 4

**What the code does.** After the refreshing Excel has saved and quit (`report_processor.py:345-366`), the code waits three seconds "for file to be released" (`:139-141`), then starts a second, hidden Excel with `Dispatch` (`:484-489`), opens the copy (logged as "read-only" although it is opened read-write, `:492-494`), reads the configured cells' `.Value` (`:507-552`, B-R82) and quits (`:569-587`).

**Inference.** Read the figures exactly as they were saved to disk, from a clean Excel that the keystrokes, focus changes and error dialogs of the first session could not have disturbed; the three-second wait shows that file locks after closing were met in practice. **MEDIUM.** Why the reading is done through Excel at all, rather than with openpyxl (which Standard 12 says is fine for *reading* a Power Query workbook, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:827`), cannot be told from the code (not sure - the author may know whether openpyxl ever returned empty cached values for these templates).

#### 8.4.7 The Info!BB2 check and the error-dialog closer (B-F20, B-F26, B-R71, B-R102, B-R103)

**What the code does.** A refresh counts as successful only if no error dialog was seen and a sheet named "info" (any letter case) has a non-empty, non-zero, non-error value in cell BB2 ⚠ (`report_processor.py:589-636`; the comment at `:605` and the message at `:632` call it the "Client Name") [GST RULE]. Separately, `_find_error_window` looks at every visible top-level window on the desktop whose title contains words such as "error" or "microsoft excel" and whose window class is a dialog class (`:368-404`), reads its text (`:406-441`) and clicks the first button whose text contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue", or sends a close message (`:443-476`).

**Inference.** Because the keystroke refresh returns nothing, the code needs two outside signals: a cell that the template fills only when its queries have run (BB2), and the screen itself, scraped for Excel's error boxes that would otherwise block the next COM call ("Call was rejected by callee"). **MEDIUM.** Nothing in B writes BB2, so it is presumably filled by the template (MEDIUM; the templates are not in the repository - question for the author).

**What it costs today.** BB2 can already hold a value from the template or an earlier refresh (B-G6); the dialog closer can reach other programs' dialogs and answer "Yes" to any question (B-G61). Which cell proves a refresh is the author's call.

#### 8.4.8 Python writes folder paths and file names into a "Links" sheet; the GST work happens in the template (B-F13, B-F14, B-R54 to B-R56)

**What the code does.** Python never reads a client's figures from the input files - the scan reads only each file's size and first 8 bytes (`core/file_parser.py:181-215`). For each report it writes into the template copy's "Links" sheet the Windows-style folder path of each category folder (for the Annual Report: the Version folder, `core/excel_handler.py:560, 605`) and the stem of the first file of each type (`core/excel_handler.py:540-627`; cell map `utils/constants.py:96-120` ⚠ [GST RULE]) [Corrected during verification - the Annual Report folder written is the Version folder, not a category folder]. The template's own Power Query is expected to read the files from there; afterwards Step 4 reads back fixed result cells (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:33-228` ⚠ [GST RULE]).

**Inference.** The reconciliation logic (GSTR-2B against the books, GSTR-3B differences, Annual Return tables) lives in the author's Excel templates, where a CA can see, maintain and check it without touching code; Python only organises the files and tells each template where they are. **MEDIUM-HIGH.** File names are written without their extension, which suggests the queries add ".xlsx" or match by name (**LOW**; the templates are not in the repository).

**What it costs today.** Cells for missing file types keep whatever the template holds (B-G2); only the first file of each type is linked (B-G3); a template without a Links sheet gives no error (B-G4); whatever else sits in a linked folder (backups, duplicates) may be read (B-G29). Which cell holds which input is the author's call.

#### 8.4.9 Copy, verify by size, never move; back up in Fresh mode (B-R42, B-R43)

**What the code does.** Each recognised file is copied with its dates (`utils/helpers.py:142-185`), the copy's size is compared with the source and a mismatched copy is deleted (`:172-178`); in Fresh mode an existing destination is first backed up as `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` (`utils/helpers.py:187-204`; `core/file_organizer.py:259-270`). Source files are never moved, renamed or changed (RAN (LT) §6.4: identical SHA-256 fingerprints before and after six runs).

**Inference.** The source folder holds the client's downloaded returns and must stay exactly as it was; copies can always be made again. **HIGH.** The README's "Original files are never modified" (`README.md:47`) is consistent with the code.

#### 8.4.10 Long-path handling: the 218-character limit, 8.3 short names and `\\?\` prefixes (B-R98 to B-R100)

**What the code does.** A path longer than 218 characters is treated as too long for Excel ("Excel's typical limit", `report_processor.py:668`). Step 3 then retries the open with the old DOS-style 8.3 short name (`core/excel_handler.py:291-301`, `utils/helpers.py:473-483`); Step 4 first rewrites the path with the `\\?\` (local) or `\\?\UNC\` (network) long-path prefix and opens that (`report_processor.py:665-685`); if that fails it closes every open workbook with the same file name without saving and tries the same path again (`:691-701`); then it tries the 8.3 short name (`:704-716`); then **either** the path without the prefix (only when a prefix was added, `:718-722`) **or**, when no prefix was added, an open with extra options (`:724-731`); and if the last try fails and the error contains "-2147352567" it logs advice including "Path length is definitely an issue!" (`:736-745`) [Corrected during verification - originally described as one fixed sequence "prefix, short name, no prefix, extra options", which left out the same-name close-and-retry and made the last two steps look consecutive; READ (verifier)].

**Clues.** All of this is in the first commit (READ (SH) §5, "Pre-git traces"). RAN (OF) §5.4: for a 44-character target folder and a 40-character client name, B's copies reach 233-268 characters.

**Inference.** Deep folder trees (target → run folder → client folder → Version folder → category folder with a bracketed client name) plus long client names pushed real paths past Excel's limit before git, and the author added fixes where the errors appeared. **HIGH** that the problem was met in use. The two different routines (one per former program) were written at different times (**MEDIUM**). The client-folder length limit (default 35, B-R32) is probably part of the same fight against long paths (**MEDIUM**).

**What it costs today.** Paths are never shortened beforehand, and 8.3 names often do not exist on network shares (B-G54).

#### 8.4.11 Retries and fixed sleeps around Excel (B-R66, B-R68, B-R114)

**What the code does.** Retries: Excel properties five times, two seconds apart (`report_processor.py:178-190`); opening three times on "Call was rejected by callee" (`:195-205`); window activation three times (`:220-227`). Fixed sleeps: 0.5 s after the template copy and after closing (`core/excel_handler.py:125, 180`); five seconds of loading (`report_processor.py:207-211`); 1 s after the window activation and 1 s after each of the first two keys (`:232, 239, 244`); the user's wait time (`:256-258`); up to 5 × 1 s of dialog checks (`:266-275`); `max(10, wait time)` seconds of "extended wait" (`:282-286`); 2 s after saving and 1 s after closing (`:307, 319`); three seconds for file release (`:139-141`) - about 39 seconds per report at the default wait of 10 s, before counting Excel's own start-up (READ (verifier); B-G57).

**Inference.** "Call was rejected by callee" is the message COM gives when Excel is busy (starting up, recalculating, showing a dialog); the comments "Increased from 3 to 5" (`:209`) and "Increased from 0.5" (`:239`, `:244`) show each wait was lengthened after a failure. **HIGH** that these come from real failures; **MEDIUM** that fixed sleeps were chosen because nothing in the keystroke approach can report "ready".

**What it costs today.** Slow runs and no timeouts (B-G57, B-G39). If all three opens are refused, the code carries on with no workbook and still sends the keystrokes (RAN (PQ) `rejected`; B-G62).

#### 8.4.12 Minute-stamped run and Version folders with day-first dates (B-R30, B-R31, B-R34, B-R39)

**What the code does.** Each processing run makes (Fresh) or reuses (Re-Run/Resume) a run folder `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` and always makes a new `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder inside each client folder (`utils/helpers.py:23-25`; `utils/constants.py:82-84`; `core/file_organizer.py:98-104, 146-179`).

**Inference.** Never overwrite an earlier batch, so every run stays available; the day-first form `DDMMYY` is the date order an Indian office reads naturally. **MEDIUM.** Minute precision was enough for runs started by hand (**MEDIUM**).

**What it costs today.** Name order is not date order, so Step 4 can pick an older batch (B-G12); runs in the same minute overwrite each other (B-G27); because every run gets a new Version folder, "Resume" skips nothing and "Re-Run" overwrites nothing (B-G13).

#### 8.4.13 The processing worker rewrites the scan data to pass on cleaned names (B-R57)

**What the code does.** After each successful copy, the organiser writes the cleaned file name back into the window's scan data under the comment "IMPORTANT: Update the file data with the sanitized filename … This ensures Excel handler gets the correct filename" (`core/file_organizer.py:216-229`).

**Inference.** The simplest way to make the Links cells name the copy that actually exists, without changing the report code's input. **HIGH.**

**What it costs today.** A skipped (Resume) or failed copy keeps its original name, so the Links cell names a file that is not there (B-G13); the worker changes the window's data from another thread (B-G75).

#### 8.4.14 "Skip refresh" passed through a module-wide dictionary (B-R63)

**What the code does.** At the start of every extraction the worker overwrites `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS['skip_refresh']` in the configuration module (`gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:54-55`), and the refresh code reads it back (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:97-98`); the other two Step 4 options travel as object attributes (`extraction_controller.py:50-51`).

**Inference.** A leftover of the old extractor window, which also changed this dictionary when its tick box was clicked (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:237-238@edac6a3`, READ (SH) §1.10); the port kept the mechanism. **HIGH.** Cost: B-G76 (the value in the file has no effect).

#### 8.4.15 A fallback state code and a raw-text client key [GST RULE] ⚠ (B-R17, B-R21, B-R22)

**What the code does.** A state name not in the fixed table gets a made-up code - the first letters of the first two words, or the first three characters of a one-word name - with a warning in the program log (`utils/helpers.py:485-511`; table `utils/constants.py:234-275` ⚠). The client key is the client text as written in the file name plus that code (`core/file_parser.py:261-262`).

**Inference (technical only).** Never stop a scan because of an unexpected state spelling; group files by what the file name says. **MEDIUM.** Whether the codes, the table or the grouping are right is the author's call; Section 7 records the technical effects (B-G16).

#### 8.4.16 Three processing modes on top of new Version folders (B-R44)

**What the code does.** Fresh, Re-Run and Resume differ only in which run folder is used and in what happens when a destination file already exists (`core/file_organizer.py:146-179, 259-270`), while the destination is always inside a brand-new Version folder (`:98-104`).

**Inference.** The modes and the Version folders are both in the first commit, so git cannot show which came first; the "skip if it already exists" logic only makes sense without per-run Version folders, which suggests Version folders were added (before git) after the modes were designed and made Resume ineffective. **LOW-MEDIUM.** Cost: B-G13. What Re-Run and Resume should mean is a question for the author (8.10).

#### 8.4.17 All Python warnings switched off (B-R104)

**What the code does.** `warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')` at import of `core/excel_handler.py:16-17` silences every Python warning in the whole program.

**Inference.** Added to hide openpyxl's console warnings about workbook features it does not support. **MEDIUM.** Cost: B-G31 (it also hides the warnings that announce dropped features).

#### 8.4.18 Step 4 outputs and an extraction log inside the run folder (`b0e7d0e`, B-F25, B-R122)

**What the code does.** The consolidated workbook and `Extraction_Log_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.txt` are written into the run folder shown on Step 4 (`gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:86-95, 109-121`); before `b0e7d0e` the report went to the target folder itself (READ (H2)).

**Inference.** Keep each batch's outputs together and leave a written record of each extraction, as the old stand-alone extractor had done for the report (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:808@47a1492`, READ (me)). **MEDIUM.** Cost: client folder names and figures sit in a plain text file next to the outputs (B-G64).

### 8.7 Pattern consistency

The audit method (process step 8) asks, for every pattern, what the project's own established way is, which files follow it and which break it. "Breaks" below are facts; whether a break is a bug is said only where the effect is known (with the Section 7 gap). Evidence for counts: RAN (me) `scripts/excepts.py`, `scripts/imports.py`, greps listed in 9.13.

#### 8.7.1 Error handling

**Established pattern (the v3 design).** Catch broadly at the lowest level, log the error, and hand back a "failure value" so that one bad file or client never stops the batch. B has 91 `except` clauses: 79 catch `Exception`, 5 `OSError`, 7 other specific types; **0 bare `except:`** (the `c258047` clean-up removed 26 - RAN (verifier): 26 at `47a1492`, 0 at `c258047`) and **15 whose body is only `pass`** (RAN (verifier) `scripts/excepts.py`: the same 91 / 79 / 5 / 7 / 0 / 15; they sit in Excel clean-up, in the destructor `__del__`, in the error-dialog routines (`report_processor.py:395, 422, 462`) or in column auto-fit [Corrected during verification - originally "all in Excel clean-up or column auto-fit"]: `core/excel_handler.py:62, 200, 210, 216, 534`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:352, 359, 365, 395, 422, 462, 575, 581, 586`; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:412`) (RAN (me), matching DC P-02). Background jobs catch everything in `run()` and send an `error` signal that the window turns into a message box (`gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:39-41`, `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:35-40`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:36-41` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:318-322, 412-415, 563-565`).

**Files that follow it.** `utils/helpers.py` (`safe_copy_file` returns False, `utils/helpers.py:183-185`; `find_excel_files` returns an empty list, `:264-266`; `create_backup` returns None); `core/excel_handler.py` (report creation returns False, `:191-193`; the summary returns False, `:344-346`); `core/file_organizer.py` (each file's result carries its error; the organisation report returns None); `models/cache_manager.py` (`_save_json` only logs, `:141-142`; `_load_json` returns `{}`, `:150-152`); `models/run_history.py` (`:135-136`, `:146-148`); `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py` (every failure becomes a status dictionary, `:154-163`, `:332-344`).

**Files and places that break it.**

| Break | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| One function, two contracts: raises for a missing template, returns False for every other failure | `core/excel_handler.py:78-79` | the caller must handle both (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:235-239` does) |
| Log and re-raise | `utils/helpers.py:45-47` (`ensure_path_exists`), `:62-64` (`safe_path_join`); `core/file_parser.py:166-169` (`scan_folder`); `core/file_organizer.py:140-144` (`create_client_structure`); `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:172-174` (`create_report`); `report_processor.py:732-747` (`_safe_open_workbook`) | intended where a whole step must stop; the consolidated workbook is then lost for one bad value (B-G43) |
| Convert to another error type | `core/file_organizer.py:62-65` (any error → `ValueError`) | the original error type is lost |
| Clean-up lines outside any `try` | `core/excel_handler.py:204-205` | if Excel has died, `Quit()` and `CoUninitialize()` are skipped (B-G38) |
| Window handlers with no protection (only `_on_scan_completed` wraps its whole body in a `try`, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:245-316`; `_on_processing_completed` guards only the Explorer call, `:406-410`, and the Step 4 disk walk catches only `OSError`, `:431-440, 452-497` [Corrected during verification - originally "only `_on_scan_completed` has a `try`"]) | e.g. `:373-405`, `:549-561`, `:594-597`, `:601-608` | an error there ends the whole program, exit code 134 (B-G35; RAN (MW) e10) |
| A handler that can never run | `report_processor.py:125-137` (B-R72) | the special "could not open" message never appears |
| Start-up errors only printed | `main.py:49-59`; `launch_extractor.py:22-24` | invisible without a console (B-G34) |
| Only `OSError` caught when writing the extraction log | `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:120` | another error there would end the run with "Extraction Error" |
| Different failure words for the same idea | `True`/`False` (`ExcelHandler`) vs `{'success', 'error', 'validation_message'}` (`ReportProcessor`); "Success" / "Failed" / "Skipped" (`core/file_organizer.py`), "OK" / "FAIL" (`gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:77-84`), "✓" / "✗" (`data_consolidator.py:100-109`) | each screen and report must translate |

**Inference.** The "never let one item stop the batch" style was deliberate and is applied consistently in the per-item code (HIGH). The breaks sit where code from different eras meets - the v3 core, the v3 extractor and the v4 window (MEDIUM-HIGH).

#### 8.7.2 Platform checks and import guards (OS-specific modules)

**Established pattern (the v3 organiser).** Check the platform, try the import, set a flag and fall back:

```python
# core/excel_handler.py:19-28
USE_WIN32COM = False
if platform.system() == 'Windows':
    try:
        import win32com.client
        import pythoncom
        USE_WIN32COM = True
        ...
    except ImportError:
        logging.warning("win32com not available. Install with: pip install pywin32")
```

**Files that follow it.** `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` (flag used at `:83-93`); `utils/helpers.py:473-483` (`win32api` imported inside the function under a Windows check, any error → the normal path); `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:404-410` (`os.startfile` only on Windows, inside `try`); `main.py:12-13` (the UTF-8 console wrapper only when a console exists).

**Files that break it.**

| Break | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Five Windows-only modules imported at module top with no guard | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` | the module cannot load without pywin32 |
| The unguarded module is imported at start-up, also unguarded | `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10` ← `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:27`, `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4`, `gui/__init__.py:7` | the whole window cannot open without pywin32 (B-G32); RAN (me) 9.5: every `gui.*` module fails to import in a fresh process |
| `win32api` imported twice and the guarded helper not reused | `report_processor.py:13` and again `:710`; direct `win32api.GetShortPathName` at `:711` instead of `utils/helpers.py:473-483` | duplicated logic; no harm |
| Two different install hints | `core/excel_handler.py:28` "pip install pywin32" (log only) vs `main.py:51-53` "pip install PyQt5 openpyxl" (shown) | the shown hint does not fix the error |

**History (HIGH).** At the split the pattern was consistent *per program*: the organiser guarded, the separate extractor did not (it could only ever run on Windows). `c258047` put both into one window, so the extractor's style decided start-up for everything (12F.5).

**Established pattern.** One module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` in each module that logs - 13 modules (`core/excel_handler.py:42`, `core/file_organizer.py:18`, `core/file_parser.py:18`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:13`, `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:16`, `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:11`, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:29`, `models/cache_manager.py:14`, `models/run_history.py:13`, `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:13`, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:18`, `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:21`, `utils/helpers.py:17`) - configured once by `main.py:16-23` (RAN (me) grep).

| Break | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Messages written to the root logger directly | `core/excel_handler.py:26, 28` (at import), `main.py:50, 57` | harmless but outside the pattern |
| `print()` for errors | `main.py:51-53, 58`; `launch_extractor.py:23` | lost without a console |
| Second entry point sets up no logging at all | `launch_extractor.py:1-28` | no log file; INFO lines lost (B-G44) |
| A third, separate set-up | `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:12-19` (`pq_extractor.log`; dead, B-F31) | never runs |
| A log helper that ignores the level | `report_processor.py:30-37` (`_log` always logs INFO; its 96 calls all use the default level "info", READ (PQ); RAN (verifier) count made by parsing the code (an AST, Python's own tree view of a file) rather than by text search: 96 calls, 0 with a level) | Step 4 errors are blue on screen and INFO in the file (B-G71) |
| Some warnings only in the program log | e.g. `report_processor.py:186, 202, 226, 230, 272, 295, 504, 522, 543, 548` (`logger.warning/error` directly) | not on screen and not in `Extraction_Log_*.txt` |
| File log without an encoding, while every other text file is UTF-8 | `main.py:20` vs `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:114`, `models/cache_manager.py:139`, `core/file_organizer.py:354` | lines with ✓ / ❌ can be lost on a cp1252 PC (B-G44; MEDIUM) |
| Three message channels fed differently | program log (`main.py:16-23`), on-screen logs (views), `Extraction_Log_*.txt` (`extraction_controller.py:43-46, 109-121`) | the three records of one run differ |

**Inference.** The logging set-up is the v3 one, written once and not revisited by the rewrite (HIGH).

#### 8.7.5 Threading and screen updates

**Established pattern (all three jobs, identical).** A plain `QObject` worker is moved to a new `QThread` (`moveToThread`); the thread's `started` signal runs `worker.run`; the worker's signals are relayed by the controller's own signals; `finished` / `error` stop the thread; the thread's `finished` calls `_cleanup`, which schedules both objects for deletion; an `isRunning()` guard refuses a second job of the same kind (`gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:57-94`, `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:256-298`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:138-184`). No worker touches a widget: every path to the screen is a signal (READ; RAN (MW) e3: all 35 scan-log writes and 16 status-bar writes ran on the window's thread; RAN (DC) T4b).

**Breaks.**

| Break | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| The processing worker changes the window's scan data | `core/file_organizer.py:216-229` (the same dictionary as `window.scan_result.client_data`, passed at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:368` → `processing_controller.py:30`) | B-G75 |
| A setting passed through a module-wide dictionary | `extraction_controller.py:54-55` | B-G76 |
| Slow disk work on the window's thread | `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:419-504` (Step 4 walk); `:326-343` (dry run, one line per file) | B-G58, B-G60 |
| Stop is a plain flag checked only between items; the scan has no Stop | `processing_controller.py:80-83, 281-284`; `extraction_controller.py:60-63, 167-170` | B-G39, B-G70 |
| Guards only per job kind; closing the window neither stops nor waits | `pyqt_main_window.py:601-608` | B-G74, B-G40; a late clean-up can destroy a newer thread (B-G41) |
| Different signal shapes for the same idea | scan progress `(int, int, str)` (`scan_controller.py:17`) vs processing / extraction progress `(float, str)` (`processing_controller.py:21`, `extraction_controller.py:18`); only processing and extraction have a `log` signal | harmless; inconsistent |
| A central signal hub that nothing uses | `models/signals.py:9-38` (18 signals [Corrected during verification - originally 19]; its docstring says "All inter-component communication goes through these signals") | dead (READ (DC) D-01; Section 2 lists it) |
| COM started and stopped inside each Excel function | `core/excel_handler.py:107, 215`; `report_processor.py:171, 363, 484, 584` | Standard 12 asks for `CoUninitialize()` after the Excel function returns (B-R110, B-G77) |

There is no lock anywhere (RAN (DC) grep: no `threading`, `Lock`, `QMutex`, `QTimer`). **Inference.** The controller pattern was designed once in `c258047` and copied three times (HIGH); the breaks are the places where old code (the organiser's in-place renaming, the extractor's global option) was plugged into it unchanged (HIGH).

| Two different long-path strategies for opening a workbook | `core/excel_handler.py:264-306` vs `report_processor.py:638-747` | 8.4.10 |
| One client named differently in different places | client folder `create_client_state_key` (`utils/helpers.py:513-537`), category bracket and copies `sanitize_filename` (`:66-112`), organisation report raw text (`core/file_organizer.py:313`), report names cleaned name + state code (`processing_controller.py:112-113`) | B-G18 |
| Report extension fixed to `.xlsx` whatever the template | `processing_controller.py:220` | B-G30 |
| Imports by top-level name in most files, relative in some | `from utils.constants …` (`core/file_parser.py:13`) vs `from .app_state …` (`models/cache_manager.py:11-12`) and `from ..config.cell_mappings …` (`report_processor.py:16`); views import their own package by full name (`gui/views/setup_view.py:14`) | the top-level style works only because `main.py:29` (or `launch_extractor.py:8`) puts the program folder on Python's import path |

**Inference.** `pathlib` and "find the code from `__file__`" are applied consistently by both the v3 core and the v4 rewrite (HIGH); the breaks are old pieces the rewrite did not revisit (the log path from `edac6a3`, the dead extractor entry point) and the quickly rewritten second launcher (MEDIUM-HIGH). The four spellings of one client come from three helpers written for different purposes - a folder key, a safe file name and a human-readable report title (MEDIUM).

**Maintenance they require.**

- Every new public helper or constant must be added twice in `utils/__init__.py` (the import list and `__all__`) - and the last additions were not, so the list already misleads (HIGH).
- Because `gui/__init__.py` imports the window eagerly, any heavy import added to the window (today pywin32) is paid by every GUI module; tests of a single view need stand-in pywin32 modules (the note authors had to create them: RAN (DC), (XL), (H1), (H2)) (HIGH).
- Because `core/__init__.py` imports `excel_handler`, the program-wide "ignore all warnings" switch is thrown by anything that touches `core` (HIGH, RAN (me)).
- Deleting or renaming a module requires checking every `__init__.py` that names it - `a62d3cc` did not, and the program could not start until `c21f788` (HIGH).

## SECTION 9: DEPENDENCIES AND ENVIRONMENT

### 9.0 How to read this section

This section lists everything project B needs from outside its own 41 files: Python packages, the Python version, the operating system, folders and files on disk, and programs such as Excel - and compares how B is started with the author's Standard 13. Labels, IDs and confidence words are as in 8.0. Where the repository itself comes from (added during self-review, from the Section 12 writer's flag for Sections 1 and 9): GitHub's records show B's repository was created on 31-08-2025 at 22:08:53 IST, three minutes before the first commit `edac6a3`, and A's on 07-02-2026 at 11:21:52 IST, six minutes before B's PyQt5 rewrite `c258047`, so B is probably the original repository (MEDIUM; Section 12A "Which repository is the original", and the summary table at the top of this audit). This does not change any dependency below. Extra terms:

- *Package*: an add-on installed into Python with `pip` (Python's package installer). *requirements.txt*: the list `pip install -r requirements.txt` reads. *Declared*: listed there. *Pinned / exact version*: `==3.1.5`; *minimum version*: `>=3.1.2` ("this or anything newer").
- *Wheel*: the ready-made file `pip` downloads for one package, one Python version and one operating system (for example `pywin32-312-cp314-cp314-win_amd64.whl` = pywin32 version 312 for Python 3.14 on 64-bit Windows).
- *Standard library (stdlib)*: the modules that come with Python itself.
- *Transitive dependency*: a package pulled in automatically because another one needs it.
- *pythonw.exe*: the Windows Python that opens no console window. *Console*: the black text window. *excepthook*: a Python hook that receives any error nothing else caught.
- *Current working folder (cwd)*: the folder a program was started "in"; a file opened by a bare name such as `gst_organizer.log` lands there.
- *UNC path*: a network path such as `\\server\share\…`. *8.3 short name*: the old DOS-style short form Windows can give a long path. *Long-path prefix*: `\\?\` in front of a path, which tells Windows to accept paths longer than 260 characters.
- *Embeddable package*: python.org's portable Python that Standard 13 puts in a shared `_runtime` folder.

Python 3.7 and 3.8 no longer receive security fixes (general knowledge, MEDIUM) ⚠ [Corrected during verification - originally "with the newest builds the real floor is therefore 3.10; '3.7' cannot be met by PyQt5 5.15.11 at all" and the 3.8 / 3.9 question was left open] | RAN (me), RAN (verifier) |
| What the developer used | Python 3.12 and 3.13 in June-August 2025 (compiled-file headers, RAN (SH) §1.16); this audit ran 3.14.6 | RAN (SH), RAN (me) |
| What Standard 13 uses | "All testing used Python 3.14" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:931`); Windows wheels for Python 3.14 exist today for every package B needs (9.1, RAN (me)) | RAN (me) |

**Behaviour that changes with the Python version** (each a fact for the author; not a recommendation):

- Cleaned client names: Python 3.14 treats a trailing dot as an extension and 3.11-3.13 do not, so a client name that ends in a dot (for example `<Client A> Co.`) gives different folder and report names on different versions (B-G80, RAN by the Section 7 writer; RAN (verifier) `scripts/dot.py`: `<Client A> Co.` style names end in `.` on 3.14 only).
- The start script's own path: since Python 3.9 the started script's `__file__` is an absolute path (general knowledge, MEDIUM); on 3.8 `Path(__file__).parent` (`main.py:28`) can be the relative path `.`, which still works as long as the program does not change folder (LOW).
- Text encoding of the log file: `logging.FileHandler('gst_organizer.log')` (`main.py:20`) uses the PC's default encoding; Python 3.14 on an English Windows normally uses cp1252, so lines with ✓ or ❌ can be lost (B-G44, MEDIUM). Python's planned switch to UTF-8 by default (PEP 686, announced for 3.15 ⚠) would change this (general knowledge, MEDIUM; not checked here).
- `Path.glob` matches extensions without regard to letter case on Windows and with regard to it on Linux (`utils/helpers.py:255-257`; RAN (LT) §6.2 on Linux) - an operating-system difference rather than a version one.

| `python main.py` | - | **no**: exit code 1; console "Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'" / "Please install required packages:" / "  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl"; one line written to `gst_organizer.log` **in the folder the program was started from**; no `~/.gst_organizer` folder created (RAN (me), cwd `run/B-S89/cwd1`) |

So the business core (scan, folders, copies, consolidation) has no Windows dependency of its own; only the refresh module has, and the window's start-up pulls it in.

1. **pywin32 is guarded in two files and unguarded in one, and the unguarded one is on the start-up path** (`core/excel_handler.py:19-28` and `utils/helpers.py:473-483` versus `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15`, pulled in by `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10`). The careful fallback in `core/excel_handler.py` can therefore never run through the window (B-R97). HIGH (RAN (me)). [Corrected during self-review - "careful" is the code's intent, not its effect: Appendix X1 (F1, RAN) shows that this fallback saves the template copy with openpyxl, drops its Power Query part and still reports success (`core/excel_handler.py:219-262`), so its being unreachable today protects the templates (Section 11, T3). It was reachable at the split: at `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) the Tkinter organiser did not load the extractor, so on a Windows PC without pywin32 it opened and Step 3 took this openpyxl path (`47a1492:core/excel_handler.py:19-27, 89-96`: "Fallback to openpyxl (no Power Query support)") - the reports made that way had lost their queries (READ; HIGH for the code path, NOT SURE whether any office PC ever ran without pywin32 - ask the author). Flag from the Appendix X1 writer.]
2. **The same function exists twice with different guards**: `utils/helpers.get_short_path` (guarded) and the direct `win32api.GetShortPathName` call in `report_processor.py:710-711`. HIGH.
3. **The README and requirements describe an optional pywin32 and support for macOS / Linux** (`README.md:52`, `requirements.txt:13-14`), which the code no longer supports. HIGH (RAN (me)).
4. **The two entry points prepare the environment differently** - UTF-8 console wrapper, logging, application name and version only in `main.py:11-23, 41-42`; `sys.path.insert(0, …)` (`main.py:29`) versus `sys.path.append(…)` (`launch_extractor.py:8`) (READ (DC) P-11). HIGH.

### 9.8 Setting B up on a fresh machine

What the code actually needs, in order (READ; RAN where marked). The README's own steps (`README.md:57-113`) are given alongside where they differ.

1. **A Windows 10 or 11 PC with a logged-in user.** B's window cannot open on any other system (RAN (me) 9.5.1). The README still lists macOS and Linux (`README.md:52`).
2. **Microsoft Excel for Windows**, activated, able to refresh the two templates by hand (Data → Refresh All) on that PC, in the same display language as the author's PC (MEDIUM: the key tips). Not checked by B.
3. **Python for Windows**, a version that today's packages support: ≥3.10 to get the newest build of every package (9.4) ⚠; 3.14 works with Windows wheels for every package (RAN (me) `pip download`). pip still finds older Windows builds for 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9 (RAN (verifier) dry-run resolution, 9.4), so the "3.7 or higher" of `requirements.txt:2` can be installed, but only 3.11-3.14 were shown to compile B (9.4) and no version was run on Windows [Corrected during verification - originally "The '3.7 or higher' of `requirements.txt:2` is not achievable with PyQt5 5.15.11", true only for that one PyQt5 build].
4. **Copy the program folder** (41 files). The README's folder tree (`README.md:72-95`) is the v3 one and does not match.
5. **Install the packages**: `pip install -r requirements.txt` (`README.md:101`) installs PyQt5 (+ PyQt5-Qt5, PyQt5-sip), openpyxl (+ et-xmlfile) and lxml - **and then, separately, `pip install pywin32`**, because the requirements line is commented out (`requirements.txt:14`). Versions are not pinned, so the day's newest versions arrive ⚠.
6. **pywin32's post-install step**: the README's troubleshooting table says to run `python Scripts/pywin32_postinstall.py -install` as administrator (`README.md:275`). The pywin32 312 wheel contains a `pywin32.pth` file that adds `win32`, `win32\lib` and `pythonwin` to Python's import path and runs `import pywin32_bootstrap` "to deal with environments where the post_install script isn't run" (RAN (me), reading the downloaded wheel), so a normal `pip install` should not need the post-install step (MEDIUM; check by step 7).
7. **Check the imports** in a console: `python -c "import pythoncom, win32com.client, win32api, win32con, win32gui, PyQt5.QtWidgets, openpyxl"`.
8. **Provide the two templates** (ITC and Sales) with a "Links" sheet, an "info" sheet whose BB2 the queries fill, and the sheets and cells Step 4 reads (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:33-228`) ⚠ [GST RULE]. They are not in the repository.
9. **Prepare a flat source folder** with the input files named by the six patterns ⚠ [GST RULE], and choose a target folder. B never shortens paths: with the RAN (OF) §5.4 example (44-character target, 40-character client name) copies already exceed 218 characters, so the length of the target path matters (technical fact).
10. **Start the program** from a console **in the program folder**: `python main.py` (`README.md:112`), so that `gst_organizer.log` is written there (`main.py:20`). `python launch_extractor.py` opens the same window on Step 4 but writes no log. There is no installer, no `.bat` file and no desktop shortcut.
11. **On first start** B creates `%USERPROFILE%\.gst_organizer\` (`models/cache_manager.py:31-37`) and, if an old `%USERPROFILE%\.gst_organizer_cache.json` exists, copies its settings once (B-F2).
12. **While B runs**: Step 3 attaches to an Excel that is already open and closes it at the end (8.4.2, B-G63); during Step 4 an Excel window appears maximised and receives keystrokes, so the PC must be left alone (B-G51).

### 9.9 How the app is started, compared with the author's Standard 13

Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`) describes how users should start every app: a desktop shortcut runs `Run [App Name].bat`, which starts the shared portable Python's `pythonw.exe -B -s main.py` from the app's folder on the office share; `main.py` first installs error hooks that write an error file to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\logs` and show a message box. B compared rule by rule (facts only; the decision is the author's):

| Standard 13 says (line) | B at the snapshot | Gap and effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Users double-click a desktop shortcut (Run: Minimized) to `Run [App Name].bat` (`:951-980`) | no `.bat`, no shortcut; the README tells users to type `python main.py` or `python launch_extractor.py` in a console (`README.md:112, 168`) | users must use a console | READ (file list) |
| One shared portable Python, python.org's embeddable package, in `_runtime` (`:908-915`) | assumes a normally installed Python with `pip`; nothing in B depends on the installed form - and B no longer needs `tkinter`, which the embeddable package lacks (MEDIUM, general knowledge) | none in the code | RAN (me) 9.3 |
| Packages put into `_runtime\python\Lib\site-packages` with `pip install --target … <package>==<version>`, then each imported with `_runtime\python\python.exe -s` before it counts as ready (`:933-936`) | pywin32 depends on its `pywin32.pth` file (RAN (me): adds `win32`, `win32\lib`, `pythonwin`; runs `pywin32_bootstrap`) | not sure whether the runtime honours `.pth` files in that folder (it depends on the runtime's own `._pth` set-up); the Standard's own check settles it: `_runtime\python\python.exe -s -c "import pythoncom, win32com.client, win32api, win32con, win32gui"` | RAN (me) wheel contents |
| Each app keeps a `requirements.txt` with the exact versions of the packages it imports (`:919`, `:937-940`) | minimum versions only; pywin32 commented out; lxml listed but not imported; transitive PyQt5-Qt5 / PyQt5-sip unpinned | a shared runtime would get whatever versions were newest when installed ⚠ | READ `requirements.txt:1-14` |
| Testing used Python 3.14 (`:931`) | B's files compile on 3.14 and Windows wheels for 3.14 exist for all its packages | none; note the Python-version-dependent naming (B-G80) | RAN (me) |
