## SECTION 10: UI/INTERFACE DOCUMENTATION

Project B has **one window**, titled "GST File Organizer v4.0", built with **PyQt5** (a Python add-on that draws Windows-style windows using the Qt toolkit). Everything the user does happens on the four **tabs** (pages you switch between by clicking their labels at the top) of that window - "Step 1: Setup", "Step 2: Validation", "Step 3: Processing" and "Step 4: Extract & Refresh" - plus small pop-up **message boxes** and the standard Windows **file / folder pickers**. Two outside programs also appear on screen because of B: **Windows Explorer**, opened on the output folder after processing (Windows only), and **Microsoft Excel**, which Step 4 opens visibly, maximised, and types keystrokes into (B-F19). There is no other user interface: no command-line options, no settings dialog, no "About" box, no confirmation dialogs.

This section describes every screen, control and message as the code at the snapshot (b0e7d0e, 09-02-2026) builds them, how the screens look, how they behave, and the typical sequence of clicks. All the screen code was written in B's own commits (c258047, a62d3cc, c21f788, 7e09e5c, b0e7d0e - all **B only (after the split)**); the shared commits (edac6a3 ... 47a1492, **shared - before the split on 30-10-2025**) had two different Tkinter programs, summarised in 10.13.

> **The UI findings that matter most (details and evidence below)**
> 1. **No window at all without pywin32.** On a PC without the pywin32 add-on (the Python add-on through which a program drives Excel and other parts of Windows) the program stops before any window appears and prints advice in the console (the black text window from which the program is started) that would not fix it (10.2; B-F1, B-R124; gap B-G32 in Section 7). RAN.
> 2. **Three of the four "Browse" buttons on Step 1 are invisible** (white on white). They still work if clicked blindly; the user is otherwise forced to type or paste paths (10.4; B-F3; B-G67). RAN (pixels: 100 % white).
> 3. **For many failures Step 4 never shows on screen why a report failed** - only "Result: ITC: FAIL, Sales: FAIL" in red. When Excel cannot be started, no report file is found, a report type was not ticked or a cell cannot be read, the reason goes only to the program log file (and, when B was started with `launch_extractor.py`, nowhere at all). The reasons that do reach the screen - a failed refresh check, the text of an Excel error pop-up, a workbook that could not be opened, a missing sheet - arrive only as ordinary blue lines among about 180 log lines per report. [Corrected during verification - originally said that a report that cannot be opened gives no on-screen reason and that only a failed refresh check or a pop-up text reaches the screen; RAN VERIFY-B-S10 v2, see 10.7.] Yet after a fully failed run the list shows every version as "Refreshed (date)" in green and the Step 4 tab gets a green "done" dot (10.7; B-F18, B-F24, B-F29; B-G7, B-G71). RAN.
> 4. **Nothing is locked while a job runs.** During processing, Step 2 "START", "DRY RUN", "SCAN FILES" and Step 4 "Start Extraction" all stay clickable; processing and extraction (both driving Excel) can run at the same time, and a processing run that ends during an extraction switches the Step 4 list to a different run folder (the "Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>" folder that each processing run creates in the target folder); closing the window during a run is accepted at once with no question (10.9; B-F34, B-R111, B-R138; B-G40, B-G74). RAN (START, SCAN FILES and Start Extraction checked during a run; jobs side by side and closing during an extraction RAN by the Section 3 writer, t34b / t34c; closing during processing by MW e11) + READ (no code ever disables the others).
> 5. **On-screen help contradicts the program**: the two descriptions of Re-Run / Resume disagree with each other and with what the code does; a note promises a warning and per-client settings that do not exist; Step 2 tells the user to click "Start Processing" where the button says "START" (10.4, 10.5; B-F33, B-R44, B-R141; B-G13, B-G72). READ + RAN.
> 6. **Dark mode is only partly applied**: Steps 1 and 2 stay white, and the status lines of Steps 3 and 4 become dark grey text on a black background (practically unreadable) (10.10; B-F28; B-G69). RAN (pixels and screenshots).
> 7. **"EXPORT LIST" does nothing** (no action is connected to it) (10.5; B-F10; B-G73). RAN.
> 8. **The window needs a large screen**: its minimum size of 1200 × 800 pixels is taller than a common 1366 × 768 laptop screen, and even at the opening size of 1400 × 900 the main "SCAN FILES" button is hidden below the visible part of Step 1 (10.3, 10.4; B-R129; B-G68). READ + RAN.

**What was run (RAN).** B's real window was opened **off-screen** (Qt draws the window into memory instead of onto a monitor; environment setting `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`) on Linux with Python 3.14.6 and PyQt5 5.15.11 (built against Qt 5.15.14 and running on the Qt 5.15.19 libraries - RAN `QT_VERSION_STR` / `qVersion()` on 23-10-2026; on Windows, pip's newest PyQt5-Qt5 package is Qt 5.15.2 according to the Section 9 writer's `pip download` check, so small drawing differences on Windows are possible), from a copy of the code in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S10/proj` (`python -B`, so nothing was written into the code folders). Because this machine has no Windows, no Excel and no pywin32, five tiny **stand-in modules** ("stubs") named `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui` were put in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S10/stubs`; the stub Excel always fails ("stub: no Excel COM on Linux"), so **Step 4 could only be shown on its failure path**, and nothing Windows-specific was exercised. Message boxes were replaced by recorders (so the run did not stop and wait for a click); every message box text below marked RAN is the text the recorder received. The user's home folder was redirected into the run folder, so the program's settings files were written there. Test data were **placeholders only**: invented clients "ClientA" (Maharashtra, all six file types), "ClientB" (Gujarat, two types missing), "ClientC" (Kerala, two Sales files), one unrecognised file and one file too small to be valid, plus two tiny placeholder templates with a "Links" sheet. On Linux, Step 3 makes its reports with openpyxl (a Python library that writes Excel files without Excel) instead of Excel (`core/excel_handler.py:19-28, 83-93`), so the Step 3 screens were exercised end to end without Excel.

**Limits.** The fonts the code asks for ("Segoe UI", "Consolas") are Windows fonts; Linux used look-alikes, and the emoji characters in the logs (for example 🏢, 📊) are drawn as small boxes in the Linux screenshots. Positions, sizes and colours come from the code's own stylesheets and are the same on Windows (HIGH for colours; MEDIUM for exact pixel sizes, which depend on the Windows display scaling). The native file pickers were not opened (they would wait for a person). Excel, Windows Explorer and real refreshes could not be run.

**Plain-English terms used in this section**

- *Widget*: any visible piece of a window - a button, a text box, a list, a label.
- *Text box* (Qt "line edit"): a one-line box the user can type into. *Spin box*: a number box with small up/down arrows. *Tick box* (check box): a square the user ticks or unticks. *Radio buttons*: a group of round buttons of which exactly one is chosen.
- *Table / tree view*: a list with columns; a *tree* has rows that open into child rows (Step 4: client → version).
- *Message box*: a small pop-up window with a message and an OK button; it is *modal* - the rest of the window cannot be used until it is closed.
- *Status bar*: the thin line of text along the bottom edge of the window.
- *Splitter*: an invisible divider between two side-by-side panels that the user can drag to make one wider. *Scroll area*: a panel with its own scroll bar when its content is taller than the space.
- *Stylesheet (QSS)*: text, similar to a web page's CSS, that sets colours, fonts, borders and sizes. B sets one stylesheet for the whole program (light or dark) and many small ones on individual widgets; a widget's own stylesheet wins over the program-wide one.
- *objectName*: a label given to a widget so a stylesheet rule can target it (for example a button named "danger" gets the red style).
- *Signal / slot*: Qt's message system - clicking a button "emits a signal", and whatever function is "connected" to it runs.
- *Worker thread*: a second line of work inside the program, so the window keeps responding while a long job runs.
- *HTML*: the markup language of web pages; B's on-screen logs insert each line as a small piece of HTML.
- *Run folder*: the "Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>" folder that a processing run creates in the target folder (the code calls it "Level 1"); inside it one *client folder* "<client>-<state code>" per client ("Level 2"), and inside that one *Version folder* "Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>" per run, which holds the three category folders and the ITC and Sales reports.
- *Program log*: the text file `gst_organizer.log` into which B writes its own messages (only when started with `python main.py`, in the folder it was started from); it is separate from the coloured logs shown on screen.

### 10.2 Starting the program - what the user sees first

**How it is started.** README.md:112 tells the user to type `python main.py` in a console; README.md:166-169 tells them to type `python launch_extractor.py` "after main processing". There is no `.bat` launcher, no desktop shortcut and no use of `pythonw` (the console-less Python) anywhere in the repository (READ: `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_files.txt`). `main.py:41-42` names the application "GST File Organizer", version "4.0" (these names are not shown anywhere on screen; the window title is set separately at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:71`). `launch_extractor.py` builds the same window and switches it to the fourth tab before showing it (`launch_extractor.py:17-18`) - RAN e5: title "GST File Organizer v4.0", tab shown "Step 4: Extract && Refresh" (index 3).

**When start-up fails there is no window, only console text.** RAN (e5, `main.py` started with no pywin32 and no stubs, from a scratch folder):

```text
<date time> - root - ERROR - Import Error: No module named 'pythoncom'

 Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'

Please install required packages:
  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl
```

The program then ends with exit code 1 (the number a program hands back when it ends; anything other than 0 means failure) (`main.py:49-54`). RAN again by VERIFY-B-S10 on 23-10-2026: the same four console lines, exit code 1, and one ERROR line in `gst_organizer.log`. The advice would not help, because the missing piece is pywin32, which `requirements.txt:13-14` leaves commented out (B-R124). Through `launch_extractor.py` the console shows only "Failed to launch: <error>" (`launch_extractor.py:22-24`, READ; RAN by the Section 3 writer, t30: "Failed to launch: No module named 'pythoncom'", exit code 1). `launch_extractor.py` also sets up no program log at all, so a session started that way writes no `gst_organizer.log`; the program's information lines are lost and, on Windows with pywin32, only its warnings and errors would reach the console through Python's own fallback (RAN by the Section 3 writer, t30; B-F30, B-G44). Any other start-up error prints "Critical error: <error>" (`main.py:56-59`); one way to reach it is a hand-edited `settings.json` holding a wrong kind of value (RAN by MW e7). If the program is started without a console (for example by double-clicking with `pythonw`), these texts go nowhere and the user sees nothing at all (READ `main.py:11-13, 49-59`; HIGH; a simulated console-less start - no standard output or error channel - ended with exit code 1, nothing visible and one line in the log file, RAN by the Section 9 writer; B-G34).

**What happens before the window appears** (B-R126, `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:35-68`): default settings; the settings folder `~/.gst_organizer` is created; run history is loaded; the old v3 settings are imported once (B-F2); saved settings are loaded; the screens are built; the Step 1 boxes and Step 4 options are filled from the saved settings (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:174-187`); then **the target folder on disk is scanned to fill the Step 4 list** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:189-190`) - in the window's own thread, before the window is shown, so a slow or disconnected network target folder delays the window (READ; MEDIUM, not measured); finally the light or dark style is applied.

**First view.** RAN (e1, e6): the window always opens on **Step 1** at **1400 × 900** pixels (minimum 1200 × 800), status bar "Ready", no coloured dots on the tabs, "RE-SCAN" greyed out - even when the previous session ended on Step 4 and `session_state.json` says `"active_tab": 3` (that file is written on close but never read, B-R117). The Step 1 boxes show the last saved paths; Step 4 already shows the clients of the run folder whose name sorts last - not always the newest, see 10.7 - if a target folder was saved ("Source: Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>"; RAN VERIFY-B-S10 v3), otherwise "No target folder configured." (RAN e1). [Corrected during verification - originally "the newest run folder's clients".]

**Comparison with the author's Standard 13 (facts only).** Standard 13 (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061) expects a `Run [App Name].bat` launcher that starts `pythonw.exe` with no console from a shared runtime, a `sys.excepthook` and `threading.excepthook` (Python's last-resort handlers for errors that nothing else caught) that write the error to a file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` and show a plain-English message box, and settings and logs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\`. B has none of these: start-up errors only go to the console; there is no error hook, so an error nothing catches inside any screen handler makes the whole window vanish at once (RAN by MW e10 and VW t3: exit code 134, "Aborted"; RAN e7 with a damaged session file, 10.8); settings live in `<home>/.gst_organizer` (`models/cache_manager.py:16-17`) and the program log in whatever folder the program was started from (`main.py:20`). Standard 12 (rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:817-898) names PySide6 (Qt 6) for desktop windows; B uses PyQt5 (Qt 5) (`requirements.txt:5`).

### 10.3 The window frame: title, menus, tab bar, status bar

**Title and size.** "GST File Organizer v4.0" (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:71`); minimum 1200 × 800 (`:72`); opens at 1400 × 900 (`:73`) (B-R129). The window can be resized and maximised like any Windows window, but never made smaller than 1200 × 800. RAN e1.

> **Screen size.** 800 pixels is taller than the usable height of a 1366 × 768 laptop screen (still common in offices). Qt does not shrink a window below its minimum, so on such a screen the lower part of the window - at least the status bar and the bottom edge of every tab - would lie off the screen or under the Windows taskbar (READ `:72`; MEDIUM - not tried on a real 1366 × 768 screen; B-G68). How Windows display scaling (for example 125 %) changes this for Qt 5 is NOT SURE - how to check: open B on an office laptop at its normal scaling and see whether the status bar is visible.

**Menus** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:95-118`; RAN e1). The "&" in the code marks the letter used with the Alt key (Alt+F opens File). No other keyboard shortcuts exist (RAN e1: every shortcut string empty).

**What is checked when SCAN FILES (or RE-SCAN) is clicked** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:218-232`; RAN e3): an empty Source box gives the box "Please select a source folder first."; a path that is not an existing folder gives "Folder not found: <path>". Nothing else is checked at this point - the templates and target are checked only when processing starts. If the checks pass: all settings are saved (status "Settings saved"), both help cards fold shut, the scan log is emptied, "Scanning: <folder>" is written, SCAN FILES is greyed, and the scan runs in a worker thread (B-F34).

**What the SCAN LOG shows** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:230-269`; `core/file_parser.py:147-158`). Colours: normal light grey #d4d4d4, info blue #569cd6, success teal-green #4ec9b0, warning yellow #dcdcaa, error red #f44747 (`gui/views/setup_view.py:573-579`). RAN e2 on the placeholder folder (20 Excel files, of which one too small):

```text
Scanning: <source folder path>                    (blue)
Scan started...                                   (blue)
Finding Excel files...                            (grey)
Found 20 files, processing...                     (grey)
[1/20] AnnualReport-ClientA-Maharashtra-2024-25.xlsx      (grey, one line per file)
...
[20/20] random_notes.xlsx

SCAN RESULTS                                      (green)
========================================          (green)
Files found: 19                                   (blue)
Parsed: 18 (94.7%)                                (blue)
Unparsed: 1                                       (yellow when > 0)
Total size: 102.0 KB                              (blue)

Clients: 3                                        (blue)
Complete: 1 (33.3%)                               (green)
Incomplete: 2                                     (yellow when > 0)
Variations: 2                                     (yellow; line shown only when > 0)

FILE TYPES:                                       (blue)
Annual Report: 3                                  (grey, one line per type, A-Z)
GSTR-2B Reco: 3
GSTR-3B Export: 4
IMS Reco: 2
Sales: 4
Sales Reco: 2
```

Points to note: "Found 20 files" but "Files found: 19", because the too-small file is excluded from "Files found" (B-R29; B-G22); the code indents the result lines with two spaces (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:253-269`), but the spaces are lost on screen because each line is inserted as HTML (RAN e2, B-R137); the problem files themselves are never named - only "Variations: 2" (B-F9; B-G20); other possible lines are "No Excel files found" (empty folder), "Error displaying results: <error>" (red, `:315`) and "SCAN ERROR: <message>" (red, `:319`, together with the "Scan Error" box). With thousands of files the log becomes very slow, because every line is added to one ever-growing block of HTML (RAN by VW: 1,000 lines 5.6 s, 5,000 lines 136.6 s of frozen window time) (B-F7, B-R137; B-G56).

### 10.5 Step 2: Validation

**Purpose.** Shows the result of the scan, one row per client, and lets the user tick the clients to process, preview them (DRY RUN) or start processing (START) (B-F7, B-F8, B-F10, B-F11). Built by `ValidationView` (`gui/views/validation_view.py:15-447`); wired at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:134-135`.

**Layout.** Again a draggable splitter with the same grey style (`:30-35`), here with the larger share on the right (`:65-66`; RAN e1: left 537 px, table 797 px wide).

- **Left column - a scroll area** (`:38-53`): the orange "VALIDATION INSTRUCTIONS" box, the blue "SCAN SUMMARY" card, the green-outlined "READY TO PROCESS?" box.
- **Right column**: one green-outlined "CLIENT SELECTION" panel holding a green title band, a light-blue hint strip, a row of three selection buttons with a count on the right, and the client table, which takes the rest of the height.

### 10.6 Step 3: Processing

**Purpose.** Shows the progress and the step-by-step log of processing (creating the client folders, copying the files, making the ITC and Sales reports, writing the summary), lets the user start it here too, stop it, and clear the log. The DRY RUN preview from Step 2 is also written here (B-F11 to B-F16). Built by `ProcessingView` (`gui/views/processing_view.py:13-166`); wired at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:137-152`.

**Layout** (`:23-128`): one column, 12 px margins, 8 px spacing: a full-width green title band, a status line, a progress bar, a row of buttons (Start and Stop on the left, Clear Log on the far right), and the dark log, which takes all remaining height (RAN e1: 1374 × 625 px at the default size).

**DRY RUN output** (written here by `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:326-343`; RAN e2, exact):

```text
🧪 ════════ DRY RUN PREVIEW ════════            (blue)

📄 Would organize: AnnualReport-ClientA-Maharashtra-2024-25.xlsx   (grey, one per file)

```

The dry run checks only that at least one client is ticked; it does not check the templates, the target or the mode, and it promises both reports for every client - which is also what real processing does (B-R50, **[GST RULE]** which reports a client gets). "moved" is inaccurate: processing copies files (B-R42). The preview is appended to whatever is already in the log and stays above the next real run (RAN e2: the processing lines followed the preview in the same log).

**End of processing** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:373-410`; RAN e2): Start is re-enabled and Stop greyed; run history and settings are saved; the Step 4 list is rebuilt from disk; Step 3 gets a green dot and Step 4 an orange one; then the information box **"Processing Complete"** appears with the text

```text
Successfully processed 3/3 clients

Files organized in:
<the Target box text at that moment>
```

After OK the window moves to Step 4 and, on Windows only, Explorer opens the new "Annual Statement-..." folder (`:403-410`; READ - not runnable here). "Successfully processed" counts clients whose folders were made without an error, even when their reports failed (B-R60; B-G19 - RAN by the Section 3 writer, part a, B-F3 trace: with a folder given as the ITC template the ITC report failed and the box still said "Successfully processed 1/1 clients"). If the Target box was edited during the run, the box names the edited folder although the files went to the original one (RAN by MW e14; B-G28). Explorer opens the run folder of the first client whose folders were made (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:100-101, 201`; `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:404-410`).

**Processing error** (`:412-415`; RAN e3 with a target path that runs through an existing file): the red-cross box **"Processing Error"** shows the raw error text - "Cannot create target folder: [Errno 20] Not a directory: '<path>'"; the status bar says "Processing failed"; Start is re-enabled; **nothing at all is written to the Step 3 log**, and the tab dots do not change (RAN e3; B-G71).

### 10.7 Step 4: Extract & Refresh

**Purpose.** Lists the reports already made in the target folder, lets the user tick which ITC and Sales reports to refresh, runs the Power Query refresh (Power Query is Excel's built-in data-import feature; "refresh" makes each report re-read the client files) in Excel and reads the configured cells, writes the consolidated workbook and a text log into the run folder, and shows progress (B-F18 to B-F26). Built by `ExtractionView` (`gui/views/extraction_view.py:16-456`); wired at `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:154-172`; filled from disk by `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:419-504`.

**Layout** (`:28-102`): a full-width teal title band; below it a row with the "Extraction Options" box on the left (natural width; RAN e1: 315 px) and the "Clients" box stretching over the rest (1051 px), both 320 px tall at the default size; then a row with Start Extraction, Stop and (far right) Clear Log; a full-width progress bar; a status line; and the dark log filling the remaining height (RAN e1: 294 px). Both boxes are Qt "group boxes" (a frame with its title set into the top border), here with a 2-pixel teal #0099BC border and teal title (`:105-120, 148-163`).

**What the Step 4 log shows.** The worker's own lines (`gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py`): "Processing <client folder> / <version folder>..." (blue, `:68`); "Result: ITC: OK, Sales: FAIL" and similar - only the ticked types are named - green if at least one is OK, otherwise red (`:76-84`); "Creating consolidated report..." (blue, `:88`); "Report saved: PQ\_Extraction\_Report\_<YYYYMMDD\_HHMM>.xlsx" (green, `:93`) or "Report error: <error>" (red, `:95`); "Extraction complete: <x>/<n> clients processed" (green, `:98`) - x counts versions attempted, not successes; "Extraction stopped by user" (yellow, `:62`). Between them come the refresh code's own lines (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py`, 96 calls of `self._log`), **all in blue "info" colour, error lines included** (the function never passes a colour, `:30-37`): for example "Creating Excel instance...", "Opening Excel file: <name>", "Waiting for workbook to fully load...", "Loading... <i>/5 seconds", "Activating Excel window...", "Starting refresh sequence...", "→ Sending Alt key...", "✓ A key sent - Refresh All command executed", "Waiting for Power Query refresh to complete... (<w> seconds)", "Waiting... <i>/<w> seconds" (one line per second), "Checking for error dialogs...", "Error check <i>/5...", "Giving additional time for complex queries...", "Extended wait... <i>/<n> seconds", "Final error check...", "Saving workbook...", "✓ Workbook saved", "Closing workbook...", "Validating refresh results for report...", "Checking cell BB2 in Info sheet...", "❌ Cell BB2 is empty (None)" / "✅ Cell BB2 populated successfully: <value>" (B-F20; **[GST RULE]** ⚠ the check cell, B-R71), "✅ Refresh completed successfully" or "⚠️ Refresh completed with errors: <text>", "Opening file in read-only mode: <name>" (the file is in fact opened read-write, B-R101), "Processing sheet: '<sheet>'", "✓ <field> (<cell>) = <value>" for every cell read, "Extraction summary:", "✓ <field>: <value>" / "✗ <field>: None", and the long-path / open-retry advice lines ("💡 This usually means:", "- File is open in another program", ...). So **every extracted tax figure is printed in the on-screen log** and saved in the run folder's Extraction\_Log text file (B-F25; B-G64). Volume: a three-version run sent 541 lines to the log - 536 "info" (blue), 4 "success", 1 "error" - about 180 lines per report (RAN by the Section 3 writer, t24b; B-G56, B-G71). Each refresh-code line arrives with two leading spaces (`report_processor.py:37`), which the HTML insertion then drops (B-R137).

> **For many failures the reason is never shown on screen.** When Excel cannot be started (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:339-344` in the refresh, `:566-568` in the reading step), a cell cannot be read (`:542-545`; the screen later shows only "✗ <field>: None" in the extraction summary), no report file is found ("No ITC report found") or a report type was not ticked ("Not selected for processing"), or any other error stops the refresh steps or the report as a whole (`:332-337`, `:154-163`), the explanation goes only to the program log file (`:155, 333, 340, 548, 567` use `logger.error`, and `:504, 522, 543` use `logger.warning` - not the on-screen log; the "No ... report found" and "Not selected" texts are only stored in the result, `:50-68, 79-87`). If B was started with `launch_extractor.py`, there is no program log file at all (10.2), so these reasons are recorded nowhere (B-G44). Four kinds of reason do reach the screen, but only as ordinary blue lines among about 180 per report:
> 1. a failed refresh check ("❌ Cell BB2 is empty (None)", "⚠️ Refresh validation failed: ...", `:310-313, 611-629`; also "⚠️ Info sheet not found" and "❌ Validation error: ...", `:602, 635`; **[GST RULE]** ⚠ the check cell Info!BB2, B-R71) (RAN by the Section 3 writer, t24b);
> 2. the text of an Excel error pop-up, shown at the end of the refresh as "⚠️ Refresh completed with errors: <text>" (`:321-322`; the earlier line "⚠️ Error detected: <text>" / "⚠️ Late error detected: <text>" goes to the program log only, `:272, 295`) (RAN by the Section 3 writer, t26);
> 3. a workbook that cannot be opened, in the refresh or in the reading step: "First attempt failed - Error code: <code>", "Error details: <text>", "Second attempt failed: <text>", "❌ All attempts failed. Final error: <text>" and, when the error contains -2147352567, the advice lines "💡 This usually means:" ... (`:688-689, 701, 733-745`); also "❌ File does not exist: <path>" and "❌ Cannot access file: <error>" (`:644, 653`) (RAN VERIFY-B-S10 v2 with a fake Excel whose open always fails: all these lines arrived on the screen channel at level "info");
> 4. a missing sheet: one line "<field> = None (sheet not found)" for every field of that sheet (`:524-526`), or "<field> = None (sheet error)" when the sheet could not be read (`:550-552`; the error text itself goes only to the program log, `:548`) (RAN VERIFY-B-S10 v2; also RAN by the Section 3 writer, t22).
>
> [Corrected during verification - originally said that a workbook that cannot be opened and a missing sheet leave no reason on screen and that "only two kinds of reason" (refresh check, pop-up text) reach it; `_safe_open_workbook` (`:638-747`) and `_extract_data` (`:521-527, 547-552`) write their own lines through the same on-screen channel.] (B-G71.) RAN e2 (stub Excel that always fails - the open step is never reached): the on-screen log for each version showed only these seven lines, once for the ITC report and once again for the Sales report - "Creating Excel instance...", "Cleaning up Excel instance...", "COM uninitialized", "Waiting for file to be released...", "Creating new Excel instance for data extraction...", "Cleaning up extraction Excel instance...", "✓ COM uninitialized" - and then "Result: ITC: FAIL, Sales: FAIL"; the cause ("stub: no Excel COM on Linux") appeared only in the program log `gst_organizer.log` (12 ERROR lines: two per report, six reports) [wording of the line list clarified during verification; RAN again by VERIFY-B-S10 v1 with the same result]. The run then ended "Extraction complete: 3/3 clients processed" in green.

**While a refresh runs the user must keep their hands off the PC** (READ; B-F19, B-R67): for each report a visible, maximised Excel window comes to the front and the program types Alt+A, R, A into **whatever window has the keyboard focus**. Because B's own window stays responsive, a click on it (for example on Stop) or on any other program during these seconds can send the keystrokes to the wrong window (MEDIUM - not runnable here; B-G51, B-G62). If Excel could not be brought to the front after three tries, B types the keys anyway; that is noted only in the program log ("Could not activate Excel window, continuing anyway...", `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:226, 230`), while the screen log shows "Starting refresh sequence..." and "✓ A key sent - Refresh All command executed" as usual (READ `:234-249`). Excel error pop-ups that appear meanwhile are clicked away automatically - and so may be pop-ups of other programs whose title looks like an error, with a button whose text contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue" (RAN by the Section 3 writer with stand-in windows, t26; B-F26, B-G61). Nothing on screen warns the user about this.

**End of extraction** (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:549-561`; RAN e2): Start re-enabled, Stop greyed; Step 4 tab dot green; status bar "Extraction complete"; results saved to run history (under a key no screen reads, B-R120); the list is rebuilt from disk, so all ticks are cleared. **No message box, no count of failures**, and the window stays on Step 4. Errors outside the per-report handling (for example in the worker's own set-up) give the red-cross box "Extraction Error" with the raw error text (`:563-565`; READ; RAN e7 by calling the handler), with no status-bar change: the bar keeps its previous text, after an earlier extraction "Extraction complete" (RAN e7; also RAN by the Section 3 writer, t29). The error itself is not written to the Step 4 log (lines logged before it stay); an error before `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:86` jumps straight to `:36-41`, so that run then gets no consolidated workbook and no Extraction\_Log file, and the list is not rebuilt (READ).

Right, a wider teal-outlined box "Clients": a light-blue strip reading "No target folder configured." with a small blue "Refresh List" button at its right end; four buttons - blue "ITC Only", orange "Sales Only", green "Select All", plain grey "Deselect All"; and an empty table with a dark-blue header "Name | ITC | Sales | Refresh Status". Below the two boxes: a teal "Start Extraction" button, a bright red "Stop" (disabled but looks active), "Clear Log" at the far right; a light-grey progress bar "0%"; "Ready for extraction" in bold dark grey; and a near-black log panel filling the bottom third.

*After processing, with the placeholder clients.* The strip reads "Source: Annual Statement-211026 0637". The table shows three bold rows "ClientA-MH", "ClientB-GJ", "ClientC-KL", each with a small open-arrow and "1 version(s)" in grey, and under each an indented row "Version-211026 0637" with two tick squares and "Pending" in orange. After "Select All" all six squares are ticked.

*During extraction.* "Start Extraction" is grey; the status line reads "Processing 1/3: ClientA-MH / Version-211026 0637"; the bar still shows "0%"; the log shows blue lines such as "Processing ClientA-MH / Version-211026 0637...", "Creating Excel instance...", "Waiting for file to be released...".

*After the (failed) extraction.* Step 4's tab dot is green, the bar is full teal "100%", the status line and the status bar both say "Extraction complete"; every version row now shows **"Refreshed (21/10/26 06:37)" in green** and empty tick squares; the log ends with a red "Result: ITC: FAIL, Sales: FAIL", then "Creating consolidated report..." in blue, and "Report saved: PQ\_Extraction\_Report\_20261021\_0637.xlsx" and "Extraction complete: 3/3 clients processed" in green [colour of "Creating consolidated report..." made precise during verification; READ `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:88` 'info', and the screenshot]. No pop-up appears.

### 10.8 Every message box and picker

All 14 message boxes (13 different texts) are created in `gui/pyqt_main_window.py`; each is a standard Qt pop-up with one OK button, **modal** (the window cannot be used until OK is clicked), and an icon chosen by its kind: a yellow warning triangle ("warning"), a red circle with a cross ("critical") or a blue "i" ("information"). Their title is set by the code; there is no other wording, help link or "details" button. RAN e2 / e3 = the text was captured from B's real code by the recorder. *Screenshot description* (READ; the recorder replaced the real boxes, so none was drawn here - MEDIUM for the exact look on Windows): a small window titled, for example, "Warning", with the icon on the left, the message text beside it (several lines where the text has line breaks, as in boxes 9 and 13), and a single "OK" button at the bottom right; in light mode on a light-grey background, in dark mode with the program's dark colours (10.10).

**Pickers** (standard Windows file dialogs, `gui/views/setup_view.py:605-627`): "Select Source Folder" (folder), "Select ITC Template" and "Select Sales Template" (file, filter "Excel Files (\*.xlsx \*.xlsm)"), "Select Target Folder" (folder). None is given a starting folder, so each opens in the program's current folder or wherever the system last was, not at the path already in the box (READ; Qt behaviour, MEDIUM). **Messages that do not exist** (each a place where a user might expect one; READ unless marked):

- No question when the window is closed during a job: `closeEvent` (`:601-608`) saves and closes at once; the job is cut off and leaves partial output (B-G40). During processing: only an empty folder skeleton was left, no run history (RAN by MW e11). During an extraction: the window vanished, the program ended with exit code 0 and no message while the worker was inside a refresh, an **unrefreshed "\_Refreshed\_" copy** was left beside the report (which Step 4 will later show as "Refreshed"), and no consolidated workbook, no Extraction\_Log and no run history were written (RAN by the Section 3 writer, t34c; on Windows the visible Excel started by the refresh would most likely stay open with the copy loaded - MEDIUM, how to check: close B during a Step 4 refresh on a test PC and look for EXCEL.EXE in Task Manager). The Tkinter version at the split asked "Processing is still running. Stop and exit?" (`47a1492:gui/main_window.py:314-325`).
- No message when a second job of the same kind is refused - the three "already in progress" guards only write to the program log (`gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:59-61`, `processing_controller.py:259-261`, `extraction_controller.py:142-144`).
- No completion box and no failure count after extraction (`:549-561`; RAN e2).
- No message when the processing summary workbook could not be written (B-R94), when the Step 4 folder walk fails part-way (`:496-497`), or when settings / run history cannot be saved (program log only).
- No "are you sure" before Start (processing copies and writes many files) or before Stop.
- No tooltips (hover help) anywhere (RAN e1: none; RAN by the Section 3 writer, t33: 0 of 205 widgets have one; B-G72).
- **No error message at all when a screen action fails unexpectedly**: B has no "catch-all" error handler (`sys.excepthook`), so an error that nothing catches inside a button or menu handler makes the whole window vanish (B-G35). Example RAN e7: with a damaged `~/.gst_organizer/session_state.json` (a JSON list instead of named values; the window still opens), each of View > Dark Mode, File > Save Settings, SCAN FILES and closing the window stopped the program with "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'" at `models/cache_manager.py:47` (process aborted, which a console reports as exit code 134) and `settings.json` was not written. Other examples RAN by MW e10 and VW t3, and by the Section 3 writer (part a: a damaged `run_history.json` aborts the program at the end of processing, after all output was written) (B-G36).

Consequences (B-F34, B-R111): scanning, processing and extraction can all run at the same time; a re-scan during processing refills the Step 2 table while the job continues with its own list; DRY RUN during processing writes its preview into the same Step 3 log, interleaved with the live run (READ + RAN by MW e4); Step 4 "Refresh List" during an extraction rebuilds the list, so it no longer shows what is being worked on (READ). The same happens without any click when a processing run ends during an extraction: RAN by the Section 3 writer (t34b) - with an extraction held inside its first Excel wait, a scan and a full processing run both ran to the end; the end of processing rebuilt the Step 4 list onto the **new** run folder ("Source: Annual Statement-<new time>", no ticks), while the extraction, when released, wrote its consolidated workbook and Extraction\_Log into the **old** run folder; the window never said so (B-G74). Disabled red Stop buttons cannot be told apart from enabled ones (RAN e4; B-G70).

### 10.10 Layout approach and styling

**Layout approach.** Every screen is built in code (no designer files), with Qt **layout managers** - invisible arrangers that stack widgets in rows and columns and stretch them with the window - so nothing has a fixed pixel position. Steps 1 and 2 use a two-column draggable splitter with a scrolling left column; Steps 3 and 4 use a single column whose log stretches to fill the height. Margins are 20 px (Steps 1-2 outer), 12 px (Steps 3-4), spacing 8-12 px. Sections are drawn as "cards" (`ColoredSection`, `CollapsibleCard`) or framed group boxes (Step 4). The window cannot be made smaller than 1200 × 800 (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:72`); at that size Step 1 shows less (scroll), and Step 2's left column overflows sideways and needs a horizontal scroll bar (RAN e1 `shots/e1_tab1_min.png`). That minimum is taller than a 1366 × 768 laptop screen (10.3; B-G68).

**Three styling layers** (B-R144). (1) One program-wide stylesheet, light (`gui/theme/theme_manager.py:25-199`) or dark (`:201-405`), set on the whole application by `apply_theme` (`:414-419`) at start (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:66`) and on View > Dark Mode (`:596`). (2) Many small stylesheets typed into the views for individual widgets (almost every coloured element). (3) Five named button styles in the program-wide sheet - "primary" (blue), "success" (green), "warning" (orange), "danger" (red), "info" (teal; no widget uses it, B-R132). A widget's own or its parent's stylesheet wins over the program-wide one, which explains most styling defects below.

**Fonts and sizes** (READ; Windows fonts - Linux used look-alikes): "Segoe UI" (fallback Arial) 10 pt for all text (`gui/theme/theme_manager.py:29-32`); "Consolas" / "Courier New" 9 pt for the three logs and the scan summary. Title sizes: 16 pt welcome title; 14 pt "READY TO SCAN?" / "READY TO PROCESS?"; 13 pt Step 3/4 title bands; 12 pt card bands, CLIENT SELECTION band, SCAN FILES / RE-SCAN; 11 pt help-card headers, Start buttons, Step 3 status line, SCAN LOG header; 10 pt body text, Step 2 buttons, Step 4 status line; 9 pt hints, notes, file-pattern lines; 8 pt "Refresh List". Tabs: grey #e0e0e0 with 8 × 20 px padding, the chosen tab white with a 2-pixel blue underline, hovered tab #d0d0d0 (`theme_manager.py:37-52`). Table headers: dark blue #366092 with white bold text (`:154-160`), alternate rows #f7f7f7, selection blue #0078D4. Progress bars 22-26 px; buttons at least 24 px tall; scroll bars 12 px wide.

**Colour palette and what each colour means on screen** (READ; the same hex values are typed by hand in many places - the `COLORS` table at `theme_manager.py:10-22` meant for this is never used, B-R132; the comment at `:9` says "Color palette matching the old Tkinter UI"):

| Blue #0078D4 | EXCEL TEMPLATES card, welcome title, "Complete Only", "ITC Only", "Refresh List", tab underline, table selection, splitter hover |

### 10.11 The typical user workflow (what the user clicks, in order)

This is the sequence the screens are designed for, as traced end to end in RAN e2 (placeholders) plus the Windows-only parts by READ. Points where the screen does not help the user are marked ⚑.

**Before starting (outside the program).** The client files must be in one folder (sub-folders are ignored) and named exactly as the patterns on the Step 1 help card (**[GST RULE]** ⚠ B-R5 to B-R11); the ITC and Sales templates must exist (with their "Links" sheet, B-R53; B does not check for that sheet - without one, the Excel path adds an empty "Links" sheet and still reports success, B-G4). ⚑ The program does not say so, but on Windows it is safer to close Excel first: Step 3 takes over an Excel the user already has open, hides its windows and closes it at the end of each report (B-R96), and Step 4 types keystrokes into Excel (B-R67).

1. **Start the program**: open a console in the program folder and type `python main.py`. The window opens on "Step 1: Setup", with the last saved paths already filled in. (⚑ Without pywin32 no window opens - 10.2. ⚑ On a 1366 × 768 laptop screen the lower part of the 1200 × 800 minimum window is out of reach - 10.3.)
2. **Source folder**: type or paste the folder path into the first box. ⚑ The "Browse" button is invisible; clicking the blank space just right of the box opens the picker "Select Source Folder".
3. **Templates**: type or paste the ITC template path and the Sales template path (or click the blank space right of each box for the pickers "Select ITC Template" / "Select Sales Template").
4. **Target folder**: click the red **BROWSE** and choose the output folder in "Select Target Folder" (or type it).
5. **Mode and options**: keep **Fresh** (default) for a first run, or choose Re-Run / Resume (⚑ both just add a new Version folder in the most recently changed run folder - 10.4). Optionally tick "Include client name in brackets for Level 4 folders" and set "Max length" (⚑ the Max length is applied even when greyed out).
6. **Scan**: scroll the left column down and click **SCAN FILES** (⚑ below the visible part at the default size). The help cards fold away, the SCAN LOG fills with one line per file and the results, and the window jumps to "Step 2: Validation"; Step 1 gets a green dot, Step 2 an orange one; the status bar reads "Scan complete: <n> clients, <m> files, <size>".
7. **Review** on Step 2: read the SCAN SUMMARY; look at the colours in the client table (green complete, orange missing, red-orange other - ⚑ the instructions mention only two colours); ⚑ the missing and duplicate counts are numbers only - which types are missing is not shown; ⚑ the problem files counted as "Variations" are not listed anywhere.
8. **Choose clients**: every client is already ticked. Untick the ones not wanted, or use **Clear All** and tick some, or **Complete Only**.
9. *(Optional)* **DRY RUN**: the window jumps to Step 3 and lists what would be copied, and "Would create: ITC Report" / "Would create: Sales Report" for every client. Click the "Step 2: Validation" tab to go back.
10. **Start**: click **START** on Step 2 (⚑ the instructions say "Start Processing", which is the Step 3 button - both do the same). If a template or the target is missing, a "Warning" box names it; fix it on Step 1 and click START again. The window moves to "Step 3: Processing".
11. **Watch** Step 3: the status line shows "Client <i>/<N>: <client> | ETA: ...", the green bar fills client by client, and the log lists each step. **Stop** halts before the next client (⚑ no feedback; the run still ends with "Processing Complete").
12. **Finish processing**: the box "Processing Complete - Successfully processed <k>/<N> clients ... Files organized in: <target>" appears; click **OK**. The window moves to "Step 4: Extract & Refresh" (Step 3 dot green, Step 4 orange) and, on Windows, Explorer opens the new "Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>" folder. (⚑ "Successfully processed" also counts clients whose reports failed - read the log.)
13. **Choose reports** on Step 4: the list shows the client folders of one run folder ("Source: Annual Statement-...") with every square empty. Tick ITC and/or Sales per version, or click **ITC Only**, **Sales Only** or **Select All**. (⚑ The run folder shown is the one whose name sorts last, which is not always the newest - 10.7.) Optionally change the wait time, the file suffix (⚑ keep "\_Refreshed" in it) or tick "Skip refresh".
14. **Start Extraction**: click it. For each ticked report, Excel opens maximised, the refresh keystrokes are typed, the program waits, saves, and then reads the cells in a hidden Excel. ⚑ **Do not touch the keyboard or mouse** until the status says "Extraction complete" (about 39 s per report at the default wait, plus Excel start-up; B-R68).
15. **Finish extraction**: the status bar and status line say "Extraction complete"; the Step 4 dot turns green; the list is rebuilt (squares empty again) with "Refreshed (date)" against each version. ⚑ No box appears and failures are only visible as red "Result: ... FAIL" lines - and for many failures the reasons are not on screen at all (failed refresh checks, Excel pop-up texts, workbooks that could not be opened and missing sheets do appear, but only as blue lines among many others - 10.7) [corrected during verification - originally named only refresh checks and pop-up texts]. The consolidated workbook "PQ\_Extraction\_Report\_<YYYYMMDD\_HHMM>.xlsx" and "Extraction\_Log\_<YYYYMMDD\_HHMM>.txt" are in the run folder; ⚑ there is no button to open them - the user goes to the folder in Explorer.
16. **Close**: File > Exit or the window's close button. Settings are saved automatically (⚑ also if a job is still running - it is cut off without a question; during an extraction this leaves an unrefreshed "\_Refreshed\_" copy that Step 4 will later show as "Refreshed", and no consolidated workbook or log - 10.8).

**Common variations.**

- **Extraction on another day**: run `python launch_extractor.py` (or `python main.py` and click the Step 4 tab). Step 4 is filled at start-up from the last *saved* target folder; continue at step 13. (⚑ Started through `launch_extractor.py`, no program log is written, so the reasons for failed reports are kept nowhere - 10.2, 10.7.)

- **Re-extracting without refreshing again**: tick "Skip refresh (use existing refreshed files)" before Start Extraction (works only if the earlier copies were named with a suffix that begins with "\_Refreshed\_", as the default does, because the search pattern is "<report name>\_Refreshed\_\*.xlsx", `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:102`; B-F21) [corrected during verification - originally "works only with the default suffix"].
- **Saving the settings without scanning**: File > Save Settings (status "Settings saved").
- **Dark mode**: View > Dark Mode (partial, 10.10).

## SECTION 11: RECONSTRUCTION BLUEPRINT

This section is the plan for rebuilding project B (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2`, branch `main`, snapshot `b0e7d0e` of 09-02-2026, the PyQt5 program that calls itself "GST File Organizer v4.0") from scratch. It follows the six items of the author's audit method (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/Project_Audit_FINAL.md:146-157`): 11.1 Foundation, 11.2 Core logic build order, 11.3 Feature priority, 11.4 Known improvements, 11.5 Estimated complexity, 11.6 Suggested skills. 11.7 collects the decisions and material the rebuild needs from the author, and 11.8 lists the runs made for this section.

### 11.0 How to read this section

**What "rebuild" means here.** A rebuild that does everything B does today (the 34 features B-F1 to B-F34 and the 144 rules B-R1 to B-R144 of the registry, `/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_registry.md`), without B's known defects (the 82 gaps B-G1 to B-G82 of Section 7). Whether the merged program is built from B, from project A or from both is decided later (the comparison); nothing here chooses between A and B.

**What this section does and does not do.**
- It gives technical recommendations only: how to structure, order, test and harden the code.
- It never decides a GST rule. Anything that decides a tax figure, which return / table / sheet / cell a figure or file belongs to, a rate, limit or threshold, rounding, the financial year or tax period, GSTIN / PAN / state-code logic, ITC eligibility or reversal, or a due date is tagged **[GST RULE]**. The rebuild copies such rules exactly as the author approves them, and every improvement that touches one is limited to making the code do what the author's rule says (for example "make the cell wiring match the mapping table the author approves"). Nothing here says whether any GST rule is right.
- Values that change over time (package and Python versions, Excel behaviour and keyboard shortcuts, the 218-character path figure, template sheet names and cell positions, table numbers, file-name conventions, the state list) carry **⚠** so the author can check them.
- Where the author's own Standards 12 and 13 (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:817-898` and `:900-1061`) say something, this section states the fact and what each choice means for the rebuild; adopting a standard is the author's decision.

**The IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT of the audit method (item 4), and how it was applied.** Before any improvement was written, Section 8 (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B/S89.md`, sub-sections 8.1 to 8.9) was checked for that topic. Every row of 11.4.2 has a "Section 8 check" column. Where Section 8 explains why B's approach was chosen over the alternative that would otherwise look obvious, the row does NOT recommend that alternative: it gives a third option that keeps the original reason, or states the trade-off honestly. These cases are collected in 11.4.3 (trade-offs T1 to T16). Two constraints are binding everywhere below - the first is recorded as a "Constraint any change must respect" by the Section 8 writer (8.4.1); the second follows from the Section 8 inference of 8.4.4 (Section 8 does not label it a constraint) [Corrected during verification - originally "Two constraints recorded by the Section 8 writer"; READ `grep -n -i constraint S89.md`: only 8.4.1 records one]:
> - **The refresh must really have finished before the save.** The keystroke refresh is older than git (the 25-06-2025 compiled copy already used `SendKeys` and no `RefreshAll`; no commit of B ever contained `RefreshAll`, `DispatchEx` or `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, RAN by the Section 8 writer, 8.4.1). Standard 12 records, as tested, that a plain `RefreshAll()` followed at once by a save stored the old data (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`). This section therefore never recommends "a plain `RefreshAll` and then Save".
> - **Step 4 shows what is on disk.** The list of reports was built from a remembered list twice (`c258047`, `7e09e5c`, both B only (after the split)) and went stale both times; `b0e7d0e` (B only (after the split)) went back to walking the target folder (8.4.4: HIGH for this history, MEDIUM-HIGH for the preference "show what is on disk") [Corrected during verification - originally "(8.4.4, HIGH)"]. This section never recommends feeding Step 4 from a remembered list in the user profile.

**Evidence markers.**
- Every statement about the code cites `file:line` at `b0e7d0e` (repository-relative; the copy `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy` has the same line numbers). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **READ** = established by reading the code. **RAN** = executed on made-up inputs in a scratch copy. "RAN (me)" = run for this section in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S11/` (scripts `s1` to `s8`, listed in 11.8) [Corrected during verification - originally "`s1` to `s6`"; 11.8 lists s1-s8]; every run used `python -B` (no compiled files written), a redirected home and temporary folder, and the copy `proj/` was checked identical to B-copy afterwards. Other RAN marks name the section whose run is cited (for example "RAN, Section 7 r2", "RAN, Section 3 B-F12 trace").
- Anything that needs Excel through COM or Windows could not run here (Linux, no Excel, no pywin32) and is READ only. Section 3 and Section 7 runs used *stand-ins* (small fake modules with the pywin32 names that only record what B asks Excel to do); such a run proves B's Python control flow, never how real Excel behaves.
- Inferences carry **HIGH** (clear from the code, a comment or a commit message), **MEDIUM** (a reasonable inference) or **LOW** (speculation). "NOT SURE" always comes with a way to check.

**IDs.** Features `B-F…`, rules `B-R…` (registry), gaps `B-G…` (Section 7, register 7.10). Section 8 has no decision numbers; its sub-sections are cited (for example "8.4.1") and its summary table as "8.1 #n". Standard 12's "Excel through COM" rules are cited with the numbering of Appendix X1 (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B/X12.md`, X1.3.1) as **X1-R1a … X1-R8**, to keep them apart from registry rules. New labels in this section: foundation decisions `FD1`-`FD10` (11.1.1), structural rules `SR1`-`SR10` (11.1.5), contracts `K1`-`K10` (11.2.3), trade-offs `T1`-`T16` (11.4.3) and skills `SK1`-`SK14` (11.6). No feature, rule or gap ID was invented; findings of Sections 3, 5 and 10 that Section 7 did not number are cited by their place there (11.4.4).

**Commit labels.** The 12 commits shared by A and B (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`) are "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025". B's own five commits `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`, `7e09e5c` and `b0e7d0e` (07-02-2026 to 09-02-2026) are "B only (after the split)". B has one branch, `main` (a second name in the local checkout, `claude/pensive-feynman-0mz1aa`, points at the same commit `b0e7d0e` and holds no extra work; it was created when this audit's copy was prepared - Section 12, "Branch awareness") [Corrected during self-review - originally stated "one branch, `main`" without the second name, but Section 12 ("Branch awareness") revealed a second ref at the same commit].

**Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name or figure appears here; only placeholders such as `<Client A>` and made-up folder names such as `ClientA-DL` (used by the Section 3 runs) appear. File-name PATTERNS the code recognises are quoted exactly because they are code, not client data.

**Plain-English terms used in this section** (each is also explained where it first matters).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| rebuild / reconstruction | Writing the program again from a clean start, using this audit as the specification |
| feature dependency | Feature X "needs" feature Y when X cannot work, or cannot be tested, until Y exists (for example the refresh needs the reports) |
| build order, phase | The order in which parts are written; a *phase* is a group of parts finished and checked together before the next group starts |
| module, package | A *module* is one `.py` file; a *package* is a folder of modules with an `__init__.py` file |
| pure logic | Code that only calculates (names, rules, decisions) and touches no window, no Excel and no network, so it can be tested on any computer in seconds |
| unit test, characterization test, guard test | A *unit test* checks one small piece; a *characterization test* records what the code does today so that a change cannot alter it unnoticed; a *guard test* reads the source code and fails if a known bad pattern comes back |
| acceptance test | A check run by a person on a real office PC with Excel (needed for everything that drives Excel, which cannot run on this Linux computer) |
| contract, contract test | The agreed shape of data that one part hands to another (names, keys, folder patterns); a *contract test* checks that the writer and every reader agree |
| run plan | A frozen copy of everything a run needs (clients, files, templates, options, target, run time), taken when Start is pressed, so later clicks cannot change a run in progress |
| manifest | A small file, written during a run, that lists what has been done (each file copied, its size, each report and its outcome), so a stopped run can be resumed exactly and later steps can read what really happened |
| atomic save | Writing a file under a temporary name and then renaming it over the final name in one step (`os.replace`), so a crash never leaves a half-written file under the real name |
| run lock, single-instance lock | A marker (in memory or a small file) that says "a run is in progress" or "the program is already open", so a second run, or a second copy of the program, cannot start on top of it |
| COM, pywin32 | *COM* is Windows' way for one program to drive another (here Python drives Excel); *pywin32* is the Python package that provides it (`pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`, `win32process`) |
| GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx | Three ways to get an Excel through COM: take the one already running; ask for "an Excel", which may still be a running one; always start a separate, private one (Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx`) |
| lazy import | Loading a module only at the moment it is first needed, instead of when the program starts; a missing Windows-only package then stops only the step that needs it |
| context manager | A Python `with` block that always runs its clean-up (closing a workbook, quitting Excel), even after an error |
| openpyxl, Power Query, DataMashup | *openpyxl* reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel, but drops Power Query when it SAVES an existing workbook; *Power Query* is Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC/Sales templates; its queries live in a hidden part of the file called *DataMashup* |
| Links sheet, Info!BB2 | The template sheet into which Step 3 writes folder paths and file names; the cell whose value Step 4 treats as proof of a refresh [GST RULE] ⚠ |
| key presses (SendKeys), key tips | Pressing keyboard keys by program into whatever window has the keyboard focus; Excel's *key tips* are the Alt shortcuts (Alt, A, R, A = Data → Refresh All in an English Excel) ⚠ |
| foreground window, process id | The window that receives key presses; a *process id* (PID) is the number Windows gives each running program (each Excel is one process) |
| Qt, PyQt5, PySide6, QSS | *Qt* is the window toolkit; *PyQt5* (used by B) and *PySide6* (named by Standard 12) are two Python packages for it (Qt 5 and Qt 6); *QSS* is Qt's CSS-like style-sheet text for colours and fonts |
| QThread worker, signal | A *worker* is an object that runs a long job in a second line of work (a *QThread*) so the window stays responsive; a *signal* is Qt's message from the worker to the window |
| excepthook | Python's "last resort" for an error nothing else caught; Standard 13 sets it to write an error file and show a message box |
| launcher, `pythonw.exe`, `_runtime`, embeddable Python | Standard 13's start-up: a `.bat` file starts `pythonw.exe` (Python without a console window) from one shared, portable Python folder `_runtime` (python.org's *embeddable* package plus packages) |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%` | The per-user, per-PC settings folder of Windows (`C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local`), where Standard 13 keeps settings and logs |
| SKILL.md | A Claude Code *skill* file: written instructions, checks and examples that Claude loads whenever it does a certain kind of task, so a pattern learnt once is reused in later projects |
| pip, `requirements.txt`, wheel | *pip* is Python's package installer; `requirements.txt` is the list of packages (and minimum or exact versions) it installs from; a *wheel* is the ready-made file pip downloads for one package, one Python version and one operating system |
| console | The black text window a program started from a command prompt writes to; under `pythonw.exe` there is none, so `print()` shows nothing |
| log levels, rotating log | A log line's level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR) says how important it is; a *rotating* log starts a new file at a size limit and keeps only a few old files |
| UTF-8, code page (cp1252) | Two ways of storing text as bytes; UTF-8 can store every character (✓, ❌, ₹), the older Windows code page cannot, so such lines are lost |
| mapped drive, UNC path | A *network share* reached by a drive letter (for example `Z:`) or by its *UNC path* `\\server\share\…` |
| fake COM, offscreen Qt | A *fake COM* object records the calls the code would make to Excel, so the call order can be tested on Linux; *offscreen* Qt draws windows in memory on a computer without a screen |
| mutation check | Deliberately putting an old bug back into a scratch copy and running the tests to see whether one fails |
| git pickaxe (`git log -S`) | A search of the whole history for every commit that added or removed a given text |
| JSON | A plain-text file format for settings and records (B's `settings.json`, `run_history.json`, `session_state.json`) [row added during verification] |
| glob, stem | A *glob* is a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`; a file's *stem* is its name without the extension [row added during verification] |
| `CoInitialize()` / `CoUninitialize()` | The pywin32 calls that open and close a thread's COM connection; Standard 12 wants the closing call only after the function that used Excel has returned [row added during verification] |
| Qt slot | A function that Qt runs when something happens (a button click, a signal from a worker) [row added during verification] |
| exit code | The number a program hands back when it ends: 0 = normal, 1 = B's own "missing module" / "critical error" exit, 134 = aborted by the system (what a Linux shell shows for an abort) [row added during verification] |
| 8.3 short name | The old DOS-style short form of a long Windows path (for example `ANNUAL~1`), which Windows may or may not keep for each folder [row added during verification] |
| escaping (log text) | Turning characters such as `<` and `>` into codes (`html.escape`) so a log window shows them instead of treating them as formatting [row added during verification] |
| schema check | A written list of the expected names, types and allowed values of a settings file, checked when the file is read [row added during verification] |
| test fixture, smoke test | A *fixture* is a piece of test set-up shared by many tests (for example a temporary home folder); a *smoke test* only checks that the program, or every module, can start or be imported [row added during verification] |
| environment marker, `.pth` file | An *environment marker* is a condition after a line of `requirements.txt` (for example `; sys_platform == 'win32'` = install only on Windows); a `.pth` file is a small file Python reads at start-up that adds folders to its search path (pywin32 ships one) [row added during verification] |
| Decimal, `data_type`, `data_only` | *Decimal* is Python's exact decimal-number type (what COM may hand back for a currency cell); in openpyxl, `cell.data_type = 's'` marks a cell as text and `load_workbook(..., data_only=True)` reads the values Excel last saved instead of the formulas [row added during verification] |
| `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended` | An option of Excel's open command that skips the "open as read-only?" question some workbooks ask (Standard 12 asks for it) [row added during verification] |

### The blueprint in brief (for the author)

1. **Decide ten things before writing code** (11.1.1): the window toolkit (stay with Qt; PyQt5 or PySide6 is your call), how users start the program, the Python version, where packages come from, the refresh method, which Excel the program uses, whether the window must open without pywin32, whether the Step 4 launcher stays, where settings and logs live, and the GST data (patterns, cells, templates) the rebuild copies.
2. **Build from the inside out** (11.2): first the author-owned data, the start-up gate and the error log; then the pure rules (file names, clients, names, the run plan, the Links values, the consolidated look-up, the choice of run folder); then file work without Excel; then one Excel layer; then the refresh; then the windows. Every phase ends with tests; everything that drives Excel ends with an acceptance test on an office PC. B has no tests at all (Appendix X3.1), so the first tests are characterization tests run against B's own code.
3. **Essential features** (11.3, Tier 1): start-up and error reporting, the four paths, scanning and recognising files, the client list, organising files, the two reports, run progress and Stop, background jobs, finding the reports for Step 4, the refresh with its success check, the naming of refreshed copies, extraction, the consolidated workbook and an error log. Nice-to-have (Tier 3): the v3 settings import, the per-client name option, EXPORT LIST, the dry run, run history and "Last Run", dark mode, the tab dots, the Step 4 launcher and the help texts. The broken old entry point (B-F31) is not carried over.
4. **Fix what Section 7 found, without undoing what Section 8 explains** (11.4): for example the 9 columns of the consolidated workbook that today show another cell's value are made to follow the mapping table the author approves by looking values up by their exact name (RAN me, s2: 22 of 22 columns hold the cell their configuration names, instead of 13 of 22) - which cell is right stays the author's call [GST RULE] ⚠ - while the editable cell-mapping file stays (8.3.4). Sixteen places where Section 8 records a reason for B's way are handled as trade-offs (11.4.3).
5. **Size of the work** (11.5): 6 features rated COMPLEX (3+ hours each), 12 MODERATE, 15 SIMPLE, 1 not carried over. The COMPLEX ones are start-up (B-F1), recognition (B-F6), the organiser (B-F12), the ITC report mechanism (B-F13, which the Sales report then reuses), the refresh (B-F19) and the consolidated workbook (B-F23). A rough total of 37-87 hours of AI-assisted work, plus cross-cutting work and the office-PC acceptance sessions (an inference, LOW-MEDIUM confidence).
6. **Reusable skills** (11.6): 14 skill ideas, from "Excel through COM session" to "one naming rule, one finder" and "rewrite with a feature list" - the last two are lessons B's own history paid for (Section 12E.6).
7. **What the author must decide or supply** (11.7): 40 items, from the window toolkit to blank copies of the two templates; 13 of them are [GST RULE] matters or touch one, and the rebuild decides none of them.

No library beyond the ones above is needed for the improvements of 11.4: atomic saves (`os.replace`), rotating logs (`logging.handlers`), escaping log text (`html.escape`), warnings into the log (`logging.captureWarnings`) and JSON schema checks (written by hand with the standard `json` module and the settings dataclass; the separate `jsonschema` package is not part of Python's standard library and is not needed) are in Python's standard library [Corrected during verification - originally "JSON schema checks are in Python's standard library", which could be read as the `jsonschema` package]; window ownership (`win32process`) is part of pywin32; a single-instance lock (`QLockFile`), a bounded log view (`QPlainTextEdit.setMaximumBlockCount`) and number-aware table sorting (`QSortFilterProxyModel`, sort roles) are part of Qt (RAN me, s6: all three present in PyQt5 5.15.11; a second `QLockFile` on the same file was refused).

#### 11.1.5 Project structure

B's layering (`core/` · `utils/` · `models/` · `gui/` with views, controllers and theme · `power_query_extractor/`, Section 8.3.1) is sound in outline; its weak points are values typed in several places (Section 5.18; 8.7.4), package files that load the whole window and switch off all warnings (8.8.1), a main window that holds logic of its own (8.3.5), the Excel-only import on the start-up path (8.3.2), Excel code mixed with pure rules (`core/excel_handler.py` holds the COM session, the openpyxl fallback, the summary workbook and the Links values), and two open-with-fallback routines from the two-program era (8.4.10, 8.5.2). The structure below keeps the layering, fixes those points, and matches the `config\ core\ gui\` layout Standard 13 shows (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:919-920`).

```text
<App>\
├── Run <App>.bat                 ← Standard 13 launcher (only if FD2 adopts Standard 13)
├── main.py                       ← Standard 13 first lines; start-up gate (B-F1); opens the window; optional "start on Step 4" argument (FD8)
├── requirements.txt              ← exact versions of the packages the app imports (no pytest)
├── requirements-dev.txt          ← pytest and other developer tools
├── pytest.ini                    ← [pytest] / pythonpath = . / testpaths = tests
├── config\                       ← AUTHOR-OWNED DATA, one place per value (SR2, SR7)
│   ├── file_patterns.py          ← B-R5..B-R13 (patterns, types, example names) [GST RULE] ⚠; B-R24, B-R25 [GST RULE] ⚠
│   ├── states.py                 ← B-R21, B-R22 [GST RULE] ⚠
│   ├── folders.py                ← B-R31, B-R34, B-R35 (folder names); B-R37 (type → folder) [GST RULE]; B-R32 limits
│   ├── template_links.py         ← B-R53, B-R54, B-R55 (Links cells), B-R71 (Info!BB2) [GST RULE] ⚠
│   ├── extraction.py             ← B-R73..B-R81 [GST RULE] ⚠ with the "HOW TO EDIT" text (8.3.4); validated at load (B-G78)
│   └── app_defaults.py           ← 35, 15-100, 10 s, 5-120 s, suffix, 218 ⚠, waits, retries, colour roles, texts
├── core\                         ← PURE LOGIC: no window, no Excel; unit-tested anywhere
│   ├── recognition.py            ← B-F6 parsing, reasons for every problem file (B-F9), ambiguity flags
│   ├── clients.py                ← client keys, state codes, completeness, statistics (B-R17, B-R21..B-R29)
│   ├── naming.py                 ← ONE name normaliser for folders, copies, reports, organisation report (B-R19, B-R20, B-R32, B-R40, B-R51)
│   ├── run_plan.py               ← frozen run plan; pre-flight: name clashes, folder clashes, path lengths, templates (K2, K9)
│   ├── links_data.py             ← which value goes to which Links cell (B-R54..B-R57) [GST RULE] ⚠
│   ├── consolidation_layout.py   ← exact-key look-up, reasons beside "Missing", value classes (B-R83, B-R86..B-R90)
│   ├── run_folders.py            ← "which run folder, which Version folder" from the date in the name (B-R38, B-R39; T6)
│   ├── refresh_naming.py         ← refreshed-copy names: make, recognise, validate the suffix (B-R61..B-R63; K4, K5)
│   └── statuses.py               ← per-file, per-report, per-client and per-run outcomes with reasons
├── services\                     ← FILE WORK WITHOUT EXCEL (openpyxl, shutil, json)
│   ├── scanner.py                ← one listing, one stat and 8-byte read per file (12E.2 #19)
│   ├── organiser.py              ← copies under temporary names, backups outside linked folders, manifest (B-F12)
│   ├── summary_workbook.py       ← B-F15 (atomic save)
│   ├── consolidated_workbook.py  ← B-F23 (incremental results, atomic save)
│   ├── step4_discovery.py        ← disk walk of the target (8.4.4), run in a worker
│   ├── settings_store.py         ← B-F27 (schema, atomic save, merge on save)
│   ├── run_history.py            ← B-F17 / B-F25 (only if kept, 11.3)
│   └── paths_and_logging.py      ← APP_DIR, per-user folder, log set-up, error files (B-F32)
├── excel\                        ← WINDOWS + pywin32 ONLY; imported lazily (SR5); acceptance-tested on an office PC
│   ├── session.py                ← one private Excel per run; the X1 rules as a context manager (T2)
│   ├── open_workbook.py          ← ONE open routine keeping every fallback that was met in use (8.4.10), each acceptance-tested
│   ├── powerquery_check.py       ← DataMashup check before any openpyxl save of a workbook the app did not create (T3)
│   ├── report_builder.py         ← B-F13, B-F14
│   ├── refresh.py                ← B-F19 (trigger per T1), success records, time limits (T12)
│   ├── dialogs.py                ← B-F26, restricted to the program's own Excel (T4)
│   └── extract.py                ← B-F22 (reader per T5)
├── gui\                          ← WINDOWS AND BUTTONS ONLY (Qt)
│   ├── main_window.py            ← wiring only (SR1); close handling; run lock shared by all jobs
│   ├── workers.py                ← the QThread worker pattern of B (8.7.5), once, for all three jobs
│   ├── theme.py                  ← colour roles, light and dark QSS (SR10)
│   ├── views\  setup.py  validation.py  processing.py  extraction.py   ← B-F3..B-F11, B-F16, B-F18, B-F24
│   └── widgets\  log_view.py  collapsible_card.py                    ← bounded, escaped log (B-G56, B-G65); B-F33
└── tests\                        ← unit, contract, guard and characterization tests (11.1.6)
```

**Structural rules** (each follows from a finding; READ):

| # | Rule | Why (evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| SR1 | No rule, name, cell or decision lives in a window file; windows only show and collect. | 8.3.5 (HIGH): `gui/pyqt_main_window.py` is 608 lines and holds the dry run (`:326-343`), the scan-statistics text (`:244-316`), the Step 4 disk walk (`:419-504`) and the tab dots (`:567-590`); its own docstring calls it "Thin" (`:2`) |
| SR2 | Every value in one place. | Section 5.18 and 8.7.4: the default 35 typed in seven places, the wait 10 in five, the suffix `_Refreshed_{timestamp}` in five, `Annual Statement-` in three (RAN verification grep: all four counts confirmed), six places that decide which extensions count as Excel, using four different sets of extensions (5.18) [Corrected during verification - originally "six different rules"; three of the six places use the same set `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.xlsm`], the type → folder table twice with a disagreement for the Annual Report (B-R13, B-R37) |
| SR3 | Package `__init__.py` files stay empty; no re-export lists. | 8.8.1 (HIGH, RAN): `gui/__init__.py:7` loads the whole window, so importing any small `gui` module needs PyQt5 and pywin32; `core/__init__.py` loads `core.excel_handler`, which switches off every Python warning; none of the re-exports is used by any file; `a62d3cc` (B only (after the split)) broke start-up because `gui/__init__.py` still named a deleted file |
| SR4 | A frozen run plan instead of state read live from the window. | B-G28 (Step 4 uses the last saved target, processing the last scan), B-G75 (the worker rewrites the window's scan data), B-G74 (nothing is locked during a run) |
| SR5 | Excel code in its own layer, imported lazily; one open routine that keeps every fallback. | 8.3.2 (HIGH): the unguarded import became a start-up requirement only because the programs were merged; 8.4.10 (HIGH): the long-path fallbacks were met in use; 8.5.2 (HIGH): two open routines exist only because the two programs grew their own (`core/excel_handler.py:264-306` vs `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:638-747`) |
