#### 11.1.6 The test foundation

B has no tests, and never had any: no committed path contains "test", no test code was ever added by any of its 17 commits, and the only trace is the commented `# pytest>=7.0.0` (`requirements.txt:11@edac6a3`, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) that `c258047` (B only (after the split)) removed (RAN, Appendix X3.1 T1-T10; T1 re-RAN in verification: `git log --name-only --format= B/main | sort -u | grep -i test` gives no output). The test foundation therefore starts from nothing.

1. **Set up first:** `pytest.ini` as Standard 13 shows it (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:944-947`); a shared test fixture that points the home folder, the temporary folder and `%LOCALAPPDATA%` at a temporary directory for every test (the Section 7 runs pointed `HOME` and `TMPDIR` into their run folder, Section 7.12, and so did the runs of this section, 11.8, so that B's settings folder `~/.gst_organizer` and its `gst_excel_temp` folder landed in scratch) [Corrected during verification - originally "every audit run here had to redirect `HOME` and `TMPDIR`", which 7.12 states only for Section 7's runs]; `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` for window tests.
2. **Characterization tests first, against B's own code.** Before anything is rebuilt, record what B does today on made-up inputs, so the rebuild can be compared with it line by line. The audit's own scripts already show what to record (Appendix X3.3: 66-70 file names, a fake source tree, the consolidator, the settings round trip); they "prove facts for the audit; they assert nothing" (X3.3) - turning them into tests is the first job. Order by Appendix X3.4's bands: Band 1 (B-F23, B-F6, B-F12, B-F13/B-F14 value preparation, B-F18 folder choice, B-F19/B-F20/B-F26 logic with fake COM, B-F1 import checks), then Band 2, then Band 3. Where a test pins a [GST RULE] ⚠ behaviour (⚠ added during the completeness check - these values change over time; Appendix X3.6: the six patterns, the expected types, the state table and fallback, the destination table, the Links cells, the BB2 check, the 22 mappings), it pins the author's rule as approved; it does not judge it.
3. **Turn every defect of B's history into a test** (Appendix X3.5): the consolidator marker test (s2 of this section), "import the main window module on a computer without pywin32" (`c258047`), "process a folder with one mis-named file and read the Variations sheet" (`c258047`), "migrate a sample v3 cache" (`c258047`), "count the EXPORT LIST button's receivers" (`c258047`), "import every package and entry point" (`a62d3cc`), "render Step 1 offscreen and compare the Browse buttons' text colour with their background" (`7e09e5c`), "create `Annual Statement-311225 1000` and `Annual Statement-211026 0335` and check which is chosen" (`b0e7d0e`) - the commits `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `7e09e5c` and `b0e7d0e` named in this item are all B only (after the split); the defect the s2 marker test catches came in with `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025, Appendix X3.5). After each fix, put the old bug back into a scratch copy and check that a test fails (a mutation check).
4. **Contract tests** for K1-K10 (11.2.3) before the parts on both sides are finished.
5. **Guard tests** that read the source and fail when a known bad pattern comes back: `GetActiveObject` (B-G63); `warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')` (B-G31); a pywin32 import outside `excel\` (B-G32); `insertHtml` of unescaped text (B-G65); `setStyleSheet` with a colour outside `gui\theme.py` (SR10); a file opened for writing without `encoding=` (8.7.3); a module-level dictionary written by a worker (B-G76).
6. **A fake-COM harness** (stand-ins that record calls, as Sections 3 and 7 used, `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S3b/stubs/`) to test the ORDER of Excel calls on any computer: private Excel, prompts off until after `Quit()`, `Quit()` in `finally`, `CoUninitialize()` after the Excel function returns.
7. **An acceptance checklist for the office PC** (everything that cannot run on Linux): each X1 rule per Excel session (Appendix X1.3.6); the refresh-method comparison (T1); which dialogs really appear (T4); read-only and locked files (B-G53); long paths and `\\?\` prefixes (B-G54); `.xlsm` / `.xltx` templates (B-G30, B-G66); what `.Value` returns for error, currency and date cells (B-G11, B-G43); `WScript.Shell` (11.1.2); display scaling (B-G68); the NOT SURE items of Section 7.12 and Section 9.10. Sections 7 to 9 give a "how to check" for each.

#### 11.2.4 Two rules for the order of work

1. **Pure before Excel, Excel before windows.** Everything in Phases 0-2 can be tested on any computer; Phases 3-4 need an office PC; Phases 5-7 are only presentation. This keeps the risky Excel work small and well defined (MEDIUM, an engineering inference from the shape of B's code and its gaps).
2. **The characterization tests against B come before any fix.** Every intended change from B (each row of 11.4.2 that changes a result) is then visible as a failing characterization test that the author approves or rejects, instead of a silent difference. This is how lesson 2 of 12E.6 ("a rewrite needs a feature list") is applied to behaviour as well as features (HIGH that B's rewrite lost behaviours silently: at least twelve v3 behaviours disappeared in `c258047` / `a62d3cc`, both B only (after the split), 12C.5).

### 11.3 Feature priority

**How the tiers were decided.** Tier 1 (essential): without it the program cannot do its job (organise a client's GST files, build the two reports, refresh them and gather the figures), or its absence would silently produce wrong output. Tier 2 (important): used in ordinary runs or protecting against mistakes, but the main results could still be produced without it. Tier 3 (nice-to-have): convenience, appearance or one-time use; B itself shows that several of these are barely used (a button with no receivers, an option no screen can switch on). The evidence for each row is given; usage figures are not available (B records none), so "used" means "on the normal path of a run" (READ, Section 3 traces). Three features are split because their parts differ in importance (B-F21, B-F25, B-F33). The author may move any feature; 11.7 lists the questions that decide the doubtful ones. Inside each tier the rows follow the workflow (start-up, Step 1 to Step 4, then cross-cutting parts), not a further ranking; where a finer order of importance is needed, Appendix X3.4 ranks the features 1 to 22 by risk (silent wrong output, HIGH gaps, client figures) [sentence added during verification - the audit method asks to "rank features by importance"].

**Tier 1 - essential (17 features)**

| Feature | Why essential (evidence) |
|---|---|
| B-F1 Start-up and dependency checks | Nothing runs without it; today a missing package stops the program before any window, with advice that names the wrong package (B-G32, B-G34; RAN Section 3 B-F1) |
| B-F32 Application log file | The only place where most failure reasons are recorded today (Section 10 U3: for many Step 4 failures the reason goes only to the program log); needed to support users |
| B-F3 Setup: source, target, templates | Every step starts from these four paths (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:196-214, 345-361`) |

| B-F12 Organise files into client and category folders | The tool's first purpose; it decides the output layout every later step reads (K3); copy, never move (8.4.9, HIGH) |
| B-F13 Create ITC report from template | The tool's second purpose (8.4.8: Python links the files, the template does the GST work) |
| B-F14 Create Sales report from template | As B-F13 (the same mechanism) |

### 11.4 Known improvements (from the Section 7 gaps)

#### 11.4.1 Method

1. Every one of the 82 gaps of the Section 7 register (7.10) has one row in 11.4.2, in the register's order, grouped by the Section 7 sub-section it comes from (7.1 to 7.7). Severities are copied from 7.10.
2. Before writing each row, Section 8 was checked for that topic (column "Section 8 check"). "—" means Section 8 records no reason for B's way. Where Section 8 records a reason, the improvement keeps that reason; the 16 cases where this changes the obvious fix are explained as trade-offs T1 to T16 in 11.4.3.
3. Improvements are technical only. Where a gap touches a [GST RULE], the improvement only makes the code do what the author's rule says, show what it did, or check the author's configuration; the rule itself is listed under "The author decides".
4. "RAN me sN" refers to the runs of this section (11.8). Everything else in the "Improvement" column is a design recommendation (an inference; MEDIUM unless stated), not a fact about B.

#### 11.4.3 Trade-offs where Section 8 records a reason for B's way

Each case below would have an "obvious" fix that Section 8 shows the author avoided, or chose against, for a reason. The rebuild does not simply reverse those choices. For each: what B does, the reason Section 8 records, the alternative that looks obvious, and what this section suggests instead (a third option) or the honest trade-off.

| # | Topic (gaps) | B's way and the reason Section 8 records | The obvious alternative | Suggested instead / the trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | How the refresh is triggered and confirmed (B-G6, B-G51, B-G57, B-G62) | Key presses into a visible Excel plus fixed waits, because that is what a person does and it updated the figures (8.4.1, MEDIUM); what failed with other methods is lost (LOW); "Keep it visible to avoid issues" (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:181`) | Standard 12's COM sequence (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`); and never "a plain `RefreshAll` and then Save", which Standard 12 itself records as storing old data | Do not decide on paper. Put both triggers behind one interface (`excel\refresh.py`: "refresh this workbook and report what happened") and run a side-by-side check on an office PC with copies of the real templates and test clients: refresh each report both ways and compare all 22 extracted cells with a manual refresh. Keep the visible Excel if prompts (privacy levels, credentials, missing source) appear only there. Whatever wins, success is decided before saving (B-G6) and the run has time limits (T12). The honest cost of keeping key presses: an unlocked, untouched PC, English key tips ⚠ and about 39 s per report; the honest risk of the COM sequence: it is untested on these templates (8.10 #1-#2) |
| T2 | Which Excel the program drives (B-G63, B-G57, B-G38) | Step 3 first attaches to a running Excel (`core/excel_handler.py:110-115`) to save start-ups and avoid two Excels on the same files (8.4.2, MEDIUM); leaving the user's Excel open was never finished (HIGH) | A new `DispatchEx` Excel per report, as Standard 12 asks (`:851-855`) - which would make B slower still (B-G57) | One private `DispatchEx` Excel per run, reused for every report of the run: it keeps the speed reason (one start-up per run instead of two per client in Step 3 and two per report in Step 4) and never touches the user's Excel; "two Excels on the same files" is prevented by the run lock (B-G74) and by never closing workbooks the program did not open. Trade-off: a long-lived Excel may slow down or leak memory over many reports - restart it every N reports if the office PC shows that (MEDIUM; N to be found in the acceptance test) |
| T3 | pywin32 at start-up and the openpyxl fallback (B-G32) | The unguarded import became a start-up requirement only through the merge (8.3.2, HIGH, unintended); but it also keeps the openpyxl fallback, which strips Power Query, unreachable (Appendix X1 finding 1, HIGH) | "Guard the import and let the window open without pywin32" - which would make the openpyxl fallback reachable and silently damage templates (`core/excel_handler.py:219-262`; RAN Appendix X1 F1: the `customXml` part was gone) | Import the Excel layer lazily AND keep an explicit gate: on Windows, a missing pywin32 is reported at start-up with the fix; Steps 3 and 4 are disabled with a reason rather than falling back; openpyxl never saves a workbook it did not create when that workbook holds `DataMashup` (Standard 12 `:846-850`). Whether Steps 1-2 should work on a PC without pywin32 is the author's choice (9.12 #1) |
| T4 | Closing Excel's error dialogs (B-G61) | Needed because a key-press refresh returns nothing and Excel's dialogs block the next COM call (8.4.7, MEDIUM) | Remove the closer | Keep a closer only while key presses stay, restricted to windows of the program's own Excel process; record the dialog's text and fail the report rather than pressing "Yes"; if a dialog cannot be closed, the time limit (T12) ends only the program's own Excel. Cost: a report that a dialog interrupts fails instead of carrying on - slower, but nothing outside the program is touched |
| T5 | Reading the figures through a second Excel (B-G57) | Read the figures exactly as saved, from a clean Excel the key presses could not disturb (8.4.6, MEDIUM); why not openpyxl is not recorded (8.10 #6) | openpyxl, which Standard 12 says is fine for reading (`:827`) | An option to verify, not a recommendation: on an office PC, read the same refreshed copies both ways (openpyxl with `data_only=True` returns the values Excel saved) and compare all 22 cells; if they always agree, the second Excel can go; if not, read in the run's private Excel (T2) |
| T6 | Which run folder Step 4 shows (B-G12, B-G28, B-G55, B-G58) | Walk the disk every time; a remembered list went stale twice (8.4.4, HIGH / MEDIUM-HIGH) | Feed Step 4 from the run history or from the last processing run | Keep the disk walk (in a worker, B-G58); read the date from each `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` name instead of sorting the text (RAN me, s3), list names that do not parse separately instead of letting them win, show which folder is used and let the user choose another (12C.7 #3) |
| T7 | Minute-stamped, day-first names (B-G27, B-G81) | Keep every run; day-first is how the office reads dates (8.4.12, MEDIUM) | Year-first names (`YYMMDD`) that sort as text, or seconds in every name | Keep the names as they are and fix the readers (T6); on a name clash add a counter instead of overwriting. Trade-off: a counter or seconds make names a few characters longer, which matters for long paths (8.4.10) |
| T8 | Long-path tricks (B-G54) | 218-character limit, 8.3 short names and `\\?\` prefixes, each added after a real failure (8.4.10, HIGH) | Drop the tricks and rely on Windows' long-path setting | Keep every fallback in the one open routine (SR5), each acceptance-tested on the office PCs, and add a pre-flight that warns before any copy when a planned path exceeds the limit ⚠. Honest limit: 8.3 names often do not exist on network shares, and which Excel versions accept `\\?\` paths is NOT SURE - check on the office PCs |
| T9 | The worker rewrites the window's scan data (B-G75, B-G13) | The simplest way to make the Links cells name the copies that exist (8.4.13, HIGH) | Stop writing back (and the Links cells would name files that are not there) | Keep the purpose with a copy map (source name → copy name) in the run plan (K2), handed to the report builder; the window's data stays unchanged |
| T10 | Configuration in Python files the author edits (B-G78, B-G52) | The author edits rules with an AI assistant, guided by "HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE" (8.3.4, MEDIUM) | A settings screen or a JSON/Excel configuration file | Keep the Python files and their instructions; add validation when they load and a printed "what the program will use" summary; a screen only if the author asks (8.10 #10) |
| T11 | All warnings switched off (B-G31) | To hide openpyxl's console warnings (8.4.17, MEDIUM) | Remove the switch and let warnings print | Route warnings into the log (`logging.captureWarnings(True)`) and silence only the known openpyxl messages; under Standard 13 there is no console at all |
| T12 | Retries, fixed sleeps, no time limits (B-G39, B-G57) | Each sleep and retry answers a real failure ("Call was rejected by callee"; comments "Increased from 3 to 5", 8.4.11, HIGH) | Remove the sleeps | Keep the retries; keep tuned waits as minimums while key presses stay; replace waits by completion checks where T1 allows; add an overall time limit per report and a Stop that is checked inside every wait |
| T13 | Three modes over per-run Version folders (B-G13) | The modes probably predate the Version folders (8.4.16, LOW-MEDIUM); Version folders keep every run (8.4.12) | Drop the Version folders so that the modes work | Keep the Version folders; the author defines what each mode means; the run plan and its manifest implement exactly that (8.10 #9) |
| T14 | Fallback state code and raw-text client key [GST RULE] ⚠ (B-G16) | Never stop a scan because of an unexpected spelling (8.4.15, MEDIUM) | Normalise or reject unknown spellings | Keep "never stop"; show every fallback and every near-identical key as a warning on Step 2; any merging is the author's rule |
| T15 | One window for both programs (FD8, B-F30) | One workflow, one settings store; the separate extractor never found the organiser's settings (8.3.2, MEDIUM-HIGH) | Split Step 4 back into its own program so that Steps 1-2 need no pywin32 | Keep one window; solve the pywin32 problem with T3; a direct Step 4 start is a start option |
| T16 | The window toolkit (FD1) | Tkinter was replaced for thread-safe updates, style sheets and a cleaner structure (8.2.2, MEDIUM-HIGH); PyQt5 rather than PySide6 is unexplained (LOW) | Go back to Tkinter (the embeddable Python lacks it anyway, Section 9.3) - not recommended | Stay with Qt; PyQt5 or PySide6 is the author's choice with the facts of FD1; the structure of 11.1.5 keeps the toolkit out of every rule |

### 11.5 Estimated complexity per feature

#### 11.5.1 Scale and method

The audit method's scale is used: **SIMPLE** under 1 hour, **MODERATE** 1-3 hours, **COMPLEX** 3 hours or more, each meaning AI-assisted work by the author (writing, reviewing and running the tests on the developer PC). Office-PC acceptance sessions are counted separately (11.5.3), because they depend on access to a PC with Excel, not on writing speed.

Each rating rests on three things: the size of B's code for the feature (RAN me, s1: the line ranges the registry's "Where it lives" column names, merged per file and counted in B-copy; "code lines" excludes blank lines and lines that start with `#` (docstrings count as code); re-RAN in verification with identical figures; the sizes are approximate because the registry also names single call-site lines in other files), the gaps to fix at the same time (Section 7, by feature: RAN me, s7), and whether Excel is involved (anything that drives Excel needs fake-COM tests plus an acceptance step). The ratings are an inference (MEDIUM for each rating; LOW-MEDIUM for the total).

**Outline of SK12, "One naming rule, one finder"** (the lesson B's history paid for three times):

```text
---
name: one-naming-rule-one-finder
description: Use whenever code creates file or folder names that other code (or a later run) must find again.
---
# One naming rule, one finder

## Rule
Every kind of name (run folder, version folder, report, refreshed copy, backup, history key)
has ONE module with three functions:
  make(parts) -> name          # the only way the name is created
  parse(name) -> parts | None  # the only way the name is recognised; None = not ours
  newest(names) -> name        # chooses by parsed DATE, never by text order
Writers call make(); every reader calls parse()/newest(). No glob pattern or string
search for these names anywhere else (a guard test greps for it).

## Dates in names
- A name may show the date day-first (DDMMYY HHMM) for people, but no code sorts the text.
- newest() parses the date; names that do not parse are returned separately, never "won".
- Clashes in the same minute get a counter, never an overwrite.

## User-editable parts (suffixes)
- Validated: not empty, contains the time-stamp placeholder, no characters Windows forbids.
- make() and parse() both read the same current value.

## Success is a record, not a name
- "Refreshed", "done", "processed" come from a manifest written when the step succeeded,
  not from the existence of a file whose name looks right.

## Tests (required)
- round trip: parse(make(p)) == p for every kind of name
- newest() across a month end and a year end (e.g. 311225 1000 vs 211026 0335)
- a folder copy made in Explorer ("<name> - Copy") is not chosen as newest
- a refreshed copy is never mistaken for a base report
- writer and every reader run on the same made-up folder tree (contract test)

## Evidence that this matters
- Refreshed-copy suffix made by one rule and searched by another (bd176bf, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025)
- Extract-tab folder key (c258047) and run-history keys (c258047, 7e09e5c, b0e7d0e) - all B only (after the split)
- Day-first names sorted as text for "latest" (the shared Tk extractor's Version folders, 47a1492, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; 7e09e5c and b0e7d0e, B only (after the split))
```

## SECTION 12: CHANGELOG ARCHAEOLOGY (FROM GIT HISTORY)

> **About this section.** It is built from reading the full diff (the exact lines a commit added and removed) of every commit (one saved change in the project's history) of project B, `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2`, up to the snapshot `b0e7d0e` (09-02-2026): 17 commits in all. The first 12 commits (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`, 31-08-2025 to 30-10-2025) are shared with project A and are labelled "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025"; their entries are written once for both audits and are inserted at the marker in 12A below. The other five commits (07-02-2026 to 09-02-2026) belong to B alone and are labelled "B only (after the split)"; their entries follow the marker, as Phases 4 to 7. Sub-sections 12B to 12F (file evolution, rule evolution, edge cases, abandoned approaches, dependencies) follow in a separate part. Despite the repository names, B is not "newer" or "better" than A: the two share their first 12 commits and went separate ways after `47a1492`.

> **Verification (task VERIFY-B-S12own, 23-10-2026).** Every `file:line` and `path:line@commit` citation in this part was opened in the scratch copy or with `git show <commit>:<path>`; every commit hash, date, time, author, trailer, parent and numstat figure (git's count of lines added and removed per file) was re-read from `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined`; the branch, `git ls-remote` and GitHub creation and push dates were re-checked read-only. The most important RAN claims were re-run independently from fresh `git archive` copies in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-S12own/trees/<commit>/` (scripts in `…/VERIFY-B-S12own/scripts/`, `python -B`, Qt offscreen, fake home folders): start-up of all five own commits with and without stand-in pywin32 modules (`start.py`), the console-less top of `main.py` at `47a1492` and `c258047` (`pythonw_top.py`), the openpyxl merged-cell report at `47a1492`, `c258047` and `b0e7d0e` (`openpyxl_merged.py`), the six-file scan at `c21f788`, `7e09e5c`, `b0e7d0e` (`scan_compare.py`), the old-settings import and day-first name order (`migrate_and_sort.py`), the client-folder name cut at maximum 5, 8, 9, 15 and 35, the HTML log insertion, the 15-floor of the maximum-length box, the help-card folding, the phantom run-history record of `7e09e5c`, and the Step 4 disk tree at the snapshot on a made-up target (`step4_disk.py`). **How to read the evidence in this part**

- Code is cited as `path:line` for the line at the snapshot `b0e7d0e` (identical to `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy`), and as `path:line@commit` for that line in an older commit's version of the file. Paths are repository-relative.
- **READ** = established by reading the code or the diff. Every one of the five own diffs was opened with `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined show <hash>` and saved under `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S12own/diffs/`. Every line that changes behaviour was read; lines that only set colours, borders or spacing were skimmed. For the new files of `c258047` the main window, the three controllers, the four `models/` files and the behaviour parts of the four views were read whole at that commit (`git show c258047:<path>`). For the 3,298 lines deleted by `a62d3cc` I rely on the history reader H-B1, who read every deleted file in full, and I re-read at `c258047` every part I cite.
- **RAN (me)** = I executed something for this part on made-up inputs, always on copies of a commit extracted with `git archive` into `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S12own/trees/<commit>/`, with `python -B` (so no compiled files are written), Qt in "offscreen" mode (no screen needed), and a fake home folder (`/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S12own/home`, `…/home2`) so that no real settings file was read or written. Nothing was written into the repositories or into `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy`. My scripts, in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-S12own/scripts/`: `start.py` (starts `main.py` of one commit with the window's event loop switched off, with or without empty stand-in modules for pywin32 in `…/stubs/`), `pythonw_top.py` (runs the top of `main.py` as if there were no console window), `make_source.py` + `scan_compare.py` (six made-up files through the scan of three commits), `migrate_and_sort.py` (the one-time import of old settings at the snapshot, and the name order of day-first folder names), `openpyxl_merged.py` (the openpyxl report path on a template with a merged cell, before and after `c258047`); short one-line checks are quoted where used. **RAN (H-B1)** / **RAN (H-B2)** = run by the history readers whose working notes are `/root/merge-scratch/notes2/B_history_part1.md` and `…part2.md`; I re-read the code behind every such claim I rely on. Anything that needs Windows or Excel was traced by reading only.
- Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence. "Not sure — here is how to check" is used where the history cannot settle a question.
- **[GST RULE]** marks code that decides a tax figure, which return, table, sheet or cell a figure or file belongs to, a state code, a period, rounding or similar. For these I only say what the code does; whether it is right is the author's call. **⚠** marks values that can change over time (return and table names, file-naming conventions, template cell positions, state lists, package versions, Excel's path limit) so the author can check them.
- Feature and rule IDs (B-F…, B-R…) are those of the project registry; features are described in Section 3, rules in Section 5, gaps (B-G…) in Section 7. Where something has no registry ID it would be marked "UNREGISTERED"; none was needed in this part.
- Times are the commit times git recorded, India Standard Time (IST, +05:30). For all five own commits the author date equals the committer date (RAN (me): `git log --format='%h | ad=%ad | cd=%cd' --date=iso 47a1492..B/main`).
- **Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name, folder path from the author's computer or figure appears in this part. **Branch awareness: what was checked, and the result**

**Result:** project B has a single branch, `main`, so every one of its 17 commits is on the production line and there is no unmerged or feature branch whose work could be wrongly attributed. B has exactly one merge commit (a commit joining two lines of work), `9c56a1c` (29-10-2025, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); none of B's five own commits is a merge — each has exactly one parent, and they form a straight line `47a1492 → c258047 → a62d3cc → c21f788 → 7e09e5c → b0e7d0e` (RAN (me): `git log --format='%h %p' 47a1492..B/main`).

**Which repository is the original (an inference, not a fact).** GitHub's creation dates say that B's repository was made on the evening of the very first upload (31-08-2025) and A's on 07-02-2026, six minutes before the PyQt5 rewrite `c258047` was committed in B (RAN (me), table above). The most likely story (MEDIUM): B is the original repository; on the morning of 07-02-2026 the author created a second repository (now A) to keep the Tkinter v3.0 program as it stood at `47a1492`, and then let the AI-assisted rewrite land in the original. The old name `AnnualStatement` now leads to A, which fits a sequence in which the original was renamed and the old name was later held by A (GitHub forwards an old name to the repository that last held it) (LOW-MEDIUM). How to check: ask the author, or look at the repositories' settings and history on GitHub. Project A's audit inferred the opposite ("A is probably the original repository, renamed", MEDIUM, from the old name alone); the creation dates were not available to it. This matters only for the later comparison, not for what either program does.

**Who made B's own commits.** All five are recorded with the git author and committer name `goyal-sidhant`, which is also the GitHub account name (RAN (verifier): `git log --format='%an | %cn' 47a1492..B/main`; [Corrected during verification — originally "recorded under the GitHub user name"; git records an author name, not a GitHub account]). The three commits of 07-02-2026 (`c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`) end with the trailer (a closing line git keeps with the message) "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6", i.e. they were written with an AI coding assistant (RAN (me): `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Co-Authored-By)'`). Their messages are long and structured ("Phase 1 … Phase 4", file lists, counts) and several of their counts and claims do not match the diff (checked one by one below). The two later commits (`7e09e5c`, 08-02-2026; `b0e7d0e`, 09-02-2026) have no trailer and use the "feat: …" prefix; their messages are short and leave out most of what the diffs do (LOW: they may have been written by an editor's commit-message tool from the diff; how to check: ask the author). In all, B's own work changed 49 files, +4,056 / −3,535 lines between `47a1492` and `b0e7d0e` (RAN (me): `git diff --shortstat 47a1492 B/main`).

**Words used in this part** (plain meanings of the technical terms; each is also explained where it first matters below)

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| commit / diff / parent | one saved change in git / the exact lines it added (+) and removed (−) / the commit just before it |
| trailer | a closing line in a commit message, here naming the AI assistant as co-author |
| refactor | rewriting the structure of code without (intending to) change what it does |
| Tkinter (Tk) / PyQt5 (Qt) | Python's built-in window toolkit, used by every shared commit / a larger desktop-window toolkit (a Python wrapper for Qt 5), used by B from `c258047` |
| widget / view / controller / model | one on-screen element / the screen code of one tab / code that runs a job (scan, processing, extraction) and reports back to the screen / plain data containers that hold the program's state, with no screen code |
| worker thread / QThread | a second line of work beside the window, so long jobs do not freeze it / Qt's way of running such a line |
| signal / slot | Qt's "this happened, now run that" wiring between parts of the program |
| QSS stylesheet | Qt's CSS-like text rules for colours and fonts; an application stylesheet applies everywhere, a widget's own stylesheet applies to it and everything inside it |
| dataclass / JSON | a simple Python container of named fields / a plain-text file format for settings |
| COM / pywin32 | Windows' way for one program to drive another (here Python drives Excel) / the Python package that provides it (`pythoncom`, `win32com`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`) |
| `GetActiveObject` / `Dispatch` | two ways to get an Excel through COM: attach to the Excel the user already has open / may attach to a running Excel or start one |
| openpyxl | a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel; when it saves a workbook it drops Power Query |
| Power Query / Links sheet | Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC and Sales templates / the template sheet into which the program writes the folder paths and file names those queries read |
| bare `except:` / `except Exception:` / narrower `except (KeyError, ValueError):` | error catchers: catch every error, even Ctrl+C / catch every normal error / catch only the listed kinds and let all others through |
| log level INFO / DEBUG | the program writes INFO lines (and above) to its log file (`main.py:17`); DEBUG lines are hidden at that setting |
| `pythonw` | the Windows Python that runs with no console window; there `print()` shows nothing and `sys.stdout` is empty (`None`) |
| import / package `__init__.py` / dangling import | one file loading another / the file that runs when a folder of code is first loaded / an import of a file that has been deleted, which fails as soon as it runs |
| stand-in (stub) module | an empty fake module I wrote so that Windows-only imports succeed on Linux during a test run |
| glob / stat / mtime | a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` / asking the operating system for a file's size and dates / a file's or folder's "last modified" time |
| `~$` lock file | the small hidden file Excel creates next to a workbook while it is open |
| file signature | the first bytes of a file that show its real type: `PK\x03\x04` = a ZIP package (`.xlsx` / `.xlsm`), `D0 CF 11 E0` = the old `.xls` format |
| Level 1 / Level 2 / Version folder | B's output tree: `<target>/Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>/` (the run folder) → `<client>-<state code>/` (the client folder) → `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>/` (holds the reports) |
| variations | the code's word for problem files (unrecognised or invalid) |
| run history | B's file `~/.gst_organizer/run_history.json` (per user, per PC) that remembers past processing and extraction runs |
| HTML insertion | adding text to a log box as web markup, so `<`, `>` and `&` in a name are read as markup instead of being shown |
| regression / patch / proper fix | something that worked and was broken by a later change / a fix that removes the symptom / a fix that removes the cause |
| exit code | the number a program hands back when it ends: 0 = finished normally, 1 (or another number) = stopped with an error |
| UTF-8 | a way of storing text that can hold every character, including ₹, ✓ and emoji |
| docstring / dictionary | the description text written at the top of a Python function or file / a Python list of name → value pairs (for example "B2" → a folder path) |
| pull request (PR) | a request on GitHub to merge one branch into another; GitHub keeps a ref for each one |
| offscreen | a Qt mode that draws windows in memory without a screen, used here to run the window on a server |

### 12A. Complete Development Timeline

This sub-section lists every commit of B's single branch `main` in date order, with what the diff actually changed (files touched with lines added and removed, then the code changes in plain English), why it most likely changed (an inference, with a confidence), what it reveals about the project's rules, data flow, edge cases and design philosophy, where the commit message disagrees with the diff, and what is still true at the snapshot `b0e7d0e`. The twelve shared commits form Phases 1 to 3 and are inserted at the marker below. B's own five commits follow as Phases 4 to 7, all within three days: an AI-assisted rewrite of the whole window from Tkinter to PyQt5 in one morning (07-02-2026), its clean-up and a start-up repair the same morning, then two commits on the following two mornings that restore the look of the old Tkinter screens and twice rebuild the way Step 4 finds the reports to refresh. No GST rule value (file-name pattern ⚠, expected file types, Links-sheet cell map ⚠, state-code table ⚠, extraction cell map ⚠) changed in any of the five commits (READ: `utils/constants.py` and `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py` appear in none of their diffs); what changed is the window, the order of work, what is shown, and where output goes.

> **About this part.** It covers the twelve commits that project A (goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1) and project B (goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2) have in common, from the first upload on 31-08-2025 to the split point 47a1492 on 30-10-2025. **How to read the evidence in this part**

- Code is cited as `path:line@commit`, meaning "that line number in that commit's version of the file", for example `core/file_parser.py:254@edac6a3`. Files that did not change between edac6a3 and 47a1492 have the same line numbers at both. A citation without `@commit` means: inside the description of the first commit (sub-sections A to Y under edac6a3) the line at edac6a3; inside a later commit's entry the line at that commit (for bd176bf the files at bd176bf and 47a1492 are identical); in "Where the two projects started" the line at 47a1492. `:N` alone means "line N of the file named just before".
- Feature and rule IDs (A-F…, A-R…, B-F…, B-R…) are not used in this part: the same text serves both audits, and those IDs describe each project's latest snapshot, while this part describes code from before the split. Sub-sections of the first commit are referred to by their letters (A to Y).
- **READ** = I read the code or the diff (`git show <hash>`, and `git show -m --first-parent 9c56a1c` for the merge). **RAN** = I executed the code on made-up data, always on my own extracted copies under `/root/merge-scratch/run/SHARED-12A/` (Linux, Python 3.14, Tk under a virtual display, run with `python -B` so nothing is written into the copies). Anything that needs Excel or Windows was traced by reading only. Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence.
- **[GST RULE]** marks code that decides a tax figure, which return, sheet or cell a figure belongs to, a state code, a period, rounding or display of figures. For these I only say what the code does; whether it is right is the author's call. **⚠** marks values that can change over time (state lists, return table numbers, template sheet names and cell positions) so the author can check them.
- Times are the commit times git recorded, in India Standard Time (+05:30). Times taken from compiled-file headers are in UTC and are labelled "UTC".
- No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name, folder path from the author's computer or figure appears in this part. Names such as `<Client A>`, "Alpha Traders" or "Beta Stores" are made up for the test runs.

**Words used in this part** (plain meanings of the technical terms used below)

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | one saved change in the git history |
| diff | the exact lines a commit added and removed |
| merge commit | a commit that joins two lines of work into one |
| split point | 47a1492, the last commit both projects share |
| regex (regular expression) | a text pattern used to recognise file names, for example "starts with `GSTR3B-`" |
| GUI | the program's windows, buttons and lists |
| Tkinter (Tk) | the window toolkit that comes with Python; every shared commit uses it |
| thread / worker thread | a second line of work running at the same time, so the window stays responsive; Tk windows should only be changed from the main thread |
| callback | a small piece of code handed to another part of the program to be run later |
| lambda / late binding | a lambda is a tiny inline function; "late binding" means it reads its variables when it finally runs, not when it was created, so inside a loop it can show the last value for every line |
| COM / pywin32 | COM is the Windows mechanism that lets a program drive Microsoft Excel; pywin32 is the Python package that provides it (`win32com`, `pythoncom`, `win32gui` ...) |
| openpyxl | a Python package that reads and writes .xlsx files without Excel |
| Power Query | Excel's built-in data-import engine; the ITC and Sales templates use it to pull data from the organised files |
| SendKeys | simulating key presses into whatever window is in front |
| cache file / JSON | a small settings file that remembers last-used folders; JSON is the text format it is written in |
| glob | a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` |
| modification time (mtime) | a file's "last changed" date and time |
| `.pyc` / `__pycache__` | compiled copies of Python files that Python writes automatically into `__pycache__` folders |
| CRLF | Windows line endings (two characters per line end); git shows LF (one character) |
| Treeview | the table-like client list on the Validation screen |
| dead code | code that is never called |
| UTF-8 | the standard way of storing text that can hold any character, including emoji |
| 8.3 short path | the old Windows short form of a path (each folder or file name shortened to 8 characters plus a 3-character extension, such as `PROGRA~1`), used to get around path-length limits |
| NTFS | the file system Windows uses on its disks; it lists the names in a folder in sorted order |
| IST / UTC | India Standard Time / Coordinated Universal Time (IST = UTC + 5 h 30 min) |
| `.xltx` | an Excel template file; double-clicking it in Windows starts a new, unsaved workbook based on it |

**The original program in detail - where both projects started**

**A. Two separate programs**

- **The organiser** is started with `python main.py`. In order (READ):
  1. `main.py:18@edac6a3` replaces the console output (`sys.stdout`) with a UTF-8 version of it, so emoji in messages can be printed.
  2. `main.py:21-28` sends all log messages of level INFO and above both to a file `gst_organizer.log` and to the console. The file name has no folder, so the file is created in whatever folder the program is started from, and it is appended to on every start.
  3. `setup_environment()` (`main.py:30-44`) puts the program folder on Python's search path, creates the folders `core`, `utils`, `gui`, `logs` and `temp` inside the program folder if missing, and writes a one-line `__init__.py` into `core`, `utils` and `gui` if missing. `logs` and `temp` are never used afterwards.
  4. `main()` (`main.py:46-80`) imports the main window, prints a banner and runs the window. On a missing module it prints the list of expected files - which still includes **`gui/app.py`** (`main.py:72`), a file that is not in the commit (see Y) - and waits for Enter (`main.py:73`). On any other error it logs the details, prints them and waits for Enter.
  5. The first line `# !/usr/bin/env python3` (`main.py:1`) has a space after `#`, so it was never a working "shebang" (the line that tells Linux/macOS which interpreter to use) (READ, HIGH).
  6. The header says "Author: Advanced AI Assistant" and "Version: 3.0 (Production Ready)" (`main.py:6-7`).
  - RAN (`test_window.py`, `t_edac6a3`): the main window builds with title "GST File Organizer v3.0" and the tabs "📁 Step 1: Setup", "✅ Step 2: Validation", "🚀 Step 3: Processing".
  - Console dependence (READ, HIGH): the program prints banners and waits for Enter on errors (`main.py:54-56,63-79`), and step 1 assumes a console exists. Started without a console (for example with `pythonw.exe` on Windows, where `sys.stdout` is empty), line 18 fails with an AttributeError before anything is logged. RAN (re-check 21-10-2026, `main.py` of edac6a3 and of 47a1492 started with its output stream closed, from an empty scratch folder): both stop at once with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'buffer'`, exit code 1, and no `gst_organizer.log` is created. Under `pythonw.exe` the error output is missing too, so the user would see nothing at all - the program simply does not open (READ of Python's documented behaviour, MEDIUM; not run on Windows) (added in re-check 21-10-2026).
- **The Power Query Extractor** is a second, separate program started with `python launch_extractor.py` "after GST Organizer processing" (`launch_extractor.py:2-3`). The launcher puts its own folder on the search path (`:10`), imports and runs `PowerQueryExtractor` (`:14-18`), and on any error shows a Tk error box and re-raises it (`:20-27`). Importing `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` sets up its own log file `pq_extractor.log` (again relative to the start folder) plus console output (`extractor_main.py:12-19`), but only if no logging was set up before. The extractor's window class is `PowerQueryExtractorApp` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:18`), title "Power Query Extractor", 1000×700 (`:43-45`).
  - The extractor is **Windows-only with pywin32 installed**: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` imports `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con` and `win32gui` at the top with no fallback, so without them the program cannot even start. RAN: importing `power_query_extractor.extractor_main` from my copy stops with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'`. The organiser, by contrast, imports pywin32 only on Windows and falls back to openpyxl (`core/excel_handler.py:19-33`). The two programs handle the same missing package in opposite ways (READ, HIGH).
- The two programs never call each other. They communicate only through the folders and file names the organiser creates (HIGH, READ of both).

- Almost every action button (Browse, Scan, Re-scan, Dry Run, Export, Start, Stop, Select All, Clear All, Complete Only) is wired with a mouse-click binding `bind('<Button-1>', ...)` instead of Tk's normal `command=` option (for example `setup_tab.py:115,161,199,306,318`, `validation_tab.py:118,130,142,190`, `processing_tab.py:74,87`). Comments call this "working mouse events" and "proper event binding" (`setup_tab.py:20,103`), which hints that `command=` had given trouble in an earlier version (LOW). Consequence: a button that is "disabled" still reacts to a click (RAN, `test_misc.py`: a disabled Tk button with such a binding still ran its handler), and pressing Space on a focused button does nothing, because there is no `command` to run (READ, MEDIUM). The extractor, written separately, uses `command=` throughout (`extractor_window.py:133,143,168,178,223`) - an inconsistency between the two programs (READ, HIGH).
- Mouse-wheel scrolling of the Setup screen is bound for the whole window with `bind_all("<MouseWheel>")` (`setup_tab.py:63-66`), the Windows/macOS wheel event.

**C. What SCAN FILES does** (READ; `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:57-95` → `core/file_parser.py:128-179`)

1. Checks that a source folder is entered and exists (`file_handler.py:120-130`).
2. `find_excel_files()` (`utils/helpers.py:249-266`) lists only the top level of the folder (no sub-folders) with the wildcards `*.xlsx`, `*.xls`, `*.xlsm`, and **silently drops** every file that fails `validate_excel_file()` (`helpers.py:210-247`): smaller than 1,024 bytes, or extension not one of .xlsx/.xls/.xlsm/.xltx/.xltm, or first bytes not the ZIP signature `PK\x03\x04` or the old-Excel signature `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0`. Such files appear nowhere - not in the client list and not in "variations" (the "Invalid or corrupted Excel file" branch at `file_parser.py:188-195` can only be reached if a file changes between the two checks) (READ, HIGH; RAN in re-check 21-10-2026 with `v_scan.py`: a 104-byte file and a file with a wrong signature, both named like Sales files, appear neither among the clients nor among the variations). The list is sorted by name (`helpers.py:262`).
3. Each file name is tried against six patterns in a fixed order (D below). A match that yields a client and a state goes into the client data under the key `<client as written>-<state code>` (`file_parser.py:228-252`); everything else becomes a "variation" with a suggested pattern (`file_parser.py:212-222,290-308`).
4. Completeness is computed per client (E below), the summary text (`gui/main_window.py:267-301`) and the client list are refreshed, and the window switches to the Validation screen (`file_handler.py:78-88`).
- The scan runs in the main thread, so the window does not respond while a large folder is scanned; the per-file status messages it sets are not repainted until the scan ends (READ, MEDIUM).

**D. File-name patterns the scanner recognises** - `utils/constants.py:13-62@edac6a3`, unchanged up to the split point. [GST RULE] ⚠ (they decide which return or report each file is treated as)

All patterns ignore upper/lower case, must match the whole name, and accept only `.xls` or `.xlsx` (`\.xlsx?$`), so an `.xlsm` file is found by the scan but always ends up as a variation. `[^-]+` means "one or more characters that are not a hyphen", so **a client name or a state name containing a hyphen is never read correctly** (READ, HIGH). [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally stated "can never be read"; a RAN scan (`v_scan.py`, edac6a3 parser, made-up files) showed two different outcomes:]
- In the three patterns that end in `(.+)` (GSTR-2B Reco, Sales Reco, Annual Report) the name is **silently mis-read**: for a client "Alpha-Beta Traders" in Maharashtra the parser takes client "Alpha", state "Beta Traders" (state code by the fallback "BT") and puts the rest into the period, so these files form a separate, wrongly named client "Alpha-BT" with no warning shown.
- In the other three patterns (GSTR-3B, IMS Reco, Sales) the name matches nothing and the file becomes a variation ("No matching pattern found").

| Order | Key | Pattern (quoted exactly) | Treated as | Copied to | Parts captured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GSTR-2B-Reco` | `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "GSTR-2B Reco", category ITC | ITC folder | client, state, period (the period may contain hyphens) |
| 2 | `ImsReco` | `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})\.xlsx?$` | "IMS Reco", category ITC | ITC folder | client, state, date (exactly 8 digits; described as DDMMYYYY) |
| 3 | `GSTR3B` | `^(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?GSTR3B-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | "GSTR-3B Export", category GSTR3B | GSTR-3B folder | client, state, month; an optional prefix such as `(2) ` (probably a duplicate-download number) is allowed only here |
| 4 | `Sales` | `^Sales-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | "Sales", category Sales | Sales folder | client, state, start month, end month |
| 5 | `SalesReco` | `^SalesReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "Sales Reco", category Sales | Sales folder | client, state, period |
| 6 | `AnnualReport` | `^AnnualReport-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "Annual Report", category Annual | the Version folder itself | client, state, year |

- [GST RULE] The period, date, month and year parts are stored (`file_parser.py:97-98`) and **never used anywhere** (READ, HIGH: no reader in any file). The code does not check a tax period or financial year at all; apart from the IMS date being 8 digits, these parts are free text.
- Client and state parts are checked by `validate_client_name()` (`helpers.py:321-342`: 2-100 characters, none of `< > : " / \ | ? *`); problems are stored as "warnings" (`file_parser.py:100-111`) that are **never shown** (READ, HIGH).
- Suggestions for unrecognised names (`file_parser.py:290-308`) are chosen by keywords in this order: "gstr" and "2b" → GSTR-2B pattern; "ims" → IMS; "gstr" and "3b" → GSTR-3B; "sales" and "reco" → Sales Reco; "sales" → Sales; "annual" → Annual Report; otherwise "Check file naming convention".

**E. When a client counts as "Complete"** - `core/file_parser.py:254-288@edac6a3`, list `utils/constants.py:68-75`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (it decides which returns and files a client must have)

- Six file types are expected: GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B Export, Sales, Sales Reco, Annual Report.
- "Missing" = expected types with no file. "Extra" = any type other than GSTR-3B Export with two or more files ("GSTR-3B can have multiple files (monthly filings - unlimited)", `:268-270`).
- Status: "Complete" ✅ when nothing is missing and nothing is extra; "Missing N files" ⚠️ when anything is missing; otherwise "Has duplicates" ⚠️. Completeness % = types found ÷ 6 × 100, rounded to one decimal (`:276-277`).
- A never-called method `validate_results()` (`:340-373`) would have flagged "Annual Report" and "GSTR-3B Export" as "critical" files - an unfinished idea.

**F. Client identity and state codes** (READ; RAN where marked)

- [GST RULE] ⚠ **State name → state code** (`utils/helpers.py:485-511`, list `utils/constants.py:234-275`): the state part of the file name is trimmed, lower-cased and looked up in a fixed list of 39 entries that map full state and union-territory names to two-letter **alphabetic** abbreviations (for example 'maharashtra' → MH, 'telangana' → TS, 'odisha' and 'orissa' → OD, 'uttarakhand' → UK, 'chhattisgarh' → CG, 'dadra and nagar haveli and daman and diu' → DD, 'delhi' and 'national capital territory of delhi' → DL, 'ladakh' → LA, 'puducherry' and 'pondicherry' → PY). If the name is not in the list, the code logs a warning and builds a fallback: with two or more words, the first letters of the first two words; with one word, the first three characters in capitals. The code never uses numeric state codes, and it does not read, build or check a GSTIN or PAN anywhere (READ, HIGH).
  - RAN (`test_tree_values.py`, the helper is identical at edac6a3 and 47a1492 apart from its import line): 'Maharashtra' → MH; ' tamil nadu ' → TN; 'MH' → MH (through the fallback, with a warning); 'NCT of Delhi' → NO; 'Jammu & Kashmir' → J&; 'Gujrat' (misspelt) → GUJ; '' → ''. So a misspelt state name produces a different client key and a different folder from the correctly spelt one.
- **Client key** = `<client exactly as written>-<state code>` (`core/file_parser.py:231-232`). It is case-sensitive: "Alpha" and "alpha" are two clients, and so are "X Private Limited" and "X Pvt Ltd" - although both later get the same output folder name (G below), so the second one's reports can overwrite the first one's (READ, MEDIUM).
- **Client-state folder name** `create_client_state_key()` (`helpers.py:513-537`): whole words "Private" → "Pvt" and "Limited" → "Ltd" (any case), then `<client>-<state code>`; if longer than the maximum (default 35, `core/file_organizer.py:42`; setting `gui/main_window.py:89`), the client part is cut to fit; if that would leave 5 characters or fewer the whole key is cut, which can cut off the state code. RAN: "Alpha Beta" with maximum 8 → "Alpha Be"; a long name can end with a space before the hyphen.
- **File-name cleaning** `sanitize_filename()` (`helpers.py:66-112`): replaces the text "Private" → "Pvt" and "Limited" → "Ltd" anywhere and case-sensitively (RAN: "Privately Limitedness" → "Pvtly_Ltdness"), replaces control characters and `` <>:"/\|?*[]{}+=!@#$%^,;'"`~ `` (`:82`) with `_`, turns runs of spaces/underscores into one `_`, trims `_`, `.` and spaces at the ends, uses "unnamed" if nothing is left, and cuts the name to `200 - len(extension) - 10` characters (RAN: a 300-character name → 190 characters; with an `.xlsx` extension → 185 + `.xlsx` = 190). Hyphens are kept on purpose (comment `:81`).

**G. Output folders and names** (READ; `core/file_organizer.py`, `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py`, `power_query_extractor/...`)

```
<Target folder>/
  Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                  Fresh Run: new each run. Re-Run/Resume: the newest existing one by modification time
    GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx      summary workbook (K below)
    PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx      written later by the extractor (Q below)
    <client-state key>/                            for example "Alpha Traders-MH" (spaces kept)
      Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                       always a new time stamp per run
        GSTR-3B Exports[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        Other ITC related files[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        Sales related files[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        <Annual Report file, cleaned name>
        ITC_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx
        Sales_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx
        ITC_Report_..._Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx  written later by the extractor
        _Organization_Report_<client as written>_<state as written>.txt
```

- Time stamps: `get_timestamp()` = day, month, two-digit year, space, hours, minutes (`helpers.py:23-25`); report names replace the space with `_` (`processing_handler.py:215,383`). With minute precision, two runs in the same minute share the same folders.
- The bracketed client name in the three category folders ("Level 4" in the screen text) is added when the global checkbox is on, or when the per-client "📁 Name" setting for key `<client>-<state code>` is on (`file_organizer.py:113-135`). The bracket uses the cleaned client (spaces → `_`), the client-state folder keeps spaces.
- Which file goes where (`file_organizer.py:285-298`): GSTR-3B Export → GSTR-3B folder; GSTR-2B Reco and IMS Reco → ITC folder; Sales and Sales Reco → Sales folder; Annual Report → the Version folder itself.

**H. Copying the files and the three processing modes** (READ)

- Processing (`processing_handler.py:54-447@edac6a3`) runs in a background thread. Per selected client: create the folders → copy the files under cleaned names → ITC report → Sales report → per-client text report; after all clients the summary workbook; then an information box and the output folder is opened (`os.startfile` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, `:425-437`). STOP is checked only between clients (`:149-151`).
- Each file is copied with `shutil.copy2` and the copy's size compared with the original; a size difference deletes the copy (`helpers.py:142-185`). After a successful copy the in-memory record gets the cleaned name, so the template is given the copied name (`file_organizer.py:216-229`).
- If the destination already exists (`file_organizer.py:259-270`): **Fresh Run** first makes a backup `<name>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` (`helpers.py:187-204`); **Resume** skips the file; **Re-Run** overwrites it silently.
- Because the Version folder always gets the current time stamp (`file_organizer.py:43,98-104`), a destination can only already exist within the same minute or when two different source files clean to the same name. In practice **Resume behaves like Re-Run** (READ, HIGH). When two source files clean to the same name (for example names that differ only in "Private" versus "Pvt" or in a space versus an underscore), Re-Run keeps only the last one copied (READ, MEDIUM).
- Optional warning before processing: if "include client name" is on and any selected client name has **more than 10 characters**, a list of up to five names is shown with "Continue anyway?" (`processing_handler.py:64-75@edac6a3`); the per-client "📁 Name" toggle has its own >10 warning (`client_handler.py:193-202@edac6a3`).
- A client counts as "Success" whenever no exception was raised, even if both its reports failed (`processing_handler.py:337-350`) (READ, HIGH).

**I. Writing paths into the templates - the "Links" sheet** - `utils/constants.py:96-120@edac6a3`, values from `core/excel_handler.py:551-661`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (it decides which file feeds which input of the ITC and Sales reports; the cell positions depend on the templates)

| Report | Cell | What is written |
|---|---|---|
| ITC | B2 | path of the GSTR-3B folder (the whole folder, so all monthly GSTR-3B files are available) |
| ITC | B4 / B5 | path of the Version folder / Annual Report file name without extension |
| ITC | B7 / B8 | path of the ITC folder / GSTR-2B Reco file name without extension |
| ITC | B10 / B11 | path of the ITC folder / IMS Reco file name without extension |
| Sales | B2 / B3 | path of the Sales folder / Sales file name without extension |
| Sales | B5 / B6 | path of the Version folder / Annual Report file name without extension |
| Sales | B8 / B9 | path of the Sales folder / Sales Reco file name without extension |

- Paths are written with backslashes (`helpers.py:311-315`); file names lose their extension (`helpers.py:446-448`), so the template must add it itself (MEDIUM). Only the **first** file of each type is used (`annual_files[0]` and so on, `excel_handler.py:577,588,599,615,631,647`) - the alphabetically first name, because the scan sorts. Further files of the same type are copied but not linked.
- Empty values are not written (`if value:`, `excel_handler.py:173,260`), so when a file type is missing the template's existing cell content stays as it was (READ, HIGH; whether the template then shows stale data depends on the template - MEDIUM).
- Through Excel the sheet is found by the exact name "Links" (any case), else any sheet with "link" in its name, else a new sheet "Links" is added (`excel_handler.py:146-164`). The openpyxl route accepts only the exact name "Links" (any case, `:249-253`) and writes nothing when there is no such sheet (`:255`) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally the "link"-in-the-name fallback read as if it applied to both routes; it exists only in the Excel route]. The organiser never reads any figure from any workbook (READ, HIGH).
- Report file names: `ITC_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` and `Sales_Report_...` in the Version folder (`processing_handler.py:212-219,276-277@edac6a3`). The template is copied to that name whether it is an .xlsx or an .xltx template (`excel_handler.py:135,239`). Whether Excel opens an .xltx template copied under an .xlsx name without complaint was not testable here - not sure; how to check: run one client with an .xltx template on Windows and open the produced report.

**J. Excel through COM in the organiser** (`core/excel_handler.py:103-228@edac6a3`; READ only - cannot run here)

- `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` (start COM for this thread); then **`GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` first** - this attaches to the user's own Excel if one is open - and only otherwise `Dispatch(...)` (`:121-126`). It sets `Visible=False`, `DisplayAlerts=False`, `ScreenUpdating=False` on that Excel (`:129-131`), so a user's own open Excel would be hidden.
- It copies the template to the output name, waits 0.5 s (`:133-136`), opens the copy (`_safe_open_workbook`, `:275-317`: reuses an already open workbook with the same path; on error -2147352567, an error mentioning "path", or a path longer than 218 characters, retries with the Windows 8.3 short path), writes the Links cells, saves, closes, checks the file exists.
- In the clean-up (`:206-228`) it sets `ScreenUpdating=True` and `DisplayAlerts=True` and calls `excel.Quit()` if `self.excel_app is None`. `self.excel_app` is set to None in `__init__` (`:55`) and never assigned anywhere, so **Quit is always called - also on a user's Excel attached through GetActiveObject**, although the comment says "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:217`) (READ, HIGH that Quit is always called). What Excel then does with the user's unsaved workbooks while hidden and with alerts switched back on is not sure (MEDIUM); how to check: on Windows, open Excel with an unsaved workbook, run one client, and watch whether that Excel closes or asks to save. The run log (X below) records only newly started Excel instances, never an attached one, so in the logged runs no open Excel was attached.
- Without pywin32 or off Windows, `_create_report_openpyxl` (`:230-273`) copies the template and saves it through openpyxl with `keep_links=True`, after logging "Power Query content may be lost!" (`:235`). The file header explains why the Excel route exists: "WINDOWS VERSION - Uses Excel COM to preserve Power Query and all Excel features" (`:2-3`).
- `warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')` (`:17`) silences every Python warning in the whole program, not only Excel ones (READ, HIGH).
- `ExcelHandler()` creates `<system temp>/gst_excel_temp` at every start (`:52-53`) and never uses it.

**K. Summary workbook, per-client text report, exported client list** (READ)

- Summary workbook `GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` in the Annual Statement folder, always written with openpyxl (`excel_handler.py:319-357`; name `processing_handler.py:383-385`): sheets "Summary" (date, totals, reports created, errors, mode, target folder, include-name Yes/No, `:380-410`), "Client Status" (Client, State, Status, Files, Missing count, Complete %, `:412-439`), "File Mapping" (original file, client key, type, destination, status, `:441-467`), "Errors" (`:469-500`), "Variations" (file name, issue, expected pattern, size, "Rename file", `:502-533`).
- Per-client text report `_Organization_Report_<client>_<state>.txt` in the Version folder (`file_organizer.py:300-362`), using the client and state exactly as written in the file names. Its "Successfully Copied" and "Folders Created" figures count **everything done so far in the whole run**, not just this client, because one FileOrganizer object is used for all clients (`processing_handler.py:110-116`, `file_organizer.py:346-351`) (READ, HIGH).
- EXPORT LIST (`client_handler.py:227-259`) writes the selected clients as "client - state" into a .txt file the user chooses (default name `selected_clients_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.txt`), with the system's default text encoding (`:243`), then opens it with `os.startfile` (`:257`), which exists only on Windows; elsewhere the file is written, the "Export Complete" box (`:253-254`) appears, and then "Failed to export" is shown as well (READ).

- Dark mode (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py`, `gui/main_window.py:150-180`): recolours every widget. Switching back sets every frame and canvas to plain white (`dark_mode_manager.py:171-172`), not the original light grey `#F8F9FA`, so after dark → light the screens differ from start-up (MEDIUM).

  ```python
  if hasattr(tree_widget, 'tag_configure'):

This file did not change in the shared range, so the defect is present at the split point.

Because the typing check runs on every key press and rejects any single digit (1-9 is below 10) but allows an empty box, a user who clears the box cannot type a new number into it key by key; only the arrows, pasting a whole number, or editing inside the existing digits work (READ, HIGH; RAN in re-check 21-10-2026 with `v_spin.py` on the real Setup screen at 47a1492: after clearing the box, the key presses "2" and "5" leave it empty, while inserting "25" in one step is accepted); in addition the arrow handler resets 0 or less to 35 (`:262-267`) and the cache loader does the same (`main_window.py:353-354`) (READ, HIGH) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally "three different limits"; the three places hold two different ranges].

**M. The Power Query Extractor - screens and flow** (READ; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py@edac6a3`)

- Heading "🔄 Power Query Report Extractor" and two tabs. **Setup**: Target Folder (entry, 📁 Browse, 🔍 Scan); "Select Clients" with ✓ Select All, ✗ Deselect All and a checkbox "Skip Refresh (Use existing refreshed files)"; a scrollable list with one checkbox per client (all ticked) and "ITC ✓" / "Sales ✓" labels where a report exists; "🚀 Start Processing" (`:95-232,408-468`). **Processing**: progress bar and a log (`:245-313`).
- At start it tries to load the target folder from a cache (S below), then scans.
- **Finding the processed clients** (`:353-406`): in the target folder, the newest `Annual Statement-*` folder by modification time; inside it every sub-folder whose name does not start with `_`; inside each, the `Version-*` folder with the **largest name** (`:385`). Names are `Version-DDMMYY HHMM`, so day-first text order is not date order - RAN (`test_misc.py`): of "Version-310825 2211", "Version-151025 0900" and "Version-291025 2146" the code picks the 31-08-2025 one. The client name shown and used in the consolidated workbook is the client-state folder name.
- **Per client, per report type** (`core/report_processor.py:37-141`): take the first file matching `<ITC|Sales>_Report_*.xlsx` in that Version folder (`:54-67`; the wildcard also matches the extractor's own refreshed copies, and the order of the list depends on the operating system - on Windows NTFS the original usually comes first because "." sorts before "_" - LOW-MEDIUM); copy it to `<name>_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` (`:69-71,96-98`); refresh the copy in Excel (N); wait 3 s (`:117-119`); read the configured cells from the copy in a second, hidden Excel (`:462-571`). "Extract data regardless of refresh status" (`:121-122`).
- **Skip Refresh** already exists here: the checkbox writes into the shared `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS` dictionary at run time (`extractor_window.py:234-243`); the processor then uses the newest `<name>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` by modification time, or refreshes if there is none (`report_processor.py:73-93`). It does not check whether that earlier refresh had passed validation (READ, HIGH).
- After all clients, the consolidated workbook is written (Q) and the user is asked whether to open it (`os.startfile`, `extractor_window.py:570-573`). The worker thread writes to the log, the progress bar and message boxes directly (`:516-601`), although Tk widgets should only be changed from the main thread (READ, HIGH).

**N. Refreshing Power Query by key presses** (`report_processor.py:143-350@edac6a3`; READ only)

- `print(f"PROCESSING: ...")` sits before the docstring (`:144-146`, "TEST: Add this line to check if logging works"), so the description is not a docstring and the line writes to the console.
- `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (`:154`; this may return an Excel that is already running - MEDIUM), then up to five tries, 2 s apart, to set **`Visible=True`**, `DisplayAlerts=False` and `WindowState=-4137` (maximised) ("Keep it visible to avoid issues", `:156-170`); open the workbook with three tries on "Call was rejected by callee" (`:174-185`); wait 5 × 1 s ("Increased from 3 to 5", `:187-191`); bring the window to the front with `WScript.Shell.AppActivate` (three tries, `:193-212`); then **send the keys Alt+A, R, A** one second apart ("Increased from 0.5", `:214-229`) - Excel's ribbon shortcut for Data → Refresh All.
- Wait 10 × 1 s - the comment says "WAIT 7 SECONDS AS REQUESTED" (`:233-238`), so comment and code disagree. Check five times, one second apart, for an error dialog (`_find_error_window`, `:352-388`: any visible, enabled top-level window whose title contains 'microsoft excel', 'error', 'problem', 'cannot', 'failed', 'unable', 'could not', 'exception', 'invalid' or 'missing', and whose window class is `#32770`, `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword`); read its text (`:390-425`) and press a button labelled ok/close/yes/continue, otherwise send it a close message (`:427-460`). Wait 10 s more "for complex queries" (`:260-265`), check once more, validate (O), save, close.
- There is no `RefreshAll()` call, no wait for asynchronous queries to finish and no check of whether a query is still refreshing; the refresh is assumed finished after the fixed waits (READ, HIGH). Because the keys go to whatever window is in front, the user must not use the computer while a refresh is running, and the program needs an interactive, logged-in desktop. Each report spends roughly 40 seconds in fixed waits alone (adding up the waits in the code; MEDIUM).
- The refreshed copy is saved even when validation fails (`:279-296`), and a later Skip Refresh run can reuse it (M above) (READ, HIGH).
- Clean-up closes without saving, quits Excel and stops COM (`:329-350`). A final `return {'success': True ...}` (`:318-321`) can never run, and the `except` in `_process_report` that looks for "Open method of Workbooks class failed" (`:101-115`) can never trigger, because `_refresh_power_query_simple` catches every error itself (READ, HIGH). Comments such as "ADD THE NEW CODE HERE (notice the indentation - 3 levels)" (`:73`) and "Rest of your code remains same..." (`:231`) are left-overs of code pasted from chat answers.
- Opening (`_safe_open_workbook`, `:622-731`): an already open workbook with the same full path is reused (`:641-644`); paths over 218 characters are converted to the Windows long-path form (`:652-664`); after the first `Open` fails there are at most three further attempts: (2) close any open workbook with the same name, wait 3 s and retry (`:675-685`); (3) the 8.3 short path (`:692-700`); (4) **either** - if the long-path prefix was added - the path without it (`:702-706`), **or** - otherwise - `Open(..., UpdateLinks=0, ReadOnly=False, IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True, Notify=False)` (`:708-715`); when the last attempt fails and the error contains -2147352567, advice is written to the log (file open elsewhere, damaged, path too long, OneDrive/SharePoint sync, `:719-729`) (READ) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally "up to four further attempts" listing the last two as separate steps; they are alternatives, so a long path never gets the `UpdateLinks=0` call].

**O. When a refresh counts as successful** - `report_processor.py:573-620@edac6a3`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (a rule about the template; the sheet and cell depend on the template)

- A sheet named "Info" (any case) must exist and its cell **BB2** must be not empty, not blank, not "0" or "0.0", and not one of `#REF! #VALUE! #NAME? #NULL! #DIV/0! #N/A #NUM! #ERROR!`. The success message calls BB2 "Client Name" (`:616`).

**P. Which cells the extractor reads** - `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py@edac6a3`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (sheet names and cell positions depend on the templates; the GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 references belong to return formats that can change)

| Output sheet | Report | Template sheet!cell → output column | Lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSTR-3B Difference | ITC | `Diff GSTR-3B`!J15 → "Diff IGST"; !K15 → "Diff CGST"; !L15 → "Diff SGST" | `:35-58` |
| GSTR-1 Difference | Sales | `Diff - GSTR-1`!N1 → "Diff Taxable Value"; !O1 → "Diff IGST"; !P1 → "Diff CGST"; !Q1 → "Diff SGST" | `:61-89` |
| Turnover GSTR-1 | Sales | `Diff - GSTR-1`!I1 → "Taxable Value" | `:92-102` |

- The file is written to be edited by hand ("MASTER VERSION ... HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE", `:1-27`); every entry can also name a calculation (subtract, add, multiply, divide; divide by zero gives the text "Div/0", non-numbers "Error", `data_consolidator.py:188-218`). No entry uses one.
- `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS` (`:122-127`): skip_refresh False (changed by the checkbox), auto_refresh_if_missing True (never read), show_timestamp False (never read), missing_data_text "Missing".
- A "backward compatibility" block (`:133-152`) turns the list into the older shape `CELL_MAPPINGS[report][sheet][cell] = "<output sheet>_<output column>"` (spaces → `_`) that the reader still uses. If two output sheets ever named the same template sheet and cell, the later one would silently replace the earlier one (READ, HIGH; no such pair exists in the shared range).
- While reading, each value is stored twice: under its field name and under its bare cell reference such as "J15" "for calculations" (`report_processor.py:519-523`). Bare references from different template sheets of the same report would overwrite each other (READ, MEDIUM; no calculation uses them here).
- Sheet names must match exactly, including case (`report_processor.py:500`); a missing sheet gives empty values. The extraction log claims "Opening file in read-only mode" (`:476-478`) but the workbook is opened normally (read-write) and closed without saving (READ, HIGH). Every value read is written into `pq_extractor.log` and the window log (`:525,541-546`).
- `cell_mappings copy.py@edac6a3` holds the older format directly (`'Diff GSTR-3B': {'J15': 'itc_diff_igst', ...}`, `'Diff - GSTR-1': {'N1': 'sales_diff_tv', ...}`) with display names such as "Diff IGST (ITC)" and commented ideas `'E5': 'reversed_itc'`, `'F5': 'net_itc'`, `'D10': 'export_sales'`, `'E10': 'exempt_sales'`. It names the same cells as the current file except `Diff - GSTR-1`!I1, which is new. The compiled-file evidence (Y) dates it to 21-06-2025.

**Q. The consolidated extraction workbook** (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:20-186@edac6a3`; READ, RAN where marked)

- `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx` (year first - a different date order from the organiser's folder and report names) in the newest Annual Statement folder; a "Summary" sheet first (date, number of clients, "ITC Reports Processed: n/total", list of sheets, `:220-248`), then one sheet per output sheet with columns Client Name, Successfully Run (✓/✗), then one column per mapping.
- [GST RULE] When a report's refresh did not succeed, every value cell of that report shows the text "Missing" (`:128-129`), even if values were read. A value that was read as empty (`None` or an empty text, for example because the sheet was not found) also shows "Missing" (`:153-154`), while a zero stays 0 (added in re-check 21-10-2026). Non-zero numbers get the Excel display format `#,##0.00` (`:161-162`); zeros keep the default format; the stored values are not rounded (READ, HIGH).
- Each column's value is looked up by a **substring test** first - "is the column name contained in a field name?" - and only then by the exact field name (`:141-150`):

  ```python
  for field_name, field_value in extracted_data.items():
      if mapping['output_column'] in field_name:     # substring test
          value = field_value
          break
  if value is None and mapping['input_cell']:        # exact name only if nothing was found
      key = f"{sheet_name}_{mapping['output_column']}".replace(' ', '_')
      value = extracted_data.get(key)
  ```

  At edac6a3 this is harmless by accident: every column name contains a space and every field name uses underscores, so the substring test never matches and the exact lookup finds every value. RAN (`test_consolidator.py`, each value set to its own "sheet!cell" label): every column at edac6a3 shows its own cell. It becomes harmful at 47a1492 (see that commit).
- Old methods `_write_section` (`:250-352`) and `_create_details_sheet` (`:354-414`) belong to an earlier single-sheet layout (ITC section, Sales section, details) and are never called; lines 73-83 build and write the header row a first time with "# ... rest of the code" place-holders, and lines 85-99 do it again properly.
