**Plain-English terms used in this appendix.**

- **Workbook / template**: `.xlsx` is a normal Excel workbook, `.xlsm` its macro-enabled version, `.xltx` / `.xltm` Excel templates. All are ZIP files holding XML "parts".
- **Power Query** (Excel's built-in data-import tool, "Get & Transform"). Its queries live inside the workbook in a hidden part `customXml/item*.xml` containing an element called **DataMashup**, with connection records in `xl/connections.xml`. **Refresh** = re-running the queries so the workbook reads its source files again.
- **openpyxl** (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel). When it **saves** a workbook it rebuilds the file from what it understands and drops the Power Query parts; reading is harmless (Standard 12 table row at `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:827`).
- **COM** (Component Object Model: Windows' way for one program to remote-control another; here Python drives Microsoft Excel). **pywin32** provides it to Python (`win32com`, `pythoncom`) together with window functions (`win32gui`, `win32api`, `win32con`).
- **GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx** (three ways for Python to get an Excel): `GetActiveObject` grabs the Excel that is already running (normally the user's own); `Dispatch` asks Windows for "an Excel" and may connect to one already running; `DispatchEx` always starts a separate one. Standard 12 requires `DispatchEx`.
- **Visible / DisplayAlerts / ScreenUpdating / WindowState** (Excel settings: is its window shown; does it show prompts such as "Save changes?"; does it repaint the screen; is its window maximised). **Quit()** closes that whole Excel, with every workbook open in it.
- **RefreshAll / BackgroundQuery / CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone / Refreshing / RefreshDate** (the COM calls and properties Standard 12 names for a safe refresh: switch off background refresh on each connection, refresh everything, wait until every query has finished, check none is still refreshing, never trust the refresh date).
- **WScript.Shell / AppActivate / SendKeys** (a Windows scripting object; `AppActivate(title)` asks Windows to bring forward a window with that title; `SendKeys` types keystrokes into **whichever window has the keyboard focus**, as if a person pressed them). **Ribbon key tips** (Excel's Alt-key shortcuts: Alt, A opens the Data tab; R, A = Refresh All).
- **win32gui EnumWindows / BM_CLICK / WM_CLOSE** (list every top-level window on the desktop; "click this button"; "please close this window").
- **Thread / worker thread** (a second line of work beside the window so the window does not freeze; B uses Qt's **QThread**). **CoInitialize / CoUninitialize** (calls a worker thread must make before and after using COM).
- **`finally` block** (code Python runs at the end of a `try`, whether or not an error happened; used for clean-up).
- **8.3 short path** (an old DOS-style short alias of a long path). **`\\?\` prefix** (a Windows prefix that lifts the 260-character path limit for programs that support it). **UNC path** (a network path `\\server\share\...`).
- **glob** (a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`). **mtime** (a file's or folder's "date modified").

**Thread names used below** (all READ, and RAN in E2E where the fake records the Python thread name): **Main** = the window's own thread ("MainThread"); **SW** = the Step 1 scan worker, a QThread started at `gui/controllers/scan_controller.py:65-80`; **PW** = the Step 3 processing worker, a QThread started at `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:265-279` (in E2E it appeared as "Dummy-2"); **EW** = the Step 4 extraction worker, a QThread started at `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:148-165` (in E2E "Dummy-3").

### X1.1 The findings that matter most (author's top priority)

> **1. B never checks a workbook for Power Query before an openpyxl save, and its openpyxl fallback silently strips Power Query while reporting success - but in B's snapshot that fallback cannot be reached through the window.** RAN (F1): on Linux, B's own `create_report_from_template` returned `True` for a template carrying `customXml/item1.xml` (DataMashup) and `xl/connections.xml`; the output had neither. The only warnings ("Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!", `core/excel_handler.py:90`; "Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!", `:224`) go to the program log, never to the screen. There is no `DataMashup` or `customXml` text anywhere in B's Python code (RAN search: 0 hits). The fallback is unreachable through the app only by accident: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` imports pywin32 unconditionally, and the window imports that module at start-up (first through `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25` → `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` → `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10`; `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:27` would import it again), so without pywin32 the window never opens (RAN M1: "Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'", exit 1; RAN traceback in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-X12/`: `gui/__init__.py:7` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25` → `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` → `extraction_controller.py:10` → `report_processor.py:11`). At the split point (47a1492) the Tkinter organiser did **not** import the extractor (READ: `git grep report_processor` at 47a1492 finds it only in `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:12`, which is reached only through `launch_extractor.py:14` → `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:9`; nothing under `main.py` or the Tkinter `gui/` imports the extractor), so a Windows PC without pywin32 took this fallback and lost the queries; c258047 (B only (after the split)) closed that door as a side effect of the PyQt5 rewrite (PyQt5: the Python package for building Qt windows). HIGH. The same save also drops shapes drawn on a template sheet (text boxes, buttons), again with `True` (RAN X1.4.3 F5, added during the completeness check). See B-R97, B-R124, B-G32, B-G31.

> **2. Step 3 takes over the user's own open Excel, hides it, and then quits it with its prompts switched back on.** `core/excel_handler.py:110-112` first calls `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` and logs "Using existing Excel instance"; only if that fails does it call `Dispatch` (`:113-115`). It then sets `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` on whatever it got (`:118-120`). In the clean-up it sets `ScreenUpdating = True` and `DisplayAlerts = True` (`:204-205`) and, because the test `if self.excel_app is None` (`:207`) is always true (`self.excel_app` is set to `None` at `:55` and never assigned anything else - READ, search), it always calls `Quit()` (`:209`); the comment "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:206`) describes intent, not behaviour. `Visible` is never set back. RAN (fake COM, S3 "user_excel"): `USER_EXCEL.Visible = False` … `USER_EXCEL.DisplayAlerts = True`, `USER_EXCEL.Quit()` while the user's own `UserOwnBook.xlsx` was still open in it. What a real Excel then does (a "save changes?" prompt in a hidden window that can block B for ever, as Standard 12 warns at `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:854-855`) is MEDIUM; not testable here. This happens once per report, twice per client. See B-R96, B-G63.

> **3. Step 4 does not refresh with Excel's refresh command: it presses keys in a visible, maximised Excel, waits fixed times, and then always saves.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:174` (`Dispatch`, not `DispatchEx`), `:181-183` (`Visible = True` "Keep it visible to avoid issues", `DisplayAlerts = False`, maximised), `:216-249` (`WScript.Shell` → `AppActivate(excel.Caption)` → `SendKeys("%a")`, `"r"`, `"a"` = Alt+A, R, A ⚠), `:253-298` (fixed waits and dialog checks), `:301` (Info!BB2 check), `:305` (`wb.Save()` - before the result is decided at `:310-330`). There is no `RefreshAll`, `BackgroundQuery`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, `Connections`, `Refreshing` or `RefreshDate` anywhere in B (RAN search: 0 hits each). RAN (fake COM, E2E): 39 seconds of fixed waits per report at the default wait of 10 s (in E2E: 4 refreshed reports × 39 s + 4 Step 3 reports × 1 s = 160 s in all), two Excel start-ups per report. Standard 12 rules R5a-R5d (X1.3.1) NOT MET. See B-F19, B-R66, B-R67, B-R68, B-R69, B-G6, B-G57.

> **4. The keystrokes are sent even when Excel could not be brought forward and even when no workbook is open.** `AppActivate` failures are only logged (`report_processor.py:220-230`); the keys follow at `:238-248` regardless. When every open attempt is refused with "Call was rejected by callee", the open loop (`:195-205`) simply ends with `wb = None` and the code carries on. RAN (fake COM, S4 "open_rejected"): nine rejected opens, then `AppActivate('Excel')`, `SendKeys('%a')`, `SendKeys('r')`, `SendKeys('a')` were still sent - into whichever window had the keyboard focus - and the report failed with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'Save'". HIGH for the code; what the keys do on a real desktop is MEDIUM. See B-G62.

> **5. The "error dialog" closer looks at every window on the desktop and clicks buttons in other programs.** `report_processor.py:368-404` collects every visible, enabled top-level window whose title contains "microsoft excel", "error", "problem", "cannot", "failed", "unable", "could not", "exception", "invalid" or "missing" and whose class is `#32770`, `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword`; `:443-476` clicks the first child button whose text contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue", else posts a close message. RAN (fake COM, S4 "error_dialog"): with an unrelated program's dialog "Upload failed - OtherProgram" listed before Excel's own error box, B recorded that program's text as the refresh error, clicked its **Close** button, and left Excel's dialog open. HIGH for the code; how often another program's dialog is first in a real desktop's order is MEDIUM/LOW. See B-F26, B-R102, B-R103, B-G61.

> **6. The only proof of a successful refresh is "Info!BB2 is not empty, not 0, not an error text"** (`report_processor.py:589-636`) [GST RULE] ⚠ (cell position). It cannot tell a value written by this refresh from one already in the file. RAN (fake COM, S4 "bb2_stale"): with BB2 holding another client's placeholder and the refresh doing nothing, B reported `success: True`, "Validated - Client Name: <Client B>", ✓ and every figure. `RefreshDate` is never used (MET in letter). See B-F20, B-R71, B-G6.

> **7. A Step 3 report whose filling fails stays on disk, unfilled, under the report's normal name.** The template is copied to the final report name first (`core/excel_handler.py:124`) and only then opened (`:129`); no temporary name is used. RAN (fake COM, S3 "long_path" and "excel_dies"): the 8,406-byte unfilled template copy remained under `ITC_Report_…xlsx`; Step 4 later lists and refreshes it like any report. If Excel has died, the clean-up itself raises at `:204` (unprotected), so `Quit()` (`:209`) and `CoUninitialize()` (`:215`) are skipped (RAN: the last recorded call was `EXCEL1.ScreenUpdating = True -> RAISES`). See B-R52, B-G5, B-G38.

> **8. Nine of the 22 figure columns of the consolidated Step 4 workbook show a different cell from the one the configuration names** - a technical mismatch between configuration and code; which cell is right is the author's call [GST RULE] ⚠. RAN (E2E, real `DataConsolidator`): with distinct invented markers in every mapped cell, the IGST / CGST / SGST columns of the sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" all showed 1101 / 1102 / 1103 - the markers placed in `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15` - instead of 1501-1503 (`IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`), 1601-1603 (`ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1`) and 1701-1703 (`ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1`). Cause: the part-of-text look-up at `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:130-133` runs before the exact-name look-up at `:136-138`. See B-F23, B-R79 to B-R83, B-G1.

> **9. A failed refresh leaves a "_Refreshed_" file that later counts as refreshed.** The copy is made (`report_processor.py:120`) before Excel is even started. RAN (fake COM, S4 "no_excel"): with Excel absent, `ITC_Report_…_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` (an unrefreshed byte copy) was left in the Version folder. The Step 4 list then shows the version as "Refreshed (date)" because any `*_Refreshed*` file exists (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:467-479`), and "Skip refresh" re-uses the newest such file with `success: True` "Skipped - Using existing refreshed file" (`report_processor.py:100-111`; RAN S4 "skip_after_failed": ✓ and every figure). Meanwhile a refresh that did fail shows every figure of that report as "Missing" although the cells were read (`data_consolidator.py:116-117`; RAN E2E `<Client B>` rows ✗ / Missing). See B-R63, B-R88, B-G7, B-G10.

> **10. Read-only state is never checked, and `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` is used only by the last fallback open.** No `.ReadOnly` property is read anywhere in B (RAN search: the only `ReadOnly` texts are Qt `setReadOnly` calls on the four log boxes and the keywords `ReadOnly=False` and `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` at `report_processor.py:728-729`). Step 3 opens with a plain `Workbooks.Open(path)` (`core/excel_handler.py:286, 301`); Step 4 passes `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` only in the third attempt's last branch (`report_processor.py:725-731`). The Step 4 reading session tells the user "Opening file in read-only mode" (`:492`) and "File opened in read-only mode" (`:494`) although the open is read-write. See B-R98, B-R99, B-R101, B-G53.

> **11. COM is switched off inside the same function while Excel objects are still held, and nothing ever times out or kills Excel.** `pythoncom.CoUninitialize()` sits in each Excel function's own `finally` (`core/excel_handler.py:215`; `report_processor.py:363, 584`), while `excel`, `wb`, `ws` and the `WScript.Shell` object are still local variables (Standard 12 asks for it after the Excel function returns, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:872-875`). No `taskkill`, no `EXCEL.EXE`, no COM timeout exists in B (RAN search); Stop is checked only between clients / versions (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:81`, `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:61`). A hung Excel hangs the worker for ever. See B-R110, B-G39, B-G77.

> **12. Steps 3 and 4 can drive Excel at the same time.** Each controller refuses only a second job of its own kind (`processing_controller.py:259-261`; `extraction_controller.py:142-144`); the window disables neither tab's Start button while the other runs (READ `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:345-371, 506-547`). Step 3's `GetActiveObject` would then grab Step 4's visible Excel (READ, HIGH for the code path; the real outcome is MEDIUM). Closing the window during a run is accepted at once (`pyqt_main_window.py:601-608`). See B-F34, B-R111, B-G40, B-G74.

> **13. Originals are never modified.** Client input files are only `stat()`-ed, read for 8 bytes and copied (`core/file_parser.py:176, 195-196`; `utils/helpers.py:169`); templates are only checked and copied (`core/excel_handler.py:78, 124, 228`); Step 4 refreshes a copy, never the Step 3 report (`report_processor.py:118-120`; an empty suffix makes the copy name equal the original, and `shutil.copy2` then refuses with "same file", RAN S4 "empty_suffix"). RAN (E2E): SHA-256 fingerprints of all 17 invented source and template files were identical before and after the whole Step 1-4 run. The only file deletions in B are `utils/helpers.py:177` (a destination copy whose size differs) and `core/file_organizer.py:375` (inside the never-called `cleanup_on_error`). HIGH.

### X1.2 (a) Every place B touches a workbook

Column meanings. **Library**: COM = Excel through pywin32; openpyxl; `shutil` (Python's file copy, `copy2` also copies the file dates); `pathlib` (Python's path and folder listing); Windows = `win32gui` / `win32api` / `WScript.Shell`. **Which workbook**: what the file is. **Can it hold Power Query?**: "yes (intended)" = the ITC and Sales templates and everything copied from them; README.md:14 ("Refresh Power Query connections in Excel reports"), README.md:24 and the module docstrings (`core/excel_handler.py:2-3`, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:2`) say these carry Power Query, but no template is in the repository, so this is the author's intent, not something I could inspect (MEDIUM-HIGH). "no" = a workbook B creates from scratch with openpyxl. "unknown" = the client input files, which B never opens. **Thread**: see X1.0. **READ/RAN**: evidence for the row.

#### X1.2.9 What B never does (RAN: search of every `.py` file at the snapshot)

No `DispatchEx`, `EnsureDispatch`, `RefreshAll`, `BackgroundQuery`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, `Connections`, `Queries`, `Refreshing`, `RefreshDate`, `.ReadOnly` (as a property read), `SaveAs`, `SaveCopyAs`, `DataMashup`, `customXml`, `taskkill`, `EXCEL.EXE`, `subprocess`, `os.system`, `winreg` (Python's access to the Windows registry, Windows' settings database) or environment-variable read such as `os.environ` / `getenv` (0 hits each; the only text containing "environ" is the function name `setup_environment`, `main.py:26, 35`). `keep_vba` appears once, inside the unused `EXCEL_SAFETY` constant (`utils/constants.py:225`). B never kills an Excel process, never times out a COM call, and never runs anything as a scheduled job.

### X1.3 (b) Each Excel session checked against Standard 12 "Excel through COM"

#### X1.3.1 The rules, numbered for this appendix

Standard 12's section "Excel through COM" (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:844-877`), plus its table rows for openpyxl and COM (`:827-828`), split into single checkable rules:

| Rule | What Standard 12 asks (paraphrased; line) |
|---|---|
| R1a | Use COM only for a workbook with Power Query queries that the app writes into or refreshes (`:846-847`; table row `:828`). |
| R1b | Before saving with openpyxl into a workbook the app did not create, check it for a `customXml/item*.xml` part containing `DataMashup` (`:847-849`). |
| R1c | If one is found, use COM or stop and tell the user; never let openpyxl save over such a workbook (`:849-850`). |
| R2a | Start a separate Excel with `win32com.client.DispatchEx("Excel.Application")` (`:851-852`). |
| R2b | `excel.Visible = False` (`:853`). |
| R2c | `excel.DisplayAlerts = False` - and still False when `Quit()` runs, or `Quit()` can wait for ever on an invisible "save changes?" prompt (`:853-855`). |
| R2d | Never take over the user's own open Excel (`:853-854`). |
| R3 | Always call `excel.Quit()` in a `finally` block, even after an error (`:856`). |
| R4a | Open the workbook with `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` (`:857`). |
| R4b | If `workbook.ReadOnly` is then true, close it and ask the user to close the workbook in Excel first (`:857-859`). |
| R5a | To refresh: `BackgroundQuery = False` on each of the workbook's connections (`:860-861`). |
| R5b | Call `workbook.RefreshAll()` (`:861`). |
| R5c | Then `excel.CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()`, and only then save (`:862-865`). |
| R5d | Before saving, check that no connection's `Refreshing` is still true (`:865-866`). |
| R5e | Never use a connection's `RefreshDate` as proof of a refresh (`:866-867`). |
| R6 | Adding a query (`Queries.Add`) works; loading it into a new table (`ListObjects.Add`) failed - ask first (`:868-871`). |
| R7a | In a worker thread, call `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` first (`:872-873`). |
| R7b | Do the Excel work in a separate function (`:873-874`). |
| R7c | Call `pythoncom.CoUninitialize()` after that function returns, so no Excel object is still held (`:874-875`). |
| R8 | Excel must be installed on every PC that runs the app; it needs a logged-in user; never a scheduled job (`:876-877`). |

| Session | Where | When | Thread |

| S2 | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:165-366` `_refresh_power_query_simple` | Step 4, once per ticked report that is not skipped (B-F19) | EW |
| S3 | `report_processor.py:478-587` `_extract_data` | Step 4, right after S2 (or after a skip) for the same report (B-F22) | EW |

- **Dependency file.** `requirements.txt:13-14` reads "# Windows-only: Excel COM automation for Power Query" / "# pywin32>=306" - commented out, so `pip install -r requirements.txt` does not install it. README.md:105-108 shows a "Requirements.txt Contents" block with `pywin32>=305; sys_platform == 'win32'` as if it were in the file, and README.md:275 gives a `pip install pywin32` plus `pywin32_postinstall.py -install` hint for "No module named 'win32com'". (READ)
- **Import chain.** `main.py:38` imports `gui.pyqt_main_window`; importing anything under `gui` runs `gui/__init__.py:7` (the main window), whose `:25` imports `gui.controllers.scan_controller` - which first runs the package file `gui/controllers/__init__.py`, whose `:4` imports the extraction controller, whose `:10` imports `report_processor.py`, whose `:11` is `import pythoncom` with no guard. (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:27` imports the extraction controller again, but the failure has already happened at `:25`.) Because `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` imports that controller, even the processing controller cannot be imported on its own. (READ; RAN traceback in my scratch copy `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-X12/`, Python 3.14 without pywin32: `gui/__init__.py:7` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:25` → `gui/controllers/__init__.py:4` → `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10` → `report_processor.py:11` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'`)
- **RAN (M1) `python main.py` without pywin32:** console "Missing module: No module named 'pythoncom'" / "Please install required packages:" / "  pip install PyQt5 openpyxl" (`main.py:49-54`) - a command that would not fix it - exit code 1; one line "ERROR - Import Error: No module named 'pythoncom'" written to `gst_organizer.log` in the folder the program was started from (and echoed first on the console, because the log is also sent to the console, `main.py:21`; re-run by this check with the same result); `~/.gst_organizer` not created.
- **RAN (M2) `python launch_extractor.py`:** "Failed to launch: No module named 'pythoncom'", exit 1, no log line (it sets up no logging, `launch_extractor.py:11-24`).
- **RAN (M3) `python -m power_query_extractor.extractor_main`:** `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'power_query_extractor.gui.extractor_window'` - fails earlier, on the deleted window.
- **RAN (M4) `platform.system()` patched to "Windows", no pywin32:** `core.excel_handler` imports, logs "win32com not available. Install with: pip install pywin32" and sets `USE_WIN32COM = False`; `gui.controllers.processing_controller` and `gui.pyqt_main_window` both fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'`.
- **What the user sees** (inference, MEDIUM-HIGH): started from a console, the three lines above and the program ends; started without a console (`pythonw.exe` - the Python program that opens no console window - or a shortcut, as Standard 13 requires, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:962, 969`) nothing at all appears (`print()` goes nowhere; no message box; no `sys.excepthook` - Python's last-chance handler for errors nothing else caught -, READ `main.py:32-59`); only the one ERROR line in `gst_organizer.log` in the start folder remains, if that folder is writable (READ `main.py:16-23, 50`).
- **Is there a silent query-dropping path in this snapshot?** Through the window: **no** - `USE_WIN32COM` can only be False where the extractor import has already stopped the window (HIGH). The only theoretical exception is a pywin32 install where `win32com.client` or `pythoncom` imports in one file and not the other; both files need both modules, so the window would still stop (HIGH). But the fallback code is intact and becomes live the moment the extractor import is made optional (which README.md:52-55's "Windows 10/11 (best), macOS, Linux" implies was intended) - then Power Query would be dropped silently with "✅ Success" on screen. Merge risk, HIGH.
- **pywin32 present but Excel missing** (RAN fake COM): Step 3 - `Dispatch` raises, the report fails with "❌ Failed to create ITC report" (no file left, because the template copy comes after `Dispatch`) (S3 "no_excel"); Step 4 - `Dispatch` raises in S2 and S3, status `{success False, error 'Invalid class string'}`, but the `_Refreshed_` byte copy made at `report_processor.py:120` **is left behind** and every figure becomes "Missing" (S4 "no_excel").
- **pywin32 installed but its post-install step not run** (DLLs not registered): `import pythoncom` can fail with an `ImportError` - same outcome as "missing" (MEDIUM, general pywin32 behaviour; not testable here).

### X1.8 What cannot be checked on this computer, and how the author can check it

Use a Windows test PC with Excel and pywin32, invented clients only, and copies of the real templates.

| Question | Why it matters | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| Does `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (Step 4) attach to an Excel the user already has open? | If yes, Step 4 maximises the user's Excel, types into it and quits it without asking to save. | Open Excel with an unsaved "Book1"; run Step 4 for one invented client; watch whether Book1's window is reused or closed. |
| What does Step 3 do to an Excel the user already has open? | `GetActiveObject` certainly attaches (code); the effect of `Visible = False` and `Quit()` with alerts on is real-Excel behaviour. | Open Excel with an unsaved book; run Step 3; note whether the windows vanish, whether a save prompt appears (perhaps hidden), and whether B hangs. |
| Does Alt+A, R, A refresh in the office Excel version and display language? ⚠ | The whole refresh relies on it. | Open a report copy in that Excel and press Alt, A, R, A by hand; check that "Refresh All" runs. |
| Are 10 s + 5 s + 10 s enough for the real queries? | B saves after fixed waits. | Time a manual Refresh All of a real report; compare with the Step 4 wait setting. |
| What does `Range(...).Value` return for error cells, currency and dates? | These go into the consolidated workbook unchecked (B-G11, B-G43). | Put `#N/A`, a currency and a date in mapped cells of a test copy; run Step 4; open the consolidated workbook. |

#### X2.1.2 What happens to the template file

- It is **never modified**. For each processed client it is copied byte for byte (`shutil.copy2`) to `<Version folder>/ITC_Report_<client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` and `…/Sales_Report_<client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` (`gui/controllers/processing_controller.py:111-130, 220`; `core/excel_handler.py:124` COM path, `:228` fallback); the copy is then opened and filled. - The report is **always named `.xlsx`** whatever the template's own extension (`processing_controller.py:220`; B-R51). In the COM path the bytes are copied unchanged, so an `.xlsm` or `.xltx` template becomes a macro-enabled or template package with an `.xlsx` name; whether Excel then refuses to open it is not testable here (MEDIUM that it shows "file format or extension is not valid"; how to check: X1.8). In the openpyxl fallback an `.xlsm` template's macro project is dropped (RAN F4).
- **Every processed client always gets both reports**, whatever input files it has (`processing_controller.py:116-130`; B-R50) [GST RULE].

### X2.2 Input files and file-name patterns

#### X2.2.1 Which files are looked at (B-R1 to B-R4)

- Only the **top level** of the chosen source folder; sub-folders are ignored without a message (`utils/helpers.py:249-266`, non-recursive glob; B-G46).
- Extensions searched, in this order: `*.xlsx`, `*.xls`, `*.xlsm` (`:255-257`); names starting with `~$` (Excel's lock files) dropped (`:259-260`); the rest sorted by full path (`:262`). Any listing error → empty list → "No Excel files found" (`:264-266`). Other extensions (`.csv`, `.xlsb`, `.pdf`, …) are ignored silently and counted nowhere (RAN E2E: `notes.csv`).
- Letter case of the extension: on Linux the search is case-sensitive - RAN (L): of `GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-Apr.XLSX`, `GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-May.xlsx`, `~$GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-May.xlsx` and `sub/GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-Jun.xlsx`, only the `May.xlsx` file was returned (upper-case extension, lock file and sub-folder all left out); on Windows Python's `Path.glob` ignores case by default, so the `.XLSX` file would be found (HIGH, Python behaviour; not runnable here). The **name patterns** below ignore case on every system (RAN L: `gstr3b-clienta-delhi-apr.XLSX` recognised).
- Per file (`core/file_parser.py:171-256`): `stat()` failure → skipped, log warning only; size < 1024 bytes → problem file "File too small to be valid Excel"; first 8 bytes not `PK\x03\x04` or `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0` → "Invalid or corrupted Excel file"; unreadable → "Cannot read file: <error>"; then the name is matched against the patterns. Problem files are kept in a list (`variations`) that is never shown; only their number reaches the screen (B-F9, B-G20). The **content** of an input file is never read by Python beyond those 8 bytes - only the templates' queries read it.

#### X2.2.2 The six patterns, exactly as coded [GST RULE] ⚠

All compiled with `re.IGNORECASE`, matched against the whole file name (`^…$`), tried in this fixed order, first match wins (`utils/constants.py:13-62`; loop `core/file_parser.py:77-118`). ⚠: the return names, file types and period formats can change over time.

| # | Key | Regular expression (a text pattern used to recognise file names; verbatim) | File type | `category` / `folder` fields (copied into the record, never used) | Parts captured | Copied to (`core/file_organizer.py:285-298`) | Links cell(s) it feeds | Example text in the code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GSTR-2B-Reco` | `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | GSTR-2B Reco | ITC / itc | client, state, period | `Other ITC related files[ (<client>)]` | ITC B7 (folder), B8 (name) | `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` |
| 2 | `ImsReco` | `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})\.xlsx?$` | IMS Reco | ITC / itc | client, state, date (exactly 8 digits) | `Other ITC related files[ (<client>)]` | ITC B10, B11 | `ImsReco-ClientName-State-DDMMYYYY.xlsx` |
| 3 | `GSTR3B` | `^(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?GSTR3B-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | GSTR-3B Export | GSTR3B / gstr3b | client, state, month | `GSTR-3B Exports[ (<client>)]` | ITC B2 (folder only) | `GSTR3B-ClientName-State-Month.xlsx` |
| 4 | `Sales` | `^Sales-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | Sales | Sales / sales | client, state, start_month, end_month | `Sales related files[ (<client>)]` | Sales B2, B3 | `Sales-ClientName-State-StartMonth-EndMonth.xlsx` |
| 5 | `SalesReco` | `^SalesReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | Sales Reco | Sales / sales | client, state, period | `Sales related files[ (<client>)]` | Sales B8, B9 | `SalesReco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` |
| 6 | `AnnualReport` | `^AnnualReport-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | Annual Report | Annual / root | client, state, year | the Version folder itself | ITC B4, B5 and Sales B5, B6 | `AnnualReport-ClientName-State-Year.xlsx` |

The same six names are typed again, by hand, in the Step 1 help card (`gui/views/setup_view.py:492-498`: "GSTR-2B-Reco-Client-State-Period", "ImsReco-Client-State-DDMMYYYY", "GSTR3B-Client-State-Month", "Sales-Client-State-Start-End", "SalesReco-Client-State-Period", "AnnualReport-Client-State-Year") and in the never-shown hint for unrecognised files (`core/file_parser.py:316-334`: tests in this order - contains "gstr" and "2b" → pattern 1's example; "ims" → 2; "gstr" and "3b" → 3; "sales" and "reco" → 5; "sales" → 4; "annual" → 6; otherwise "Check file naming convention"). The `folder` field "root" for the Annual Report disagrees with where it is really copied (the Version folder), but nothing reads that field (B-R13).

#### X2.2.4 How a file becomes a client; state codes [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Client key** = `"<client text>-<state code>"` with the client text as written (trimmed, letter case kept) (`core/file_parser.py:258-278`). "Delhi" and "DL" give the same key (both DL, RAN L); "Tamil Nadu" (TN) and "Tamilnadu" (TAM, RAN L) give two keys; "ClientA" and "clienta" give two keys (READ: the key is built from the text as written; RAN L shows the lower-case client text is kept; re-run by this check). See B-G16.
- **State codes** (`utils/constants.py:234-275`, look-up `utils/helpers.py:485-511`) ⚠ - 39 lower-case names, 36 distinct two-letter codes: andhra pradesh AP; arunachal pradesh AR; assam AS; bihar BR; chhattisgarh CG; goa GA; gujarat GJ; haryana HR; himachal pradesh HP; jharkhand JH; karnataka KA; kerala KL; madhya pradesh MP; maharashtra MH; manipur MN; meghalaya ML; mizoram MZ; nagaland NL; odisha OD; orissa OD; punjab PB; rajasthan RJ; sikkim SK; tamil nadu TN; telangana TS; tripura TR; uttar pradesh UP; uttarakhand UK; west bengal WB; andaman and nicobar islands AN; chandigarh CH; dadra and nagar haveli and daman and diu DD; delhi DL; national capital territory of delhi DL; jammu and kashmir JK; ladakh LA; lakshadweep LD; puducherry PY; pondicherry PY. These are letter abbreviations, not the numeric GSTIN state codes; B has no GSTIN or PAN logic.
- **Unknown state**: two or more words → first letters of the first two words ("New Delhi" → ND); one word → the first three characters upper-cased ("Tamilnadu" → TAM; "DL" → DL) (RAN L). Each fallback writes a warning to the log.
- The code is used in the client key, the client folder name and both report names (X2.4).

#### X2.2.5 Which files a client is expected to have [GST RULE] ⚠

`EXPECTED_FILE_TYPES` (`utils/constants.py:68-75`): GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B Export, Sales, Sales Reco, Annual Report. Status (`core/file_parser.py:280-314`): "Complete" when none is missing and no type other than GSTR-3B Export has two or more files; "Missing <n> files" (n = number of missing types); otherwise "Has duplicates". GSTR-3B Export may have any number of files ("monthly filings - unlimited", `:294-296`); the number of months and their years are not checked. Completeness % = types found ÷ 6 × 100, one decimal.

#### X2.2.6 What the input files must contain

Nothing is checked by Python beyond the 8-byte signature. Their content matters only to the templates' Power Query queries, which the repository does not hold - so the required sheets, columns and layouts of a GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B export, Sales, Sales Reco and Annual Report file are unknown from the code (READ, HIGH). This is why the checklist in X2.8 asks for one real (anonymised) sample of each.

### X2.3 The folder layout the code READS

| What | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Source folder | One flat folder chosen in Step 1; must exist (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:218-225`); top-level Excel files only (X2.2.1). The scan reads the box text at the moment SCAN FILES is pressed; processing later uses that scan, even if the box was changed since. | READ |
| Target folder - Re-Run / Resume | Sub-folders whose name starts with `Annual Statement-`; the one with the newest **modification time** is reused (`core/file_organizer.py:158-169`); none → a new one is created with a warning (`:170-179`). | READ; RAN L ("Annual Statement-020126 0900", modified later, chosen) |
| Target folder - Step 4 list | The same sub-folders; the one with the **highest name** (Z→A) is shown (`gui/pyqt_main_window.py:432-448`). Names are day-first (`DDMMYY HHMM`), so this is not date order. Only that one run folder is ever offered. The target used is the last **saved** one (`self.settings.target_folder`, `:421`), not the text in the box. | READ; RAN L ("Annual Statement-311225 0900" chosen over "…-020126 0900"); at the split the extractor used mtime (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:517@47a1492`), changed in b0e7d0e (B only (after the split)) |
| Step 4 tree inside that run folder | Every sub-folder (client folder, any name - not checked against the naming rules) A→Z; inside it every sub-folder (version folder, any name) Z→A that contains `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` or `Sales_Report_*.xlsx` (`:450-495`); status "Refreshed (dd/mm/yy HH:MM)" if any `*_Refreshed*` file with `.xlsx/.xls/.xlsm` (not `~$`) exists - one per version folder, not per report - else "Pending". | READ; RAN E2E |
| Step 4 report to refresh | First file the listing returns for `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` / `Sales_Report_*.xlsx` in the version folder (`report_processor.py:76-89`) - also matches refreshed copies. | READ; RAN S4 |
| Step 4 "Skip refresh" | Newest `<stem>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` (`report_processor.py:102-105`) - fixed text, ignores a custom suffix. | READ; RAN S4 |

**The two "latest run folder" rules disagree** (mtime for Step 3, name for Step 4): after work across a month or year boundary, Step 4 shows and writes its consolidated workbook and log into an older batch (B-G12).

### X2.4 The folder layout the code CREATES

Created by Step 3 (`core/file_organizer.py`, `gui/controllers/processing_controller.py`, `core/excel_handler.py`) and Step 4 (`report_processor.py`, `data_consolidator.py`, `extraction_controller.py`). RAN E2E produced exactly this tree (stamps `231026 1510`):

```text
<Target folder>/                                        created if missing (core/file_organizer.py:61-65; utils/helpers.py:39-47)
└── Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                     run folder ("Level 1"): utils/constants.py:82; Fresh: new each run (same name within one minute)
    ├── GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx       Step 3, openpyxl, only if ≥1 client succeeded (processing_controller.py:183-193)
    ├── PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx       Step 4, openpyxl (data_consolidator.py:163-167) - year first
    ├── Extraction_Log_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.txt              Step 4, UTF-8 text (extraction_controller.py:109-121) - year first
    └── <client>-<state code>/                          client folder ("Level 2"): utils/helpers.py:513-537
        └── Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                      new for every Step 3 run in every mode (utils/constants.py:84; core/file_organizer.py:98-104)
            ├── AnnualReport-….xlsx                     the Annual Report copy goes here (file_organizer.py:294)
            ├── ITC_Report_<client>_<code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx      Step 3 (processing_controller.py:117-122, 220)
            ├── Sales_Report_<client>_<code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx    Step 3 (processing_controller.py:124-130, 220)
            ├── ITC_Report_…<suffix>.xlsx               Step 4 copy, default suffix _Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM> (report_processor.py:91-94, 118-120)
            ├── Sales_Report_…<suffix>.xlsx             Step 4 copy
            ├── _Organization_Report_<client>_<state>.txt          Step 3 text report (file_organizer.py:300-362)
            ├── GSTR-3B Exports[ (<client>)]/           always created (utils/constants.py:86) - GSTR-3B copies
            ├── Other ITC related files[ (<client>)]/   always created (:87) - GSTR-2B Reco and IMS Reco copies
            └── Sales related files[ (<client>)]/       always created (:88) - Sales and Sales Reco copies
<system temp folder>/gst_excel_temp/                    created at every Step 3 run, never used, never deleted (core/excel_handler.py:52-53)
```

Exact naming rules (READ; RAN E2E, L):

| Name part | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `<DDMMYY HHMM>` | the PC's local time, day first, two-digit year, to the minute (`datetime.now().strftime("%d%m%y %H%M")`). Taken first at the start of the worker (`processing_controller.py:44`; report and summary names, with `_` for the space) and again a moment later when the organiser is created (`core/file_organizer.py:43`; run and Version folders) - the two can differ by a minute (B-G81). Same minute = same folders and names, reused and overwritten. | `utils/helpers.py:23-25, 31-33`; `core/file_organizer.py:43`; `processing_controller.py:44, 114, 187` |
| `<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>` | year first - only for the consolidated workbook and the Extraction_Log | `data_consolidator.py:163`; `extraction_controller.py:112` |
| `<client>-<state code>` (client folder) | whole words "Private" → "Pvt", "Limited" → "Ltd" in any letter case, then "-" and the state code; cut to the "Max length" value (15-100, default 35; 0 or less → 35) even when that box is greyed out (B-G24); no other cleaning (spaces, `&`, commas, dots stay) | `utils/helpers.py:513-537`; `core/file_organizer.py:42, 79-83`; RAN L ("ClientA Private Limited", Delhi → `ClientA Pvt Ltd-DL`) |
| `<client>` in report names and in the brackets of the category folders | `sanitize_filename`: case-sensitive "Private" → "Pvt", "Limited" → "Ltd" anywhere in the text; control characters and `<>:"/\|?*[]{}+=!@#$%^,;'"` back-tick `~` → `_`; runs of spaces/underscores → one `_`; ends stripped of `_`, `.`, spaces; text after the last dot treated as an extension | `utils/helpers.py:66-112`; RAN L (`ClientA_Pvt_Ltd`) |
| `<code>` in report names | the scan's state code (B-R21, B-R22) | `processing_controller.py:113` |
| ` (<client>)` on the three category folders | only when "Include client name in brackets for Level 4 folders" is ticked; the per-client override can never be set in B | `core/file_organizer.py:113-135`; `models/app_state.py:83` |
| `<client>` / `<state>` in `_Organization_Report_…txt` | the raw client text and the raw **full** state name (not cleaned, not abbreviated) | `core/file_organizer.py:313` |
| `<suffix>` on refreshed copies | the Step 4 "File suffix" text, `{timestamp}` → `DDMMYY_HHMM`; empty → the copy fails ("same file"); no `{timestamp}` → the same name every run, overwritten | `report_processor.py:91-94`; RAN S4 "empty_suffix" |
| Copied input files | `sanitize_filename(original name)`; copied with `shutil.copy2` (keeps file dates), size-checked | `core/file_organizer.py:253-277`; `utils/helpers.py:142-185` |
| Backups | Fresh mode, destination already exists (a run in the same minute, or two inputs whose cleaned names coincide - B-G14): `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` in the same category folder, kept for ever | `utils/helpers.py:187-204` |

Overwriting: reports, refreshed copies, the summary and consolidated workbooks and the Extraction_Log are overwritten without backup when a run repeats within the same minute (B-G27). Nothing locks the target folder against a second user or a second copy of the program (B-G82).

**Path lengths** (RAN L; invented office-like target `\\fileserver\clients\FY 2024-25\Annual Statements\Batch 1` and a 40-character client name, Maharashtra): ITC report 214 characters; refreshed ITC copy 236 (over the code's 218-character Excel limit); a GSTR-2B copy with "Include client name" ticked 287 (over 218 and over Windows' classic 260). No code shortens paths beforehand; only the client folder name is limited (B-G54).

Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`) says: settings and logs go in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` (the user's own local application-data folder, `C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local`), never in the shared app folder (`:1039-1040`; `LOG_DIR` at `:997`); find the app's own files from `APP_DIR`, never from the current folder (`:1034`); no console - `print()` shows nothing, report problems in the window and log them (`:1035-1038`); an error hook writes `error_<date>.txt` and shows a message box (`:1001-1025`); never keep a file several people write at the same time in the shared folder (`:1046-1047`); the launcher starts `pythonw.exe -B -s` with the app folder as the current folder (`:951-963`, `:962`, `:969`); exact package versions (`:919`, `:937-938`); passwords only in Windows Credential Manager (`:1041-1045`).

## APPENDIX X3: TEST SUITE

### X3.0 How to read this appendix

- **Test** (in this appendix): a small program kept in the project that runs part of the real code on known inputs and checks the result automatically, so that a later change which breaks something is noticed at once. **Test suite**: all such programs together. **pytest**: the usual Python tool that finds and runs them. **Regression**: something that worked before and stopped working after a later change.
- **Commit**: one saved step in the project's history (identified by a short code such as `c258047`). **git**: the tool that keeps that history. **PyQt5** and **Tkinter**: the two window toolkits (libraries that draw windows, buttons and lists); B's current program uses PyQt5, the older program described by the README used Tkinter. **openpyxl**: a Python add-on that reads and writes Excel files without Excel itself. **Power Query**: Excel's built-in tool that pulls data from other files into a workbook when it is "refreshed".
- **Pure Python part**: code that needs neither Windows nor Excel (for example file-name recognition, folder naming, the consolidated workbook written with openpyxl). Such parts can be tested on any computer. **COM part**: code that drives the real Microsoft Excel through Windows (COM = Windows' mechanism by which one program remote-controls another; pywin32 = the Python add-on that provides it). Such parts can only be tested on a Windows PC with Excel, or partly with **stand-ins** (fake modules that imitate Excel's replies, so that only the order of the program's own steps is checked).
- Every statement says how it was established: **READ** (by reading code or `git` output) or **RAN** (by executing something). "(me)" = done by this task (scripts and outputs in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-X345/`); a note abbreviation in brackets (for example "(DO)") = done by the reader agent whose notes are named in X6.0; "(verify)" = re-done during the verification pass of this appendix (scripts and outputs in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-X345/`, on a fresh copy of the code, `python -B`, no file written into the copy). Confidence words for inferences: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW. Places changed by the verification pass carry the note `[Corrected during verification - …]`.
- Commits: the 12 commits `edac6a3` … `47a1492` are marked [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025]; `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`, `7e09e5c`, `b0e7d0e` are marked [B only (after the split)]. Where a hash appears in a table cell without its tag (to keep the tables readable), the tag is the one fixed here: `edac6a3`, `cbfa4a5`, `6237597`, `9c56a1c`, `d674386`, `5ea77c2`, `1cb878b`, `01862a0`, `1c48722`, `4c42758`, `bd176bf`, `47a1492` = shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; `c258047`, `a62d3cc`, `c21f788`, `7e09e5c`, `b0e7d0e` = B only (after the split). B has one branch, `main` (a second branch name in the original checkout points at the same commit, X3.1 T9). Feature IDs (B-F…), rule IDs (B-R…) are from the registry; gap IDs (B-G…) are from Section 7 (gap register, Section 7.10).

> **Summary.** Project B has no tests at all - not at the snapshot `b0e7d0e`, and not in any of its 17 commits. The only executed checks of B's code that exist are the scratch scripts written for this audit, outside the repository (X3.3). Section 7 found 82 gaps (20 rated HIGH); X3.4 lists, feature by feature, where tests would matter most and why.

### X3.7 Limits of this appendix

- Nothing that needs Excel through COM could be run here (Linux, no Excel, no pywin32). Whether a COM part works on the office PCs cannot be decided from this computer; how to check: a Windows test PC with Excel and pywin32, dummy clients and the real templates.
- The ITC and Sales templates are not in the repository, so no test could check what the Links cells feed or what fills Info!BB2.
- The ranking in X3.4 is a technical judgement from the gap register (HIGH confidence for the facts, MEDIUM for the order of features within a band).

## APPENDIX X4: OLDER DOCUMENTS VERSUS THE CODE

### X4.0 What was checked, how, and the verdict labels

The author's audit method asks that any written statement of intent (it names `HANDOVER.md` and `FILE_INDEX.md`) be read as "a primary source of intent and reasoning - but NOT as a source of truth", and that every disagreement with the code be flagged as a high-value finding (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/Project_Audit_FINAL.md:9-12`); comments and docstrings (the descriptive text at the top of a Python file, class or function) must likewise be checked against the code (`Project_Audit_FINAL.md:22`, step 7), and dependencies used in the code but missing from the dependency file must be flagged (`Project_Audit_FINAL.md:221`, Section 12F).

**HANDOVER.md and FILE_INDEX.md do not exist in project B, now or at any time** (RAN (me), RAN (verify); the verification also compared the checkout's file list outside `.git` with `git ls-tree -r B/main`: the same 41 files): `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined log --all --name-only` (every commit of every branch of A and B) lists no file whose name contains `handover`, `file_index` or `fileindex` (any letter case; exit code 1); a `find` over the original checkout `/home/user/AnnualStatement_oldv2` (outside `.git`) finds none; the checkout's only branches, `main` and `claude/pensive-feynman-0mz1aa`, both point at `b0e7d0e`. B also has no `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md`, no `docs/` folder and no `tests/README.md` (those exist only in project A; RAN (me) `git log B/main -- PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md docs tests` → nothing). So B's only written statements of intent are:

| Document | Lines | Written / last changed (READ `git log B/main -- <file>`) | Status in this appendix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 364 (363 lines ending in a newline plus one that does not; RAN (me) `wc -l` = 363) | `edac6a3` (31-08-2025) rewritten by `d674386` (29-10-2025 21:15), both [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025]; never changed afterwards; identical in A and B (RAN (me): `git diff A/main B/main -- README.md` → empty) | X4.1 |
| `requirements.txt` | 14 | `edac6a3` [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025], rewritten by `c258047` [B only (after the split)] | X4.2 |

**Verdicts** (as the task defines them): **STILL TRUE** (true when written and true at `b0e7d0e`); **NO LONGER TRUE (commit)** (true when written, changed since by the commit named); **NEVER TRUE** (wrong even when written - checked in the shared code at `d674386` / `47a1492` - and still wrong); **CANNOT VERIFY** (needs Windows, Excel, the real templates, the author, or is an opinion or advice). Where one README sentence makes two claims, the row gives one verdict per part, spelled out (for example "STILL TRUE (copies) + NEVER TRUE (reports)"). Rows about files that B later deleted are NO LONGER TRUE with the deleting commit.

**Evidence.** The claim-by-claim check was first done by the DOCS reader (`/root/merge-scratch/notes2/B_docs.md`, READ of the README and of every source file the claims touch, plus runs in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-D/`). I re-read the whole README myself and re-checked in the code, by reading or running, every claim marked **(me)** in the "Checked" column, including every claim that the high-value list in X4.6 relies on. Line numbers are at `b0e7d0e` unless written `path:line@commit`.

**Confidentiality.** The README's naming table (README.md:128-133) uses one generic company-style example name; it is written `<example client>` below (Appendix X5 lists it). No client data is quoted anywhere in this appendix.

### X4.1 `README.md` (`d674386`, 29-10-2025, [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025]) versus B's code

**What it is.** The user guide of the Tkinter "v3.0" program, rewritten the day before the split. It was written **before** the last seven shared commits (`5ea77c2`, `1cb878b`, `01862a0`, `1c48722`, `4c42758`, `bd176bf`, `47a1492`, all [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025]) and before all five B-only commits, and was never updated in B. B's code at the snapshot is the PyQt5 "v4.0" program (PyQt5 = the window toolkit B uses; Tkinter = the older one the README describes).

#### X4.1.4 Templates and the file-naming convention (README 115-133) [GST RULE] ⚠

#### X4.1.14 README instructions that are wrong for a user following them on B today

1. **Installing** (RM38, RM39): `pip install -r requirements.txt` does not install pywin32, so the window will not open; the README's own "Requirements.txt Contents" block never matched the file.
2. **Operating system** (RM28): macOS and Linux cannot open B at all.
3. **The error message** (RM88): B prints "No module named 'pythoncom'" and advises `pip install PyQt5 openpyxl`; the README's remedy (pywin32) is the right package but is listed under a different message.
4. **Templates** (RM41): the README recommends `.xltx`; B's picker offers `.xlsx`/`.xlsm` and always names the report `.xlsx` (B-G30).
5. **Dry Run** (RM59) is on Step 2, not Step 3; the extractor button is "Start Extraction", not "Refresh & Extract" (RM64).
6. **Variations** (RM58, RM80, RM96): there is no list of mis-named files to review; the summary sheet is always empty.
7. **Resume** (RM53) does not continue an interrupted run.
8. **Output names** (RM69, RM74) use `DDMMYY_HHMM`, not `DDMMYYYY_HHMMSS`; the per-client text report's statistics are batch totals (RM75).
9. **Logs** (RM93-RM95): `pq_extractor.log` is never written; `gst_organizer.log` appears in whatever folder the program was started from; `launch_extractor.py` writes no log file.
10. **"Template not found"** (RM91) means a wrong template path, not a missing Links sheet.
11. **Editing `skip_refresh` in `cell_mappings.py`** (RM85) has no effect; the Step 4 tick box always wins.

### X4.6 High-value discrepancies (most important first)

> These are places where a document says one thing and the code does another. They are stated as facts; for [GST RULE] items nothing here says which version is right.

**D1 - B cannot start at all without pywin32, while the README and `requirements.txt` say pywin32 is needed only for Power Query and that macOS and Linux work** (README 24, 52, 55, 104-108, 275; `requirements.txt:13-14`; RM13, RM28, RM38, RM88, RQ6, DS37, DS38). Import chain `main.py:38` → `gui/pyqt_main_window.py:27` → `gui/controllers/extraction_controller.py:10` → `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` (no fallback), while `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` (guarding `win32com.client` and `pythoncom`) and `utils/helpers.py:473-483` (guarding `win32api`) guard their pywin32 imports. RAN (me), RAN (verify): `main.py` and `launch_extractor.py` both exit 1 with "No module named 'pythoncom'", and `main.py` advises `pip install PyQt5 openpyxl`.

```python
# power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15 (excerpt) - no try/except around these lines
import pythoncom
import win32com.client
import win32api
import win32con
import win32gui
``` Introduced by `c258047` [B only (after the split)]. HIGH. (B-G32, registry B-R124.)

**D2 - [GST RULE] ⚠ The consolidated extraction workbook fills the IGST / CGST / SGST columns of "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" (9 of 22 columns) from `Diff GSTR-3B` J15/K15/L15, not from the cells `cell_mappings.py` names** (README 15, 25, 175-176, 231; `cell_mappings.py:2-3`; RM8, RM14, DS27). Cause: `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:130-133` takes the first extracted field whose name *contains* the column label; one-word labels match the earlier `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST/CGST/SGST` fields. RAN (me) `consol_check.py`, RAN (verify): 9 mismatches, exactly these columns. When the README was written all labels had two or more words and every column received the cell configured for it; the three sheets came in `47a1492` [shared - before the split on 30-10-2025]. Which cells are right is the author's call. HIGH. (B-G1, B-R79-B-R83.)

```python
# power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:130-138 (excerpt; indentation shortened)
for field_name, field_value in extracted_data.items():
    if mapping['output_column'] in field_name:
        value = field_value
        break
# Fallback: try exact match
if value is None and mapping['input_cell']:
    key = f"{sheet_name}_{mapping['output_column']}".replace(' ', '_')
    value = extracted_data.get(key)
```

The first loop takes the first extracted field whose name contains the column label: for the one-word label "IGST" that is `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST`, because the "Diff GSTR-3B" cells are read first (READ (verify) `report_processor.py:507-539`, `cell_mappings.py:264-278`).

That script has no check for home-folder paths or "OneDrive"; those two were added in the verification re-run `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-B-X345/scan/secret_scan2.sh` (same 102 versions; `\Users\`, `/home/`, `/Users/` and "onedrive" in any letter case) [Corrected during verification - the text first said the B-X345 script covered home-folder paths and "OneDrive"]. ## SELF-CONSISTENCY REVIEW

> **How this record was made.** The review below was carried out on 23-10-2026 (task B-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW), after the twelve sections and six appendices had been assembled into this one document. The reviewer read the whole document from Section 1 to the end in chunks, checked it against the writers' 177 cross-section flags (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/B_cross_flags.md`: 118 facts for other sections, 3 UNREGISTERED items and 59 corrections to the working notes), and made every correction directly in the text with an exact-text edit. Each correction is marked where it was made, as `[Corrected during self-review - originally stated X, but Section Y revealed Z]`, or as "(added during self-review)" / "[clarified during self-review]" where something was only added. Before a claim about the code was changed, the code was opened again (READ) or a small run was made (RAN). Nothing was shortened or removed. The working log is `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW/review_log.md`.
>
> **Runs made for this review.** All were made in `/root/merge-scratch/run/B-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW/`, on the copy `proj/` (byte-identical to `/root/merge-scratch/B-copy`), with `python -B` (no compiled files written), a redirected home folder and made-up inputs only. Afterwards `diff -rq proj /root/merge-scratch/B-copy` reported no difference and neither folder held a `__pycache__` folder or `.pyc` file. B's own checkout `/home/user/AnnualStatement_oldv2` was only read (it is still at `b0e7d0e`, with no local changes). The scripts are `assemble.py`, `check_headings.py`, `check_ids.py`, `check_ids2.py`, `scripts/flagcheck.py` (finds where a flagged fact appears, section by section), `scripts/pyver_sanitize.py` (name cleaning on Python 3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16 and 3.14.6) and `scripts/tz_consolidator.py` (the consolidated workbook with a time-zone-aware date; its leftover file is in `work/`).

### What was checked, and how

|---|---|---|
| Assembly | `assemble.py` joined `B/S1.md`, `S2.md`, `S3a.md`, `S3b.md`, `S45.md`, `S67.md`, `S89.md`, `S10.md`, `S11.md`, `S12own.md` (with its SHARED-12A marker line replaced by `/root/merge-scratch/audit/shared/S12A_shared.md`), `S12BF.md`, `X12.md`, `X345.md`, with a blank line between files. `check_headings.py` (which skips text inside code blocks) confirmed the 24 section and appendix headings and this one. It was re-run after all edits. | Before the edits: 2,280,557 characters, 13,347 lines. Every heading appears once and in order. Code blocks are balanced. No marker is left. The only level-1 heading outside code blocks is the title. (The `# One naming rule, one finder` line in 11.6 sits inside a code block, as an example skill file.) |

### Checked and found consistent (no edit needed)

- **Section 1 vs the rest.** The headline counts (17 commits = 12 shared + 5 B only; 41 files, 38 Python, 7,821 lines; 34 features, 144 rules, 82 gaps), the start-up chain without pywin32, B-G1 (9 of 22 columns, from `47a1492`) and the public-repository warning all agree with Sections 2, 3, 7, 12 and X5.
- **Gap register 7.10.** The counts by origin and by severity agree with the 82 entries (recounted after the edits).
- **Section 11 vs Section 8.** See check 1a. Also: the complexity counts in 11.5 (6 COMPLEX, 12 MODERATE, 15 SIMPLE, 1 not carried over = 34) agree with the 11.5.2 table, and 11.7's "13 items" (10 tagged [GST RULE] plus 3 that touch one) agree with its table.
- **Section 12.** These all agree with 12B.1 (`filehist.txt`), 12C.2 and 12C.3, and with Sections 2, 5 and X4:
  - No GST-rule value was changed or removed by any B-only commit; `utils/constants.py` and `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py` are byte-identical to `47a1492`.
  - B-G1 began at `47a1492`, when the one-word column titles were added.
  - At `a62d3cc` the program could not start until `c21f788`, 28 minutes later (12B.7, X3.5).
  - The commit-message claims that the diffs contradict (c258047's "New Files (20)" / "Modified Files (15)" against 18 and 14, ".claude already in .gitignore", "12-field AppSettings" against 11; a62d3cc's "All functionality has been reimplemented"; 6237597's "Corrected app.py reference") agree between Sections 1, 2.9, 12A and X4.5.
  - B has never had tests, a `pytest.ini` or CI (2.8.12, 9, 12F.6, X3.1).
- **Python 3.7.** Sections 1, 9.4 and 12F.3 agree that 3.7 can still be installed but that only 3.10 or newer gets the newest build of every package. The S89 writer's flag "3.7 cannot be met" was itself corrected during verification of Section 9 (9.4: pip resolves builds for 3.7), so no section repeats it.
- **The openpyxl imports.** The X345 writer's correction to the notes, "the openpyxl imports are at `core/excel_handler.py:30-32`", is **wrong** and was not applied. READ: line 30 is the comment "# Fallback to openpyxl if not on Windows"; the three imports are at lines 31-33, as the document says (Sections 2, 12F.2 and X1).
- **Write and read paths.** Section 4.6 and Appendix X2.5 agree on every file and on every on-disk item B's steps share. The "Latest run folder" mismatch (B-G12), the refreshed-copy naming mismatch (B-G9), the run-history key mismatch (B-G25) and the empty Variations sheet (B-G20) are each stated once and cited consistently.
- **Older documents.** README.md is treated as a source of intent everywhere. Every disagreement is flagged in 4.8, 5.20, 6.2.8, 7.9, 8.9, 9.10, 10.12, 12B.8, 12C.6, 12D.6, 12E.7, 12F.8, X1.6, X2.9 and X4, and these agree with one another.

**Corrections to the working notes found by this check.** `B_excel_pq_safety.md` §4.1 and `B_outside_files_state.md` §1.3 record that B's openpyxl fallback drops Power Query and macros, but not that the same save also drops shapes drawn on a sheet (RAN here, X1.4.3 F5) - an omission, not a wrong statement. **Limits of this check.** Plain English was checked by the first use of a list of about 200 terms and by each section's glossary, not by re-reading all 13,500 lines. The shared part of 12A (the twelve shared commits) was only read, not edited, so that it stays the same text in both audits. The shape test used a drawing part written by hand, not one saved by a real Excel, and nothing that needs Windows or Excel was run; that the COM path keeps shapes is MEDIUM (READ). The judgement-word search finds words, not meanings; a judgement phrased without any of the searched words could remain.
